title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Is every degree of decidable categoricity also a degree of categoricity, and does the converse hold? More precisely, the record asks whether the class of degrees of decidable categoricity coincides with the class of degrees of categoricity.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given of the equivalence between the class of degrees of decidable categoricity and the class of degrees of categoricity, resolving both directions.

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval — question q: zero singular
open: In phase retrieval, how many zero coefficients may the expansion of $f$ with respect to the frame $F$ contain while $f$ remains uniquely recoverable?
solved_when: A characterization (sharp bound or exact criterion) is given for the maximum number of vanishing coefficients $F_x$ permitting unique recovery of $f$.
why: It identifies the precise degeneracy threshold at which uniqueness of phase retrieval breaks down, delimiting when reconstruction methods can be trusted.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval — question q: truncation
open: Which band limit must be assumed to guarantee unique recovery in phase retrieval when symmetric measurement windows are used? More generally, what is the quantitative relation between the vanishing of $|F_x|$ and the band-limitedness of $f$, as measured in terms of WDD?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper, a curated list of open problems in phase retrieval: arXiv:2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene), 2025.
solved_when: A precise band-limit condition is identified that guarantees uniqueness for symmetric windows, together with a quantitative characterization relating vanishing $|F_x|$ and band-limited $f$ via WDD.
why: It would pin down exactly when symmetric-window phase retrieval is unambiguous, replacing ad hoc assumptions with a usable uniqueness criterion.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval — question q: scan position
open: Can the Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD) method be extended to arbitrary, reasonable scanning patterns in ptychography, and what assumptions on the object are needed to make such a derivation work?
solved_when: A derivation of WDD is given that applies to arbitrary (reasonable) scan positions, together with an explicit characterization of the necessary object assumptions.
why: It would free WDD-based phase retrieval from restrictions on how the scan is laid out, clarifying the fundamental requirements on the object for direct reconstruction methods.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval
open: Beyond Gaussian and other standard window classes, which window functions $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ permit recovery of a signal up to a global phase from STFT magnitude measurements sampled on a lattice?
solved_when: A characterization (or a broad, provably sufficient class) of windows $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ for which lattice-sampled STFT phaseless measurements determine every signal up to global phase is established, or a counterexample window outside the known families is shown to fail uniqueness.
why: It delineates exactly which short-time Fourier transform measurement setups are admissible for phaseless recovery, directly informing which practical window choices in optics and signal processing can guarantee reconstruction.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval — question q: scan position cont
open: For a fixed "nice" window function $w$, are there uniqueness results for phase retrieval from spectrogram measurements $|V_w f|^2$ taken on spiral-like sampling sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$? More broadly, what characterizes the sampling sets that are informative enough to recover $f$ up to a global phase from these measurements?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source survey of open problems in phase retrieval (arXiv:2505.15351v1, by Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, and Wim Coene, 2025); no partial results are recorded there.
solved_when: A uniqueness theorem (or a characterization) is established identifying sampling sets — in particular spiral-like sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ — for which $f$ is determined up to global phase by $|V_w f|^2$, for a suitable fixed window $w$.
why: It would settle when spectrogram-based phase retrieval on nonuniform, geometry-driven sampling patterns is possible, giving a principled criterion for designing measurement sets rather than relying on ad hoc conditions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval
open: Which functions in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, beyond the Gaussian window itself, can be recovered up to a global phase from their Gabor magnitude measurements $|Gf|^2$ sampled on a lattice $\Lambda = a\mathbb{Z} \times b\mathbb{Z}$? Since a dense set of functions provably cannot be so recovered while the Gaussian $w$ can, one asks whether there is a dense set of recoverable functions as well — and, if so, whether that set is of the first or second Baire category, so as to gauge whether a "typical" function is more likely to be recoverable from Gabor magnitude measurements or not.
status: Stated as open in the 2025 survey "A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval" (arXiv:2505.15351v1, Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene). Known context there: the Gaussian $w$ is recoverable up to a global phase from $|Gw|^2$ on $a\mathbb{Z} \times b\mathbb{Z}$, while a dense set of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ functions cannot be recovered up to a global phase from these measurements.
solved_when: A dense subset of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ of functions recoverable up to a global phase from $|Gf|^2$ on $\Lambda = a\mathbb{Z} \times b\mathbb{Z}$ is exhibited (or shown not to exist), together with a determination of whether that set is of the first or second category.
why: It determines whether phase retrieval from sampled Gabor magnitudes is generic or exceptional, sharpening our understanding of which signals STFT-based phase retrieval can actually reconstruct in practice.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval
open: When a phase-retrieval reconstruction is obtained by solving an optimization problem, is there a way to detect — and ideally quantify — how far the recovered solution is from the true underlying object? Formally, given a solution $z$ of the minimization $\min_z \|AG(z) - y\|_2$, can we detect or even bound the bias $|G(z) - f_0|$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), the survey arXiv:2505.15351 by Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, and Wim Coene; no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A method or criterion is established that, from the computed solution $z$, either detects whether the bias $|G(z) - f_0|$ is non-negligible or provides a quantitative bound on its magnitude.
why: It would give practitioners a way to assess the trustworthiness of a phase-retrieval reconstruction without access to the ground truth, turning an optimization output into a certifiable estimate.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351v1 (Marc Allain, Selin Aslan, Wim Coene)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024 — conjecture conj:8
open: Is a uniform random 3-regular graph globally synchronizing with high probability? Formally, does the probability of global synchronization tend to 1 as the number of vertices $n$ grows?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024" (arXiv:2504.20539v1, Afonso S. Bandeira, Anastasia Kireeva, Antoine Maillard).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for a uniform random 3-regular graph, global synchronization holds with probability tending to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
why: Resolving it would establish a sharp, canonical example of sparse-network synchronization, settling a natural sparse-graph case of the general synchronization question.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20539v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Anastasia Kireeva, Antoine Maillard)

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory
open: For integers $r \ge 1$ and sufficiently large $m$, consider a non-bipartite graph $G$ with $m$ edges that contains no copy of the book graph $B_{2,r+1}$. Conjecture 9 of the source survey asserts an extremal upper bound on the spectral radius of every such $G$ — is this conjecture true?
status: The conjecture was stated as open in the 2025 survey by Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, and Minjie Zhang (arXiv:2512.19395v1); no resolution is recorded there.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjectured spectral-radius upper bound for every $B_{2,r+1}$-free non-bipartite graph of size $m$, for all $r \ge 1$ and $m$ sufficiently large.
why: It resolves one entry in the edge-spectral-Turán catalogue, extending classical extremal edge counts to the spectral radius setting for book-free non-bipartite graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: If $X$ is a weak Asplund space, must the product of $X$ with a one-dimensional space again be a weak Asplund space?
solved_when: A proof that $X \times \mathbb{R}$ is weak Asplund for every weak Asplund space $X$, or a counterexample exhibiting such an $X$ for which the product fails to be weak Asplund.
why: It would clarify whether the weak Asplund property is stable under even the simplest finite-dimensional products, a basic structural question for this class of spaces.

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: If $X$ is a weak Asplund space, must the product $X \times \ell^{2}$ again be a weak Asplund space?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) that for every weak Asplund space $X$, the product $X \times \ell^{2}$ is weak Asplund.
why: It would clarify whether the weak Asplund property is stable under products with even the simplest infinite-dimensional factors, a basic structural question in nonsmooth analysis.

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: If $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $Y$ is a separable space, must the product $X \times Y$ again be weak Asplund? In particular, is the product of a weak Asplund space with a one-dimensional space weak Asplund?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) that $X \times Y$ is weak Asplund for every weak Asplund space $X$ and separable space $Y$ is given.
why: This concerns whether the class of weak Asplund spaces is stable under products with separable factors — a basic closure property whose failure would sharply delimit the class.

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: If $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $Y$ is a reflexive space, must the product $X \times Y$ again be a weak Asplund space?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) settling whether the product of any weak Asplund space with any reflexive space is weak Asplund.
why: It would clarify whether the weak Asplund property is stable under products with reflexive factors, a basic structural question about this class of spaces.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: What is the topological type of the achievement set $E(x_n)$ for the sequence defined by $x_{2n-1} := \frac{1}{2^{2n-1}}$ and $x_{2n} := \frac{1}{2^{2n}+1}$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Achievement sets — current results and open problems" by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski (http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1).
solved_when: The achievement set $E(x_n)$ of this specific sequence is explicitly determined up to homeomorphism — that is, its topological type is identified (for example, as a finite union of intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval).
why: Classifying the achievement set of this explicit sequence would sharpen the known picture of how the terms of a sequence control the topology of its subsum set, a central question in the theory of achievement sets.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Does every geometric sequence $(q^n)_{n N}$ with $q ( 12,1)$ contain a subsequence $(q^{n_k})_{k N}$ such that $E(q^{n_k})$ is a Cantorval?

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: For a Ferens sequence $(x_n)$, must the set of parameters $q$ in the interval $\big(1/(s-2m+3),\, 1/(s-2m+1)\big)$ for which the achievement set $E(x_n)$ has measure zero be only countable? Formally: is the exceptional set of $q$-values producing a measure-zero achievement set at most countable?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that, for every Ferens sequence $(x_n)$, the set $\{q \in (1/(s-2m+3), 1/(s-2m+1)) : E(x_n) \text{ has measure zero}\}$ is countable.
why: It would pin down how rare measure-zero achievement sets are within this family, sharpening the picture of the size structure of achievement sets of Ferens sequences.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Does the achievement set of a Ferens sequence satisfy the Palis dichotomy for the stated range of parameters q — that is, for q between 1/(s−2m+3) and 1/(s−2m+1), must E(x_n) either have measure zero or contain an interval? A second sentence sharpening formally: is it true that for q ∈ (1/(s−2m+3), 1/(s−2m+1)) no intermediate case (positive measure but empty interior) can occur?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2512.17285v1 by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski, "Achievement sets — current results and open problems" (problem 8).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every Ferens sequence (x_n) and every q in the interval (1/(s−2m+3), 1/(s−2m+1)), the achievement set E(x_n) either has Lebesgue measure zero or contains an interval.
why: It would extend the Palis dichotomy, a fundamental zero-one type alternative for sets of subsums, to a class of sequences where the general theory does not yet decide the question.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Given an achievable Cantorval $D$, must there exist achievable Cantorvals $D'$ and $D''$ such that $D + D'$ is again a Cantorval while $D + D''$ is an interval? In other words, can every achievable Cantorval be algebraically "steered" by Minkowski summation into either kind of achievable outcome?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2512.17285v1 by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given that for every achievable Cantorval $D$ there exist achievable Cantorvals $D'$ and $D''$ with $D + D'$ a Cantorval and $D + D''$ an interval; a single explicit counterexample $D$ for which no such $D'$ or $D''$ exists would settle it negatively.
why: It probes how flexible the class of achievable Cantorvals is under Minkowski addition, revealing whether these hybrid sets behave more like Cantor sets or intervals when summed.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Can every infinite achievement set be written as the sum of two achievement sets, each of Hausdorff dimension $0$? More precisely, does such a decomposition always exist for the achievement sets arising as subsum sets of divergent series?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the statement: every infinite achievement set decomposes into the sum of two achievement sets, each of Hausdorff dimension $0$.
why: It would clarify the fine additive structure of achievement sets by showing that even large ones can be built from dimension-zero pieces, a basic structural question in this corner of fractal/descriptive set theory.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Does there exist an achievement set $E$ such that both its set of frontier points ${Fr}\,E$ and its set of accumulation points $E^*$ are themselves achievement sets?
solved_when: An explicit example of an achievement set $E$ is produced for which both ${Fr}\,E$ and $E^*$ are achievement sets, or a proof is given that no such $E$ exists.
why: It probes how robust the class of achievement sets is under basic point-set operations, clarifying which derived sets can themselves arise as achievement sets.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Is the boundary of any achievable Cantorval an achievable set? In other words, does every Cantorval arising as an achievement set have a boundary that is itself an achievement set?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that the boundary of every achievable Cantorval is, or is not, an achievable set.
why: It would clarify the stability of the class of achievement sets under boundary-taking, a basic structural question for Cantorvals.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Can two achievable Cantorvals have a union that is a closed interval? That is, do there exist sequences $(x_n)$ and $(y_n)$ such that the achievement sets $E(x_n)$ and $E(y_n)$ are Cantorvals, yet $E(x_n) \cup E(y_n)$ is a closed interval?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Achievement sets — current results and open problems" by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski (http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: Explicit sequences $(x_n)$ and $(y_n)$ are constructed whose achievement sets are both Cantorvals and whose union is a closed interval, or a proof is given that no such pair exists.
why: It probes how achievable Cantorvals can overlap and complement each other, clarifying the boundary between achievement sets that are Cantorvals and those that fill intervals.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Do there exist achievable Cantorvals whose boundary has positive Lebesgue measure? Equivalently, can the boundary of an achievement set that forms a Cantorval carry nonzero Lebesgue measure?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), a curated open-problems paper by Szymom Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski, arXiv:2512.17285v1 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1).
solved_when: An explicit construction of an achievable Cantorval with boundary of positive Lebesgue measure is given, or a proof that no such Cantorval exists.
why: It would clarify the fine boundary structure of achievement sets, a central object in the theory of subsum sets of series.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Is there an analogue of the Nymann–Saenz Lemma for the endpoints of interval components of an achievement set that is a Cantorval? More precisely, if $E(x_n)$ is a Cantorval and $a$ and $b$ are left endpoints of two distinct $E$-intervals, does there exist some $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the conclusion analogous to the Nymann–Saenz setting holds?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Achievement sets — current results and open problems" (http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1, Szymon Głąb, Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via counterexample) of the proposed analogue for Cantorvals, addressing the situation where $E(x_n)$ is a Cantorval and $a, b$ are left endpoints of two distinct $E$-intervals, is established.
why: The Nymann–Saenz Lemma is a known tool in the structure theory of achievement sets, and an endpoint analogue for Cantorvals would sharpen our description of how the interval components of these hybrid sets are arranged.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Which subsets of the plane can arise as achievement sets, up to homeomorphism? More precisely, give a topological characterization of the homeomorphism classes of achievement sets in \(\mathbb{R}^2\).
solved_when: A complete list of, or structural criterion for, the homeomorphism types of achievement sets in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) is given, with proof.
why: It would settle the basic classification question for achievement sets in the plane and reveal which topological behaviors the achievement construction can and cannot produce.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Which sets can arise as the achievement set of the geometric-pair sequence \((p^n, q^n)\)? Formally, characterize \(E(p^n, q^n)\) for all \(p, q \in (0,1)\).
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1 (Szymon Głąb, Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski).
solved_when: A complete characterization of the achievement set \(E(p^n, q^n)\) — e.g., membership of each pair \((p,q)\) in a classification determining when the set is a finite union of intervals, a Cantor set, or another type — is given for all \(p, q \in (0,1)\).
why: It would extend the classical achievement-set theory for single geometric sequences to pairs, sharpening our understanding of how subsum sets of rapidly shrinking sequences transition from interval-like to Cantor-like structure.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Does the known characterization of minimal representations for achievable multi-interval sets extend to Cantorvals? That is, for an achievable Cantorval \(E\), must it still hold that \((x_n)\) is a minimal representation for \(E\) if and only if \(x_n < r_{n+1}\) for only finitely many \(n\)?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2512.17285v1 (Szymon Głąb, Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski). The multi-interval case is settled: for an achievable multi-interval set \(E\), \((x_n)\) is a minimal representation if and only if \(x_n < r_{n+1}\) for only finitely many \(n\).
solved_when: A proof or counterexample showing whether, for every achievable Cantorval \(E\), the sequence \((x_n)\) is a minimal representation for \(E\) if and only if \(x_n < r_{n+1}\) for only finitely many \(n\).
why: It would complete the characterization of minimal representations across the full class of achievement sets, rather than only the multi-interval case.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Is it true that for any Borel set \(A \subset [0,\infty)\), there exists a Borel set \(B \subset \mathbb{R}\) whose achievement set \(\mathrm{E}(B)\) equals \(A\) — that is, does every nonnegative Borel set arise as the achievement set of some Borel set of terms?
solved_when: A proof that every Borel \(A \subset [0,\infty)\) is realized as \(\mathrm{E}(B)\) for some Borel \(B \subset \mathbb{R}\), or an explicit counterexample of a Borel set not so realized, resolves the problem.
why: It would characterize exactly which sets can occur as achievement sets, settling a basic structural question about subsums of real series.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: What is a maximal distance minimizer for the ball $M = B_R$ when $R > r$? In particular, characterize the minimizer in the regime $4.98r > R > r$, where the problem remains open.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2511.18217v1 (Yana Teplitskaya); no solution is known for $4.98r > R > r$.
solved_when: An explicit description of a maximal distance minimizer for $M = B_R$ is given for the range $4.98r > R > r$.
why: It completes the classification of maximal distance minimizers for balls, a basic yet unresolved case of the general theory.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: What are the maximal distance minimizers for an $R$-stadium, i.e. the boundary of the $R$-neighborhood of a segment? In particular, this remains unknown for the parameter range $r < R < 5r$.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18217v1 (Yana Teplitskaya).
solved_when: A complete characterization of the set of maximal distance minimizers for the $R$-stadium is given, at least for all $r < R < 5r$.
why: Resolving it advances the study of maximal distance minimizers, a geometric optimization object closely tied to Steiner trees, by settling a basic explicit case left open by the source paper.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: Must every maximal distance minimizer in $\mathbb{R}^d$ be a union of a finite number of injective curves? This remains open already for $d = 3$.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), Yana Teplitskaya, arXiv:2511.18217v1.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that any MDM in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a finite union of injective curves, in particular resolving the case $d = 3$.
why: It would settle the basic structural regularity of maximal distance minimizers, which is the foundational step toward any finer description of their geometry.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: If a set is an $r$-minimizer for some $M$, must it be the unique $r$-minimizer for $B_r(M)$? In other words, does taking the $r$-neighborhood of $M$ force the minimizer to become unique?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every $r$-minimizer for some $M$ is the unique $r$-minimizer for $B_r(M)$.
why: Resolving it would clarify how uniqueness of maximal distance minimizers behaves under the natural operation of thickening the boundary set by its own radius.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: For a given compact set $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and radius $r > 0$, what can be said about the structure of maximal distance minimizers — the compact sets $\Sigma$ minimizing the maximum distance from points of $M$ to $\Sigma$ subject to a length constraint?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18217v1 (Yana Teplitskaya); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A characterization or existence/regularity result for the maximal distance minimizer associated to arbitrary $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $r > 0$ is established.
why: Maximal distance minimizers generalize Steiner trees and their structure is poorly understood beyond special cases; a solution would advance the geometric measure-theoretic theory of optimal networks approximating a given set.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: Does there exist a finite set of terminals in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d \geq 3$, with two distinct Steiner trees $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ such that the directions of all segments incident to the terminals are the same in both trees? Equivalently, can two different Steiner trees for the same terminal set coincide in a neighborhood of every terminal?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), the curated open-problems paper by Yana Teplitskaya, http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18217v1; no progress beyond its statement is recorded.
solved_when: An explicit finite terminal set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for some $d \geq 3$ is produced together with two distinct Steiner trees whose segments incident to terminals have identical directions; or, alternatively, a proof that no such pair of trees exists for any finite terminal set in any dimension $d \geq 3$.
why: It probes the extent to which the local behavior of a Steiner tree near its terminals determines the tree globally, a basic uniqueness question for Steiner trees in higher dimensions.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: What is the exact value of the Steiner ratio in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 2$ — that is, the infimum over finite point sets of the ratio between the length of a shortest Steiner tree and the length of a minimum spanning tree? More precisely, can this constant be determined (or sharply bounded) as a function of the dimension $d$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers," question 11, by Yana Teplitskaya (http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18217v1).
solved_when: The Steiner ratio of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is determined exactly, or sharp quantitative bounds on it as a function of $d$ are established.
why: The Steiner ratio is the fundamental constant governing how much length Steiner points can save over ordinary spanning trees, and its exact values are a basic benchmark for the theory of Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: What is the largest possible number of points in $B_{tr}(x)$ when $t = 1/2$ — and, more generally, for other values of $t \in (0,1)$? In other words, determine the sharp upper bound on the cardinality of this set as a function of the parameter $t$.
solved_when: An explicit bound (ideally sharp) on the number of points of $B_{tr}(x)$ is established for $t = 1/2$, or for general $t \in (0,1)$, with matching examples showing it cannot be improved.
why: A sharp answer would clarify the local structure of maximal distance minimizers near branch points, constraining how Steiner-type trees can bifurcate in this setting.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers — question questRandom
open: Does the length of a Steiner tree for a random $N$-point input in $\mathbb{R}^d$ grow asymptotically as $N^{\frac{d-1}{d}}$? More precisely, is there a constant depending only on the dimension and the random model such that the length behaves like that constant times $N^{\frac{d-1}{d}}$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), the open-problems paper available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18217v1 (Yana Teplitskaya).
solved_when: The asymptotic behavior of the Steiner tree length for a random $N$-point input in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is established, with the growth rate $N^{\frac{d-1}{d}}$ and a constant depending on $d$ and the random model.
why: It would give a sharp law for the expected size of optimal Steiner trees on random inputs, a basic benchmark for network-design heuristics and for the theory of random geometric optimization.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: Is it true that one can always connect $n$ points lying in a rectangle by a Steiner tree that stays within the rectangle?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) is given for whether every finite set of points in a rectangle admits a connecting Steiner tree contained entirely in that rectangle.
why: It would clarify basic geometric constraints on Steiner trees for points confined to a region, a natural question in the study of maximal distance minimizers and Steiner-type optimization.

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers

title: on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
open: Can one construct a non-planar example of a unique full Steiner tree with infinitely many branching points? More precisely, does there exist such a tree embedded outside the plane, or is infinitude of branching points possible only in planar configurations?

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar — problem p1
open: If a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a circle as its boundary, must the surface be either a planar disk or a spherical cap?

solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every compact embedded CMC surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ spanning a circle is a planar disk or a spherical cap, or an explicit embedded CMC surface spanning a circle that is neither.
why: It would resolve a fundamental classification question for CMC surfaces with circular boundary, completing our understanding of the simplest boundary curve possible.

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar — problem p2
open: When is a compact embedded constant mean curvature surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ spanning a planar closed curve $C$ contained entirely on one side of the boundary plane? In particular, does this one-sidedness hold when $C$ is convex?
status: Stated as an open problem by Rafael López in the 2025 paper arXiv:2505.01143v1.

why: It would extend the classical maximum-principle picture of how CMC surfaces interact with planes to the free-boundary-with-fixed-boundary setting, clarifying which boundary data force a barrier-type behavior.

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar — problem p3

solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) classifying all compact star-shaped CMC surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ spanning a circle as planar disks or spherical caps.

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar — problem p4
open: Let $C$ be a simple closed convex curve in a plane $P$, and let $\Sigma$ be a compact embedded constant mean curvature surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with boundary $\partial\Sigma = C$. If $\Sigma$ lies entirely on one side of $P$, must $\Sigma$ be a topological disk?

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar — problem p5

why: It would clarify the global symmetry and decomposition structure of compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary, constraining how such graphs can sit in space.

title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Appli — problem prob:top_expanders
open: Do there exist, for each $d \geq 2$, families of $d$-dimensional bounded-degree topological expanders? A sharper formulation asks for explicit sequences of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes with uniformly bounded degree whose topological expansion properties do not degenerate.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), "Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Appli" by Michael Chapman and Alexander Lubotzky (http://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06706v3).
solved_when: For every $d \geq 2$, an explicit (or existence) construction of an infinite family of $d$-dimensional bounded-degree topological expanders is given, with the degree bound uniform across the family.
why: Bounded-degree topological expanders are the higher-dimensional analogue of expander graphs and underpin applications from property testing of PCP-type statements to topological high-dimensional expanders in coding; without them, many higher-dimensional expansion results remain conditional on unbounded-degree constructions.

why: Coboundary expanders are a key tool in the stability of homomorphisms, coverings, and cocycles; a positive answer would supply the higher-dimensional analogs of expander graphs needed for such stability results over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions — problem prob: defective Segre veronese
open: Which Segre–Veronese varieties are defective, and what is the dimension of their secant varieties in each case? In other words, give a complete classification of defective Segre–Veronese varieties together with a formula for the corresponding secant dimensions.
solved_when: A complete classification of the defective Segre–Veronese varieties is available, with the dimension of each secant variety determined.
why: Secant dimensions govern tensor rank and border rank, so the classification tells exactly when the expected dimension count fails, which is the basic data needed to apply geometric methods to tensor decomposition.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Which line bundles on a product of projective spaces are special, and can they be classified? More broadly, can special line bundles be classified on other interesting classes of varieties?
solved_when: A complete classification of special line bundles on products of projective spaces is given, or, for the general form, a classification on a specified interesting class of varieties.
why: A classification would clarify the geometry of products of projective spaces and provide a template for understanding special line bundles on broader classes of varieties.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions — problem probl: Terracini
open: Given a variety $X$, a line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $X$ and an integer $r$, does there exist a 0-dimensional scheme $\mathcal{Z}\subset X$ which is a union of disjoint schemes of degree 2, such that the reduced scheme $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{red}}$ imposes independent conditions on $\mathcal{L}$ but $\mathcal{Z}$ does not?
solved_when: An example is produced (for some $X$, $\mathcal{L}$, $r$) of a 0-dimensional scheme that is a union of disjoint double schemes whose reduction imposes independent conditions on $\mathcal{L}$ while the scheme itself does not — or a proof that no such scheme exists.
why: Such a scheme would show that passing from reduced points to degree-2 schemes can destroy the independence of imposed conditions, directly informing the Terracini-type behavior of secant varieties and osculating spaces of tensors.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Can we classify all varieties of small dimension whose second, or third, secant variety has minimal degree? More generally, for a given $r$, can we produce a variety $X$ whose $r$-th secant variety $\sigma_r(X)$ is a hypersurface of the smallest possible degree?
solved_when: A classification of small-dimensional varieties whose second and/or third secant variety is of minimal degree is achieved, together with a general construction producing, for each $r$, a variety $X$ with $\sigma_r(X)$ a hypersurface of the smallest possible degree.
why: Secant varieties of minimal degree are the extremal cases of the classification, and identifying them clarifies which varieties have the smallest possible degree for their higher secants — a basic structural question in classical algebraic geometry with direct ties to tensor decomposition.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions — problem prob: real singular tuples
open: Given real vector spaces $V_1, \dots, V_d$ with $\dim V_i = n_i + 1$, does there exist a tensor $T \in V_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes V_d$ whose $c(\cdot)$ critical points are all defined over the real numbers?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper "Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions" by Fulvio Gesmundo, http://arxiv.org/abs/2304.10570v1 (2023).
solved_when: A tensor is exhibited whose critical points are all defined over the real numbers, matching the expected count $c(\cdot)$, for the given dimensions $\dim V_i = n_i + 1$.
why: A positive answer would show that the full real-geometry of the singular tuples of a tensor can be realized, not just its complex counterpart.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: What is the Euclidean distance degree of the secant variety of the rational normal curve in projective $d$-space? Formally, determine $\operatorname{edeg}(\sigma_2(v_d(\mathbb{P}^1)))$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), the curated open-problems paper arXiv:2304.10570v1 (Fulvio Gesmundo); no value or bound is given there.
solved_when: A closed-form expression (or exact value) for the Euclidean distance degree of the secant variety of the rational normal curve in $\mathbb{P}^d$ is established and verified.
why: The Euclidean distance degree quantifies the algebraic complexity of finding the nearest point on this secant variety, so a formula would sharpen the theory of optimization and nearest-point problems on low-rank tensor varieties.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Can we explicitly determine the defining equations of the variety $_{r,V}S^d V$ when the parameters $r$ and $V$ are small? That is, for low values of $r$ and small spaces $V$, give equations cutting out this secant-type variety of tensors.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2023), the curated open-problems collection http://arxiv.org/abs/2304.10570v1 (Fulvio Gesmundo).
solved_when: Explicit defining equations are determined for $_{r,V}S^d V$ for small values of $r$ and $V$.
why: Explicit equations for these tensor varieties would advance the algebraic study of secant varieties and tensor decomposition, a central tool in the geometry of tensors.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Can the Geometric Complexity Theory (GCT) program be concretely implemented for the variety of small algebraic branching programs $_{r,V}$ — that is, can the GCT machinery of symmetries, orbit closures, and representation-theoretic obstructions be carried out for this specific variety?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2304.10570v1, Fulvio Gesmundo, 2023), a curated collection of open problems and research directions on the geometry of tensors.
solved_when: A concrete GCT treatment of the variety $_{r,V}$ is developed, carrying the general program over to this setting; the problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023).
why: It would extend Geometric Complexity Theory from its usual settings to the variety of small algebraic branching programs, connecting algebraic complexity lower bounds to explicit representation-theoretic obstructions for this class.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: What is the border subrank of a generic tensor, and which tensors have border subrank strictly larger than the generic value? Formally, determine the generic border subrank and characterize the conditions under which an individual tensor exceeds it.
solved_when: The border subrank of a generic tensor is computed, and a characterization (or sufficient conditions) is given for tensors whose border subrank exceeds the generic value.
why: The generic border subrank is a fundamental asymptotic complexity invariant of tensors; knowing it and the exceptional tensors that surpass it would sharpen our understanding of the geometry of tensor degenerations and the limits they impose on algorithms.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Can the stabilizer rank of an n-qubit state grow faster than any linear function of n? A super-linear lower bound on stabilizer rank remains unproven.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), "Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions" by Fulvio Gesmundo, arXiv:2304.10570v1.
solved_when: An explicit family of n-qubit states is exhibited whose stabilizer rank exceeds c·n for every constant c, asymptotically.
why: Stabilizer rank quantifies the cost of classically simulating quantum circuits via stabilizer decompositions; a super-linear lower bound would establish fundamental limits on these simulation methods.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: John-Zizler
open: Does every weakly compactly generated (WCG) Banach space admit a norming Markushevich basis? In other words, can the classical basis structure available in separable spaces be extended, with norming functionals, to the whole WCG class?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2024), arXiv:2402.18442v3 by Petr Hájek and Tommaso Russo.
solved_when: A proof that every WCG Banach space admits a norming M-basis, or a counterexample of a WCG space with no such basis, resolves the problem.
why: It would settle a basic structural question about how far norming Markushevich bases reach beyond separable Banach spaces, a key tool in biorthogonal-analysis arguments.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: Godefroy
open: If an Asplund Banach space admits a norming Markushevich basis, must the space be weakly compactly generated?

why: It would settle a fundamental structural implication linking the existence of a well-behaved biorthogonal system to weak compactness generation in Asplund spaces, a basic question in Banach space geometry.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: Godefroy for C(K)
open: If $K$ is a scattered compact space such that $C(K)$ admits a norming Markushevich basis, must $K$ be Eberlein?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every scattered compact space $K$ with $C(K)$ admitting a norming M-basis is Eberlein, or an explicit scattered non-Eberlein compactum $K$ whose $C(K)$ nevertheless admits a norming M-basis.
why: It would settle when the existence of a norming M-basis in a space of continuous functions forces Eberlein compactness, sharpening the structure theory of $C(K)$ spaces on scattered compacta.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: norming => Valdivia
open: Suppose a scattered compactum $K$ is such that its space of continuous functions $C(K)$ admits a countably norming Markushevich basis. Must $K$ be Valdivia?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2024), Petr Hájek and Tommaso Russo, arXiv:2402.18442v3.
solved_when: A proof that every scattered compactum with $C(K)$ admitting a (countably) norming M-basis is Valdivia, or a counterexample of such a compactum that is not Valdivia.
why: It would clarify the extent to which the existence of norming M-bases forces the Valdivia property on scattered compacta, a key structural link between Banach space geometry and topology of compact spaces.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: norming in subspace
open: If a Banach space admits a norming Markushevich basis and $Y$ is a subspace of it, must $Y$ also admit a norming Markushevich basis?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, that every subspace of a Banach space with a norming M-basis inherits a norming M-basis.
why: It tests whether the norming M-basis property is hereditary to subspaces, a basic structural question about how norming bases behave under passage to subspaces.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
open: Does every subspace of $\ell_1(\Gamma)$, for $\Gamma$ uncountable, admit a norming Markushevich basis? In other words, is there a biorthogonal system in such a subspace whose associated functionals norm the subspace?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2024), Petr Hájek and Tomymmo Russo, "Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems," http://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18442v3.
solved_when: A proof that every subspace of $\ell_1(\Gamma)$ with $\Gamma$ uncountable admits a norming M-basis, or a counterexample exhibiting a subspace with no such basis.
why: It would settle a basic structural question about subspaces of non-separable $\ell_1$ spaces and clarify when norming biorthogonal systems exist beyond the separable setting.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: Plichko subspace
open: Is the Plichko property inherited by arbitrary subspaces? That is, if a Banach space is Plichko, must every closed subspace of it also be Plichko?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2024), Petr Hájek and Tommaso Russo, "Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems," http://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18442v3.
solved_when: A proof that every subspace of a Plichko Banach space is again Plichko, or a counterexample exhibiting a Plichko Banach space with a non-Plichko subspace.
why: Resolving the question settles a basic structural inheritance property of Plichko spaces, a class central to the theory of norming Markushevich bases and correlated spaces.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
open: If a Banach space has a bidual that is Plichko, must the space itself be Plichko?
solved_when: A proof that every Banach space whose bidual is Plichko is itself Plichko, or a counterexample of such a space that is not Plichko, is given.
why: It would clarify whether the Plichko property is determined at the level of the bidual, a basic structural question in the theory of Banach spaces with countably norming Markushevich bases.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems — problem probl: complemented of Plichko
open: If a complemented subspace of a Plichko space is itself a Banach space, must it again be Plichko? In other words, is the class of Plichko spaces closed under taking complemented subspaces?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2024), "Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems" by Petr Hájek and Tommaso Russo (http://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18442v3).
solved_when: A proof that every complemented subspace of a Plichko space is Plichko, or a counterexample exhibiting a complemented subspace of a Plichko space that fails to be Plichko.
why: It tests whether Plichko spaces form a stable class under basic Banach-space operations, which affects how structure results (such as norming Markushevich bases and countably norming sets) transfer from an ambient space to its complemented subspaces.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
open: If a Banach space admits a norming Markushevich basis and $Y$ is a complemented subspace of it, must $Y$ also admit a norming M-basis?
solved_when: A proof that every complemented subspace of a Banach space with a norming M-basis inherits a norming M-basis, or an explicit counterexample.
why: It tests whether the norming M-basis property is stable under complemented subspaces, a basic structural question for which spaces can be coordinatized by such bases.

title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
open: If a Banach space admits a norming Markushevich basis, must its dual unit ball, equipped with the weak-star topology, be semi-Eberlein? In other words, does the existence of such a basis force a specific topological regularity on the dual ball.

why: It would clarify the structural consequences of norming M-bases, a central tool in Banach space theory, by tying them to semi-Eberlein compacta in the dual.
