status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2023), "a list of open problems," available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 by Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, and Fabrizio Bianchi.
solved_when: A complete description or characterization of the set of kneading sequences $K$ is given.
why: Solving it would clarify the combinatorial structure governing the dynamics under study, as posed in a curated list of open problems in the field.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Do any two distinct kneading sequences determine a unique pair of parameters $(a,b)$, thereby governing all the other kneading sequences of $\mathcal{K}$?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether any two distinct kneading sequences uniquely determine a pair of parameters $(a,b)$ and in doing so govern all remaining kneading sequences of $\mathcal{K}$.
why: It would settle a basic uniqueness question about how kneading sequences encode parameters, extracted from a curated open-problems paper.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Which kneading sequences K can occur for the Hénon map $H_{a,b}$ with $(a,b)$ in $WY$? In other words, give a description of the set of kneading sequences realized by this family of maps.
solved_when: A characterization of the set of kneading sequences of $H_{a,b}$ for $(a,b)$ in $WY$ is given, determining exactly which sequences arise.
why: It would complete the combinatorial picture of the dynamics of this Hénon family, tying orbit behavior to symbolic data.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Can we describe the dynamics of $H_2$ near the origin in $\mathbb{C}^2$? More precisely, the problem asks for a dynamical description of this local behavior that goes beyond the currently known statements.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2023), "A list of open problems" by Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, and Fabrizio Bianchi (http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1).
solved_when: A characterization of the local dynamics of $H_2$ in a neighborhood of the origin in $\mathbb{C}^2$ is given. No further quantitative targets are stated in the record.
why: The problem appears in a curated list of open problems in complex dynamics, so settling it advances the program laid out there and removes a stated gap in the local understanding of this map.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Does the system $H_2$ simultaneously possess small saddle cycles and small elliptic cycles? In dynamical terms, can both types of periodic behavior be found at small scales in this map?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $H_2$ has both small saddle cycles and small elliptic cycles, resolving the question as posed.
why: Resolving it would clarify the local periodic structure of $H_2$, specifically whether saddle-type and elliptic-type cycles coexist at small scales, a basic structural question for this system.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems — question Q17
open: If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, is $\mathrm{int}(K^+)$ the union of finitely many basins of sink orbits? That is, does quasi-hyperbolicity force the interior of the filled Julia-type set to decompose into a finite number of attracting basins?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that for every quasi-hyperbolic $f$, the interior of $K^+$ is a finite union of basins of sink orbits.
why: A resolution would clarify the structure of the attracting dynamics inside $K^+$ for quasi-hyperbolic maps, a basic finiteness question in this setting.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems — question Q20
open: If a map $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, do its unstable slices satisfy a John-type condition?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that unstable slices of quasi-hyperbolic maps satisfy a John-type condition, resolving question Q20 of the source paper.
why: It is extracted from a curated open-problems paper; resolving it would clarify the fine geometry of unstable sets for quasi-hyperbolic dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems — question Q21
open: If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic and dissipative and its Julia set $J$ is connected, do the external rays land on $J$? And is $J$ then a finite quotient of the real solenoid?
solved_when: An answer (positive or negative) to both questions for quasi-hyperbolic, dissipative maps with connected Julia set: whether external rays land at $J$, and whether $J$ is a finite quotient of the real solenoid.
why: It would settle the fine topology and structure of Julia sets in the quasi-hyperbolic dissipative regime, determining whether the classical solenoid picture extends there.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: If a real surface automorphism $f$ has the property that the entropy of its real part $f_{\mathbb{R}}$ equals the entropy of $f$ itself, must $f$ be quasi-hyperbolic? Formally, does equality of entropies $\mathrm{h}(f_{\mathbb{R}}) = \mathrm{h}(f)$ force quasi-hyperbolicity?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, is given for the implication: equality of the entropy of $f_{\mathbb{R}}$ with that of $f$ implies $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic.
why: It would clarify when real dynamics fully captures the complex entropy of a surface automorphism, a key step toward understanding the relation between real and complex dynamical behavior in quasi-hyperbolic systems.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Is the locus $H_C$ connected? More precisely, is this subset a connected set in its ambient space?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2023), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi).
solved_when: A proof or disproof of the connectedness of $H_C$ is given.
why: The question comes from a curated list of open problems in holomorphic dynamics, and resolving it advances the understanding of the structure of such loci within that program.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Construct an algorithm to compute a rigorous upper bound for the topological entropy of a real H\'enon map $f_{c, b}|_{ {R}^2}$.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: What is the asymptotic behavior of the Hausdorff dimension of the set $J^+_{a,c}$ as the parameters $(a,c)$ tend to $(0,0)$? In particular, does there exist a uniform lower bound for $\dim(J^+_{a,c})$ of the form $\dim(J^+_{a,c}) \geq 3 + h(a)$ with $h(a)>0$ in a neighborhood of $c=0$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023): arXiv:2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi).
solved_when: An asymptotic expansion of the Hausdorff dimension of $J^+_{a,c}$ as $(a,c)\to(0,0)$ is given, together with (as the sharpened subquestion asks) a uniform lower bound of the form $\dim(J^+_{a,c}) \geq 3 + h(a)$ with $h(a)>0$ near $c=0$, or a proof that no such bound exists.
why: A solution would give precise control of how the geometry of the Julia set $J^+_{a,c}$ degenerates in the parabolic/neutral limit $(a,c)\to(0,0)$, a regime where dimension estimates are typically hardest.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Does there exist a generalized complex Hénon map $f$ with the property asked for in the source problem list — namely, can such a map be found as posed in question 34 of the paper?
solved_when: An explicit generalized complex Hénon map $f$ answering the question as stated in question 34 of the source paper, or a proof that no such map exists.
why: The problem comes from a curated list of open problems, so settling it advances a specific research frontier identified by experts in complex dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: To what extent is a generalized Hénon map determined by the list of its unstable multipliers, or by the list of their moduli? That is, how much of the map's dynamical identity can be recovered from this spectral data alone?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2023), a curated list of open problems by Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, and Fabrizio Bianchi (arXiv:2312.03907v1).
solved_when: A precise characterization is given of which generalized Hénon maps share the same list of unstable multipliers (resp. the same list of moduli of unstable multipliers), together with the extent to which such data determines the map up to natural equivalences.
why: It would reveal how much of a Hénon map's dynamics is encoded in its linear spectral data, informing rigidity and classification questions for real and complex Hénon maps.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Is the dynamical degree of any polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^d$ equal to a weak Perron number? That is, must this growth invariant of the iterates always be a weak Perron number, as asked in question 46 of the source problem list?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that the dynamical degree of every polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^d$ is, or is not, a weak Perron number.
why: It would pin down the arithmetic constraints on dynamical degrees of polynomial automorphisms, a basic structural question in complex dynamical systems.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: On some open problems concerning perfect powers — conjecture conj1
open: Given an integer $n \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0, 1\}$, if the term $A352991(n)$ happens to be a perfect power of an integer, must the exponent be nontrivial in the strong sense that there exists $k \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0, 1, 2\}$ with $A352991(n) = c^k$ for some $c \in \mathbb{N}$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) of the assertion: whenever $A352991(n)$ is a perfect power for $n \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0, 1\}$, there exist $c \in \mathbb{N}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0, 1, 2\}$ such that $A352991(n) = c^k$.
why: It would settle a provocative conjecture about the structure of the sequence $A352991$, constraining which perfect powers can appear among its terms.

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Is there a variational principle governing a system of material particles moving in $d$-dimensional space with $d>1$ that stick together upon collision? In other words, can the sticky-particle dynamics in dimension greater than one be derived as Euler–Lagrange equations of a suitable action functional?
solved_when: A variational formulation is given whose critical points reproduce the sticky-particle dynamics in dimension $d>1$.
why: A variational description would connect sticky-particle collisions to the geometric-hydrodynamics framework, potentially enabling tools like Arnold's least-action methods for these non-smooth systems.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Describe a model for an $L^2$ left-invariant metric on the group $\mathrm{D}(M)$ of diffeomorphisms of a manifold $M$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), the curated open-problems paper "Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems" (arXiv:2205.01143v2, by Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, and Alexander Shnirelman); no further progress is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A mathematically well-defined model of the $L^2$ left-invariant metric on $\mathrm{D}(M)$ is constructed and its basic geometric properties (e.g., geodesics, completeness) are established, as called for in the source problem.
why: The $L^2$ metric is the foundational case of right-invariant metrics on diffeomorphism groups underlying Euler-Arnold equations; a workable model would anchor the geometric-hydrodynamic framework for this extremal case.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Are particle trajectories of ideal fluid motion analytic functions of time, in any space dimension? More precisely, does the flow map of the Euler equations admit time-analyticity for its particle paths without dimensional restrictions?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether particle trajectories in ideal hydrodynamics are analytic in time in any dimension, resolving the question as stated in the source problem.
why: Time-analyticity of trajectories would sharpen regularity knowledge of ideal fluid flow beyond current results and constrain the fine structure of Lagrangian particle motion, a foundational question in geometric hydrodynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Is it true that for any GM-flow, the level lines of the vorticity, where curl u(x,t) is constant, are real-analytic curves?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the claim that for any GM-flow u(x,t), the level lines of curl u(x,t) = const are real-analytic.
why: It would establish a fundamental regularity property of vorticity level sets in geometric hydrodynamics, constraining the fine structure of generalized motion in ideal fluids.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: How badly does the $L^2$ exponential map fail to be Fredholm on the diffeomorphism group ${D}^s_(M)$, and can that failure be quantified? A precise measure would replace the vague "not Fredholm" obstruction with computable invariants of the map's loss of regularity or surjectivity defect.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), the curated open-problems collection "Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems" by Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, and Alexander Shnirelman (http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2). No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A quantitative characterization of the failure of the Fredholm property of the $L^2$ exponential map in ${D}^s_(M)$ is given — for example, explicit bounds or invariants measuring the deviation from Fredholm behavior — as called for by problem 18 of the source paper.
why: The Fredholm property underlies solvability and stability arguments for the geodesic equations of ideal hydrodynamics; quantifying its failure would delineate exactly where such arguments break down and what substitutes are needed.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Does the "kink" in the fluid configuration persist for all time as the fluid evolves? More precisely, prove that the kink does not disappear under the time evolution of the fluid.
solved_when: A proof (or rigorous demonstration) that the kink persists under the fluid's time evolution; equivalently, a counterexample would resolve it negatively. No quantitative targets are stated in the record.
why: Resolving it would establish whether such singular features of the flow geometry are stable under the dynamics, a question of persistence in geometric hydrodynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Why do solutions of the Euler equations exhibit a decrease in entropy? More precisely, can this phenomenon of entropy decrease for Euler solutions be given a rigorous mathematical explanation?
solved_when: A rigorous account of the entropy-decrease phenomenon for solutions of the Euler equations is provided, resolving the question as posed in the source paper.
why: It would clarify a counterintuitive aspect of ideal fluid behavior, where the geometric picture of Euler flow as geodesics on diffeomorphism groups meets thermodynamic intuition.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Is the 2D Euler equation non-integrable as a dynamical system on its natural geometric phase space? A proof would make precise the intuition that its flow is too rich to admit a complete set of conserved quantities beyond the known Casimirs.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), a curated open-problems collection by Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiołek, and Alexander Shnirelman (http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2). No solution is recorded.
solved_when: A rigorous proof of non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation is established.
why: Integrability of 2D Euler would fundamentally reshape our understanding of vortex dynamics and constrain turbulence phenomenology; proving non-integrability would confirm that no finite set of invariants governs the flow, legitimizing statistical and chaotic approaches.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: What is the detailed dynamics of a small number of point vortices moving on a manifold, and how do their trajectories and relative equilibria bifurcate as the manifold and vortex strengths vary? In particular, describe the motion and bifurcations of few-vortex systems on various manifolds.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), the curated open-problems paper arXiv:2205.01143v2 by Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, and Alexander Shnirelman. No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A detailed description of the motion and bifurcations of a small number of vortices on various manifolds is given, as posed in problem 28 of the source paper.
why: Point-vortex dynamics is the simplest model capturing the geometric features of ideal fluid motion, so resolving it on general manifolds would clarify how curvature and topology shape vortex interactions and bifurcation behavior in geometric hydrodynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: What happens to point-vortex dynamics and Euler flows on a non-orientable surface, where the orientable theory's algebraic machinery breaks down? Concretely, describe the full set of Casimirs and construct finite-dimensional approximations for the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces, and study the first non-integrable cases for a small number of point vortices, in analogy with the known orientable cases.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), "Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems" (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman, http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2).
solved_when: A description of the complete Casimir set for the area-preserving diffeomorphism group of non-orientable surfaces, together with finite-dimensional analogues of the orientable approximations, and an analysis of the first non-integrable point-vortex cases with a small number of vortices on such surfaces.
why: Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations are the basic tools for studying Euler-type equations and vortex dynamics on surfaces, so extending them to non-orientable surfaces opens the geometry of ideal hydrodynamics on Klein bottles and similar manifolds to the same analysis available in the orientable setting.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: What does a "typical" steady fluid flow look like, and what is the right notion of genericity for steady fields? More precisely, find a natural genericity concept under which the paradoxical behavior of steady Euler fields described in the source can be explained.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2022), "Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems," problem 33, by Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, and Alexander Shnirelman (http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2).
solved_when: A precise definition of genericity for steady fields is proposed and used to characterize typical steady flows, resolving the paradox raised in the source paper.
why: It would clarify the foundational question of which steady solutions of the Euler equations are actually representative, affecting how geometric hydrodynamics results about steady fields are interpreted.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Does there exist an infinite sequence of higher helicity invariants for vector fields such that, whenever all preceding invariants of a given field vanish, the first nonzero invariant in the sequence provides a lower bound on the field's energy?
solved_when: A sequence of higher helicity invariants is constructed with the stated property: for any vector field whose earlier invariants all vanish, the first nonzero invariant bounds the field's energy from below.
why: Such invariants would give a hierarchy of energy lower bounds for divergence-free fields, extending the classical role of helicity in constraining energy and deepening the geometric picture of ideal fluid dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Is there a direct link from the 3D nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation to the 1D NLS equation, obtained as a reduction to singular solutions? In other words, can the 1D equation be realized directly through the collapse of 3D solutions onto a singular, lower-dimensional setting?
solved_when: A rigorous construction or proof is given that reduces the 3D NLS equation to the 1D NLS equation via singular solutions.
why: It would connect higher- and lower-dimensional dispersive dynamics within geometric hydrodynamics, clarifying how dimension reduction arises from singularity formation.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: What is the differential geometry of shape spaces when these are equipped with the $H^{-1/2}$-metrics that arise as metrics on dynamic boundaries or vortex sheets? In other words, give a geometric description of such shape spaces with these weak metrics.
solved_when: A characterization of the differential geometry of these $H^{-1/2}$-metric shape spaces is provided (the natural criterion for this theory-type problem, as the record states no quantitative targets).
why: It would extend geometric hydrodynamics — where metrics on shape and diffeomorphism groups govern fluid motion — to the weak $H^{-1/2}$ setting coming from dynamic boundaries and vortex sheets.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Can the observed correspondence between droplets and quantum particles be derived rigorously as a combined effect of averaging and the Madelung transform?
solved_when: A mathematical derivation is given showing that the droplet–quantum particle correspondence follows from averaging together with the Madelung transform.
why: It would place a striking physical analogy between fluid droplets and quantum particles on firm analytic footing, connecting geometric hydrodynamics to quantum mechanics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Is there a mechanism analogous to the Arnold geometric framework that describes energy cascades in real hydrodynamics? More precisely, can a cascade in actual fluid motion be characterized through the geometry of diffeomorphism groups, as steady Euler flows are?
solved_when: A geometric mechanism is identified that describes a cascade in real hydrodynamics.
why: It would extend the geometric description of ideal fluid dynamics to turbulent cascade phenomena, connecting Hamiltonian/geometric structure with real energy transfer in fluids.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Regularity estimates and open problems in kinetic equations — conjecture c:kinetic-krylov
open: Does every classical solution of a kinetic equation of the type considered — defined on $[0,1] \times B_1 \times B_1$ — satisfy a Krylov–Safonov-type regularity estimate? More precisely, the problem asks to establish the conjectured regularity bounds for such solutions as stated in the source paper.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the regularity conjecture for classical solutions $f: [0,1] \times B_1 \times B_1$ of the stated class of kinetic equations.
why: It would extend Krylov–Safonov-type regularity theory to the kinetic setting, a key step toward well-posedness and quantitative estimates for kinetic equations with rough coefficients.

title: Is There an Online Learning Algorithm That Learns Whenev — problem prob:optimistic-online
open: Does there exist an online learning algorithm that is optimistically universal, learning whenever the process is learnable at all? The question is posed in both the weak and the strong sense.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2021), "http://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09542v1" (Steve Hanneke).
solved_when: An optimistically universal online learning algorithm is constructed, or its impossibility is proved, in either the weak or the strong sense.
why: It would characterize exactly when online learning is possible under general stochastic processes, settling a foundational universality question in online learning theory.

title: Related to Quantum Query Complexity
open: Does there exist an oracle relative to which QMA is separated from QCMA — that is, where quantum proofs genuinely outperform classical proofs for verification? Formally, the question asks for an oracle $A$ such that ${QMA}^A \neq {QCMA}^A$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2021), the curated open-problems paper by Scott Aaronson, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06917v1. No separation oracle is known.
solved_when: An oracle $A$ is explicitly constructed (or its existence proved) relative to which ${QMA}^A$ and ${QCMA}^A$ differ; equivalently, a language is exhibited that is verifiable with a quantum proof but not with a classical proof relative to that oracle.
why: Such an oracle would give the first black-box evidence that quantum proofs are more powerful than classical proofs for Merlin–Arthur verification, and would block the possibility that QMA collapses to QCMA in relativized worlds.

title: Related to Quantum Query Complexity
open: What is the largest possible gap between $Q(f)$ and its classical counterpart for a Boolean function? That is, how big can the separation between quantum and classical query complexity be?
solved_when: A tight characterization of the maximum achievable gap between $Q(f)$ and classical (deterministic or bounded-error randomized) query complexity is established, with matching upper and lower bounds.
why: It pins down the ultimate power of quantum algorithms in the query model, bounding how much speedup any quantum algorithm can hope for.

title: Related to Quantum Query Complexity
open: Are there sets of injective functions for which a quantum computer achieves a query-complexity advantage over any classical computer, and if so, how large can that advantage be?
solved_when: A construction (or impossibility proof) is given: either explicit sets of injective functions exhibiting a proven quantum-over-classical query advantage, or a proof that no such sets exist.
why: It would clarify how much of quantum speedup survives in the restricted, structurally simple setting of injective functions.

title: in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields — problem prob:log term
open: When is a wild quotient singularity log terminal? More precisely, find a characterization of those wild quotient singularities that are log terminal.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2021), http://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07073v1 (Takehiko Yasuda), a curated collection of open problems in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields.
solved_when: A criterion is given that determines exactly which wild quotient singularities are log terminal.
why: Log terminality is a fundamental measure of mildness for singularities in birational geometry, and a characterization would clarify which wild quotient singularities behave well under the minimal model program.

title: in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields
open: Does the quotient variety $(k x,y)/G$ having log terminal singularities depend only on the pair $(r,n)$? In other words, is log terminality of such a quotient determined purely by the data $(r,n)$, independently of any other choices involved?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2021), "Open problems in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields" by Takehiko Yasuda (http://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07073v1).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing whether log terminality of $(k x,y)/G$ is, or is not, determined solely by the pair $(r,n)$.
why: It would clarify which invariants actually govern the singularities appearing in the wild McKay correspondence, where classification data is scarce and structure results are hard to come by.

title: in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields
open: Is the equality $D_V = p$ not only necessary but also sufficient? That is, does this equality of numerical invariants fully characterize the situation it is associated with, so that it becomes an equivalent condition?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via counterexample) that $D_V = p$ is sufficient, not merely necessary, is given.
why: The condition $D_V = p$ is currently known only as a necessary condition; establishing sufficiency would turn it into a complete characterization in the setting of the wild McKay correspondence.

title: in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields
open: Is there a necessary condition for the wild McKay correspondence, expressed in terms of the divisors $D_{V}^{(0)}, D_{V}^{(1)}, \ldots, D_{V}^{(n-1)}$? More precisely, can one formulate a criterion built from these divisors that any candidate in the correspondence must satisfy?
solved_when: A necessary condition stated in terms of $D_{V}^{(0)}, D_{V}^{(1)}, \ldots, D_{V}^{(n-1)}$ is formulated and proved.
why: It would give a concrete divisor-theoretic criterion constraining the wild McKay correspondence, turning a largely conjectural picture into something testable in explicit examples.

title: in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields

status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1, by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao; no resolution is recorded here.
solved_when: A proof that every core compact $T_0$ space is Rudin, or an explicit example of a core compact $T_0$ space that is not Rudin.
why: It would clarify how core compactness — the natural $T_0$ analogue of local compactness — interacts with the Rudin property, a key notion in the study of well-filtered and sober spaces; a counterexample would expose a genuine structural gap between these classes.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question WDinfinite-prodquestion
open: Let $\mathbf{K}$ be a full subcategory of $\mathrm{Top}_0$ containing $\mathrm{Sob}$ (in particular, a Keimel–Lawson category). Is the product space of an arbitrary family of $\mathbf{K}$-determined spaces again $\mathbf{K}$-determined?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao, arXiv:2005.00539v1 (2020).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that arbitrary products of $\mathbf{K}$-determined spaces are $\mathbf{K}$-determined for every full subcategory $\mathbf{K}$ of $\mathrm{Top}_0$ containing $\mathrm{Sob}$, including all Keimel–Lawson categories.
why: Determination by a coreflective subcategory underlies the construction and analysis of well-filtered and sober reflections; closure under arbitrary products would secure these categorical tools for large product constructions in domain-theoretic topology.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question WD set infinite prod question
open: Is well-filtered determinedness preserved under arbitrary products at the level of sets? Specifically, if each $A_i \subseteq X_i$ is a well-filtered determined subset of a $T_0$ space $X_i$, must the product set $\prod_{i \in I} A_i$ be well-filtered determined in the product space $X = \prod_{i \in I} X_i$?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, is given for whether the product set $\prod_{i \in I} A_i$ is well-filtered determined whenever each factor set $A_i \subseteq X_i$ is well-filtered determined.
why: This would clarify how the well-filtered determined property — a key notion linking well-filteredness and sobriety in $T_0$ spaces — behaves under products, a basic closure question the current theory leaves unresolved.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question WD space infinite prod question
open: Is the product of an arbitrary family of well-filtered determined spaces again well-filtered determined? In other words, does the class of well-filtered determined spaces behave well under infinite products?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1 by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing whether arbitrary products of well-filtered determined spaces are, or are not necessarily, well-filtered determined.
why: It tests how robust the class of well-filtered determined spaces is under basic categorical constructions, directly informing the development of pointfree and topological domain theory built on such spaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question Smyth WF question
open: Is the Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ of a well-filtered determined $T_0$ space $X$ again well-filtered determined? In other words, is the property of being well-filtered determined preserved under forming the Smyth power space construction?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing whether $P_S(X)$ is well-filtered determined for every well-filtered determined $T_0$ space $X$.
why: Resolving it clarifies the stability of well-filtered determinedness under a fundamental power-space construction in domain theory and non-Hausdorff topology.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question CI WF U V topol=Scott topol question
open: For a first-countable well-filtered space $X$, do the upper Vietoris topology and the Scott topology coincide on the hyperspace of compact saturated subsets of $X$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao, arXiv:2005.00539v1.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every first-countable well-filtered space $X$, the upper Vietoris topology on $K(X)$ equals the Scott topology on $K(X)$.
why: A positive answer would extend a key topological coincidence from the locally compact setting to the broader class of first-countable well-filtered spaces, clarifying the relationship between order-theoretic and topological structures on hyperspaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question Smyth consonant question
open: If a $T_0$ space $X$ is consonant, must the Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ also be consonant? Equivalently, does consonance pass from a space to its Smyth powerspace construction?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao (http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1).
solved_when: A proof that $P_S(X)$ is consonant for every consonant $T_0$ space $X$, or an explicit counterexample of a consonant $T_0$ space whose Smyth power space fails to be consonant.
why: Consonance is a key property linking a space to its powerdomain constructions; knowing whether it is preserved would clarify the behavior of the Smyth powerspace in domain-theoretic topology and support further study of well-filtered and sober spaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question Hoare consonant question
open: If a $T_0$ space $X$ is consonant, must its Hoare hyperspace $P_H(X)$ also be consonant? In other words, is consonance preserved under passing to the Hoare power space?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1 by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao; no progress beyond the statement is recorded here.
solved_when: A proof that $P_H(X)$ is consonant for every consonant $T_0$ space $X$, or an explicit counterexample of a consonant $T_0$ space whose Hoare hyperspace fails to be consonant.
why: Settling it would clarify how consonance, a key property linking topology to domain theory, behaves under powerdomain constructions central to the theory of well-filtered and sober spaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question K-reflectionprod question
open: Does the product of well-filtered spaces remain well-filtered, as raised in the K-reflectionprod question of Xu and Zhao's open-problems paper on well-filtered and sober spaces?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1 (Xiaoquan Xu, Dongsheng Zhao).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) resolving the K-reflectionprod question — specifically, whether products of well-filtered spaces are well-filtered — is established.
why: It addresses a basic closure property of the category of well-filtered spaces, a class central to recent work connecting topology, domain theory, and lattice-theoretic reflection.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question K-L reflectionprod
open: Does every well-filtered space arise as the product of a K-L reflection construction — that is, can the Keimel–Lawson reflection be characterized through products in the way suggested in the source paper? A precise formulation would determine whether the K-L reflection of a sober space interacts with arbitrary products in the way conjectured.
solved_when: The product question raised in the source paper is affirmatively resolved or refuted, i.e., a proof or counterexample is given for the behavior of the K-L reflection under products as stated in the paper.
why: It clarifies how well-filteredness and sobriety behave under products, a basic structural question for these reflective constructions in pointfree and topological lattice theory.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question d-reflection infinite prod question
open: Does the $d$-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of $T_0$ spaces? In formal terms, is $(\prod_{i \in I} X_i)^d = \prod_{i \in I} X_i^d$ (up to homeomorphism) for any family $\{X_i : i \in I\}$ of $T_0$ spaces?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1 by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing, for arbitrary families of $T_0$ spaces, whether $(\prod_{i \in I} X_i)^d$ is homeomorphic to $\prod_{i \in I} X_i^d$.
why: Resolving it would clarify how the $d$-reflection construction — central to the study of well-filtered and sober spaces — interacts with limits, which affects how reflection-based arguments can be carried over to product spaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question WF-reflection infinite prod question
open: Does the well-filtered reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of $T_0$ spaces? Equivalently, does $(\prod_{i \in I}X_i)^w = \prod_{i \in I}X_i^w$ (up to homeomorphism) hold for every family $\{X_i : i \in I\}$ of $T_0$ spaces?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, establishing whether $(\prod_{i \in I}X_i)^w$ is homeomorphic to $\prod_{i \in I}X_i^w$ for arbitrary families of $T_0$ spaces.
why: The well-filtered reflection is a basic closure operation in the theory of $T_0$ spaces sitting between sobriety and core-compactness considerations; knowing whether it commutes with products determines how reflection constructions behave under limits and is needed to compute well-filtered reflections of product spaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question SmythWD
open: If $K$ is an adequate Smyth category and $X$ is a $K$-determined $T_0$ space, must the Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ also be $K$-determined?
solved_when: A proof that for every adequate Smyth category $K$ and every $K$-determined $T_0$ space $X$, the Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ is again $K$-determined (or a counterexample exhibiting some adequate $K$ and $X$ for which it fails).
why: It tests whether $K$-determinedness is stable under forming Smyth power spaces, a basic closure property needed to iterate these constructions in the theory of well-filtered and sober spaces.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question KBsob reflective question
open: Is the category $\mathsf{KBSob}$ of $k$-bounded sober spaces reflective in the category $\mathsf{Top}_k$ of all $k$-spaces? In other words, does the inclusion functor $\mathsf{KBSob} \hookrightarrow \mathsf{Top}_k$ admit a left adjoint?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao (arXiv:2005.00539v1, 2020).
solved_when: A construction of a reflector (left adjoint to the inclusion $\mathsf{KBSob} \to \mathsf{Top}_k$) is given, or a proof that no such reflection exists.
why: A positive answer would provide a canonical way to associate a $k$-bounded sober space to every $k$-space, placing these spaces on the same categorical footing as classical sobrification.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question strong d-space prod question
open: Is an arbitrary product of strong $d$-spaces again a strong $d$-space? In other words, is the class of strong $d$-spaces closed under arbitrary products?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2020), "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1.
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, settling whether arbitrary products of strong $d$-spaces are always strong $d$-spaces.
why: Closure under products is a basic structural question for strong $d$-spaces, and resolving it determines whether the class can serve as a productive framework alongside related categorical properties in domain-theoretic topology.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question strong d-space function question
open: If $X$ is a $T_0$ space and $Y$ a strong $d$-space, must the function space ${Top}_0(X, Y)$ with the pointwise convergence topology again be a strong $d$-space?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao (http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that ${Top}_0(X, Y)$ (with the pointwise convergence topology) is a strong $d$-space for every $T_0$ space $X$ and strong $d$-space $Y$, or a counterexample to this statement.
why: It tests whether the strong $d$-space property is stable under forming function spaces, a basic closure question in the topology of $T_0$ spaces central to domain-theoretic and sober-space theory.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question super H-sober reflective question
open: Is the category $S$-$Top_d$ reflective in the category $Top_0$ of $T_0$ spaces? In other words, does every $T_0$ space admit a universal map to a space in $S$-$Top_d$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1 by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao; no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that $S$-$Top_d$ is reflective in $Top_0$, or a counterexample establishing that no such reflection exists.
why: A positive answer would provide a canonical "super $H$-sober reflection" for arbitrary $T_0$ spaces, extending the reflection machinery available for sober and well-filtered spaces and clarifying the structural relationship among these sobriety-type separation axioms.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question Smyth co-sober question
open: Is every Smyth powerdomain of a sober space co-sober? More formally, the question asks whether the Smyth powerdomain construction, applied to a sober space, always yields a co-sober space.
status: The question was stated as open in the source paper (2020), "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao (http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1), and no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that the Smyth powerdomain of any sober space is co-sober, or a counterexample exhibiting a sober space whose Smyth powerdomain fails to be co-sober.
why: It would clarify the boundary between soberness and its dual notion, co-soberness, under a fundamental domain-theoretic construction, informing the topological foundations underlying domain theory and denotational semantics.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question kernel co-sober question
open: If $(X,\tau)$ is a co-sober space and $k : (X,\tau) \to (X,\tau)$ is a continuous kernel operator with respect to the specialization order of $X$ — meaning $k(x) \le \{x\}$ and $k(k(x)) = k(x)$ for all $x \in X$ — must the subspace $(k(X), \tau|_{k(X)})$ also be co-sober?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1 by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao.
solved_when: A proof that $(k(X), \tau|_{k(X)})$ is co-sober for every such $X$ and $k$, or an explicit counterexample.
why: It tests whether co-soberness, a key duality partner to sobriety in the study of well-filtered spaces, is stable under images of continuous kernel operators — a basic closure property whose answer shapes the theory's structure.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question co-sober retract question
open: Is a retract of a co-sober space again co-sober? More precisely, does the class of co-sober spaces — those whose opposite-lattice specialization structure reflects sobriety — pass to retracts?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" (Xiaoquan Xu, Dongsheng Zhao, http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that every retract of a co-sober space is co-sober, or a counterexample exhibiting a co-sober space with a non-co-sober retract.
why: Retract-closure is a basic structural property separating "well-behaved" classes of spaces; settling it clarifies how co-soberness interacts with sobriety and well-filteredness in pointfree and general topology.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question co-sober prod question
open: Is an arbitrary product of co-sober spaces again co-sober? Formally, if $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ is a family of co-sober spaces, must the product $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ be co-sober?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), arXiv:2005.00539v1 by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao.
solved_when: A proof that products of co-sober spaces are always co-sober, or an explicit counterexample exhibiting a family of co-sober spaces whose product fails to be co-sober.
why: It would settle a basic closure property of co-soberness, complementing what is known for sober and well-filtered spaces, and clarifying how duality with sobriety behaves under products.

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question co-sober reflectiv question
open: Does the full subcategory of co-sober $T_0$ spaces admit a reflector in the category of all $T_0$ spaces? Formally: is Co-Sob reflective in Top$_0$?
solved_when: A construction of a reflection functor from Top$_0$ onto Co-Sob is given (equivalently, every $T_0$ space is shown to have a universal co-sober reflection), or a proof that no such reflection exists.
why: A reflector would give a canonical co-sober approximation of any $T_0$ space, extending the reflective machinery known for sober and well-filtered spaces to the co-sober setting and clarifying the lattice of corefection/reflection relationships among these duality-related classes.

title: Answering An Open Problem on $T$-Norms for Type-2 Fuzzy Sets — question Q-1
open: Does there exist, apart from the known $t$-norms, any other binary operation (for type-2 fuzzy sets)? This sharpens the open question Q-1 of the source paper.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2019); no progress is recorded in the census. Key work: arXiv:1907.12394v2 (Xinxing Wu, Guanrong Chen).
solved_when: A complete answer is given to question Q-1: either new binary operations on type-2 fuzzy sets beyond the existing $t$-norms are constructed and verified, or it is proved that no such operations exist.
why: It settles question Q-1 of the source paper, clarifying the structure of binary operations available for type-2 fuzzy set theory, which underlies operations on type-2 fuzzy sets used wherever these generalized fuzzy sets are applied.

title: in a Logic of Gossips — problem pro:4
open: Does the semantic relation $_{ck}$ admit a sound and complete axiomatic proof system? More precisely, find an axiomatization of the relation $_{ck}$ in the logic of gossips.
solved_when: A sound and complete axiomatization of $_{ck}$ is given, in the setting of the logic of gossips.
why: It would complete the proof-theoretic picture of the gossip logic studied in the source paper, allowing reasoning about $_{ck}$ to be carried out syntactically.

title: in a Logic of Gossips — problem pro:bound
open: Can every instance of the gossip problem be handled with strictly more than $2n-4$ calls? Put formally: prove that the known lower bound of $2n-4$ calls cannot be attained.
solved_when: A proof establishes that $2n-4$ calls is not achievable for the gossip problem.
why: Resolving it pins down the exact call complexity of gossip protocols studied in the logic of gossips, closing the gap between the known lower bound and what is actually attainable.

title: in a Logic of Gossips — problem pro:bound2
open: Is the number of calls required, in the worst case, to reach a state of gossip uniformly bounded below by $2n-3$? Formally, prove that this lower bound holds.
solved_when: A proof that the lower bound $2n-3$ on the number of calls needed (in the considered gossip setting) is established.
why: It settles a sharp worst-case bound in the logic of gossips, giving a baseline against which protocols must be judged.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Is the single-machine scheduling problem with weighted total tardiness, $1||w_jT_j$, fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the maximum processing time $p_{\max}$? That is, can an optimal schedule be computed in time $f(p_{\max}) \cdot |I|^{O(1)}$ for some computable function $f$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2017), a curated collection of open problems on the parameterized complexity of machine scheduling, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3 (Matthias Mnich, René van Bevern).
solved_when: An algorithm for $1||w_jT_j$ with running time $f(p_{\max}) \cdot n^{O(1)}$ (for some computable function $f$ of the maximum processing time alone) is given, or the problem is shown to be W[1]-hard under this parameterization.
why: Weighted tardiness is one of the core objective functions in scheduling theory, and settling its parameterized complexity by $p_{\max}$ would clarify which scheduling problems admit efficient algorithms when processing times are uniformly small.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Does the single-machine scheduling problem $1||w_jC_j$ admit a polynomial-size problem kernel when parameterized appropriately? More precisely, is there a polynomial kernelization for this problem in the framework of parameterized complexity?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2017), "Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems" by Matthias Mnich and René van Bevern (http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3); no resolution is recorded here.
solved_when: A polynomial-size problem kernel for $1||w_jC_j$ is exhibited, or the problem is shown to exclude such a kernel under standard assumptions.
why: It is one of fifteen curated open problems in parameterized complexity of machine scheduling; resolving it would clarify which scheduling problems admit efficient preprocessing, a central question in this corner of parameterized complexity.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems — openproblem sgall
open: Which of the fifteen open questions on the parameterized complexity of machine scheduling, posed by Matthias Mnich and René van Bevern, can be resolved — for instance, by classifying them as fixed-parameter tractable or W[1]-hard with respect to natural scheduling parameters?
status: All fifteen problems are stated as open in the source paper (2017); see http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3 (Matthias Mnich, René van Bevern).
solved_when: Each of the 15 open problems stated in the source paper has a resolution (e.g., an FPT algorithm or a hardness classification); the natural criterion is a settled parameterized-complexity classification for every problem on the list.
why: These problems delineate where parameterized algorithms for scheduling succeed and where they provably cannot, so resolving them would give a systematic map of tractable scheduling under natural parameterizations.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Is this fourth open problem from Mnich and van Bevern's curated list on the parameterized complexity of machine scheduling resolved?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2017). Reference: http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3 (Matthias Mnich, René van Bevern).
solved_when: A resolution of open problem 4 as stated in the source paper is published.
why: Resolving it would advance the parameterized-complexity classification of machine scheduling problems surveyed in that list.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Is the problem $P||C_{\max}$ with high-multiplicity encoding fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number $p$ of distinct processing times? Here the processing times $p_j$ and the number of jobs having each processing time are encoded in binary, so the input length is logarithmic in the number of jobs.
solved_when: An FPT algorithm (or a proof of W[1]-hardness) for $P||C_{\max}$ under high-multiplicity encoding, parameterized by the number of distinct processing times $p$.
why: It would clarify whether compact high-multiplicity encodings preserve the tractability that parameterization by few distinct processing times offers, a basic question in the parameterized complexity of scheduling.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Is the single-machine scheduling problem with release dates, unit processing times, and the objective of minimizing the weighted number of late jobs, \( |r_j, p_j{=}p|\, w_jU_j \), fixed-parameter tractable? Formally: does this problem admit an FPT algorithm with respect to a natural parameter such as the number of jobs accepted on time, or the number of tardy jobs?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2017): Matthias Mnich, René van Bevern, "Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems," http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3, as its open problem 7.
solved_when: A definitive answer to the parameterized complexity status of \( |r_j, p_j{=}p|\, w_jU_j \) is established — either an FPT algorithm with a stated parameter, or a proof of W[1]-hardness (or comparable lower bound) for that parameter.
why: Settling this would clarify the boundary between tractable and intractable scheduling problems with release dates even in the restricted unit-processing-time setting, guiding the design of exact and parameterized algorithms in practice.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems — openproblem cis
open: Which of the fifteen open problems on the parameterized complexity of machine scheduling, posed by Matthias Mnich and René van Bevern, can be resolved — that is, settled in either direction (fixed-parameter tractability or hardness) within the parameterized framework?
status: The record states only that these problems were posed as open in the source paper (2017), "Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems" by Matthias Mnich and René van Bevern (http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3); no resolutions are recorded.
solved_when: Each of the fifteen open problems stated in the source paper has a definitive answer establishing its parameterized complexity (FPT membership or W[1]-hardness/intractability as appropriate to the question).
why: Resolving these problems would map the parameterized landscape of fundamental scheduling problems, determining whether structural parameters can circumvent the classical NP-hardness of machine scheduling in practice.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Is the family of scheduling problems considered in the source paper fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number p of distinct processing times? More precisely, can each of these problems be solved in time f(p) · poly(n) for some computable function f?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2017), "Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems" by Matthias Mnich and René van Bevern (arXiv:1709.01670v3); no resolution is recorded here.
solved_when: An FPT algorithm (running time f(p) · poly(input size) for a computable function f) is given for the problems in question, or a hardness result (e.g., W[1]-hardness) rules this out.
why: Resolving it would clarify whether a small number of distinct processing times alone is enough to tame the combinatorial difficulty of these scheduling problems, a natural structural parameter for realistic instances.

title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems
open: Is the scheduling problem with unit processing times, release dates, and the weighted number of late jobs as objective — \( |p_{ij}{=}1,r_j| w_jU_j\) — fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of jobs? In other words, does there exist an algorithm deciding it in time \(f(k)\cdot n^{O(1)}\), where \(k\) is the parameter and \(n\) the input size?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2017), Matthias Mnich and René van Bevern, http://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01670v3.
solved_when: An FPT algorithm for \( |p_{ij}{=}1,r_j| w_jU_j\) (with respect to the natural parameterization) is given, or the problem is shown to be W[1]-hard, thereby placing it outside FPT unless W[1] = FPT.
why: Resolving it would complete the parameterized-complexity picture for a fundamental single-machine scheduling objective with release dates, one of the basic open cases in the parameterized classification of scheduling problems.

title: Some Open Problems related to Creative Telescoping
open: Does there exist a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm that, given a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term, computes its telescoping relations? More precisely, can reduction techniques be extended to handle inputs that are simultaneously hypergeometric and hyperexponential?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2016), arXiv:1609.03768v1 (Shaoshi Chen, Manuel Kauers).
solved_when: An algorithm of this kind is given together with a proof of correctness and termination on arbitrary hypergeometric-hyperexponential inputs.
why: It would extend the reach of creative telescoping, a core tool for proving and discovering hypergeometric and special-function identities, to a class of inputs not currently covered by reduction-based methods.

title: Some Open Problems related to Creative Telescoping
open: Does there exist a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm that works for a given Fuchsian D-finite input? More precisely, can the reduction-based approach to creative telescoping be extended to handle arbitrary Fuchsian D-finite functions?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2016), http://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03768v1 (Shaoshi Chen, Manuel Kauers).
solved_when: An algorithm of reduction-based creative telescoping type is developed that accepts a Fuchsian D-finite function as input and computes its telescoping relation.
why: It would extend the reach of creative telescoping, a core tool for proving and discovering hypergeometric and D-finite identities, to the full Fuchsian class via the reduction-based paradigm.

title: Some Open Problems related to Creative Telescoping
open: Does every general D-finite function admit an order-degree curve — an explicit trade-off relation between the order and degree of telescoping relations — and if so, can it be derived? A sharper version asks for a bound describing how the order and degree of a creative-telescoping relation for a general D-finite function vary jointly.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2016), arXiv:1609.03768v1 (Shaoshi Chen, Manuel Kauers), and no resolution is recorded here.
solved_when: An explicit order-degree curve is derived for general D-finite functions, in the generality posed in the source paper.
why: Such a curve would give a priori control over the size of creative-telescoping certificates, informing algorithm choices and complexity predictions for symbolic summation and integration of D-finite functions.

title: Some Open Problems related to Creative Telescoping
open: How large, in bits, can a telescoper for a hypergeometric or hyperexponential term actually be? A precise version asks for explicit upper bounds on the bit size of telescopers for hyperexponential terms, in terms of natural parameters of the input.

title: Regularity Properties of Sectorial Operators: Counterexamples and Open
open: If $A$ is an $R$-sectorial operator on $L_p$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, must the usual sectoriality angle $\omega(A)$ coincide with the $R$-sectoriality angle $\omega_R(A)$ — in particular when $A$ generates a positive, contractive, or positive contractive analytic $C_0$-semigroup?
