title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 1 1
open: Are reversible and irreversible couplings for quantum control quantitatively comparable, so that they can be viewed as manifestations of a single underlying resource, or are they genuinely distinct resources? More precisely, one asks whether there exists a measure under which both kinds of coupling can be jointly quantified and traded off against one another.
solved_when: A quantitative framework is provided in which reversible and irreversible couplings are measured on common ground and shown to be interchangeable manifestations of one resource, or alternatively a proof is given that no such unifying measure exists and the resources are necessarily distinct.
why: A unifying measure would allow control protocols to mix coherent and dissipative dynamics optimally, trading one against the other; if they are distinct resources, control design must treat them separately, changing how optimal quantum control schemes are formulated.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 2 2
open: Is coherent feedback — control implemented by directly coupling an auxiliary system to the target — strictly better than continuous measurement-based feedback when both are given the same dissipative resources? And if coherent feedback does win in that setting, does its advantage survive when the dissipative resources are removed?
solved_when: A precise characterization (theorem or explicit construction) of the relative power of continuous measurement-based feedback versus direct-coupling coherent feedback is established, both with the same dissipative resources and without them, resolving whether superiority holds in each regime.
why: It would clarify the fundamental design principle for quantum control architectures — when engineers should build coherent couplings rather than measurement loops — and determine whether measurement is ever an unavoidable cost in feedback control.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 3 3
open: How large must a quantum auxiliary system be, and what dynamics must it have, to replace the classical post-processing of a measurement record in measurement-based control? Coherent feedback mediated by fields already subsumes continuous measurement-based control apart from the computer's ability to process the measurement results; the question is what quantum resources suffice to replicate various kinds of that classical information processing.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the size and dynamics of a quantum auxiliary that approximates specified kinds of classical processing of the measurement record, for each class of processing considered.
why: It would quantify the genuine resource cost of moving classical controllers into fully coherent quantum feedback, indicating when coherent feedback offers real advantages over measurement-based control.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 5 5
open: Which geodesics on the relevant control manifold correspond to specific quantum control objectives, and how well can those geodesics be approximated using the interactions actually available in mesoscopic systems?
solved_when: A characterization is given of the geodesics realizing given control objectives, together with bounds on how closely these geodesics can be approximated by physically available mesoscopic interactions.
why: It would connect abstract geometric control theory to the practical design of control protocols in mesoscopic quantum systems, where only a restricted set of interactions can be implemented.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 6 6
open: Coherent feedback implemented through unitary interactions is intrinsically a periodic process. What kind of Hamiltonians are needed to achieve continuous or quasi-continuous control, and can simple analytic expressions for the steady-state performance be obtained in some regimes?
solved_when: A characterization of the Hamiltonians that yield continuous or quasi-continuous coherent feedback control is given, together with analytic expressions for steady-state performance in at least some regimes.
why: It would extend coherent feedback control beyond its inherently periodic formulation, making it applicable to continuous-time regulation with tractable performance analysis.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 7 7
open: What is the optimal protocol for preparing a desired state of a system using a unitary interaction, in the regime of good control, when the norm of the interaction Hamiltonian is bounded and the Hamiltonian can only be changed at a bounded rate?
solved_when: A protocol is given that achieves state preparation optimally under the stated constraints — a bound on the norm of the interaction Hamiltonian and a bound on the rate at which the Hamiltonian can be changed — together with a proof of its optimality in the good-control regime.
why: It would establish the fundamental speed and resource limits for controlling quantum systems via bounded-strength, bounded-rate interactions, which is central to practical quantum control.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 9 8
open: How well can coherent feedback control perform relative to continuous measurement-based feedback control when both are given equivalent resources? The goal is to determine bounds on measurement-based feedback performance in the good-control regime by finding optimal protocols for coherent feedback using the same resources.
solved_when: Explicit optimal coherent-feedback protocols are constructed under resource constraints equivalent to those of the measurement-based scheme, yielding bounds on the achievable performance of continuous measurement-based feedback control in the good-control regime.
why: It would establish quantitative limits on how much control performance measurement-based feedback can deliver, and clarify whether coherent (measurement-free) feedback can match or beat it under equal resources.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 14 13
open: What is the optimal control protocol when a system is well controlled but its auxiliary (ancillary) system experiences significant damping? In other words, determine the optimal control in the good-control regime under strongly damped auxiliary dynamics.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2013), arXiv:1304.0819v3 (Kurt Jacobs), "Twenty open problems in quantum control"; no solution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: An explicit description (or derivation) of the optimal control protocol is obtained for the good-control regime with significant damping of the auxiliary system.
why: It fills a gap in the toolbox of quantum control: optimal protocols are known in other regimes, and this case is a common physical situation where the missing answer limits performance guarantees for damped ancilla-based control schemes.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 15 14
open: What are the limits to controlling a quantum system when the controller itself is subject to noise comparable to that of the system? In particular, how do these limits scale as the size of the auxiliary (controller) system grows relative to the system being controlled?
solved_when: A characterization is given of the achievable control fidelity (or its limits) as a function of the noise strength and the ratio of auxiliary-system size to system size, valid in the regime where controller and system noise are of the same order.
why: It would establish fundamental bounds on quantum control with realistic, noisy controllers, clarifying whether enlarging the auxiliary system genuinely improves control or is ultimately limited by its own noise.

title: Twenty open problems in quantum control — problem 17 16
open: Does coherent quantum feedback still outperform measurement-based control when the controller itself is subject to damping or noise? More precisely, at what noise level does the advantage of coherent feedback disappear, and does that threshold matter for real-world applications?
solved_when: A quantitative characterization is given of the noise/damping level at which the advantage of coherent feedback over measurement-based control is eliminated, together with an assessment of whether this level is relevant to real applications.
why: It determines whether coherent feedback — often assumed superior in principle — is actually usable in realistic noisy settings, or whether noise fundamentally negates its advantage in practice.

title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
open: How can one actually compute, estimate, or bound the invariant $e(S)$ for a given linear series? Progress here could take the form of effective algorithms, usable bounds, or a conceptual framework that explains the behavior of $e(S)$.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2011), "Recent developments and open problems in linear series" (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3.
solved_when: A method — computational or theoretical — is available that evaluates, estimates, or bounds $e(S)$ in general, not merely in special cases.
why: Such methods would turn an invariant currently accessible only case-by-case into a workable tool for the study of linear series.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3 (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper)

title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series — conjecture chudnovsky conjecture
open: Does equality hold in the Chudnovsky inequality for symbolic powers — specifically, is $a(S,1) + N - 1 = N \cdot e(S)$ for the relevant graded system of divisors? A resolution would settle when the inequality bounding Waldschmidt constants is sharp.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the equality $a(S,1) + N - 1 = N \cdot e(S)$, in the setting formulated in the source paper.
why: It determines exactly when the Chudnovsky bound on Waldschmidt constants is attained, sharpening the asymptotic theory of symbolic powers and containment results for linear series.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3 (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper)

title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
open: What is the structure of the multigraded Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}_I S$ arising in this setting — in particular, is it locally closed, and which incidence relations/adjacencies hold between its components? A precise description of its geometry and degenerations is the goal.
solved_when: A complete description of $\mathrm{Hilb}_I S$ is given, including a proof or disproof of local closedness and a determination of the adjacency relations among its strata.
why: Understanding $\mathrm{Hilb}_I S$ would clarify how the parametrized linear-series degenerations behave, resolving a basic structural question left open in the source survey.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3 (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper)

title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series — conjecture BNC
open: What can be said about the birational behavior of linear series on smooth projective surfaces — in particular, does the conjecture BNC hold? More precisely, is the asserted relation among the dimensions and degrees of linear series on a smooth projective surface $X$ true as conjectured in the source paper?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2011), "Recent developments and open problems in linear series" (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper), http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3. No further progress is recorded here.
solved_when: Conjecture BNC, as stated in arXiv:1101.4363v3, is proved for smooth projective surfaces (or a counterexample is produced).
why: A resolution would advance the study of linear series and their birational geometry on surfaces, a central topic addressed by the curated open-problems collection from which it comes.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3 (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper)

title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series
open: Let $f: Y \to B$ be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold $Y$. What can be said about such morphisms in the framework of linear series on threefolds, in analogy with the classical theory for surfaces?
solved_when: A resolution of the question as posed in the source paper, namely a characterization (or decisive structural result) of morphisms from smooth projective threefolds $Y$ in terms of their linear series, as the problem's intent specifies; the record states no further quantitative target.
why: Extending the theory of linear series from surfaces to threefolds would clarify how morphisms of higher-dimensional varieties are governed by their linear series, a basic structural question in birational and projective geometry.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4363v3 (Thomas Bauer, Cristiano Bocci, Susan Cooper)

title: Excited random walks: results, methods, open problems
open: Can the assumption that the cookie environment is independent and identically distributed (IID) be replaced by the weaker assumption of strong ellipticity (SE) — that is, do the results for excited random walks extend to cookie environments that are stationary or otherwise non-IID but still strongly elliptic?
solved_when: The main results established under the IID cookie-environment assumption are reproved under only the (SE) condition, so that no independence or identical-distribution hypothesis on the environment remains.
why: It would show the known behavior of excited random walks is driven by ellipticity of the cookies rather than independence, extending the theory to a much broader and more realistic class of environments.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1895v2 (Elena Kosygina, Martin P. W. Zerner)

title: Excited random walks: results, methods, open problems
open: Can the standard ballisticity assumption (BD) for excited random walks be weakened to the positivity-type condition (POS$_1$)? That is, do the paper's conclusions still hold if (BD) is replaced throughout by (POS$_1$)?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that the results established under assumption (BD) remain valid — or fail — under the weaker assumption (POS$_1$).
why: It would extend the main ballisticity and limit results for excited random walks to a strictly larger class of models, refining the minimal hypotheses needed for the theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1895v2 (Elena Kosygina, Martin P. W. Zerner)

title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and o
open: Can the ``oscillatory'' behavior of solutions to the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation, as observed in physical experiments, be established rigorously as a genuine mathematical phenomenon?
solved_when: A rigorous derivation and justification of the oscillatory behavior observed in the physical experiments is given for the focusing NLS equation variants considered in the source paper.
why: It would close the gap between experimentally observed oscillations and rigorous theory for focusing NLS variants, grounding the models of Dumas, Lannes, and Szeftel in proven mathematics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2 (Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel)

title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and o
open: Does adding a partial off-axis dependence to the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation prevent the finite-time breakdown of solutions? More broadly, what are the local and global well-posedness properties of the resulting modified equation?
solved_when: A characterization of local and global well-posedness for the focusing cubic NLS with partial off-axis dependence is established, in particular determining whether the modification prevents finite-time blow-up of solutions.
why: It clarifies whether the off-axis-dependent structure arising in the physical derivation genuinely stabilizes the focusing dynamics, or whether collapse persists in this more realistic model.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2 (Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel)

title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and o
open: Can we give a complete description of the blow-up scenarios for the finite-time blow-up solutions of this equation? In other words, what is the full classification of the ways in which solutions that blow up in finite time do so?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2014), the curated open-problems paper by Eric Dumas, David Lannes, and Jeremie Szeftela, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2.
solved_when: The blow-up behavior of finite-time blow-up solutions is fully characterized — e.g., the blow-up rate, profile, and concentration mechanism are determined for all such solutions of the equation in question.
why: A classification would complete the qualitative theory of the model, replacing the mere existence of blow-up solutions with a precise account of how collapse occurs, which is essential for the rigorous justification of the equation as a water-wave/physical model.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2 (Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel)

title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and o
open: Are the solutions to the variant of the focusing NLS equation considered in this problem global in time in space dimensions 2 and 3? In other words, prove that no finite-time blow-up occurs for these solutions in those dimensions.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2014), arXiv:1405.7308v2 by Eric Dumas, David Lannes, and Jeremie Szeftela; no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A rigorous proof establishes global-in-time existence of solutions to the equation in both dimension 2 and dimension 3.
why: Global well-posedness in these dimensions is a basic prerequisite for the derivation and justification program for variants of the focusing NLS equation to be complete; without it, the validity of the model can only be asserted on the lifespan of local solutions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2 (Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel)

title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and o
open: Do the open problems formulated for the scalar focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the source paper carry over meaningfully to its vectorial counterpart, and if so, what are their solutions? In particular, investigate for the vectorial equation the analogues of the open problems on derivation and justification stated in the referenced sections of that paper.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2014), Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel, arXiv:1405.7308v2; no progress beyond that statement is recorded here.
solved_when: The vectorial counterparts of each of the open problems formulated for the scalar equation in the source paper have been investigated and resolved, in the same sense (derivation and justification results) demanded by the corresponding scalar problems.
why: A resolution would extend the derivation and justification theory of the scalar focusing NLS to systems with vector-valued unknowns, where coupling between components can change the behavior and validity of the NLS approximation.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2 (Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel)

title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and o
open: Can the NLS-type models derived for the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation be rigorously justified as valid approximations over the physically relevant long time scale, including up to the focusing time? Formally, one seeks a rigorous justification of one of the derived NLS-type models on a time scale $[0,T/\varepsilon]$ with $T \sim T_{foc}$.
solved_when: A rigorous justification (approximation result with error bounds) is proved for at least one of the NLS-type models derived in the source paper, valid on the time scale $[0,T/\varepsilon]$ with $T$ of the order of the focusing time $T_{foc}$.
why: Such a result would confirm that the derived focusing NLS variants genuinely describe the underlying dynamics through the onset of focusing, closing the gap between formal derivation and rigorous theory for these models.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7308v2 (Eric Dumas, David Lannes, Jeremie Szeftel)

title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems — problem o:loc
open: Is there a rigorous proof of a formula for the local escape rate in open billiards, analogous to the pressure-function formula used for the global escape rate, for sufficiently chaotic systems? In other words, can the local escape rate be expressed through a suitable analog of the existing escape-rate formula in this setting?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2010), arXiv:1007.4166v1 (Carl P. Dettmann), "Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems."
solved_when: A proof of such a local escape rate formula for sufficiently chaotic open billiards is established, matching the analog of the formula referenced in the source paper.
why: It would extend rigorous escape-rate theory from the global to the local level in open billiards, refining the quantitative description of how trajectories exit different regions of the phase space.

title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
open: Where should a hole be cut in a billiard table so as to make escape as fast, or as slow, as possible? More precisely, given a billiard system and a suitably defined measure of escape, determine the hole placement that maximises or minimises that measure.
solved_when: A characterisation (analytic or sharp sufficient conditions) of hole positions that maximise and minimise the chosen escape measure is given, for a specified class of billiards.
why: It would turn heuristic hole-placement intuition into usable design principles for open systems, and clarify how geometry controls escape rates.

title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems — problem o:tri
open: Existence of periodic orbits: Do all triangular (or more generally polygonal) billiards

title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
open: Is there a rigorous formulation of the escape rate for dispersing billiards with small holes? That is, can the rate at which trajectories leak out of a dispersing billiard through a small hole be given a precise mathematical definition with provable properties?
solved_when: A rigorous formulation of the escape rate of dispersing billiards with small holes is provided and established.
why: A rigorous formulation would place the widely used escape-rate quantities for open dispersing billiards on solid mathematical footing, enabling rigorous analysis of their asymptotics as the hole shrinks.

title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
open: Does the fractal Weyl conjecture hold, i.e. does the number of resonances (quantum states) with Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C grow according to a power law governed by the fractal dimension of the trapped set, rather than by phase-space volume?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2010), "Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems" (Carl P. Dettmann, arXiv:1007.4166v1), where it appears as problem 15 among the curated open problems.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given of the fractal Weyl law for the counting function of resonances in the region Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C, with the growth exponent matching the dimension of the trapped set.
why: The fractal Weyl law controls how many metastable states of an open billiard survive near the real axis; establishing it would place resonance-based descriptions of scattering and decay in open chaotic systems on rigorous footing.

title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
open: For a given open (generalised) billiard problem, can the survival probability admit an exact expansion? The source poses this as whether such an expansion — in exact form, beyond asymptotic or heuristic estimates — can be obtained for the survival probability.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2010), the curated open-problems paper by Carl P. Dettmann, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/1007.4166v1.
solved_when: An exact expansion of the survival probability is derived for a given open (generalised) billiard problem, as posed in the source paper. No further quantitative targets are specified in the record.
why: Exact expansions of the survival probability would replace asymptotic and numerical estimates with rigorously computable formulas, giving precise control over escape statistics in open billiards.

title: 66 and 67 on sums of residue classes and primes of András Sár — problem 66 1
open: Do the classical Goldbach-type problems for prime sums carry over to the multiplicative group of reduced residue classes modulo $m$ — specifically, can every element of $\mathbb{Z}_m^*$ be represented as a sum of two reduced residue classes (part a) or three reduced residue classes (part b)? This is an analogue of the binary and ternary Goldbach conjectures, transplanted from the positive integers to $\mathbb{Z}_m^*$.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, with counterexample) is given for the analogue of Goldbach's conjecture in $\mathbb{Z}_m^*$: whether every element of $\mathbb{Z}_m^*$ can be written as a sum of two reduced residue classes (part a), and correspondingly as a sum of three (part b).
why: It extends the Goldbach phenomenon from the additive integers to the multiplicative group of residues modulo $m$, testing how robust additive-prime decompositions are in a finite group setting where classical tools may or may not transfer.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02433v1 (Yuchen Ding, Christian Elsholtz, Yu-Chen Sun)

title: 66 and 67 on sums of residue classes and primes of András Sár — problem 67 2
open: Can the Vinogradov circle-method approach to representing numbers as sums of primes be made to work when only slightly more than half of all primes are available, or do serious obstacles arise that rule out such an extension?
solved_when: A proof, or disproof, that the Vinogradov circle method extends to sums of primes restricted to any subset consisting of a bit more than half of all primes; the natural criterion is a complete answer to whether such a restriction preserves the method's conclusions or admits genuine counterexamples.
why: It tests the robustness of the circle method against density restrictions on the prime set, which would clarify how much of the full prime sequence the method genuinely needs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02433v1 (Yuchen Ding, Christian Elsholtz, Yu-Chen Sun)

title: Linear Systems and Eigenvalue Problems: Open Questions from a Simons W
open: Let $B$ be an $n \times n$ (upper) bidiagonal matrix. Does there exist an algorithm that computes $k$ certified approximate singular value triplets $(\sigma_i, v_i, u_i)$ — with $\sigma_i \geq 0$ and $v_i, u_i \in \mathbb{C}^n$ unit vectors — in only $O(kn)$ operations, each accurate to machine precision $\epsilon$?
solved_when: An algorithm is given that, for an $n \times n$ (upper) bidiagonal matrix $B$, outputs $k$ triples $(\sigma_i, v_i, u_i)$ with $\sigma_i \geq 0$, $v_i, u_i \in \mathbb{C}^n$ unit vectors, accurate to machine precision $\epsilon$, using $O(kn)$ operations.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Can a convex domain be essentially visible without being fully visible? Specifically, does there exist a bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs, such that $\Omega$ is essentially visible but not visible; and can such an example be taken to be smoothly bounded?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in ...", by Filippo Bracci and Ahmed Yekta Ökten (http://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19967v2). No example is known.
solved_when: An example is produced of a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^N$ with no non-trivial analytic discs in its boundary that is essentially visible but not visible; ideally, one that is smoothly bounded.
why: It would separate the notions of essential visibility and visibility for convex domains, clarifying which boundary geometry properties each concept genuinely captures.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in — question Q:continuity
open: Does there exist a non-visible bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^d$ such that every complex geodesic extends continuously up to the boundary? Equivalently, is continuous extension of all complex geodesics up to the boundary sufficient to guarantee visibility of the domain?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2025), Bracci and Ökten, "Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in $\mathbb{C}^d$", arXiv:2507.19967v2 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19967v2).
solved_when: Either a bounded convex domain is exhibited that is not visible yet all of its complex geodesics extend continuously to the boundary, or it is proved that such continuous extension forces visibility.
why: It isolates whether visibility is genuinely stronger than geodesic boundary-regularity for convex domains, sharpening the boundary structure theory of complex geodesics.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Is visibility of a bounded convex domain $ ^N$ equivalent to complex visibility? In other words, can the geometric notion of visibility be characterized purely by the complex-geometric notion of complex visibility?
status: Stated as open (conjecture 4) in the source paper arXiv:2507.19967v2, "Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in ," by Filippo Bracci and Ahmed Yekta Ökten (2025). No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via counterexample) that for every bounded convex domain $ ^N$, visibility holds if and only if complex visibility holds.
why: It would clarify the relationship between the geometric and complex-geometric visibility conditions that underpin results on iteration theory and holomorphic dynamics on convex domains.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Does there exist a bounded convex domain $ $ which is not visible and such that all geodesic rays land?

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Is it true that, for a bounded convex domain in complex Euclidean space, visibility of the domain is equivalent to uniform equicontinuity of the geodesics $G_{z_0}$ issuing from a base point $z_0$? The proposed equivalence is between $G_{z_0}$ viewed as maps from $[0,+\infty)$ with the Euclidean topology into the domain with the Euclidean topology.
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) of the equivalence: bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ is visible if and only if $G_{z_0}$ is uniformly equicontinuous as a family of functions from $[0,+\infty)$ with the Euclidean topology to $\mathbb{C}^N$ with the Euclidean topology.
why: It would give a purely equicontinuity-based characterization of visibility for bounded convex domains, linking Kobayashi geodesic behavior to a classical function-family compactness condition.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: For a bounded convex domain $D \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ containing no non-trivial analytic discs, is it true that the Denjoy–Wolff property is equivalent to the condition that the closure of every sequential horosphere meets $D$ in exactly one point?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given, for bounded convex domains without non-trivial analytic discs, that the Denjoy–Wolff property holds if and only if the closure of any sequential horosphere touches $D$ at just one point.
why: It would characterize when Denjoy–Wolff-type dynamics extend to higher-dimensional convex domains, tying the iteration behavior of holomorphic self-maps to an intrinsic geometric/horosphere condition.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Is it true that, for a bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$, visibility of the boundary is equivalent to the Denjoy–Wolff property? In other words, must every bounded convex domain in which geodesics see the boundary also satisfy the dynamical Denjoy–Wolff phenomenon, and conversely?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given of the equivalence: a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^N$ is visible if and only if it enjoys the Denjoy–Wolff property.
why: It would tie together the metric geometry of the domain (visibility) with its holomorphic dynamics (the Denjoy–Wolff property), giving a single geometric criterion for a key dynamical behavior on bounded convex domains.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Suppose $N \geq 1$ and $F: \mathbb{C}^N \to \mathbb{C}^N$ is holomorphic and fixed-point free. Must there exist a component index $j \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ and a point $w \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $\pi_j(F^{\circ n}(z)) = w$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}^N$, where $\pi_j(z) = z_j$ is the projection onto the $j$-th component?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) is given for the stated conjecture: for every fixed-point-free holomorphic self-map $F$ of $\mathbb{C}^N$, some iterated coordinate $\pi_j(F^{\circ n}(z))$ is constant in $z$ for suitable $j$ and $n$; a counterexample resolves it negatively.
why: It constrains how complicated fixed-point-free holomorphic dynamics in several variables can be: a positive answer would force every such map to trivialize along some coordinate under iteration.

title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in
open: Does the visibility and iteration property in question 10 of the source paper hold as conjectured?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of question 10 as stated in the source paper is given.
why: The question comes from a curated open-problems paper; resolving it advances understanding of visibility and iteration in holomorphic dynamics.

title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon — conjecture lblockc1
open: For each integer $k$, does there exist an integer $n$ such that every $k$-blocked point set has at most $n$ vertices in its visibility graph? Informally: is the number of edges (or vertices) in a visibility graph of a $k$-blocked point set bounded by a function of $k$ alone?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2010), "Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon" (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4.
solved_when: For every integer $k$, an integer $n$ is exhibited such that every $k$-blocked point set has a visibility graph with at most $n$ vertices (equivalently, bounded size in terms of $k$ alone).
why: A positive answer would give a structural finiteness principle for visibility graphs of $k$-blocked point sets, constraining how complicated such visibility graphs can be as a function of the blocking parameter alone.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4 (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami)

title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon — conjecture lblockc2
open: Must every $k$-blocked point set be finite of bounded size, specifically with at most $O(k^2)$ points? Formally, is there a constant $c$ such that every $k$-blocked point set contains at most $c\,k^2$ points?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2010), "Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon" (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via explicit construction) of the bound $O(k^2)$ on the number of points in any $k$-blocked point set.
why: It would give a tight structural limit on how large visibility-restricted point configurations can be, a basic parameter in the combinatorics of visibility graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4 (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami)

title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon — conjecture lblockc3
open: Does every $k$-blocked point set admit a colouring in which each colour class contains at most $k$ points? More precisely, is it true that in every $k$-blocked point set there are at most $k$ points in each colour class?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every $k$-blocked point set has at most $k$ points in each colour class is given.
why: It would resolve a basic structural question about $k$-blocked point sets arising in the study of visibility graphs, clarifying how colour classes are constrained by the blocking parameter.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4 (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami)

title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon — conjecture lspann1
open: Does every segment visibility graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle? That is, must the visibility graph induced by a finite set of segments in the plane always admit a cycle visiting each vertex exactly once?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2010), "Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygon" (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami), http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4.
solved_when: A proof that every segment visibility graph is Hamiltonian, or a counterexample exhibiting a segment visibility graph with no Hamiltonian cycle.
why: It would settle a basic structural property of segment visibility graphs, placing them alongside other visibility graph classes with known Hamiltonicity behavior.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5187v4 (Subir Kumar Ghosh, Partha Pratim Goswami)

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
open: Foreman asks: if $C$ is the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold $M$ that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism, and $E$ is topological conjugacy restricted to $C$, is $E$ Borel reducible to equality?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that the conjugacy relation $E$ on $C$ is Borel reducible to the equality relation.
why: It would determine whether conjugacy within the structurally stable class admits a Borel classification by countable invariants, a basic question linking descriptive set theory to smooth dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman)

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
open: Is the topological conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel relation? In other words, can conjugacy between these systems be realized at the Borel level of complexity?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2023), the curated open-problems paper "Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems" (http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1, Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman).

title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions — question 4.1 1

status: The question is stated as open in the source paper, arXiv:0912.2662v2 (Weimin Chen, 2009), a curated open-problems survey of group actions on 4-manifolds.
solved_when: A concrete result exhibiting a group action on a 4-manifold (or an obstruction to one) that goes beyond topological considerations — for example, distinguishing actions that are topologically equivalent but differ in the smooth or symplectic category.
why: It would show that smooth or symplectic structure, not just topology, governs finite group actions on 4-manifolds, sharpening the classification landscape in dimension four.

title: Mining Top-k Sequential Patterns in Database Graphs:A New Challenging — problem the_problem
open: Given a database graph $G$, an integer $k > 0$, and a fixed pattern length $l > 0$, can we efficiently find the top-$k$ sequential patterns of length $l$ with the largest frequencies in $D_l$ of $G$? The question asks for the $k$ patterns of that prescribed length whose frequencies in $D_l$ are maximal.

why: Top-$k$ sequential pattern mining in database graphs would let users extract the most frequent length-$l$ patterns without a frequency threshold, a common practical bottleneck in graph mining; solving it fills a gap explicitly flagged in the source paper.

title: Mean Curvature Flow through Singularities — problem 5.1 1
open: Is the round cylinder the only complete embedded self-shrinking surface for mean curvature flow? More precisely, is the rigidity of the cylinder the full story: does no other complete embedded shrinker exist with the same asymptotic structure?

title: Mean Curvature Flow through Singularities — conjecture 5.3 3
open: Does the intrinsic diameter of a surface remain uniformly bounded as it evolves by mean curvature flow through its singularities? More precisely, is there a uniform bound on the intrinsic diameter throughout the flow, including at and beyond singular times?

title: Mean Curvature Flow through Singularities — problem 5.5 5

title: Mean Curvature Flow through Singularities — conjecture 5.10 12

title: Tightness of maximum likelihood semidefinite relaxations — conjecture Conjecture:Procrustes
open: Do maximum likelihood semidefinite relaxations recover the ground truth in the noisy orthogonal Procrustes / synchronization setting with random data? Formally, let $d>1$, $n>2$, $m>d+1$, and let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m}$ represent $m$ random points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with i.i.d. uniform coordinates in $[0,1]^d$; let $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be any sequence of orthogonal transformations and $A_i = O_iA + \sigma_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times m}$, where $\sigma_i$ has i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries. There exists $\sigma_*>0$ such that, for $\sigma<\sigma_*$, with high probability the solution of the SDP has rank $d$, and hence matches the quasi-MLE.

why: Establishing tightness of the SDP relaxation in the presence of noise certifies that the relaxation, not just the nonconvex quasi-MLE, provably recovers the underlying orthogonal transformations, giving a tractable and statistically reliable estimator for structure-from-motion and synchronization problems.

open: For which pairs $(k,d)$ does there exist a convex $d$-polytope whose combinatorial flags fall into exactly $k$ orbits under its combinatorial symmetry group?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2016), "Open problems on k-orbit polytopes" by Gabe Cunningham and Daniel Pelcker [sic] (http://arxiv.org/abs/1608.07993v1); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A characterization of the set of pairs $(k,d)$ for which such a polytope exists is given, i.e., a complete answer to the realizability question above.
why: It would delimit exactly how much symmetry a convex polytope of each dimension can and cannot have, refining the classical dichotomy between transitive (single-orbit) and general polytopes.

title: on k-orbit polytopes
open: Which $k$-orbit $d$-polytopes admit a faithful realization as a geometrically $k$-orbit polytope in $E^d$? That is, when can a polytope whose combinatorial automorphism group has $k$ orbits on flags be realized so that its geometric symmetry group also has exactly $k$ flag orbits?
solved_when: A characterization is given of the $k$-orbit $d$-polytopes that admit a faithful geometrically $k$-orbit realization in $E^d$ (for arbitrary $k$ and $d$, or a nontrivial specified range).
why: It would delimit exactly when combinatorial symmetry classes of a polytope can be matched by genuine geometric symmetries, separating the combinatorial theory of $k$-orbit polytopes from its geometric counterpart.

title: Mining Top-k Sequential Patterns in Database Graphs:A New Challenging — problem count_problem
open: How hard is it to count the number of length-$l$ sequential patterns in a database graph whose frequencies exceed a given threshold? Formally, given a database graph $G$, a threshold $\tau > 0$ and a fixed length $l > 0$, count the number of length-$l$ patterns with frequency larger than $\tau$ in $D_l$ of $G$.
solved_when: An algorithm (or complexity classification) resolving the counting problem for length-$l$ patterns with frequency above the threshold in $D_l$ of $G$ is provided, or its hardness is established.
why: Resolving it would clarify whether top-$k$ sequential pattern mining in database graphs is tractable, guiding the design of practical mining algorithms or proving fundamental limits.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03320v1 (Mingtao Lei, Lingyang Chu, Zhefeng Wang)

title: Current Trends and Open Problems in Arithmetic Dynamics — conjecture DMM
open: Does the dynamical Manin–Mumford conjecture hold, given that it has been shown to be false as originally stated?
solved_when: A corrected formulation of the conjecture is established, or a counterexample shows no reasonable reformulation holds; the record states no quantitative targets.

title: Symmetric functions in superspace: a compendium of results and open pr
open: Are the coefficients $K_{\Lambda,\Omega}(q,t)$, indexed by superpartitions, always polynomials in $q$ and $t$ with nonnegative integer coefficients? That is, does the $q,t$-structure of these superspace coefficients exhibit positivity in the same spirit as classical Macdonald–Kostka theory?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2019), "Symmetric functions in superspace: a compendium of results and open problems" (Ludovic Alarie-Vezina, Olivier Blondeau-Fournier, Patrick Desrosiers), arXiv:1903.07777v1; no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with explicit counterexample) that for all superpartitions the coefficients $K_{ }(q,t)$ are polynomials in $q$ and $t$ with nonnegative integer coefficients.
why: Positivity of these coefficients would mirror the celebrated positivity phenomena in ordinary symmetric function theory, giving the superspace extension a combinatorial footing; failure would reveal a genuine obstruction to extending Macdonald-type positivity to superspace.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07777v1 (Ludovic Alarie-Vezina, Olivier Blondeau-Fournier, Patrick Desrosiers)

title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
open: Does there exist a global approximation result in 2D only under the spectral gap assumption?
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/1903.09439v2 (J. Ignacio Cirac, José Garre-Rubio, David Pérez-García)

title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces — question K-infiniteset-prodquestion
open: If each factor space of an arbitrary product is determined by its $K$-saturation with respect to a full subcategory $K$ of $Top_0$ containing $Sob$ (in particular, a Keimel–Lawson category), must the product of the $K$-determined subsets also be $K$-determined? Formally, for a family $\{X_i : i \in I\}$ of $T_0$ spaces with each $A_i \subseteq X_i$ $K$-determined, is $\prod_{i \in I} A_i$ $K$-determined in the product space $X = \prod_{i \in I} X_i$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2020), "Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces" by Xiaoquan Xu and Dongsheng Zhao (http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00539v1).
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, is given for the preservation of $K$-determinedness under arbitrary products for every full subcategory $K$ of $Top_0$ containing $Sob$, including Keimel–Lawson categories.
why: It tests whether the key notions linking domain theory to general topology (well-filteredness and sobriety) behave well under products, a property central to transferring results between the categorical and topological settings.

title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Quest
open: Let $t_1 = x^n - ax^n - b $ and $t_2 = x^n - a'x^{n-i} - b' $ and $ (t_1) = (t_2)$. Let $C_1$ be the set of all polycyclic codes associated with $t_1$ and $C_2$ be the set of all polycyclic codes associated with $t_2$. Then $C_1$ and $C_2$ are in a one-to-one correspondence where corresponding codes are equivalent to each other.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12065v1 (Nuh Aydin, Peihan Liu, Bryan Yoshino)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems — problem prob-closed
open: Does the group of Sobolev diffeomorphisms $D^s(M)$ contain a closed geodesic? More precisely, does the geodesic flow on this infinite-dimensional group, with respect to a right-invariant metric, admit a nontrivial periodic orbit?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), the curated open-problems collection "Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems," problem prob-closed, by Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiołek, and Alexander Shnirelman (arXiv:2205.01143v2, http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2).
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, of the existence of a closed geodesic in $D^s(M)$ is established.
why: Closed geodesics on diffeomorphism groups correspond to periodic solutions of the governing Euler equations of ideal hydrodynamics, so the answer directly determines whether periodic behavior is possible in the geometric formulation of fluid motion.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems — problem prob-cpts
open: Along which $L^2$ geodesic starting from the identity does the first conjugate point occur, and what is its order? Formally, determine the order of the first conjugate point along any $L^2$ geodesic emanating from the identity.
solved_when: The order of the first conjugate point along any $L^2$ geodesic starting from the identity is determined.

title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
open: Do there exist solutions of the 3D Euler equation whose trajectories wander in the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, rather than staying confined near a fixed region? Formally, is the action of the geodesic flow on the diffeomorphism group of Euler solutions non-wandering?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2022), arXiv:2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman), a curated collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics.
solved_when: A construction (or proof of existence) of wandering solutions of the 3D Euler equation, or a proof that no such solutions exist, is given.
why: Wandering would signal a mechanism of effective mixing and drift in ideal fluid motion, contrasting with the recurrent behavior long expected for Euler flows; it is a basic question about the long-time dynamics of ideal fluids.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01143v2 (Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek, Alexander Shnirelman)

title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
open: What is the computational complexity of the {No-Even-Split} 4-uniform $s$-$t$ cut problem? That is, where does this problem sit between polynomial-time solvability and NP-hardness?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2023), http://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11464v1 (Sinan G. Aksoy, Ryan Bennink, Yuzhou Chen); no progress toward a resolution is recorded here.
solved_when: The problem is classified as either polynomial-time solvable or NP-hard.
why: Resolving it completes the complexity picture for this variant of $s$-$t$ cuts in 4-uniform hypergraphs, a natural family of cut problems arising in applied combinatorics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11464v1 (Sinan G. Aksoy, Ryan Bennink, Yuzhou Chen)

title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
open: What is the computational complexity of the {No-Even-Split} 4-uniform $s$-$t$ cut problem — is it polynomial-time solvable, or is it hard? A precise answer would settle the tractability boundary for this variant of the $s$-$t$ cut problem on 4-uniform hypergraphs.
status: The problem was stated as open in 2023 in a curated open-problems paper, "Seven open problems in applied combinatorics" (http://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11464v1, by Sinan G. Aksoy, Ryan Bennink, and Yuzhou Chen); no complexity result for it is recorded there.
solved_when: A proof either gives a polynomial-time algorithm for the {No-Even-Split} 4-uniform $s$-$t$ cut problem or establishes its hardness (e.g., NP-hardness).
why: Resolving it would locate where cut-problem tractability breaks in the uniform-hypergraph setting, informing which cut heuristics and algorithms used in applications can be guaranteed efficient.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11464v1 (Sinan G. Aksoy, Ryan Bennink, Yuzhou Chen)

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Which irreducible components can appear in a non-reduced scheme arising as the eigenscheme of a tensor? More precisely, given such a scheme $X$, what degrees can its irreducible components have, and which schemes arise as those components?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), the curated open-problems collection by Fulvio Gesmundo, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2304.10570v1. No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the possible degrees of the irreducible components of a non-reduced eigenscheme of a tensor, together with a description of the schemes that can arise as such components.
why: It would map the non-reduced behavior of eigenschemes of tensors, sharpening our understanding of how eigenvector structure of tensors degenerates beyond the reduced case.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions
open: Which numbers of real elements can occur among the critical points of a probability tensor? Formally, determine the possible counts of real points among the $\binom{n}{n_1 \dots n_d}$ critical points of a probability tensor.
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the subsets of real numbers that arise as the number of real critical points of a probability tensor.
why: It would clarify how complex algebraic geometry of tensor critical loci interacts with real probability constraints, informing real-world inference and optimization on statistical tensor models.

title: Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions — problem prob: equations TNS
open: What are the defining equations of a tensor network variety? If a full answer is out of reach, determine equations for restricted settings, such as particular classes of underlying graphs or particular assignments of bond and local dimensions.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), "Geometry of Tensors: Open problems and research directions" (Fulvio Gesmundo), arXiv:2304.10570v1.
solved_when: An explicit description of the equations cutting out the tensor network variety is obtained — either in general, or for specified classes of graphs and specified bond/local dimension assignments.
why: Equations for tensor network varieties are the basic algebraic obstructions to which tensors are representable by a given network geometry, underpinning questions about expressivity and identifiability in tensor network methods.

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
open: Is there an open dense subset (or a dense $G_\delta$ subset) of $Diff^\infty(M)$, for a compact manifold $M$ of dimension at least 2, on which the equivalence relation of topological conjugacy is Borel?
status: The question is attributed to Gorodetski and stated as open in the source paper (2023), the curated open-problems paper http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman).
solved_when: An explicit open dense (or dense $G_\delta$) subset of $Diff^\infty(M)$ with $\dim M \geq 2$ is produced on which topological conjugacy is a Borel equivalence relation, or it is shown no such subset exists.
why: It probes whether generic smooth systems can be classified by countable invariants, a key tension point between descriptive set theory and smooth dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman)

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
open: Is the measure isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval exactly as complex, in the Borel-reducibility hierarchy, as the most complex Polish group action? Put formally: is it bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that the measure isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval is bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action.
why: It would pin down the exact position of a central equivalence relation of ergodic theory within the Borel reducibility hierarchy, completing our picture of how complicated classification of measure-preserving transformations really is.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman)

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
open: Is the conjugacy relation on $[T_0]$ a Borel relation? And if it is not Borel in general, does it become Borel when restricted to ergodic transformations?
solved_when: The Borelness of the conjugacy relation on $[T_0]$ is settled, or, in the negative case, the Borelness of its restriction to the ergodic transformations is settled.
why: Resolving it clarifies the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the conjugacy equivalence relation on $[T_0]$, a key step toward understanding when dynamical classification can or cannot be carried out by Borel means.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman)

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
open: Does every measure-preserving action of a free group admit a uniquely ergodic topological model? That is, can each such action be realized as the unique invariant measure of some continuous action on a compact space?
status: The question is attributed to Seward and was stated as open in the source paper (2023), "Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems" (http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1, by Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman).
solved_when: A construction is given that, for every measure-preserving action of a free group, produces a topological dynamical system whose unique invariant measure models the action.
why: It would extend the Jewett–Krieger-type modeling phenomenon beyond amenable and single-transformer settings, clarifying how far unique ergodicity persists for non-amenable groups.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman)

title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems — question question: Main
open: Given an ergodic toral automorphism $(T^d, R)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure, and a homeomorphism $(Y, S)$ of a Polish space admitting no invariant probability measure, must $(Y, S)$ admit an equivariant Borel embedding into $(T^d, R)$?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given, in full generality, of the existence of an equivariant Borel embedding of every such $(Y, S)$ into the ergodic toral automorphism $(T^d, R)$.
why: It probes how universal ergodic toral automorphisms are as Borel dynamical systems, connecting descriptive set theory with measurable dynamics for systems lacking invariant measures.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00248v1 (Jérôme Buzzi, Nishant Chandgotia, Matthew Foreman)

title: in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes an — problem problem:VCLthree
open: Consider the locus $L_{78}$. Is this locus a component (and if so, of the relevant Hilbert scheme / deformation space)?
solved_when: A proof or disproof that the locus $L_{78}$ is a component, as stated as open in the source paper.
why: Resolving it would clarify the component structure of the Hilbert scheme / deformation space of Artinian algebras in question, a basic structural question in this corner of deformation theory.

title: a list of open problems
open: Construct an entire symplectic automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^2$ that has no periodic points, yet possesses a non-empty set of Lyapunov unstable points with bounded orbits.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi).
solved_when: An explicit entire symplectic automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^2$ is constructed that simultaneously has no periodic points and whose set of Lyapunov unstable points with bounded orbit is non-empty.
why: It would exhibit a concrete example combining aperiodicity with Lyapunov instability on bounded orbits, advancing the dynamical classification of entire symplectic automorphisms of $\mathbb{C}^2$.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: For any real Hénon map, does the closure of the set of periodic orbits support all the invariant probability measures?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that, for every real Hénon map, the closure of the set of periodic orbits supports all invariant probability measures.
why: A positive answer would show periodic orbits are dynamically dense enough to capture every invariant measure, giving a complete ergodic description of real Hénon maps from their periodic structure.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Do any two distinct kneading sequences of the Hénon map $H_{a,b}$, with $(a,b)$ in the specified parameter region ${WY}$, uniquely determine the pair of parameters $(a,b)$, and thereby govern all the other kneading sequences in ${K}$ of $H_{a,b}$?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that two distinct kneading sequences of $H_{a,b}$ determine a unique parameter pair $(a,b) \in {WY}$ and control the remaining kneading sequences in ${K}$.
why: It would give a symbolic-dynamics parametrization of Hénon maps in this regime, tying kneading data to the underlying dynamics. The problem comes from a curated open-problems list, so it marks a recognized gap in the area.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: Does the map $H_2$ have a Herman ring? That is, does this specific map admit an invariant annulus on which it is conjugate to an irrational rotation?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2023), http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi).
solved_when: A proof or disproof that $H_2$ has a Herman ring.
why: Resolving it settles a concrete case in the curated open-problems list of Berger, Bedford, and Bianchi concerning the existence of Herman rings for explicit maps.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems — question Q18
open: If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, must the Julia set satisfy $J = J^*$?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that $J = J^*$ holds for every quasi-hyperbolic $f$.
why: This is question Q18 of a curated list of open problems in complex dynamics; settling it would clarify the structure of Julia sets for quasi-hyperbolic maps.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems — question Q19
open: If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, can it have a wandering Fatou component? In other words, does quasi-hyperbolicity of $f$ preclude wandering Fatou components?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2023), a curated list of open problems by Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, and Fabrizio Bianchi (arXiv:2312.03907v1).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that a quasi-hyperbolic map $f$ has no wandering Fatou component.
why: Resolving it would clarify how quasi-hyperbolic dynamics constrains the global orbit structure of the Fatou set, a basic structural question in complex dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: a list of open problems
open: What is the growth type of the sequence of iterates $\{f^n\}$ for an arbitrary polynomial automorphism $f$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$ with $d \geq 3$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2023), arXiv:2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi).
solved_when: A characterization of the growth type of $\{f^n\}$ is given for every polynomial automorphism $f$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$ in dimension $d \geq 3$.
why: It extends the dynamical classification known in low dimensions to the general higher-dimensional setting, completing our picture of the asymptotic behavior of polynomial automorphisms.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03907v1 (Pierre Berger, Eric Bedford, Fabrizio Bianchi)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024
open: Does every positive multiple of 4 occur as the order of a Hadamard matrix? Formally, for every positive $n$ divisible by $4$, does an $n \times n$ Hadamard matrix exist?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2504.20539v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Anastasia Kireeva, Antoine Maillard).
solved_when: A construction (or existence proof) of an $n \times n$ Hadamard matrix is given for every positive $n$ with $4 \mid n$, or a counterexample order is exhibited.
why: It is the long-standing Hadamard conjecture; resolving it would complete the classification of maximally efficient orthogonal designs used in coding theory, combinatorial design, and signal processing.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20539v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Anastasia Kireeva, Antoine Maillard)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024
open: Consider the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass with an arbitrary external field. Does Glauber dynamics mix rapidly — in time polynomial in the system size — at all temperatures up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold α = 1?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025) by Afonso S. Bandeira, Anastasia Kireeva, and Antoine Maillard, "Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024," http://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20539v1 (openproblem 14).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that Glauber dynamics on the SK model with an arbitrary external field mixes in polynomial time for all parameters below the replica symmetry breaking threshold α = 1, or a construction showing exponential slowdown at some point in that regime.
why: Rapid mixing up to the RSB threshold would confirm that equilibrium spin-glass structure at low — but not yet glassy — temperature is computationally accessible, while a negative answer would reveal a computational-to-structural gap driven by the external field.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20539v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Anastasia Kireeva, Antoine Maillard)

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar — problem p7
open: If a compact embedded constant mean curvature surface spans two coaxial circles lying in parallel planes, must it be a surface of revolution? Equivalently, is rotational symmetry forced by this symmetric boundary data?
solved_when: A proof that every compact embedded cmc surface spanning two coaxial circles in parallel planes is a surface of revolution, or an explicit counterexample of such a surface that is not rotationally symmetric.
why: It is the natural analogue, for two boundary components, of the classical question of whether embedded cmc surfaces spanning a single circle are spherical caps; a positive answer would extend the known rigidity of symmetric boundaries to the annular case.

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar
open: Let $H=0$ and let $\Sigma$ be a compact $H$-surface spanning a circle $\mathbb{S}^1(r)$. If $\Sigma$ is included in the slab $\mathbb{S}_w$, with $|H| < \frac{2}{w}$, is $\Sigma$ a spherical cap? And if we replace $\frac{2}{w}$ by $w\sqrt{1/w}$, is $\Sigma$ a small spherical cap?
solved_when: For a compact $H$-surface spanning the circle $\mathbb{S}^1(r)$ and contained in the slab $\mathbb{S}_w$, it is proved that the surface is a spherical cap whenever $|H| < \frac{2}{w}$; and that it is a small spherical cap under the sharper bound obtained by replacing $\frac{2}{w}$ with $w\sqrt{1/w}$.
why: These questions extend the classical capillarity theory of compact constant mean curvature surfaces spanning a circular boundary, determining how slab width controls the shape and size of the solutions.

title: on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundar
open: Let $C_1, C_2$ be two simple planar convex curves with disjoint interiors. Does there exist a constant $V_0 > 0$ such that any compact constant mean curvature surface with boundary $C_1 \cup C_2$ and volume $V < V_0$ must be disconnected?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given of the existence of such a threshold $V_0 > 0$ for every pair of simple planar convex curves with disjoint interiors: for all cmc surfaces spanning $C_1 \cup C_2$ with volume $V < V_0$, the surface is not connected.
why: It would establish a small-volume connectivity threshold for cmc surfaces spanning two convex boundary curves, constraining the topology of solutions in the Plateau-type problem with two boundary components.

title: in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
open: If $G$ is an oligomorphic group, must its outer automorphism group $Out(G)$ be profinite? In other words, does oligomorphy of $G$ impose enough compactness on automorphisms-mod-inner to force $Out(G)$ to carry a profinite topology?
solved_when: A proof that $Out(G)$ is profinite for every oligomorphic group $G$, or a counterexample: an oligomorphic group $G$ whose outer automorphism group fails to be profinite.
why: It clarifies the structural constraints that oligomorphy places on automorphism groups, connecting computability-theoretic and descriptive-set-theoretic questions about these groups to profinite rigidity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03972v1 (George Barmpalias, Nikolay Bazhenov, Chi Tat Chong)

title: in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
open: Every degree of decidable categoricity is a degree of categoricity. Is the converse true — is every degree of categoricity also a degree of decidable categoricity?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, settling whether the class of degrees of categoricity coincides with the class of degrees of decidable categoricity.

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: Must every Gâteaux differentiability space also be a weak Asplund space? In other words, does the existence of Gâteaux differentiability bumps or norms on a Banach space guarantee the stronger property that every continuous convex function on it is Gâteaux differentiable on a dense set?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2510.26827v4 (Shaoqiang Shang).
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) that every Gâteaux differentiability space is a weak Asplund space is given.
why: It would clarify the hierarchy between Gâteaux differentiability spaces and weak Asplund spaces, a basic structural question in the geometry of Banach spaces concerning how weak differentiability guarantees propagate.

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: If $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $M$ is a closed subspace of $X$, must $M$ itself be a weak Asplund space?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2510.26827v4 (Shaoqiang Shang).
solved_when: A proof that every closed subspace of a weak Asplund space is weak Asplund, or a counterexample exhibiting a weak Asplund space with a closed subspace that fails the property.
why: It tests whether weak Asplundness is a hereditary property, which determines how robust the class is under basic Banach-space operations and whether results about a space can be transferred to its subspaces.

title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a w
open: Let $X$ be a weak Asplund space. Must $X \times l^{p}$ be a weak Asplund space?
solved_when: A proof that the product of any weak Asplund space $X$ with $l^{p}$ is again weak Asplund, or a counterexample exhibiting a weak Asplund space whose product with $l^{p}$ fails to be weak Asplund.
why: It would clarify how weak Asplundability behaves under products, even with the simplest infinite-dimensional factors, a basic stability question in the structure theory of weak Asplund spaces.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: What is the topological type of the achievement set $E(x_n)$ for the sequence $x_n := \frac{1}{2^n} + \frac{(-1)^n}{3^n}$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1 (Szymon Głąb, Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski).
solved_when: The topological type of this particular achievement set $E(x_n)$ is determined.
why: This concrete sequence probes the boundary between the known topological types of achievement sets, so resolving it advances the classification program for achievement sets of fast-decreasing sequences.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Does there exist a sequence $(x_n)$ such that the ratio $\frac{x_{n+1}}{x_n}$ exists and the achievement set $E(x_n)$ is a Cantorval?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1 (Szymon Głąb, Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski).
solved_when: An explicit example of such a sequence is constructed, or the nonexistence of any such sequence is proved.
