title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Given a positive sequence $(x_n)$ with a strictly larger companion sequence $r_n > x_n$ for every $n$, must there exist a subsequence $(x_{n_k})$ whose achievement set $E(x_{n_k})$ is a Cantorval?
solved_when: A proof that such a subsequence always exists, or a counterexample sequence $(x_n)$ with corresponding $r_n > x_n$ admitting no subsequence whose achievement set is a Cantorval.
why: It would clarify how flexibly achievement sets can be steered toward Cantorvals by subsequence selection, a central structural question in the theory of achievement sets of series.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Given any achievable Cantor set $C$, must there exist achievable Cantor sets $C'$ and $C''$ such that the sum $C + C'$ is again a Cantor set while the sum $C + C''$ is a Cantorval?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), namely arXiv:2512.17285v1 by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski, "Achievement sets — current results and open problems" (problem 10).
solved_when: A proof that for every achievable Cantor set $C$ such sets $C'$ and $C''$ exist, or a counterexample — an achievable Cantor set $C$ for which no such $C'$ or $C''$ exists.
why: It would clarify how flexible the arithmetic of achievable Cantor sets is under Minkowski sums, showing whether each such set can be made to sum to either a Cantor set or a Cantorval by suitable choice of achievable partner.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Does every achievable Cantor set $C$ admit achievable Cantorvals $D'$ and $D''$ such that $C + D'$ is a Cantorval while $C + D''$ is an interval? In other words, can the sum of an achievable Cantor set with suitably chosen achievable Cantorvals realize both of these fundamentally different outcomes?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), "Achievement sets — current results and open problems" by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski (arXiv:2512.17285v1), where it appears as problem 11.
solved_when: An answer is provided: either, for every achievable Cantor set $C$, achievable Cantorvals $D'$ and $D''$ are constructed with $C + D'$ a Cantorval and $C + D''$ an interval, or an achievable Cantor set is exhibited for which no such pair exists.
why: It would clarify how Minkowski sums of achievement sets behave at the boundary between Cantorvals and intervals, a key structural question in the theory of achievement sets of subsum-type series.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Can the constant $3$ appearing in the first implication of the achievement-set results be replaced by a strictly smaller number?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), the curated open-problems paper 2512.17285 by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski (http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1); no progress beyond the question is recorded.
solved_when: An explicit constant strictly smaller than $3$ is shown to suffice in the first implication, or it is proved that $3$ is optimal.
why: Sharpening the constant tightens the quantitative link between the conditions in the implication, directly refining the known structure theory of achievement sets.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Is the Palis dichotomy generically true for central Cantor sets — that is, does a generic central Cantor set either have an achievement set that is a finite union of closed intervals, or have a nonempty interior, with no generic exceptions in between?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2512.17285v1, by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski (http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285v1).
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) establishing that the Palis dichotomy holds — or fails — for generic central Cantor sets, per the formulation of the source problem.
why: Resolving it would settle a basic structural question about how sums of subseries behave for the classical family of Cantor sets, sharpening the boundary of the dichotomy in fractal geometry.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Is every achievable Cantorval standard? In other words, does every Cantorval that arises as an achievement set share the structure of the classical (standard) Cantorval, or can an achievement set produce a Cantorval of some genuinely different, non-standard kind?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper "Achievement sets -- current results and open problems" (2025), arXiv:2512.17285v1, by Szymon Głąb and Franciszek Prus-Wiśniowski.
solved_when: A proof that every achievable Cantorval is standard, or an explicit construction of an achievable Cantorval that is not standard.
why: It would settle the basic structural classification question for Cantorvals arising as achievement sets, determining whether the known standard model exhausts the possibilities.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: If \(E \subset \mathbb{R}^2\) is an achievable set, must every vertical section \(E_x\) be a set of \(P\)-sums?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every vertical section of every achievable set in the plane is a set of \(P\)-sums, for the classes of sets and summation notions considered in the source paper.
why: It would clarify how the achievement operation interacts with taking sections, a basic structural question about achievable sets that is currently unknown.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Given an arbitrary compact subset C of [0, ∞), can it be realized as the set of all possible sums of subseries of some sequence — that is, does there exist a compact set K of real numbers (necessarily an achievement set of a positive series) whose achievement set E(K) equals C?
solved_when: A construction is given that, for every compact C ⊆ [0, ∞), produces a compact K ⊆ ℝ with E(K) = C; or a proof that some compact C ⊆ [0, ∞) is not the achievement set of any compact set.
why: It would characterize exactly which compact sets arise as achievement sets, settling a basic realization question in the structure theory of subseries sums.

title: Achievement sets -- current results and open problems
open: Do there exist fast convergent sequences \((x_n)\) such that the adjoint Cantorval \( {E(x_n)}\) is achievable? In other words, can a sequence whose terms shrink so rapidly that its achievement set has Cantorval-type structure still be realized as an achievement set?
solved_when: An explicit fast convergent sequence \((x_n)\) is produced for which the adjoint set \( {E(x_n)}\) is achievable, or a proof is given that no such sequence exists.
why: Resolving it would clarify how convergence speed constrains the topological structure of achievement sets, a central theme in this corner of fractal/descriptive set theory.

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory — problem problem1
open: For a fixed forbidden family $\mathcal{F}$ and a fixed number of edges, which graph maximizes the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix among all $\mathcal{F}$-free graphs with $m$ edges, and what does that extremal graph look like?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), the survey arXiv:2512.19395v1 by Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, and Minjie Zhang.
solved_when: A formula (or sharp bounds) for the maximum spectral radius over $\mathcal{G}(m, \mathcal{F})$ is established, together with a characterization of the extremal graphs attaining it, for the families $\mathcal{F}$ treated in the source paper.
why: A resolution would extend classical edge-extremal (Turán-type) results to the spectral setting, where the spectral radius can detect structure that edge counts alone miss, and would pin down the exact extremal graphs rather than just the extremal value.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory — problem pb001
open: Which graph, among all non-bipartite graphs containing no triangle and having exactly $m$ edges (with $m$ even), achieves the maximum spectral radius, and what is that graph? Formally, determine the extremal $C_3$-free non-bipartite graph on $m$ edges maximizing the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), a survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems: arXiv:2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang). No extremal graph is known for the even-$m$ case.
solved_when: The extremal graph is identified (and its structure described) for every even $m$, with a proof that it attains the maximum spectral radius over all $C_3$-free non-bipartite graphs with $m$ edges.
why: It resolves a representative case of the edge-spectral-Turán program, where spectral extremal questions are posed with the edge count, rather than the vertex count, as the fixed resource.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory — problem pb3
open: For even $m$, which $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free non-bipartite graph with $m$ edges maximizes the spectral radius?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2025), arXiv:2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An explicit extremal graph is identified for even $m$ among all $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free non-bipartite graphs with $m$ edges, with a proof that its spectral radius is maximum.
why: It completes the edge-spectral-Turán picture for $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free non-bipartite graphs, resolving the natural extremal question left open by the survey.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory — problem pb:5.3
open: Among all non-$r$-partite $K_{r+1}$-free graphs with $m$ edges, which graph attains the maximal spectral radius? Formally, for every $r \ge 3$ and every positive integer $m = ar + b$, where $a$ is a non-negative integer and $1 \le b \le r$, determine the extremal graph with maximal spectral radius over all non-$r$-partite $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on $m$ edges.
solved_when: For every $r \ge 3$ and every $m = ar + b$ with $a$ a non-negative integer and $1 \le b \le r$, the extremal non-$r$-partite $K_{r+1}$-free graph maximizing the spectral radius is explicitly identified.
why: It would complete the edge-spectral-Turán picture for graphs just beyond the Turán threshold, showing exactly how a minimal departure from $r$-partiteness raises the spectral radius.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory — conjecture conj:5.2
open: For integers $k \ge 1$, $r \ge 3$, and sufficiently large $m$, is it true that every graph $G \in \mathcal{G}(m, B_{r,k+1})$ satisfies $\rho(G) \le 2m(r-1)/r$? Moreover, does equality hold if and only if $G$ is a complete regular $r$-partite graph?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the bound $\rho(G) \le 2m(r-1)/r$ for all $G \in \mathcal{G}(m, B_{r,k+1})$ with $k \ge 1$, $r \ge 3$, and sufficiently large $m$, together with the characterization of the equality cases as exactly the complete regular $r$-partite graphs.
why: It settles a spectral extremal question of edge-spectral-Turán type, extending the classical Turán structure to the spectral radius setting and identifying the extremal graphs precisely.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: A survey of edge-spectral-Turán type problems in spectral graph theory — problem pb:5.2
open: Given a color-critical graph \( F \) with \( \chi(F)=r+1 \), which graphs attain the maximum spectral radius among all \( F \)-free graphs with a fixed number \( m \) of edges? A precise determination of these extremal graphs is the goal.
solved_when: The extremal \( F \)-free graphs on \( m \) edges maximizing the spectral radius are explicitly determined for every color-critical graph \( F \) with chromatic number \( r+1 \).
why: It identifies the exact spectral extremal structure in edge-spectral-Turán problems, extending classical Turán-type extremal results to the spectral setting.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19395v1 (Yuantian Yu, Huihui Zhang, Minjie Zhang)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Gr — problem 1 1
open: If a graph $G$ fails to be graceful, must its line graph $L(G)$ nevertheless be graceful? Equivalently, does nongracefulness of a graph imply gracefulness of its line graph?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Graph Theory" (Adithya Kulkarni, Mohna Chakraborty, Jay Bagga), http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05059v1.
solved_when: A proof that every nongraceful graph has a graceful line graph, or an explicit counterexample of a nongraceful $G$ whose $L(G)$ is also nongraceful.
why: It would extend the reach of graceful labeling from a graph to a natural derived class, clarifying how gracefulness behaves under the line-graph operation.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05059v1 (Adithya Kulkarni, Mohna Chakraborty, Jay Bagga)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Gr — problem 1 3
open: If a graph $G$ fails to be graceful, must its line graph $L(G)$ nevertheless be graceful? In other words, does taking the line graph always supply a graceful labeling whenever the original graph admits none?
solved_when: A proof that for every nongraceful graph $G$, the line graph $L(G)$ is graceful; or an explicit example of a nongraceful $G$ whose line graph is also nongraceful.
why: It would reveal whether gracefulness is recovered under the line-graph operation, constraining the boundary between graceful and nongraceful graphs in a structural way.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05059v1 (Adithya Kulkarni, Mohna Chakraborty, Jay Bagga)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Gr — problem 2 5
open: If the line graph $L(G)$ of a graph $G$ admits a graceful labeling, must $G$ itself be graceful? A positive answer would show that gracefulness is inherited downward from line graphs, a natural converse direction in the study of graceful labelings.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Gr" (Adithya Kulkarni, Mohna Chakraborty, Jay Bagga), http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05059v1.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given: either every graph $G$ whose line graph $L(G)$ is graceful is itself graceful, or a specific $G$ is exhibited with $L(G)$ graceful but $G$ not graceful.
why: It would settle a basic structural question about how graceful labelings behave under the line-graph operator, clarifying which graphs are graceful and informing the broader program around Ringel–Kotzig-type labeling questions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05059v1 (Adithya Kulkarni, Mohna Chakraborty, Jay Bagga)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Solved and Unsolved Problems in Gr — problem 2 6
open: Does gracefulness of a line graph force gracefulness of the underlying graph? Formally, since the line graph operator loses information — nonisomorphic graphs can share the same line graph, and structural properties of $L(G)$ do not uniquely determine labeling properties of $G$ — the question is whether a general structural theorem can lift graceful labelings from $L(G)$ back to $G$, or whether a counterexample family exists instead.
solved_when: Either a general structural theorem lifting graceful labelings from $L(G)$ to $G$ is proved, or an explicit counterexample family of graphs for which the implication fails is constructed.
why: The reverse implication is the obstruction: techniques that work for forward implications do not transfer, so resolving it settles whether line graph structure preserves graceful-labeling behavior at all.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05059v1 (Adithya Kulkarni, Mohna Chakraborty, Jay Bagga)

title: Linear Systems and Eigenvalue Problems: Open Questions from a Simons W — problem problem46
open: Is the nuclear Nyström approximation error submodular when the matrix $L$ is SDDM and positive-definite, or when it is merely SDD and positive-definite? In other words, determine whether the submodularity property, established under the assumptions discussed in the source, extends to these broader classes of diagonally dominant matrices.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Linear Systems and Eigenvalue Problems: Open Questions from a Simons W" (arXiv:2602.05394v3, by Noah Amsel, Yves Baumann, Paul Beckman); no case is resolved.
solved_when: A proof or counterexample is given for the submodularity of the nuclear Nyström error under (a) SDDM positive-definite $L$, and separately under (b) SDD positive-definite $L$.
why: Submodularity would justify greedy column-selection schemes for nuclear Nyström approximations with provable guarantees on these widely used matrix classes; a counterexample would show such guarantees cannot be obtained this way.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05394v3 (Noah Amsel, Yves Baumann, Paul Beckman)

title: Linear Systems and Eigenvalue Problems: Open Questions from a Simons W
open: Let $p^*$ be a minimizer of the analogue in which the approximation error is measured in the $L^2$-norm. Does $p^*(x) - \mathrm{sign}(x)$ satisfy the equioscillation property?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $p^*(x) - \mathrm{sign}(x)$ satisfies the equioscillation property for the $L^2$-norm analogue.
why: It would clarify whether the classical equioscillation characterization extends from the $L^\infty$ setting to the $L^2$-norm minimizer, a basic structural question about best approximation of the sign function.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05394v3 (Noah Amsel, Yves Baumann, Paul Beckman)

title: Linear Systems and Eigenvalue Problems: Open Questions from a Simons W
open: What is the true bit complexity of solving an $n \times n$ linear system with $nnz(A)$ non-zeros? In particular, can the $O(n \cdot nnz(A))$ runtime be extended to the Word-RAM model?
solved_when: An algorithm (or lower-bound matching the $O(n \cdot nnz(A))$ bound) for solving such linear systems is given in the Word-RAM model, with the full bit-complexity accounting made explicit.
why: It settles whether the known sparsity-sensitive runtime is robust to realistic machine models or an artifact of a more permissive cost model, directly informing what can be claimed about practical solvers.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05394v3 (Noah Amsel, Yves Baumann, Paul Beckman)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
open: Is there a degree-4 Sum-of-Squares proof that no seven Mutually Unbiased Bases exist in $\mathbb{C}^6$? More precisely, can the nonexistence of $7$ MUBs in dimension $6$ be certified by a degree-$4$ SOS certificate?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025," available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29571v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Daniil Dmitriev, Kevin Lucca). No prior results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An explicit Sum-of-Squares degree $4$ refutation exists (or a proof that none exists) for the assertion that $7$ Mutually Unbiased Bases exist in $\mathbb{C}^6$.
why: Dimension $6$ is the smallest case where the existence of a complete set of Mutually Unbiased Bases is unresolved, and a low-degree SOS certificate would give the first rigorous computational evidence against it — or reveal the limits of the semidefinite hierarchy on a flagship quantum-information instance.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29571v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Daniil Dmitriev, Kevin Lucca)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
open: Can we prove that seven mutually unbiased bases cannot exist in dimension six — that is, that the largest number of simultaneously mutually unbiased bases in $\mathbb{C}^6$ is strictly less than seven, $\mathrm{MUB}(6)<7$?
status: Stated as an open conjecture (conjecture 5) in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2603.29571v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Daniil Dmitriev, Kevin Lucca).
solved_when: A rigorous proof (or disproof) of the inequality $\mathrm{MUB}(6)<7$ establishing the exact impossibility of a complete set of 7 MUBs in $\mathbb{C}^6$.
why: This is the smallest dimension where the maximal number of MUBs is unknown, resolving a basic open case of the general MUB existence question central to quantum information.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29571v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Daniil Dmitriev, Kevin Lucca)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
open: Does every dimension admit a complex equiangular tight frame of maximal redundancy — that is, for each $d$, is there an ETF in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with exactly $n = d^2$ vectors?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2603.29571v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Daniil Dmitriev, Kevin Lucca). No further progress is recorded.
solved_when: A construction (or existence proof) of an ETF in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with $n = d^2$ vectors is given for every dimension $d$, or the conjecture is refuted by exhibiting a $d$ for which no such frame exists.
why: Complex ETFs with $n = d^2$ vectors sit at the Gerzon maximum for complex equiangular lines, so a resolution either supplies a powerful family of optimal tight frames for applications such as compressed sensing and quantum information, or reveals a fundamental obstruction to achieving maximal equiangularity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29571v1 (Afonso S. Bandeira, Daniil Dmitriev, Kevin Lucca)

title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025
open: Can a generic system of phaseless quadratic measurements recover every signal? Formally, let $N=4M-5$ and let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{N\times M}$ be drawn so that $\operatorname{im}(A)$ is a uniformly random point of the Grassmannian of $M$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{C}^{4M-5}$ (e.g., via iid Gaussian entries): is the probability $p_M$ that the mapping $x\mapsto |Ax|^2$ is injective positive — indeed, what is $p_M$?
solved_when: The value (or positivity) of $p_M$ is determined for $N=4M-5$, i.e., a proof of whether the intensity mapping $x\mapsto|Ax|^2$ is injective for generic measurement vectors in this dimension.

title: Separating Geometric and Algorithmic Compression via Cay
open: Can Cayley-table completion be made into a rigorous theorem — that is, can we prove that the global minimizer of the flatness-regularized empirical loss exactly recovers a finite group's multiplication table with high probability from only $O(n\log n)$ uniformly sampled entries? Since finite groups give linearly full-rank matrices ($r=n$), standard matrix completion theory only yields vacuous bounds exceeding $O(n^2)$, so new ideas are needed; such a theorem would give the first rigorous proof of the geometric-versus-algorithmic compression separation demanded in the source paper's Open Problem 1.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2605.29885v1 (Dongsung Huh).
solved_when: A formal exact-recovery guarantee is established: with high probability over $O(n\log n)$ uniformly sampled entries, the global minimizer of the flatness-regularized empirical loss perfectly completes the $n \times n$ group table.
why: It would be the first rigorous mathematical proof of the separation between geometric and algorithmic compression demanded in Open Problem 1, with Cayley-table completion as the concrete testbed.

title: Non-degeneracy of Killing forms on real conjugacy classes of finite gr — conjecture conj:non-degeneracy

solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every non-trivial real conjugacy class of every finite non-abelian simple group, the Killing form restricted to the class is non-degenerate.
why: The conjecture governs a basic structural invariant of real conjugacy classes in finite simple groups; resolving it settles non-degeneracy of Killing forms in this setting.

A precise determination of this extremal density, or tight bounds matching the conjectured value, is sought.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León).
solved_when: The inducibility of $F_{29}$ is determined exactly, with matching upper and lower constructions.
why: The inducibility of small graphs is a basic extremal-combinatorics quantity, and completing the 6-vertex case settles part of a curated list of open problems in the area.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León)

title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs — conjecture conj:34
open: What is the maximum possible density of induced copies of the 6-vertex graph $F_{34} := (6, \{01, 02, 03, 04, 12, 15\})$ in a large host graph? Formally, determine the exact inducibility of $F_{34}$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León). No value for the inducibility of $F_{34}$ is given there.
solved_when: The inducibility of $F_{34}$ — the limit of the maximum induced-density of $F_{34}$ over all host graphs on $n$ vertices as $n \to \infty$ — is determined exactly, with the extremal construction identified and proven optimal.
why: Inducibility of small graphs is a basic extremal quantity; resolving it completes the census of 6-vertex graphs and sharpens our understanding of how induced subgraph densities are maximized.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León)

title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs — conjecture conj:43
open: What is the inducibility of the 6-vertex graph $F_{43} := (6, \{01, 02, 05, 13, 15, 45\})$ — that is, the maximum possible density of induced copies of this fixed graph in arbitrarily large host graphs?
solved_when: The exact value of the inducibility of $F_{43}$ is determined, via a matching construction and an upper-bound proof.
why: It would complete the determination of inducibility values for 6-vertex graphs, a basic case in extremal graph theory where inducibility is known only for small orders.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León)

title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs — conjecture conj:51
open: What is the inducibility of the 6-vertex graph $F_{51} := (6, \{02, 04, 12, 13, 35, 45\})$? That is, determine the maximum limiting density of induced copies of this graph in arbitrarily large host graphs.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), a curated open-problems paper: arXiv:2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León). No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: The exact value of the inducibility of $F_{51}$ is determined (together with extremal constructions attaining it).
why: It completes the census of inducibility values for 6-vertex graphs, a basic case of the general inducibility program that is still largely uncharted.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León)

title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs — conjecture conj:62
open: What is the maximum possible density of induced copies of the 6-vertex graph $F_{62} := (6, \{01, 03, 04, 05, 12, 13, 45\})$ in arbitrarily large host graphs? Formally, determine the inducibility $I(F_{62})$, i.e. the limit supremum of the proportion of induced 6-subsets spanning a copy of $F_{62}$.
solved_when: The exact value of $I(F_{62})$ is determined (with a matching construction attaining it), or a proof that no such limit value exists is given if that is the outcome.
why: Resolving it completes the inducibility classification for a specific outstanding 6-vertex graph left open in a curated open-problems list, extending the extremal theory of small induced subgraphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00290v3 (Levente Bodnár, Jun Gao, Jared León)

title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs — conjecture conj:67
open: What is the inducibility of the 6-vertex graph $F_{67} := (6, \{02, 03, 05, 12, 14, 15, 45\})$ — the maximum density of induced copies of this graph attainable in arbitrarily large host graphs?
solved_when: The exact value of the inducibility of $F_{67}$ is determined, together with a proof that it is achieved (or approached) by a limiting construction.

title: Hardness of Approximate Hylland-Zeckhauser Equilibria
open: Is it NP-hard, even approximately, to find allocations in the Hylland–Zeckhauser model that are simultaneously relaxed Pareto optimal and envy-free? Formally, are there constants ε, δ, ε′ > 0 for which there is a polynomial-time reduction from the Gap(ε, δ)-Pareto problem to the problem of finding an ε′-relaxed Pareto Optimal + Envy Free allocation?
solved_when: Constants ε, δ, ε′ > 0 and a polynomial-time reduction from the Gap(ε, δ)-Pareto problem to finding an ε′-relaxed Pareto Optimal + Envy Free allocation are exhibited (or the existence of such constants is refuted).
why: It would establish the first hardness-of-approximation result for relaxed Pareto optimal plus envy-free allocations in the Hylland–Zeckhauser setting, delineating the limits of efficient algorithm design there.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00951v2 (Mark Braverman, Jingyi Liu, Eric Xue)

title: Recursive Jump Operators and Optimal Proof Systems
open: Does MATH — the set of propositional tautologies — admit an optimal proof system? In other words, is there a proof system for tautologies that p-simulates every other proof system?
status: Stated as one of the main open questions in proof complexity in the source paper (2026), "Recursive Jump Operators and Optimal Proof Systems" (http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01242v1, Fabian Egidy); no resolution is given there.
solved_when: A proof system for the propositional tautologies is exhibited (or shown not to exist) that simulates every other proof system for MATH.
why: An optimal proof system would give a canonical setting for propositional reasoning and would clarify the structural landscape of proof complexity; its nonexistence would show that no single system can dominate all others.

title: Recursive Jump Operators and Optimal Proof Systems
open: Does the existence of recursive jump operators imply the non-existence of optimal proof systems? Khaniki explicitly asked whether the existence of recursive jump operators is equivalent to the non-existence of optimal proof systems; the paper's main result contributes to this question.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given, in an unrelativized setting, that recursive jump operators exist if and only if optimal proof systems do not exist; in particular, resolving whether any relativizable proof technique can establish the implication.
why: The constructed oracle shows that no relativizable proof can establish the implication, so any resolution requires fundamentally new, non-relativizing techniques — directly advancing our understanding of the structure of optimal proof systems.

title: Jordan types for pairs of commuting nilpotent matrices: A survey
open: Which pairs of Jordan types can be realized by a pair of commuting nilpotent matrices? A complete characterization of commuting Jordan types remains the central open question in this area.
solved_when: An explicit, checkable characterization of all pairs of commuting Jordan types is given.
why: It would settle the basic structural question about commuting nilpotent pairs, completing recent progress on commuting Jordan types.

title: A Domatic Analogue of $χ$-Bounded Graph Classes and the Gyárfás-Sumner
open: For a fixed integer $t \geq 3$, must every graph of clique-width at most $t$ have their domination number bounded in terms of their clique number? In other words, is the class of graphs of clique-width at most $t$ DOM-bounded?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that, for every fixed $t \geq 3$, there is a function bounding the domination number by a function of the clique number alone for all graphs of clique-width at most $t$.
why: It would extend the $\chi$-boundedness program to a domatic analogue, testing whether Gyárfás–Sumner-type phenomena survive under clique-width restrictions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02030v1 (Quentin Chuet, Selma Djelloul, Hoang La)

title: Band bases as common triangular bases in cluster algebras from surface — conj conj:band-is-triangular
open: Is the (quantized) band basis, after localizing at the frozen variables, the common triangular basis of the skein algebra? In other words, does the band basis of a cluster algebra from a surface coincide with the common triangular basis once frozen variables are inverted?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the quantized band basis equals the common triangular basis of the skein algebra localized at the frozen variables.
why: It would identify an explicitly computable, geometrically natural basis of surface-type cluster algebras with the powerful structural basis of the triangular-bases framework, transferring triangular-basis machinery to skein algebras.

title: Quantum-Classical Equivalence for AND-Functions
open: For every total Boolean function, do the bounded-error quantum and randomized query complexities coincide up to the same asymptotic behavior? In other words, is there no total Boolean function for which a quantum algorithm achieves a polynomial — or even super-constant — speedup over the best randomized algorithm in the query model?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.03249v1 (Sreejata Kishor Bhattacharya, Farzan Byramji, Arkadev Chattopadhyay). No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the conjecture as stated in the source paper, showing that for every total Boolean function the bounded-error quantum query complexity and randomized query complexity are asymptotically equal.
why: A proof would establish a sweeping equivalence between quantum and classical computation for all total Boolean functions, showing quantum query algorithms offer no advantage in this broad setting; a refutation would exhibit a total function with a genuine quantum speedup.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03249v1 (Sreejata Kishor Bhattacharya, Farzan Byramji, Arkadev Chattopadhyay)

title: On the maximum size of $(a,b)$-town (mod $k$) families — conjecture conj_ab
open: When the two parameters coincide, is the maximum size of an $(a,b)$-town (mod $k$) family exactly $n$? Formally, for integers $a,b,k,n$ with $n \ge k \ge 2$ and $0 \le a,b \le k-1$: if $a = b$, must $m_{k,n}(a,b) = n$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $m_{k,n}(a,b) = n$ whenever $a = b$, for all $n \ge k \ge 2$ and $0 \le a,b \le k-1$.
why: It pins down the extremal size of these modular town families in the diagonal case, a basic parameter for the theory introduced in the source paper.

title: Combinatorial and analytic aspects of independence polynomials of zero
open: Is the independence polynomial of the zero divisor graph of the ring $\mathbb{Z}_n$ always unimodal? That is, do the coefficients of this polynomial, counted by independent-set size, rise and then fall without oscillation?
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.04789v1 (Bilal Ahmad Rather).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) that for every $n$, the independence polynomial of the zero divisor graph of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is unimodal.
why: Unimodality of such graph polynomials is a structural property linking ring arithmetic to combinatorics of the associated zero divisor graph; settling it advances the combinatorial and analytic study of independence polynomials arising from rings.

title: Combinatorial and analytic aspects of independence polynomials of zero
open: Is the independence polynomial of the graph $Z_{pqr}$, built from primes $p<q<r$, always unimodal and log-concave? Formally, prove that $I(Z_{pqr},x)$ has coefficients that first rise and then fall, with no internal zeros, and whose consecutive terms satisfy the log-concavity inequality.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with an explicit counterexample) that $I(Z_{pqr},x)$ is unimodal and log-concave for all choices of primes $p<q<r$.
why: It resolves a concrete case of the general question of when independence polynomials inherit log-concavity, extending the combinatorial theory of such polynomials to this family of prime-parameterized graphs.

title: Tighter Bounds on the Degree-Truncated Choice Number of Planar Graphs — conjecture conj-1
open: Is every 3-connected non-complete planar graph degree-truncated 10-choosable? In the notation of the source paper, the conjecture is that the degree-truncated choice number of the class of planar graphs equals 10.
solved_when: A proof that every 3-connected non-complete planar graph is degree-truncated $10$-choosable, establishing $ch^{d}(P)=10$ (or a refutation showing the equality fails).
why: It pins down the exact degree-truncated choice number of planar graphs, sharpening the fine-grained interplay between local degree constraints and choosability in planarity beyond what ordinary choosability captures.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06216v1 (Huijuan Xu, Huan Zhou, Jialu Zhu)

title: Erdős-Hajnal conjecture beyond five-vertex graphs — conjecture conj:E-H
open: Does every graph $H$ obey the Erdős–Hajnal property — that is, for every graph $H$, is there a constant $c = c(H) > 0$ such that every $n$-vertex $H$-free graph contains a clique or a stable set of size at least $n^c$?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the conjecture as stated: for every graph $H$, exhibiting $c(H) > 0$ such that all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs have a clique or stable set of size at least $n^c$.
why: It asserts that excluding any single pattern forces much larger homogeneous sets than Ramsey's bound guarantees, a structural dichotomy central to understanding how forbidden subgraphs shape graph structure.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06258v3 (Shenwei Huang, Yiao Ju, Yidong Zhou)

title: Correlation inequalities for Schur positivity
open: Under what conditions does equality hold in the ADS inequality? A complete characterization appears difficult, since even the equality conditions for the closely related RLS inequality remain open.
status: Stated as an interesting and difficult open challenge in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06688v1 (Swee Hong Chan, Hong Chen, Igor Pak), which notes that equality conditions for the RLS inequality remain open.
solved_when: A full characterization of the equality cases of the ADS inequality is given.
why: Resolving it would sharpen a fundamental Schur-positivity correlation inequality from equality-blind to tight, and likely force progress on the still-open equality conditions for the RLS inequality.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06688v1 (Swee Hong Chan, Hong Chen, Igor Pak)

title: Correlation inequalities for Schur positivity
open: Can the supermodularity results for Grothendieck polynomials be extended to the skew setting, and can Speyer's Schur-positivity inequality be given a skew version? Sharpening this, is there a "four functions" analogue of Speyer's inequality, and does supermodularity (in Buch's definition of the polynomials) carry over to skew stable Grothendieck polynomials?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.06688v1 (Swee Hong Chan, Hong Chen, Igor Pak); no skew or four-functions version is known.
solved_when: A proof (or construction) of a skew version of Speyer's inequality and of supermodularity for skew (stable) Grothendieck polynomials under Buch's definition is given, ideally together with a four functions version of the inequality.
why: These correlation inequalities connect symmetric function theory with probabilistic and combinatorial positivity phenomena; a skew or four-functions extension would broaden the inequality's reach to a much wider class of symmetric functions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06688v1 (Swee Hong Chan, Hong Chen, Igor Pak)

title: Dirac subgraphs of powers of cycles are Hamiltonian — conjecture conj:mainconj
open: Is every Dirac-type spanning subgraph of a power of a cycle Hamiltonian? Formally, consider the Cayley graph on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with generating set $\{-k, 0, k\}$ and ask whether Dirac subgraphs of it must contain a Hamilton cycle.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.07471v1 (Richard Lang, Alp Müyesser, Mathias Schacht); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) of the conjecture conj:mainconj from the source paper is given.
why: It extends Hamiltonicity guarantees from the dense host graph itself to its Dirac-density spanning subgraphs, a natural robustness question for Hamiltonicity in circulant graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07471v1 (Richard Lang, Alp Müyesser, Mathias Schacht)

title: Dirac subgraphs of powers of cycles are Hamiltonian
open: Is it true that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a large enough $k$ such that, for any $n \ge k$, independently sampling each edge of the $k$-th power $C_n^k$ of the cycle with probability $n^{-\varepsilon}$ yields, with high probability, a graph in which every subgraph of minimum degree at least $(1/2+\varepsilon)$ of its order is Hamiltonian?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given of the statement: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $k$ such that for all $n \ge k$, the random subgraph of $C_n^k$ obtained by keeping each edge with probability $n^{-\varepsilon}$ has, with high probability, all of its $(1/2+\varepsilon)$-subgraphs Hamiltonian.
why: It would extend Dirac-type Hamiltonicity guarantees to sparse random subgraphs of cycle powers, bridging minimum-degree conditions and random sparsification in a structured host graph.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07471v1 (Richard Lang, Alp Müyesser, Mathias Schacht)

title: A closed subspace of a Gateaux differentiability space is a Gateaux di
open: Let $X$ be a Gâteaux differentiability space. Must every closed subspace of $X$ again be a Gâteaux differentiability space?
solved_when: A proof that closed subspaces of Gâteaux differentiability spaces are Gâteaux differentiability spaces, or a counterexample exhibiting a Gâteaux differentiability space with a closed subspace that fails the property.
why: It clarifies whether Gâteaux differentiability spaces form a hereditary class under closed subspaces, a basic structural question for the geometry of Banach spaces.

title: A closed subspace of a Gateaux differentiability space is a Gateaux di
open: If $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $M$ is a closed subspace of $X$, must $M$ also be a weak Asplund space? In other words, is the weak Asplund property inherited by closed subspaces?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08192v3 (Shaoqiang Shang). No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof that every closed subspace of a weak Asplund space is weak Asplund, or a counterexample exhibiting a weak Asplund space with a closed subspace failing the property.
why: Resolving it settles whether the class of weak Asplund spaces is stable under passing to closed subspaces, a basic structural question for the class analogous to known closure properties of Gateaux differentiability spaces subclasses.

title: A closed subspace of a Gateaux differentiability space is a Gateaux di
open: If $X$ is a Gâteaux differentiability space and $M$ is a closed subspace of $X$, must $M$ itself be a Gâteaux differentiability space?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08192v3 (Shaoqiang Shang).
solved_when: A proof that every closed subspace of a Gâteaux differentiability space is again a Gâteaux differentiability space, or a counterexample exhibiting a closed subspace that fails the property.
why: It tests whether Gâteaux differentiability spaces are stable under closed subspaces, a basic structural question about the class; resolving it clarifies the scope and closure properties of these spaces.

title: On the maximum and negative frustration indices of graphs — conjecture conjecture:multipartite
open: Is the complete multipartite graph $K_{n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}$ with $k \geq 3$, signed so that every edge is negative, an extremal graph for the frustration index? In other words, do these all-negative complete multipartite graphs attain the maximum frustration index among signings of their underlying graphs?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that complete multipartite graphs $K_{n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}$ with $k \geq 3$ signed all negative attain the maximum frustration index.
why: It would identify extremal signings for a natural graph family central to signed-graph theory, advancing the classification of graphs whose frustration index is maximized by the all-negative signing.

title: A Proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture
open: For which odd values of $n$ and which 2-regular graphs $F$ on $n$ vertices can the complete graph $K_n$ be decomposed into edge-disjoint copies of $F$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11178v1 (Michelle Delcourt, Luke Postle).
solved_when: A characterization is given of the odd integers $n$ and the 2-regular graphs $F$ on $n$ vertices for which $K_n$ admits a decomposition into edge-disjoint copies of $F$, together with a proof of its correctness.
why: It would settle the first question of the Nash-Williams conjecture treated in the source paper, resolving when such 2-factor decompositions of complete graphs exist.

title: A Proof of Nash-Williams' Conjecture
open: Given an odd integer $n$ and $(n-1)/2$ possibly distinct 2-regular graphs $F_1, \ldots, F_{(n-1)/2}$, each on $n$ vertices, when can the complete graph $K_n$ be decomposed into edge-disjoint copies of these factors? That is, for which odd $n$ and which choices of $F_1, \ldots, F_{(n-1)/2}$ does such a decomposition exist?
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the pairs $(n, F_1, \ldots, F_{(n-1)/2})$, with $n$ odd and each $F_i$ a 2-regular graph on $n$ vertices, for which $K_n$ decomposes into edge-disjoint copies of $F_1, \ldots, F_{(n-1)/2}$.
why: It would settle the natural generalization of Nash-Williams' conjecture to arbitrary 2-factors, extending decomposition results for Hamiltonian cycles to the full space of 2-regular spanning graphs.

title: Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs — question ques:LOCAL_shannon
open: Does there exist a randomized algorithm that, given an $n$-vertex multigraph $G$ of constant maximum degree $\Delta$, finds a proper $3/2$-edge-coloring of $G$ in time $o(n)$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher).
solved_when: Such a randomized algorithm is exhibited: on any $n$-vertex multigraph of constant maximum degree $\Delta$, it produces a proper $3/2$-edge-coloring in time $o(n)$.
why: A sublinear-time algorithm for a fractional-quality edge coloring would show that matchings and near-matchings can be computed without even reading the whole graph, pushing distributed/local algorithms techniques into the sublinear regime.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher)

title: Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs — question ques:LOCAL_matching
open: Does there exist a randomized algorithm that, given an $n$-vertex graph $G$ of constant maximum degree $\Delta$ with an unbalanced bipartition $(A,B)$, finds in time $o(n)$ a matching in $G$ that covers $A$? The implied constants in the $o(\cdot)$ notation may depend on $\Delta$.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher); no algorithm is known.
solved_when: Such a randomized algorithm is exhibited, running in $o(n)$ time on any $n$-vertex graph of constant maximum degree $\Delta$ with an unbalanced bipartition $(A,B)$, and producing a matching covering $A$ (with constants in the $o(\cdot)$ allowed to depend on $\Delta$).
why: It would settle whether local, sublinear-time algorithms can find perfect-like matchings in unbalanced bounded-degree bipartite graphs, a basic test case at the intersection of distributed/local computation and matching theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher)

title: Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs — question ques:meas_index_diff
open: Does there exist a Borel multigraph $G$ of finite maximum degree with a probability measure such that the measurable chromatic index-type quantity $\ '_ (G)$ exceeds $\ '(G)$ by more than 1? In other words, can the difference $\ '_ (G) - '(G)$ be made arbitrarily large?
solved_when: Either an example is produced with $\ '_ (G) > '(G) + 1$ (or arbitrarily large difference), or a proof is given that no such Borel multigraph of finite maximum degree with a probability measure exists.
why: It would show how far measurable edge-coloring parameters can diverge in unbalanced graphs, settling a basic gap question in the Borel combinatorics of matchings.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher)

title: Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs — question ques:paradox
open: For a Borel action of a group on a standard Borel space, must the type semigroup have the property that any plain paradox already forces a doubling paradox? Formally, if an element of $\mathcal{S}(X, \Gamma, \mathcal{B})$ satisfies $n\cdot m$ in $\mathcal{S}(X, \Gamma, \mathcal{B})$ for some $n > m$, must $2x$ hold as well?
solved_when: It is shown that for every Borel action on a standard Borel space, the type semigroup $\mathcal{S}(X, \Gamma, \mathcal{B})$ has plain paradoxes in the sense above, or a counterexample action is constructed for which $n\cdot m$ holds but $2x$ fails.
why: It would clarify when Borel equidecomposition paradoxes collapse to the strongest form, connecting measurable matching and type-semigroup structure for unbalanced Borel graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher)

title: Measurable matchings in unbalanced graphs — question ques:amenable_unp
open: If a finitely generated amenable group acts by Borel automorphisms on a standard Borel space $X$ with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{B}$, must the associated type semigroup $\mathcal{S}(X, \mathcal{B})$ be almost unperforated? More concretely: can "many small pieces" of a measurable set always be traded for "fewer large pieces" in the comparison order of the type semigroup?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, via an explicit amenable Borel action whose type semigroup fails almost unperforation) resolving the question as stated in the source paper is given.
why: Almost unperforation of the type semigroup governs the strength of measurable comparison and matching results for actions of amenable groups; settling it determines how far the theory of measurable matchings extends beyond the settings currently understood.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11558v2 (Anton Bernshteyn, Matt Bowen, Felix Weilacher)

title: Special Matchings, Brenti's Conjecture, and the Combinatorial Invarian — conj comb-inv-con
open: The Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $P_{u,v}(q)$ depends only on the isomorphism type of the interval $[u,v]$ as a partially ordered set under Bruhat order.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Fabrizio Caselli and Mario Marietti (http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11776v1).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the assertion that $P_{u,v}(q)$ is determined by the poset isomorphism type of the Bruhat interval $[u,v]$; success means either establishing this for all Coxeter groups and all intervals, or exhibiting an explicit pair of poset-isomorphic intervals with distinct Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials.
why: It would reduce the computation of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials to a purely order-theoretic, combinatorial problem, making them accessible to poset-isomorphism-invariant techniques (such as special matchings) rather than the full algebraic structure of the group.

title: Sparse Polynomial Divisibility Test over Finite Field is CoNP-hard — open problem 1 1
open: Given two polynomials $f, g$ over a field, both presented in sparse representation, how hard is it to decide whether $g$ divides $f$? In particular, is this divisibility test solvable in time polynomial in the sparse sizes of the inputs, or is it NP-hard?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.12130v1 (Yichuan Cao, Ruichen Qiu, Qiao-Long Huang).
solved_when: A resolution of the complexity of sparse divisibility testing over a field: either a polynomial-time algorithm (in the sparse representation sizes of $f$ and $g$) deciding divisibility, or a proof of NP-hardness for the problem.
why: Divisibility is a basic operation underlying sparse polynomial arithmetic and factorization, and knowing whether it can be done efficiently — or is intractable — determines which sparse-polynomial algorithms can be built on top of it.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12130v1 (Yichuan Cao, Ruichen Qiu, Qiao-Long Huang)

title: Output-sensitive Sparse Polynomial GCD over Finite Fields is NP-hard — open problem 1 1
open: Find an algorithm for computing $ (f,g)$ that is polynomial-time in $\|f\|_0$, $\|g\|_0$, and $\| (f,g)\|_0$.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12144v1 (Ruichen Qiu, Yichuan Cao, Qiao-Long Huang)

title: Cooling graph products
open: What is the complexity of cooling spiders? More precisely, one seeks a determination of the computational complexity of the cooling problem when the underlying graph is a spider (a tree with a single high-degree vertex).
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.12330v1 (Anthony Bonato, MacKenzie Carr, Caleb Jones).
solved_when: The complexity of cooling spiders is resolved — for example, by a polynomial-time algorithm or a hardness classification (with matching algorithm and lower bound) for spider inputs.
why: It settles a basic unresolved case within the cooling problem on graph products, delineating which graph classes make cooling tractable and which do not.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12330v1 (Anthony Bonato, MacKenzie Carr, Caleb Jones)

title: Monochromatic $k$ in a row — conjecture conj:D(k,Z2)
open: For every integer $k \geq 3$, is $D(k, \mathbb{Z}^2) < 1 - \frac{2}{k}$? That is, does this upper bound hold for the quantity $D(k, \mathbb{Z}^2)$ in the planar lattice?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the inequality $D(k, \mathbb{Z}^2) < 1 - \frac{2}{k}$ for every $k \geq 3$.
why: Resolving it settles conjecture conj:D(k,Z2), advancing understanding of monochromatic $k$-in-a-row configurations in the square lattice.

title: Monochromatic $k$ in a row — conjecture conj:[k]^d
open: Is the diagonal Ramsey-type density for a monochromatic run of length $k$ in the grid $[k]^d$ as low as it can plausibly be? The conjecture asserts that for every $k \geq 2$ and every $d$, $D(k,[k]^d) = 1 - \frac{2}{k}$.
solved_when: The conjecture is proved (or refuted): for every $k \geq 2$ and every $d$, it is established whether $D(k,[k]^d) = 1 - \frac{2}{k}$.
why: It pins down the exact threshold density forcing a monochromatic $k$-in-a-row in grid hypercubes, completing the density picture for this family of grids.

title: Generalised Prisms and Euclidean Ramsey Theory — conjecture conj:block
open: Given a template $T$ over $[m]$ and any number of colours $k$, must some high-dimensional grid $[m]^n$ contain a monochromatic block set of some degree $d$ with template $T$ under every $k$-colouring? Formally: for all positive integers $m, k$ and every template $T$ over $[m]$, do there exist positive integers $n$ and $d$ such that every $k$-colouring of $[m]^n$ yields a monochromatic block set of degree $d$ with template $T$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.13472v1 (Maria-Romina Ivan, Imre Leader, Mark Walters).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that for every $m$, $k$, and template $T$ over $[m]$ there exist positive integers $n$ and $d$ such that any $k$-colouring of $[m]^n$ contains a monochromatic block set of degree $d$ with template $T$.
why: It is a Euclidean Ramsey-type statement for generalised prisms; a positive answer would extend monochromatic-structure guarantees from simple grids to arbitrary templates, while a negative answer would exhibit templates that colourings can always avoid.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13472v1 (Maria-Romina Ivan, Imre Leader, Mark Walters)

title: Generalised Prisms and Euclidean Ramsey Theory — conjecture conj:onepoint
open: If $X$ is a Ramsey set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $z$ is a point in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ lying outside the hyperplane containing $X$, must the lifted set $X \cup \{z\}$ again be Ramsey? Formally, the conjecture asserts that adjoining such an off-hyperplane point to a Ramsey configuration always preserves the Ramsey property.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Generalised Prisms and Euclidean Ramsey Theory" by Maria-Romina Ivan, Imre Leader, and Mark Walters, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13472v1.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $X \cup \{z\}$ is Ramsey for every Ramsey set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and every $z \in \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ not in the hyperplane spanned by $X$.
why: The conjecture is a basic structural closure property of Ramsey sets in Euclidean Ramsey theory: it would show that a single point can always be lifted out of the ambient hyperplane while keeping the configuration Ramsey, a natural step toward classifying which finite configurations are Ramsey.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13472v1 (Maria-Romina Ivan, Imre Leader, Mark Walters)

title: Degree-Four Vector-Coordinate SoS Cannot Detect the MUB Upper Bound
open: Is it true that no degree-four Sum-of-Squares certificate can establish the non-existence of seven mutually unbiased bases? Specifically, in the vector-coordinate quartic equality formulation described in Randomstrasse101 Open Problem 23, does no degree-four Sum-of-Squares proof exist that seven mutually unbiased bases do not exist?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.13903v1 (Shreyhaan Sarkar).
solved_when: A rigorous argument is given showing that the degree-four Sum-of-Squares relaxation of the vector-coordinate quartic equality formulation admits no refutation of the existence of seven mutually unbiased bases (or, conversely, such a proof is exhibited, resolving the stated expectation).
why: It would delineate the power of low-degree Sum-of-Squares reasoning for a central feasibility question in quantum information, indicating whether stronger relaxations are needed to certify MUB non-existence bounds.

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — conj 1
open: Is the ideal $I_M$ generated in degree two? Formally: does $I_M$ admit a generating set consisting entirely of homogeneous elements of degree two?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $I_M$ is generated in degree two.
why: It settles the first conjecture in a line of inquiry showing the Gröbner version of White's conjecture is false, clarifying which quadratic-generation properties survive in this setting.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — conj conj:dyadic
open: Does the matroid base polytope of every dyadic matroid admit a quadratic triangulation? Formally, is there a triangulation of the base polytope in which every maximal simplex has squared volume equal to a perfect square integer?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with an explicit counterexample) that the matroid base polytope of every dyadic matroid has a quadratic triangulation.
why: It would resolve the natural positive-characteristic analogue of White's conjecture on quadratic triangulations for representable matroids, delineating exactly where the Gröbner-version statement fails and where it may still survive.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — conj mainconjecture
open: Does every matroid $M$ admit a quadratic triangulation? Formally, is the toric ideal $I_{P(M)}$ of the matroid base polytope always generated by a quadratic Gröbner basis?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every matroid $M$, the toric ideal $I_{P(M)}$ has a quadratic Gröbner basis — equivalently, that $P(M)$ has a quadratic triangulation.
why: This is a Gröbner-basis form of White's conjecture: a positive answer would give a uniform, computational route to quadratic generation of toric ideals of matroid base polytopes, while a counterexample would delimit exactly where the conjecture fails.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — open open:Koszul
open: Is the base ring $R/I_M$ associated to a matroid $M$ always a Koszul algebra? Equivalently, does quadratic algebra structure always hold for these toric-style matroid base rings?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń), which shows that the Gröbner version of White's conjecture is false while leaving Koszulness of the base rings open.
solved_when: A proof that every base ring $R/I_M$ is Koszul, or an explicit matroid $M$ for which $R/I_M$ fails to be Koszul.
why: Koszulness of base rings would give a strong homological handle on the toric ideals of matroid bases, controlling graded Betti numbers and resolution structure; a counterexample would show these rings are wilder than expected.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — open 4
open: Is the base ring of the Fano matroid a Koszul ring?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the base ring of the Fano matroid is Koszul.
why: Resolves a concrete test case in the study of Koszulness for matroid base rings, complementing the source paper's refutation of the Gröbner version of White's conjecture.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — open T8
open: Does the matroid $T_8$ admit a quadratic triangulation? Equivalently, is there a quadratic Gröbner (or squarefree quadratic) triangulation of the toric ideal attached to $T_8$, in the sense left open by the refutation of the Gröbner version of White's conjecture?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $T_8$ admits a quadratic triangulation; either answer resolves the open question stated in the source paper.
why: It is an explicit test case left open by the discovery that the Gröbner version of White's conjecture fails, so resolving it clarifies which matroids still admit quadratic triangulations.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — open 6
open: Does the matroid $AG(2,3)$ admit a quadratic triangulation? Equivalently, is there a triangulation whose topology respects a degree-$2$ Gröbner-degenerate structure in the toric ideal of the matroid?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that $AG(2,3)$ has a quadratic triangulation, or a proof that it does not, resolves the question.
why: It tests the reach of quadratic triangulations for toric ideals of matroids, a natural class where the Gröbner version of White's conjecture is known to fail.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: The Gröbner Version of White's Conjecture is False — open 8
open: Does the toric ideal of every matroid admit a Gröbner basis whose degree is bounded by a universal constant, independent of the matroid? More precisely, is there a constant C such that for every matroid the toric ideal has a Gröbner basis all of whose elements have degree at most C?
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń).
solved_when: A universal constant C is exhibited (or proved not to exist) bounding the degree of some Gröbner basis of the toric ideal of every matroid.
why: A uniform degree bound would give a universal complexity control on Gröbner computations for toric ideals of matroids, which underpin combinatorial algebraic geometry and integer programming applications; failure would show these ideals are inherently unbounded in complexity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13960v1 (Spencer Backman, Nathan Cheung, Michał Lasoń)

title: A constant-factor step towards Vizing's conjecture
open: Is Vizing's conjecture from the early 1960s true — that for all graphs MATH and MATH, the domination number is super-multiplicative under the Cartesian product, MATH (G H) (G) (H), where G H has vertex set MATH with two distinct vertices MATH and MATH adjacent if and only if either MATH and MATH, or MATH and MATH?
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026); Vizing's conjecture, attributed to Vizing 1963, has attracted a large body of partial results on the conjecture and its variants, a full account of which the source notes would be impossible to give.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the inequality MATH (G H) (G) (H) for all graphs MATH and MATH is established; a constant-factor step toward it would constitute meaningful progress.
why: Vizing's conjecture is perhaps the most famous open problem on domination in graphs, and settling it would resolve a question that has drawn tremendous attention from graph theorists while clarifying the behavior of domination under products.

title: A constant-factor step towards Vizing's conjecture
open: Is there an absolute constant C such that every two graphs G and H satisfy the domination number of their Cartesian product being at most C times the product of their domination numbers? Such a constant-factor bound has remained open and has been highlighted as an open problem in several previous works.
solved_when: Explicit absolute constants C and a proof that for all graphs G and H, the product domination number is within a constant factor of the product of the individual domination numbers.
why: It would give the first quantitative form of Vizing's conjecture, converting a qualitative multiplicative domination question into a concrete approximation guarantee.

title: Pairwise Compatibility Representations of Multidimensional Grid Graphs
open: What is the minimum number of intervals sufficient to represent all three-dimensional grid graphs — or, more generally, grid graphs of higher dimension — via pairwise compatibility representations? The source paper resolves the three-dimensional case, and its first open problem asks what lies beyond.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Sheikh Azizul Hakim and Md. Shamsuzzoha Bayzid, http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14656v1, which establishes that the minimum number of intervals sufficient for all three-dimensional grid graphs is exactly two, resolving a previously posed open problem.
solved_when: A proof establishing the exact minimum number of intervals for the grid graphs in question — the record notes the three-dimensional minimum is exactly two — or, for higher dimensions, the corresponding exact value.
why: Determines how economically multidimensional grid graphs admit pairwise compatibility representations, a structural question about interval-based graph representation.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14656v1 (Sheikh Azizul Hakim, Md. Shamsuzzoha Bayzid)

title: Coarse Balanced Separators in Biclique-Induced-Minor-Free Graphs — conjecture conj: coarse bal sep and tw constant radius
open: For every k and r, does there exist a constant k′ such that every graph admitting (k, r)-balanced separators also admits a (k′, r)-coverable tree decomposition? Informally, when balanced separators of bounded width exist at a fixed radius r, must they cohere into a tree decomposition whose bags are coverable by a bounded number of r-neighborhoods?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, and Claire Kaneshiro (arXiv:2606.14974v2).
solved_when: Positive constants k′ = k′(k, r) are exhibited (or a construction refuting the implication for some k, r is given); the statement concerns graphs G admitting (k, r)-balanced separators, with r fixed and k′ required to depend only on k and r.
why: It would tie balanced-separator structure directly to tree-decomposition structure at constant radius, a key step toward coarse balanced-separator theorems for biclique-induced-minor-free graph classes.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14974v2 (Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Claire Kaneshiro)

title: Constructor--Blocker games forbidding even cycles
open: What is the correct order of the game score $g(n, K_r, C_{2k})$ in Constructor–Blocker games that forbid even cycles, for general values of $k 4$ and $3 r 2k-2$? More precisely, the question asks for the asymptotic behavior of this score across the stated ranges of $k$ and $r$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026); see Lanchao Wang, Zhifei Yan, http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15063v1.
solved_when: The order of $g(n, K_r, C_{2k})$ is determined (up to constants) for all $k 4$ and $3 r 2k-2$.
why: It resolves the general-case behavior of the Constructor–Blocker game score for even-cycle-forbidden boards, completing the picture left open by the source paper's analysis.

title: Conjugacy Class Averages and Sidorenko's Conjecture — conjecture conj:sidorenko
open: Does Sidorenko's conjecture hold in the setting of conjugacy class averages, as formulated in the source paper?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.15368v1 (Yuqi Zhao).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjecture as stated in the source paper, resolving the conjugacy class averages formulation of Sidorenko's conjecture.
why: It is a curated open problem whose resolution would advance the theory surrounding Sidorenko's conjecture in this corner of extremal/graph theory.

title: On the number of symmetric chain decompositions of the minuscule latti — question stanquest
open: Do the minuscule lattices $L(m,n)$ and $M(n)$ admit a symmetric chain decomposition? That is, can each of these lattices be partitioned into saturated chains that are symmetric about the middle rank?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Robert Dorward, arXiv:2606.15891v1.
solved_when: An explicit symmetric chain decomposition is constructed for $L(m,n)$ and $M(n)$, or a proof is given that no such decomposition exists for either lattice.
why: A symmetric chain decomposition yields strong structural and enumerative information — rank-unimodality, strong Sperner properties, and symmetric chain structures — for these lattices, resolving the main structural question left open about them.

title: Ornaments and Difference Distance Magic Oriented Graphs
open: What is the minimum number of edges a connected difference distance magic oriented graph on n vertices can have? The authors conjecture that the example shown in their paper attains this minimum.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) (Roza Aceska, McKailyn Lort, Allison Ripperger, http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16001v3), where the authors observe a DDMOG on n vertices in a figure and conjecture it is the sparsest such graph.
solved_when: The sparsest connected DDMOG on n vertices is determined — specifically, a proof (or disproof) that the n-vertex example constructed in the source paper has the fewest edges possible among all connected DDMOGs on n vertices.
why: It would establish a baseline extremal result for difference distance magic oriented graphs, showing how sparse such labelings permit a connected orientation to be, and confirming the authors' conjectured extremal example.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16001v3 (Roza Aceska, McKailyn Lort, Allison Ripperger)

title: Euler Stratifications of Second Hypersimplices via Delta-matroids — conjecture conjecture:main-delta-matroid-invariance
open: Do isomorphic delta-matroids determine the same maximum likelihood degree? Precisely: if $C_1, C_2$ are scaling matrices whose associated delta-matroids are isomorphic, must the ML degrees of $V_d^{c_1}$ and $V_d^{c_2}$ coincide?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that ML degrees of $V_d^{c_1}$ and $V_d^{c_2}$ agree whenever the delta-matroids of $C_1$ and $C_2$ are isomorphic.
why: It would show that the ML degree of these hypersimplex stratifications is a delta-matroid invariant, reducing its computation to combinatorics rather than explicit algebraic geometry.

title: Euler Stratifications of Second Hypersimplices via Delta-matroids
open: Given a rank-four scaling matrix $C^{dd}$, is the minimum number of non-vanishing principal $4$-minors equal to $\binom{d-1}{3}$? In particular, does the corresponding delta-matroid necessarily lie in the orbit consisting of the families $\binom{[d]}{2} \setminus \binom{[d]}{3}$, where $K \in \binom{[d]}{4}$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the minimum number of non-vanishing principal $4$-minors of a rank-four scaling matrix $C^{dd}$ is $\binom{d-1}{3}$, together with the claimed classification of the corresponding delta-matroid orbit.
why: It settles the second conjecture of the source paper on Euler stratifications of second hypersimplices via delta-matroids, pinning down the minimal stratum and its combinatorial type.

title: Quasi-kernels in Hereditary Classes and Applications to Break — conjecture small
open: Does every sink-free digraph admit a quasi-kernel of size at most half its vertex set? Formally: if $D$ is sink-free, must $D$ have a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q| \le \frac{1}{2}|V(D)|$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.16571v2 (Jiangdong Ai, Tianyu Huang, Xiangzhou Liu); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every sink-free digraph has a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q| \le \frac{1}{2}|V(D)|$; success is a settled answer to this conjecture.
why: A positive answer would give a sharp structural guarantee on quasi-kernels in sink-free digraphs, a basic object in digraph theory; a negative answer would exhibit sink-free digraphs forcing larger quasi-kernels.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16571v2 (Jiangdong Ai, Tianyu Huang, Xiangzhou Liu)

title: On the chromatic number and equilateral dimension of $\mathbb{R}^n$ wi
open: What is the tropical equilateral dimension of tropical projective space $\mathbb{TP}^n$ — that is, the maximal number of points in $\mathbb{TP}^n$ any two of which are at the same tropical distance from each other?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Amnon Rosenmann, arXiv:2606.16642v2 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16642v2). No bounds or partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An exact formula, or sharp bounds, for the maximal cardinality of a tropically equilateral set in $\mathbb{TP}^n$ is established, for general $n$.
why: It is the tropical analogue of the classical equilateral dimension problem for Euclidean space, and resolving it reveals how equidistance behaves under the tropical metric, where it can differ sharply from the Euclidean case.

title: On the chromatic number and equilateral dimension of $\mathbb{R}^n$ wi
open: Does every maximal equilateral set lie on a tropical sphere? Put formally, is it the case that any maximal equilateral set is contained in a tropical sphere?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every maximal equilateral set lies on a tropical sphere, in the setting of the source paper.
why: It would clarify the structure of maximal equilateral sets in tropical geometry, a basic question about how equidistant configurations sit in tropical space.

title: A Natural Game on Integer Partitions
open: Which positions in this natural game on integer partitions have Conway pair $(1, 0)$? That is, give a characterization of exactly those positions whose Conway pair equals $(1, 0)$.
solved_when: A complete characterization of the positions with Conway pair $(1, 0)$ is given.
why: It settles one of the open questions posed in the source paper on this game, advancing the combinatorial theory of integer-partition games.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16828v1 (Ina Bašić, Eric Gottlieb, Matjaž Krnc)

title: A Non-Multiplicable Upho Poset Constructed from the Petersen Graph — conj conj:upho-lattice-multiplicable
open: Is every finitary upho lattice multiplicable? In particular, does every finite-type $\mathbb{N}$-graded upho lattice admit a multiplication making it multiplicable?
solved_when: A proof that every finitary upho lattice (in particular every finite-type $\mathbb{N}$-graded upho lattice) is multiplicable, or an explicit counterexample.
why: Multiplicability is a key structural property connecting upho lattices to algebraic constructions; establishing it would complete the basic structural theory of finitary upho lattices.

title: A Non-Multiplicable Upho Poset Constructed from the Petersen Graph
open: Is the total number of general upho lattices associated with a given core finite? If the conjecture {conj:upho-lattice-multiplicable} holds, it would resolve this question elegantly.
solved_when: A proof or disproof that the number of general upho lattices associated with any fixed core is finite.
why: Finiteness would give a complete classification of upho lattices core by core; the conjectured multiplicability route would yield this automatically.

title: Characterizing uniform hypergraphs via Seidel matrix and Seidel energy — conjecture CCcc
open: Is the complete graph $K_n$ the graph of minimum Seidel energy among all graphs on $n$ vertices? Formally, the conjecture asserts that for every graph $G$ of order $n$, ${E}(S(G)) \geq {E}(S(K_n)) = 2n-2$.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that ${E}(S(G)) \geq 2n-2$ holds for every graph $G$ of order $n$, with equality exactly at the complete graph $K_n$.
why: It would give a sharp extremal characterization of the Seidel energy, anchoring the spectrum-based study of uniform hypergraphs via their Seidel matrices.

title: Characterizing uniform hypergraphs via Seidel matrix and Seidel energy
