open: Which $k$-uniform hypergraphs have Seidel energy exceeding that of the complete graph $K_n$, and which do not? Formally, characterize all $k$-uniform hypergraphs that are Seidel hyperenergetic and all that are Seidel non-hyperenergetic.
solved_when: A complete structural characterization is given of the $k$-uniform hypergraphs that are Seidel hyperenergetic and those that are Seidel non-hyperenergetic.
why: It completes the extension of Seidel-matrix energy theory from graphs to hypergraphs, yielding a full classification where currently only the definitions and the question exist.

title: Characterizing uniform hypergraphs via Seidel matrix and Seidel energy
open: Which $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices attains the maximum, and which the minimum, Seidel energy? In other words, characterize the extremal $k$-uniform hypergraphs for Seidel energy over all hypergraphs with a fixed number $n$ of vertices.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.17817v1 (Alexander Guterman, Shib Sankar Saha).
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the $k$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices that maximize and minimize the Seidel energy, together with the corresponding extremal energy values.
why: It would extend the classical extremal theory of Seidel energy from graphs to the hypergraph setting, identifying the extremal structures that the Seidel matrix formalism makes accessible.

title: Characterizing uniform hypergraphs via Seidel matrix and Seidel energy
open: Which $r$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices attains the maximum, and which the minimum, of the Seidel energy? In other words, characterize the extremal $r$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs for the Seidel energy among all such hypergraphs with $n$ vertices.
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the $r$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices that maximize and minimize the Seidel energy over all $r$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs with $n$ vertices.
why: It settles the extremal theory of Seidel energy for regular uniform hypergraphs, extending classical spectral graph extremal results to the hypergraph Seidel setting.

title: Extremal problems on the $p$-Seidel energy of graphs — question qe.3.1
open: Which graphs of order $n$ minimize the $p$-Seidel energy when $p>2$? Formally, determine the minimum value of the $p$-Seidel energy over all graphs on $n$ vertices and characterize the extremal graphs attaining it.
solved_when: The minimum $p$-Seidel energy among all graphs of order $n$ is determined for $p>2$, together with a characterization of the graphs that attain it.
why: It completes the extremal picture for $p$-Seidel energy beyond the classical case, identifying the minimal graphs for this spectral invariant.

title: Extremal problems on the $p$-Seidel energy of graphs
open: For a fixed $p>2$, which graphs on $n$ vertices attain the largest $p$-Seidel energy? In other words, characterize the extremal graphs maximizing the $p$-Seidel energy over all graphs of fixed order $n$.
solved_when: A complete characterization of the graphs of order $n$ that maximize the $p$-Seidel energy is given, valid for every $p>2$.
why: Solving it would complete the extremal picture for $p$-Seidel energy analogously to the classical energy case, giving sharp bounds and structural information about the graphs that achieve them.

title: Extremal problems on the $p$-Seidel energy of graphs
open: For a fixed exponent $0<p<2$, which graphs on $n$ vertices attain the smallest possible $p$-Seidel energy? In other words, characterize the minimizers of the $p$-Seidel energy among all graphs of a given order $n$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17828v2 (Alexander Guterman, Shib Sankar Saha).
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the graphs of order $n$ minimizing the $p$-Seidel energy for every $0<p<2$ (or for each specified range of $p$ in $(0,2)$), with proof.
why: A solution would complete the extremal picture for $p$-Seidel energy at the lower end, complementing whatever is known about maximizers and enabling sharp energy-based comparisons between graphs.

title: Extremal problems on the $p$-Seidel energy of graphs
open: Among all $r$-regular graphs on a fixed number of vertices, which ones have the largest — or smallest — $p$-Seidel energy when $0<p<2$? The task is to characterize the extremal $r$-regular graphs of given order $n$ for this spectral invariant.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.17828v2 (Alexander Guterman, Shib Sankar Saha); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: For each $0<p<2$, a characterization is given of the $r$-regular graphs of order $n$ that maximize, and those that minimize, the $p$-Seidel energy.
why: Resolving it would complete the extremal theory of the $p$-Seidel energy on regular graphs, the natural home for Seidel-type spectral invariants, and extend the classical energy-extremal picture to this generalized family.

title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
open: Does there exist an adaptive sublinear-time algorithm that determines the edge set of an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform linear hypergraph using $O(n)$ queries? That is, can the entire edge structure of such a hypergraph be learned with a linear query budget?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18048v2 (Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo).
solved_when: An adaptive algorithm is given that, on any $n$-vertex $k$-uniform linear hypergraph, outputs its edge set correctly using $O(n)$ queries (hence sublinear in the input representation).
why: A positive answer would show that the structure of uncrowded linear hypergraphs is so constrained that it can be reconstructed with a linear number of queries, a key step toward sublinear-time algorithms for list-coloring problems at the shattering threshold.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18048v2 (Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo)

title: Structured lattices and their applications to security
open: Does the Minkowski conjecture hold in some lattice dimensions where Woods' conjecture fails? In other words, can the Minkowski conjecture survive in dimensions beyond those in which Woods' stronger statement is false?
solved_when: A proof or disproof, in some dimension, of the Minkowski conjecture in a case where Woods' conjecture is known to fail.
why: It would delineate the true boundary between the Minkowski conjecture and Woods' conjecture, clarifying which covering-radius-type properties of lattices persist when the stronger conjecture breaks down.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18920v1 (Lenny Fukshansky, Camilla Hollanti, Rahinatou Y. Njah Nchiwo)

title: Tree-independence number of $K_{1,d}$-free graph classes
open: Is there a polynomial $f$ such that, for any integer $d \ge 2$, every $K_{1,d}$-free graph with no $d \times d$ grid as an induced minor has tree-independence number bounded by $f(d)$? In other words, does excluding a claw and a grid as induced subgraph/minor force the tree-independence number to be polynomially bounded in $d$?
solved_when: A polynomial $f$ is exhibited such that for every $d \ge 2$, every $K_{1,d}$-free graph containing no $d \times d$ grid as an induced minor satisfies $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G) \le f(d)$ — or a counterexample family is constructed showing no such polynomial bound exists.
why: It would establish an induced-grid analogue of grid-theorem boundedness for tree-independence number in claw-free-type classes, yielding polynomial-time algorithms for problems tractable under bounded tree-independence number on such graph classes.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20256v1 (Kenny Bešter Štorgel, Mujin Choi, Hidde Koerts)

title: Dice Relabeling Using Square-Sided Dice — question qu:three
open: How many relabelings of dice exist when the number of sides is $m = p^2q$ or $m = pqr$, where $p, q, r$ are distinct primes?
solved_when: An enumeration (formula or algorithm) for the number of relabelings is obtained for the cases $m = p^2q$ and $m = pqr$ with $p, q, r$ distinct primes.
why: It extends the dice-relabeling count beyond the cases already handled in the source paper, completing the enumeration for these composite side counts.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20311v1 (Evelyn Fiore, George D. Nasr, Cooper Stone)

title: Dice Relabeling Using Square-Sided Dice — question qu:dif_size_square
open: Can the outcome frequencies of a set of $n$ $m$-sided dice be reproduced by a collection of dice whose side counts are perfect squares, where the dice need not all have the same number of sides?
solved_when: A construction (or a proof of impossibility) is given that matches the frequency distribution of $n$ $m$-sided dice using dice each having a perfect square number of sides, not necessarily equal.
why: It tests how flexible square-sided dice are as a relabeling medium for nonuniform distributions, a natural relaxation of the equal-sided dice setting.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20311v1 (Evelyn Fiore, George D. Nasr, Cooper Stone)

title: Simplex faces and quadratic toric ideals of lattice polytopes
open: Is the toric ideal of every smooth lattice polytope generated by quadrics? Equivalently, does every smooth polytope define a projective toric variety whose ideal admits a quadratic Gröbner-free generating set?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.20430v3 (Aki Mori, Hidefumi Ohsugi).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the statement that the toric ideal of any smooth polytope is quadratic.
why: A positive answer would give a clean algebraic characterization of smooth polytopes' toric ideals and improve tools for computing their toric varieties; a counterexample would refine the boundary between smooth and general lattice polytopes.

title: Simplex faces and quadratic toric ideals of lattice polytopes — conjecture Mconj
open: Is the toric ideal of the base polytope of every matroid generated by quadrics? In formal terms, does every matroid base polytope have a quadratic toric ideal?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Aki Mori and Hidefumi Ohsugi, arXiv:2606.20430v3.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that the toric ideal of the base polytope of any matroid is generated by its degree-two elements.
why: A positive answer would extend the study of quadratic toric ideals from graph-related and lattice polytopes to the broad class of matroid base polytopes, giving a wide new family of polytopes with nice algebraic properties.

title: Relating tournaments and permutations with xrays — conjecture conj:D4Conj
open: Is the number of certain combinatorial objects counted by ${C}(2^n)$ exactly equal to the number counted by ${S}^4(1^n)$, for every positive integer $n$? Formally, does $|{C}(2^n)| = |{S}^4(1^n)|$ hold for all positive integers $n$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Matthew Davis and Michael W. Schroeder, http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21532v1; no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the identity $|{C}(2^n)| = |{S}^4(1^n)|$ for every positive integer $n$; a disproof requires exhibiting an $n$ for which the two cardinalities differ.
why: Establishing the identity would reveal a structural connection between tournaments and permutations through their xrays, potentially yielding new bijections and counting techniques in this corner of algebraic combinatorics.

title: The Twin-Width of Graphs of Bounded VC-Dimension
open: Graphs of bounded VC-dimension can have unbounded twin-width — but can their twin-width be bounded by a linear function of their number of vertices? Formally, does every graph on n vertices of VC-dimension at most d have twin-width at most f(d)·n for some function f?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.21640v1 (Therese Biedl, Taite LaGrange, Sophie Spirkl); it is known that graphs of bounded VC-dimension can have unbounded twin-width.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that graphs of bounded VC-dimension have twin-width linear in the number of vertices, with an explicit bound f(d)·n.
why: A linear bound would give concrete twin-width-based algorithmic (e.g., model-checking and FPT) consequences for the large class of bounded VC-dimension graphs; a refutation would clarify the true separation between VC-dimension and twin-width.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21640v1 (Therese Biedl, Taite LaGrange, Sophie Spirkl)

title: Asymptotics of the Average Stack-Sorting Depth — conjecture conj:r
open: Is the sequence of consecutive differences of the average stack-sorting depth, $(D_n' - D'_{n-1})_{n \geq 2}$, monotonically increasing? In other words, does each increment of the average depth grow with $n$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.24110v2 (Jerry Zhang); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, with counterexample) that $D_n' - D'_{n-1}$ is monotonically increasing in $n$ for all $n \geq 2$.
why: Resolving it settles conjecture conj:r of the source paper and clarifies the fine asymptotic behavior of the average stack-sorting depth, a basic statistic of the stack-sorting map on permutations.

title: Asymmetric induced saturation — question q:evennormal
open: Is every induced-saturation instance on an even cycle symmetric enough that the $2t$-vertex cycle is normal, for every integer $t \ge 2$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.24763v1 (Xinyue Fan, Sahab Hajebi, Sepehr Hajebi); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that the $2t$-vertex cycle is normal for every integer $t \ge 2$.
why: It would settle the basic normality question for even cycles in asymmetric induced saturation, a foundational case of the theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24763v1 (Xinyue Fan, Sahab Hajebi, Sepehr Hajebi)

title: Intractability of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz implies algebraic hardness — quest conj:ER-in-CH
open: Is the existential theory of the reals (∃ℝ) contained in the counting hierarchy? In other words, can every sentence of the existential theory of the reals be decided within the levels of the counting hierarchy?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that ∃ℝ ⊆ CH is given.
why: Establishing such a containment would tie the complexity of real-algebraic decision problems to counting classes, clarifying the algebraic hardness landscape around Hilbert's Nullstellensatz intractability.

title: Proofs of five conjectural identities on modular rank four Nahm sums — conj conj:SW14
open: Are the five conjectural identities among rank four Nahm sums with modular properties, as conjectured by SW14, actually true? More precisely, can each of the five conjectured identities be given a rigorous proof?
solved_when: Each of the five conjectural identities on rank four Nahm sums stated in SW14 is proved rigorously.

title: Proofs of five conjectural identities on modular rank four Nahm sums — conj conj:CW33
open: Can the five conjectural identities relating rank four Nahm sums stated in arXiv:2606.25866 be proved? More precisely, are these conjectural identities between modular rank four Nahm sums actually true, and if so, what proof technique establishes them?
solved_when: Each of the five conjectural identities on modular rank four Nahm sums from arXiv:2606.25866 carries a rigorous proof.

title: The Power of Small Symmetries
open: Can proof length in MATH — the weakest of the three proof systems equipped with dynamic symmetries — be forced to grow superpolynomially? That is, can one prove superpolynomial lower bounds on proof length in MATH?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) [arXiv:2606.25895v1, Nikita Gaevoy].
solved_when: A proof is exhibited that some family of tautologies requires superpolynomially long proofs in MATH.
why: Establishing such a lower bound even in the weakest dynamic-symmetry proof system would be the first demonstration that these symmetries cannot compress proofs below superpolynomial length, a key step toward understanding whether symmetry reasoning adds genuine proof-theoretic power.

title: Geometric Complexity Theory and Graph Isomorphism
open: Is every finite simple undirected graph on at least 3 vertices reconstructible from its $1$-vertex deck?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Geometric Complexity Theory and Graph Isomorphism" by Joshua A. Grochow and Jacob Urisman (http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26244v2); the record lists no partial results.
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) showing that every finite simple undirected graph on at least 3 vertices is, or is not, reconstructible from its $1$-vertex deck; no further quantitative targets are stated in the record.
why: A positive answer would resolve this conjecture from the source open-problems paper; the record itself does not state further consequences, so any claimed applications would be speculation.

title: Geometric Complexity Theory and Graph Isomorphism
open: Is every finite simple undirected graph with at least 4 edges determined by its collection of single-edge-deleted subgraphs? Formally, such a graph is reconstructible from its $1$-edge deck.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every finite simple undirected graph with at least 4 edges is reconstructible from its $1$-edge deck.
why: This is a strengthening of graph reconstruction in the direction relevant to Geometric Complexity Theory and Graph Isomorphism, where it would clarify how much local edge-deletion information suffices to pin down a graph.

title: Artin monoids, their homomorphisms and twins
open: Do the assignments $T_1 \mapsto T_{w_{\circ}^{[1,a]}}$ and $T_2 \mapsto T_{w_{\circ}^{[b,n-1]}}$ define a homomorphism between the corresponding Artin monoids whenever $1 < b \le a < n-1$ and $a > 1$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that, under the stated conditions $1 < b \le a < n-1$ and $a > 1$, the given assignments extend to a well-defined homomorphism of the Artin monoids in question.

title: Another proof of the result on rotation compatible planar covers — conj conj:Negami
open: Is it true that a connected graph admits a finite planar cover exactly when it embeds in the projective plane? In other words, does planar-cover membership coincide with projective-planar membership for connected graphs?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.27703v1 (Shohei Koizumi, Yusuke Suzuki, Kensuke Tamura).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it can be embedded on the projective plane.
why: Settling this would give an alternative route to the result on rotation-compatible planar covers, clarifying which graphs are captured by planar covering and connecting covering theory to projective-planar embeddability.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27703v1 (Shohei Koizumi, Yusuke Suzuki, Kensuke Tamura)

title: 2-adic Valuations of Coefficients of the Fifth and Ninth Powers of the
open: Does the general case of Conjecture 5.2 hold — that is, can exact 2-adic valuation formulas be established for the coefficients of the fifth and ninth power series in the odd-exponent family? A proof would give closed-form valuation identities where currently only the conjecture stands.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28718v1 (Zhao Shen, Xinping Wang).
solved_when: Exact 2-adic valuation formulas for the coefficients in the general case of Conjecture 5.2 (odd exponents, including the fifth and ninth powers) are proved.
why: It would complete the conjectured valuation framework for the odd-exponent family, extending exact coefficient-level arithmetic information beyond the cases already handled.

title: A solution to Ditor's problem — question q:2
open: Assuming the consistency of a Mahlo cardinal, is it consistent that there is no lower finite lattice of finite breadth and cardinality $\aleph_2$?
solved_when: A model is exhibited, built from the consistency of a Mahlo cardinal, in which no lower finite lattice of finite breadth has cardinality $\aleph_2$; or the question is shown to have a negative answer.
why: It resolves the second question of Ditor's problem, clarifying the possible sizes of lower finite lattices of finite breadth under large-cardinal assumptions.

title: $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture — conjecture conj:knrs
open: Is every finite graph KNRS? Equivalently, does every finite graph $H$ satisfy the $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture (conjecture conj:knrs)?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.30010v1 (Yuqi Zhao).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every finite graph $H$ satisfies the KNRS conjecture in its $L^p$ form, as stated in conjecture conj:knrs of the source paper.
why: It resolves the $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture, completing the conjectured theory for all finite graphs rather than restricted families.

title: A Counterexample to Ziegler's Cross-Polytope Conjecture for Simplicial — question ques:ziegler
open: Is every simplicial $d$-dimensional $0/1$-polytope with $2d$ vertices affinely isomorphic to the cross-polytope?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026) [Kaibel, Volker; Pokutta, Sebastian, http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31640v2].
solved_when: A proof that every simplicial $d$-dimensional $0/1$-polytope with $2d$ vertices is affinely isomorphic to the cross-polytope, or an explicit counterexample that is not.
why: Resolving it settles whether the cross-polytope is the unique simplicial $0/1$-polytope in its dimension–vertex-count class, characterizing a basic extremal family of $0/1$-polytopes.

title: List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability -- A Dynamic Survey
open: Is it true that for all positive integers $a$ and $b$, a graph $G$ is $(a:b)$-choosable if and only if the $b$-th graph power $(G)_{b}$ is $a$-choosable? In other words, does paintability with lists of size $b$ chosen from $a$ available colors exactly correspond to ordinary list-coloring of a derived power graph?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability — A Dynamic Survey," conjecture 18, by Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram, N Narayanan (http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702v1); no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: The conjecture is proved (or refuted) for all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, i.e., a proof or counterexample establishing whether $(a:b)$-choosability of $G$ is equivalent to $a$-choosability of $(G)_{b}$ in full generality.
why: It would give a clean bridge between generalized list-coloring parameters and ordinary choosability of a graph power, allowing questions about $(a:b)$-choosability to be translated into standard $a$-choosability questions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702v1 (Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram, N Narayanan)

title: List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability -- A Dynamic Survey
open: Is every claw-free perfect graph chromatic-choosable, that is, does its choice number coincide with its chromatic number?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the statement that every claw-free perfect graph $G$ satisfies $\text{ch}(G) = \chi(G)$.
why: It would extend list-coloring results from known subclasses to the whole class of claw-free perfect graphs, clarifying how forbidding induced claws and odd holes forces list-colorings to behave like ordinary colorings.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702v1 (Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram, N Narayanan)

title: List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability -- A Dynamic Survey
open: Is every square graph chromatic-choosable — that is, does list-chromatic number equal ordinary chromatic number for the square of any graph? Formally, is $\operatorname{ch}(G^2) = \chi(G^2)$ for every graph $G$?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing, for all graphs $G$, that the choice number of the square equals the chromatic number of the square.
why: It would extend the class of graphs known to be chromatic-choosable to all squares, a basic test case for the general conjecture that every graph satisfies $\operatorname{ch}(G) = \chi(G)$.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702v1 (Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram, N Narayanan)

title: List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability -- A Dynamic Survey
open: If a graph is $(a:b)$-choosable, must it also be $(ka:kb)$-choosable for every positive integer $k$? Formally: is it true for all $a,b,k \in \mathbb{N}$ that $(a:b)$-choosability of $G$ implies $(ka:kb)$-choosability of $G$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2606.31702v1 (Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram, N Narayanan).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given of the statement that every $(a:b)$-choosable graph $G$ is $(ka:kb)$-choosable for all positive integers $a, b, k$.
why: It would establish a basic scaling law for list-coloring, showing that choosability with lists of size $a$ and color choices $b$ is preserved under uniform multiplication, directly connecting the study of fractional-type choosability parameters.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31702v1 (Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram, N Narayanan)

title: Order polytopes of generalized snake posets are $h^*$-real-rooted
open: Does every flow polytope have a real-rooted $h^*$-polynomial? While some families of flow polytopes are known to enjoy this property, the question remains open in general.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper, arXiv:2607.00922v1 (Benjamin Braun, Aryaman Jal), where it is noted that some families of flow polytopes are known to have real-rooted $h^*$-polynomials, but the general case is unresolved.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the $h^*$-polynomial of every flow polytope is real-rooted; no further quantitative targets are stated in the record.
why: It would settle a natural unifying question about the Ehrhart theory of flow polytopes, extending the real-rootedness phenomenon beyond the families where it is currently known to hold.

title: A $2/3$ Bound for Vizing's Conjecture
open: Is it true that for all graphs $G$ and $H$, the domination number of the Cartesian product satisfies $\gamma(G \square H) \geq \frac{2}{3}\gamma(G)\gamma(H)$? This weakens Vizing's conjecture, which asserts the same inequality with constant $1$ and is one of the central open problems in domination theory; see the survey and the monographs for its history.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the inequality $\gamma(G \square H) \geq \frac{2}{3}\gamma(G)\gamma(H)$ for all graphs $G$ and $H$.
why: A constant-factor weakening of Vizing's conjecture that is provable would give the first universal lower bound of this shape for the domination number of Cartesian products.

title: The Narayana transformation — conj 1
open: Do the real-rootedness properties of the Narayana transformation extend to its iterates — specifically, do the real generating functions of $A^2$ and $D^2$ have only real nonpositive roots?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) that the RGFs of $A^2$ and $D^2$ have only real nonpositive roots.
why: Establishing real-rootedness of these iterates would confirm the stability of the Narayana transformation under composition, a key step toward understanding its combinatorial and asymptotic behavior.

title: Total positivity of transformation matrices for uniform subdivisions — conj CON
open: Are the transformation matrices arising from uniform subdivisions totally positive? A formal answer would determine whether every minor of such a matrix is nonnegative.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, with counterexample) that every minor of every transformation matrix for uniform subdivisions is nonnegative.
why: Total positivity would yield strong structural control over these subdivision matrices, enabling tools from total-positivity theory; a counterexample would show where that structure fails.

title: AVD Total Colorings of Subdivision Graphs, Joins, and Deleted Lexicogr — conjecture Conjecture 1.1
open: Does every graph admit an adjacent-vertex-distinguishing total coloring with at most two more colors than some natural parameter of the graph? Formally, the conjecture asserts the bound $\chi''_a(G) \le (\text{parameter})(G) + 2$ for every graph $G$.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the conjectured bound with the additive constant $2$, establishing it for all graphs $G$.
why: Settling it would pin down the AVD total chromatic number within a small additive constant, completing the picture this conjecture is designed to provide.

title: AVD Total Colorings of Subdivision Graphs, Joins, and Deleted Lexicogr — question Question 1.7
open: Does the adjacent-vertex-distinguishing total coloring conjecture (AVD-TCC) hold for the central graph of any graph? That is, must the total coloring of every central graph admit a proper total coloring whose palettes distinguish adjacent vertices?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that AVD-TCC holds for the central graph of every graph, settling Question 1.7 of the source paper.
why: It extends the AVD total coloring conjecture to a graph transformation (the central graph) widely used in graph coloring questions, so a positive answer would unify the conjecture across this operation.

title: One-Weight Colorings, the Symmetric Class, and Lower Bounds for Hales- — question q:frontiers
open: Does the symmetric simplex instance of the Hales–Jewett–type problem at parameters $(3,3)$ with $n=22$ admit a one-weight coloring? More precisely, the record asks to decide the symmetric simplex instance at $(3,3)$ with $n=22$ (the figure $276$ also appears, but its role is truncated in the record).
solved_when: The symmetric simplex instance at $(3,3)$, $n=22$ is decided (together with the quantity $276$ mentioned in the record).
why: Deciding this instance would settle a concrete symmetric-class case relevant to lower bounds for Hales–type theorems, where explicit small instances are the obstruction to sharper bounds.

title: On the Harborth Conjecture. Part I — conjecture conj:harborth
open: Does every planar graph admit a plane straight-line drawing in which every edge has integer length? Equivalently, can each planar graph be embedded in the plane with straight edges and all edge lengths drawn from the integers?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02535v2 (Shiva Kintali).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every planar graph has a plane straight-line drawing with all edge lengths integers; partial progress should specify precisely which classes of planar graphs are settled.
why: A positive answer would give a complete integer-distance realisation theory for planar graphs, resolving a long-standing barrier between combinatorial planarity and metric embeddability; a negative answer would exhibit planar graphs with no integral geometric realisation at all.

title: On the Harborth Conjecture. Part I — conjecture conj:kleber
open: Does every planar graph admit a plane straight-line drawing in which the distance between every pair of adjacent vertices is an integer? This is the Harborth Conjecture (conjecture conj:kleber): every planar graph has an integral drawing.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.02535v2 (Shiva Kintali), a curated open-problems collection; no partial resolution is recorded there.
solved_when: A proof — or disproof with an explicit counterexample — of the statement that every planar graph has an integral drawing is given.
why: A positive answer would settle a long-standing question at the intersection of graph drawing and number theory, establishing that the geometry of planar graphs can always be realized with integer edge lengths.

title: Disproof of the tree product conjecture via the Heisenberg group
open: Does the circle of ideas around the Heisenberg group and the tree product conjecture, as developed in the source paper, admit a definitive disproof or confirmation of the conjecture itself? The record states only that a consequence of a related result resolved a longstanding open problem on the queue-number of planar graphs, with further applications following.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03041v1 (Freddie Illingworth, Sergey Norin, Raphael Steiner). A consequence of the related result solved a longstanding open problem about the queue-number of planar graphs, and many more applications followed soon after.
solved_when: A proof or disproof of the tree product conjecture via the Heisenberg group construction is established and published; the record gives no further quantitative targets.
why: A resolution settles the conjecture directly and, given the precedent that a consequence already resolved the queue-number problem for planar graphs, is likely to yield further structural applications.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03041v1 (Freddie Illingworth, Sergey Norin, Raphael Steiner)

title: On Ramsey-type problems for paths and cycles with few colour changes — conjecture conj:path.cover
open: If the edges of $K_n$ are coloured with $q$ colours, must the vertices be coverable by $q$ monochromatic paths? Formally, is it true that for every $n, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $q$-colouring of the edges of $K_n$, the vertex set can be partitioned into $q$ vertex sets each of which spans a monochromatic path?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Allen, Böttcher, and Clemens, http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03243v1.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit colouring) of the statement that for all $n, q \in \mathbb{N}$, every $q$-edge-colouring of $K_n$ admits a cover of the vertices by $q$ monochromatic paths.
why: A positive answer would extend the classical path-cover paradigm for few colours to arbitrarily many colours, giving a sharp handle on covering complete graphs by monochromatic connected substructures in Ramsey-type settings.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03243v1 (Peter Allen, Julia Böttcher, Dennis Clemens)

title: On Ramsey-type problems for paths and cycles with few colour changes — conjecture conj:spanning.good.path
open: Is it true that for every number of colours, every edge-colouring of a complete graph on $n$ vertices contains a Hamiltonian path whose colouring uses at most $k-1$ colour changes? Formally, the conjecture asserts that for all $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $R_k^{k-1}(P_n) = n$.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "On Ramsey-type problems for paths and cycles with few colour changes" by Peter Allen, Julia Böttcher, and Dennis Clemens (http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03243v1).
solved_when: The equality $R_k^{k-1}(P_n) = n$ is proved for all positive integers $k$ and $n$ (or disproved by an explicit counterexample).
why: It would pin down the exact Ramsey-type threshold for spanning paths under a bounded number of colour changes, showing that no extra vertices are needed beyond the path itself even as the number of colours grows.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03243v1 (Peter Allen, Julia Böttcher, Dennis Clemens)

title: Oddomorphisms, Split-Off Minors, and the Strong Roberson Conjecture
open: Is it true that every proper minor-closed graph class that is also closed under disjoint unions has a homomorphism indistinguishability relation distinct from isomorphism? Formally, for every such class that is not the class of all graphs, homomorphism indistinguishability over the class should fail to coincide with graph isomorphism.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.03405v1 (Arnar Á. Kristjánsson).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given that for every class of graphs that is minor closed, closed under disjoint unions, and not the class of all graphs, the homomorphism indistinguishability relation is not equal to isomorphism.
why: This is a case of the Strong Roberson Conjecture; settling it would clarify exactly when counting homomorphisms from a minor-closed family can capture isomorphism, a fundamental question in the structural theory of homomorphism indistinguishability.

title: Improved bounds for the chromatic index of $k$-uniform hypergraphs — conjecture Alon Kim
open: Is the chromatic index of every $t$-simple $k$-uniform hypergraph of bounded maximum degree asymptotically equal to $(t-1+1/t)D$? Formally: for every $k \ge t \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, does there exist $D_0$ such that every $k$-uniform, $t$-simple hypergraph with maximum degree at most $D \ge D_0$ satisfies $\chi'( \mathcal{H}) \le (t-1+1/t+\varepsilon)D$?
solved_when: For every $k \ge t \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, a $D_0$ is exhibited such that all $k$-uniform, $t$-simple hypergraphs of maximum degree at most $D \ge D_0$ have chromatic index at most $(t-1+1/t+\varepsilon)D$.
why: It would pin down the asymptotically tight leading constant for edge-coloring $t$-simple $k$-uniform hypergraphs, the natural hypergraph analogue of the classical chromatic index problem for graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03573v1 (Sarah Frederickson, Yanli Hao, Tom Kelly)

title: Magic Positivity for the Ehrhart Polynomials of Partial Permutohedra — prob Open-problem
open: Do the Ehrhart polynomials of partial permutohedra admit a "magic positivity" property — that is, can their coefficients be realized through a construction that makes their positivity evident?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03854v1 (Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang); no progress beyond this statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the Ehrhart polynomials of partial permutohedra possess magic positivity, as stated as open in the source paper.
why: A positive answer would give a transparent structural explanation for coefficient positivity of these Ehrhart polynomials, settling a question raised in the source literature.

title: Magic Positivity for the Ehrhart Polynomials of Partial Permutohedra
open: Which partial permutohedra have magic positive Ehrhart polynomials? In other words, characterize or classify all partial permutohedra that are magic positive, as Ferroni and Higashitani asked in their survey.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Feihu Liu and Zihao Zhang (http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03854v1), following the open problem raised by Ferroni and Higashitani in their survey.
solved_when: A complete characterization or classification is given of the partial permutohedra whose Ehrhart polynomials are magic positive.
why: A classification would reveal which combinatorial structures of partial permutohedra force positivity behavior in their Ehrhart polynomials, connecting enumeration theory of these polytopes to the broader positivity program for Ehrhart theory.

title: The Second Largest Eigenvalue of Stiffness Matrices of Normalized Comp — conjecture conj1-1
open: Is the second largest eigenvalue of the stiffness matrix of a normalized configuration on the complete graph always exactly \(n/2\), with multiplicity exactly \(n-1\)? Formally: let \(d \ge 3\), and let \(p: [n] \to \mathbb{R}^d\) satisfy \(\|p(i)\| = 1\) for all \(i \in [n]\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p(i) = 0\), and suppose the image of \(p\) has size at least \(3\); must the second largest eigenvalue of \(L(K_n, p)\) equal \(n/2\) with multiplicity exactly \(n-1\)?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that, under the hypotheses above, the second largest eigenvalue of \(L(K_n, p)\) is \(n/2\) and its multiplicity is exactly \(n-1\).
why: It pins down the exact extremal spectral behavior of stiffness matrices for normalized configurations on the complete graph, a basic case for understanding how rigidity-type Laplacians depend on framework geometry.

title: Schur positivity of nabla on Petrie symmetric functions
open: Is nabla of a Petrie symmetric function Schur positive, and if so, for exactly which parameters? In other words, determine the complete sign pattern for Schur positivity in this setting, resolving the conjecture posed as Conjecture 5.2 in the source paper.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Menghao Qu, http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06351v1.
solved_when: The conjecture stated as Conjecture 5.2 in arXiv:2607.06351 is resolved — that is, the sign pattern for Schur positivity of nabla on Petrie symmetric functions is completely determined.
why: A complete determination of the sign pattern settles an explicitly posed conjecture in symmetric function theory and clarifies when the nabla operator preserves positivity outside the classical setting.

title: Some new results on Sylvester colorings of cubic graphs — conjecture conj:BFConjecture
open: Is every bridgeless cubic graph Berge-Fulkerson colorable, as conjectured in 1972?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the Berge-Fulkerson conjecture: that every bridgeless cubic graph admits a Sylvester (Berge-Fulkerson) coloring.
why: The conjecture is a central open problem on colorings of cubic graphs; a resolution would settle a fundamental question about the structure of bridgeless cubic graphs that has stood since 1972.

title: Some new results on Sylvester colorings of cubic graphs — conjecture conj:5CDC
open: Does every bridgeless cubic graph admit a family of Sylvester colorings whose even subgraphs cover each edge in a prescribed pattern? Formally, is the (5, 2)-even-subgraph-cover conjecture (conjecture conj:5CDC) true for all bridgeless cubic graphs?
solved_when: The conjecture conj:5CDC — the (5, 2)-even-subgraph-cover statement for bridgeless cubic graphs — is proven or refuted.
why: It is extracted from a curated open-problems collection, and resolving it would extend the new results on Sylvester colorings of cubic graphs established in the source paper.

title: Computation of small reflective and dihedral Ramsey numbers — conjecture palt_pmon_dih_conj
open: Is the reflective/dihedral Ramsey number of an alternating path on $a$ vertices against a monotone path on $b$ vertices always exactly one more than a product of their parameters? Formally, the conjecture asserts that for any $a \ge 3$ and $b \ge 4$, $R_{dih}(P_a^{alt}, P_b^{mon}) = 1 + (a - 1)(b - 2)$.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.06817v2 (Ivan Damnjanović, Irena Đorđević); no partial resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the identity $R_{dih}(P_a^{alt}, P_b^{mon}) = 1 + (a - 1)(b - 2)$ for all $a \ge 3$ and $b \ge 4$.
why: It would give exact values for a family of small dihedral Ramsey numbers, extending the exact-computation program for path-type Ramsey numbers to the reflective/alternating setting.

title: Computation of small reflective and dihedral Ramsey numbers — conjecture palt_cmon_dih_conj
open: Is the dihedral Ramsey number of an alternating path against a monotone cycle always given by the simple product formula — specifically, does $R_{dih}(P^{alt}_a, C^{mon}_b) = 1 + (a-1)(b-1)$ hold for the stated ranges of $a$ and $b$? A proof would establish the exact value of these reflective/dihedral Ramsey numbers for all parameters in the conjecture.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06817v2 (Ivan Damnjanović, Irena Đorđević). No resolution is recorded.
solved_when: The identity $R_{dih}(P^{alt}_a, C^{mon}_b) = 1 + (a - 1)(b - 1)$ is proved for all $a$ and $b$ in the ranges stated by the conjecture, or a counterexample exhibits parameters where equality fails.
why: Determining these small reflective and dihedral Ramsey numbers exactly supplies the concrete data points needed to place such results within Ramsey theory, and settling the conjecture (conjecture palt_cmon_dih_conj) closes a specific gap left open by the source paper.

title: Computation of small reflective and dihedral Ramsey numbers — conjecture palt_k_dih_conj
open: Is the dihedral Ramsey number of an alternating path against a clique always given by the simple product formula — that is, does $R_{dih}(P^{alt}_a, K_b) = 1 + (a-1)(b-1)$ hold for all natural numbers $a, b$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06817v2 (Ivan Damnjanović, Irena Đorđević).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the identity $R_{dih}(P^{alt}_a, K_b) = 1 + (a-1)(b-1)$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$.
why: It would settle the exact value of small reflective and dihedral Ramsey numbers, giving a clean closed form where currently only the conjectured relation is available.

title: Coloring digraphs with $Δ-b$ colors — conjecture conj:reed
open: Is it true that every graph's chromatic number is at most the average of its maximum degree plus one and its clique number — formally, that every graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G) \le \lceil \tfrac{1}{2}(\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G)) \rceil$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.06928v1 (Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the inequality $\chi(G) \le \lceil \tfrac{1}{2}(\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G)) \rceil$ for all graphs $G$.
why: It would give a tight interpolation between the trivial bounds $\chi \le \Delta+1$ and $\chi \ge \omega$, showing that a graph cannot be simultaneously sparse in clique number and hard to color.

title: On minimally 1-tough $(K_1\cup P_4)$-free graphs — problem problem
open: Is every 1-tough, $(K_1 \cup P_4)$-free graph on at least three vertices hamiltonian? In other words, does forbidding this one induced subgraph allow 1-toughness to force a Hamilton cycle?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.07239v1 by Shiyu Cao, Jing Chen, and Wei Zheng.
solved_when: A proof that every $(K_1 \cup P_4)$-free, 1-tough graph with at least three vertices is hamiltonian, or an explicit counterexample.
why: It would extend the classical link between toughness and hamiltonicity to a natural hereditary graph class, sharpening the boundary between classes where 1-toughness guarantees a Hamilton cycle and those where it does not.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07239v1 (Shiyu Cao, Jing Chen, Wei Zheng)

title: Minimum Edge-Outerplanar Embeddings are Polynomial-Time Computable
open: Can the minimum edge-outerplanarity of a planar graph be computed in polynomial time?
solved_when: A polynomial-time algorithm is given that computes the minimum edge-outerplanarity of any planar graph, thereby resolving the open problem of Bentz (2009).
why: It determines whether outerplanarity-style embedding measures of planar graphs are algorithmically tractable, closing a question left open in the literature.

title: Dilated Hankel determinants
open: Is there a closed form for the dilated Hankel determinants of odd order? The source paper proves the even-order cases in closed form, leaving the odd orders unresolved.
status: The even half is proved in closed form in the source paper, which states the odd orders as open; the problem comes from a curated open-problems paper, http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08279v1 (Guo-Niu Han), stated as open there (2026).
solved_when: A closed-form expression is given for the dilated Hankel determinants of every odd order, complementing the even half already proven.
why: Completing the odd orders would yield a full closed-form description of these determinants, finishing the classification begun by the even case.

title: Dilated Hankel determinants — problem prob:lgv
open: Is there a combinatorial proof of the dilated Hankel determinant evaluations? That is, can these determinants be shown to enumerate some family of combinatorial objects, for instance via a Lindström–Gessel–Viennot-style argument?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.08279v1 (Guo-Niu Han); no combinatorial proof is currently known.
solved_when: A combinatorial (bijective or sign-reversing/LGV-type) proof of the dilated Hankel determinant evaluations is given, reproducing the evaluations established in the source paper.
why: A combinatorial proof would reveal what these determinant values count, turning an algebraic identity into enumerative structure and likely connecting the determinants to lattice-path or plane-partition combinatorics.

title: Spectral Radius Conditions for 3-Uniform Intersecting Families
open: Is the Erdős Matching Conjecture true — that is, does the classic extremal characterization of families with bounded matching number hold as conjectured?
solved_when: The Erdős Matching Conjecture is proved (or disproved) in its standard form, as stated in the source paper.
why: It is a central extremal set theory problem whose resolution would settle the maximum size of set families with restricted matchings, a benchmark against which related results (such as spectral radius conditions for intersecting families) are calibrated.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08468v1 (Lusheng Fang, Guorong Gao, An Chang)

title: Three Results on Generalized Quasikernels in Digraphs — conj conj:small-qk
open: Does every source-free digraph on $n$ vertices contain a quasikernel of size at most $n/2$? Formally, the conjecture asserts that such a digraph always admits a quasikernel — an independent set whose closed in-neighborhood covers all vertices — of cardinality no greater than $n/2$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2607.09031v1, by Zejun Huang and Chenxi Yang, 2026); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the bound: every $n$-vertex source-free digraph has a quasikernel of size at most $n/2$.
why: It would settle a natural quantitative limit on how small a quasikernel can be guaranteed in source-free digraphs, a basic parameter in digraph structure theory.

title: A Single-Exponential Erdős--Hajnal Bound for Graphs of Bounded VC-Dime
open: Does every proper hereditary class of graphs have the Erdős–Hajnal property — that is, must graphs in such a class always contain a clique or stable set of polynomially large size? This asks for a positive answer in full generality, over all proper hereditary classes.
solved_when: A proof that every proper hereditary graph class satisfies the Erdős–Hajnal property (or, equivalently, that no proper hereditary class is a counterexample); conversely, a single proper hereditary class lacking the property refutes it.
why: It would settle the general Erdős–Hajnal program for hereditary classes, showing large homogeneous sets are unavoidable whenever a graph class excludes some induced structure.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09049v1 (Shuang Sun, Yan Wang, Jiasheng Zeng)

title: Reducing stable forking dependence to finitely many pregeometries — conjecture stability of the forking relation over a base
open: Is the forking relation over a base stable, so that stable forking dependence reduces to finitely many pregeometries? A precise formulation would show that dependence over any base set behaves with the tameness expected of a stable forking relation.
solved_when: The forking relation over a base is proved stable, yielding the reduction of stable forking dependence to finitely many pregeometries; no further quantitative targets are stated in the record.

title: Reducing stable forking dependence to finitely many pregeometries — conjecture stable forking conjecture
open: Does stable forking dependence reduce to finitely many pregeometries — i.e., is the stable forking conjecture true?
solved_when: The stable forking conjecture is proved.

title: On the codegree Turán density of projective geometries — prob prob1
open: What is the codegree Turán density of projective geometries, as raised by Keevash and Zhao? In other words, determine the limiting maximum codegree threshold at which hypergraphs can avoid containing copies of the projective geometry.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.09173v1 (Xiaona Fang, Yaojun Chen), attributed there to Keevash and Zhao.
solved_when: An exact value (or matching upper and lower bounds determining the limit) for the codegree Turán density of the projective geometries in question is established.
why: It would resolve a natural extremal question connecting design-theoretic structures to the codegree Turán problem, where exact answers are rare.

title: On the codegree Turán density of projective geometries
open: Is the Keevash–Zhao question on the codegree Turán density of projective geometries resolved, and if so, what is the value of that density? In the terminology of their 2007 paper in the Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B, this asks for a determination of the codegree Turán density of projective geometries.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.09173v1 (Xiaona Fang, Yaojun Chen), which formulates it as a resolution of the open problem proposed by Keevash and Zhao (JCT-B, 2007).
solved_when: The codegree Turán density of projective geometries, as posed by Keevash and Zhao (JCT-B, 2007), is determined.
why: A solution settles a named open problem in extremal hypergraph theory, fixing the exact codegree threshold at which projective-geometric configurations must appear.

title: Planarity and dimension II
open: Is the dimension of a planar poset computable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard? While computing the dimension of a poset is NP-hard in general, the computational complexity of the problem for planar posets remains open.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09294v1 (Heather S. Blake, Jędrzej Hodor, Piotr Micek). No resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof either establishes a polynomial-time algorithm for computing the dimension of planar posets, or proves that the problem is NP-hard for planar posets.
why: It would settle the last major complexity gap for poset dimension restricted to structural classes, resolving whether planarity is enough to tame a problem that is intractable in general.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09294v1 (Heather S. Blake, Jędrzej Hodor, Piotr Micek)

title: Planarity and dimension II
open: Is computing the dimension of a partially ordered set NP-hard even when restricted to posets whose order diagrams are planar? In other words, does the NP-hardness of poset dimension persist under the planarity restriction on the diagram?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of NP-hardness of computing dimension for posets with planar diagrams is given.
why: It would settle whether planarity of the diagram makes dimension tractable or preserves the complexity hardness of the general problem, a basic gap in the complexity of poset dimension.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09294v1 (Heather S. Blake, Jędrzej Hodor, Piotr Micek)

title: The perfect 1-factorisation conjecture holds asymptotically — conj conj:kotzig
open: Does every complete graph on an even number of vertices admit a perfect 1-factorisation? Formally, for every even integer $n \geq 4$, the complete graph $K_n$ admits a 1-factorisation in which the union of any pair of perfect matchings forms a Hamiltonian cycle.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given that every even integer $n \geq 4$ admits such a perfect 1-factorisation of $K_n$.
why: A perfect 1-factorisation would resolve Kotzig's long-standing conjecture, a basic structural question about complete graphs with connections to scheduling and decomposition problems.

title: Completing the rank identity for Hadamard powers of Euclidean distance
open: What is the rank of the Hadamard power of the Euclidean distance matrix, in closed form, for all powers and dimensions? The numerical evidence points toward a structured factorisation involving multinomial coefficients, analogous to the known product formula for the special case.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), namely arXiv:2607.09671v1 by Boris Horvat, Alen Orbanić, and Iztok Kavkler; a product formula is known for a special case, and numerical data suggest a factorisation in terms of multinomial coefficients.
solved_when: A closed-form expression for the rank of the Hadamard power of the Euclidean distance matrix for general power and dimension is established, matching the structure suggested by the numerical data and analogous to the product formula of the known special case.
why: It completes the rank identity for Hadamard powers of Euclidean distance matrices, giving an exact structural description where currently only a special case and numerical evidence exist.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09671v1 (Boris Horvat, Alen Orbanić, Iztok Kavkler)

title: Multiset resolvability parameters in graphs: A survey with new results
open: What is the computational complexity of the Outer Multiset Dimension Problem when the input graph is restricted to be a tree? In other words, is computing this parameter polynomial-time solvable on trees, or does it remain NP-hard?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Multiset resolvability parameters in graphs: A survey with new results" (Mohammad Farhan, Sandi Klavžar, Dorota Kuziak), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10311v1, and no resolution is recorded there.
solved_when: A complete classification of the computational complexity of the Outer Multiset Dimension Problem on trees is established — specifically, either a polynomial-time algorithm for it on trees or a proof of NP-hardness (or another well-defined complexity class) for that restriction.
why: Resolving this case would clarify whether the difficulty of computing the outer multiset dimension is genuinely tied to graph structure or persists even in the highly restricted, well-understood class of trees, a standard first testbed for such parameter problems.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10311v1 (Mohammad Farhan, Sandi Klavžar, Dorota Kuziak)

title: Multiset resolvability parameters in graphs: A survey with new results
open: Can the outer multiset dimension be determined for every non-regular graph of diameter two? That is, is there a characterization or formula for this parameter across the entire class of non-regular diameter-two graphs?
solved_when: The outer multiset dimension is computed (or shown computable via a general characterization) for every non-regular graph of diameter two.
why: It would complete our understanding of this resolvability parameter on a natural and large graph class, extending the results collected in the source survey.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10311v1 (Mohammad Farhan, Sandi Klavžar, Dorota Kuziak)

title: Independent Set Reconfiguration via Dilworth Decompositions
open: Are Token Jumping and Sliding Token fixed-parameter tractable when parameterised by the Dilworth number D(G)? More precisely, does each problem admit an algorithm running in f(D(G))·n^{O(1)} time for some computable function f?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.10629v2 (Ziad Ismaili Alaoui).
solved_when: An algorithm is given for each of Token Jumping and Sliding Token running in f(D(G))·n^{O(1)} time for some computable function f, or a hardness result rules out such an algorithm.
why: It would extend the tractability landscape of independent set reconfiguration beyond solution-size parameters, showing the Dilworth number suffices as a structural parameter; failure would reveal a structural limit of this measure.

title: Independent Set Reconfiguration via Dilworth Decompositions
open: Given two independent sets of a threshold signed graph that are reachable from one another under {Sliding Token}, can a shortest reconfiguration sequence between them be computed in polynomial time?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10629v2 (Ziad Ismaili Alaoui).
solved_when: A polynomial-time algorithm is exhibited that, for any two reachable independent sets of a threshold signed graph under Sliding Token, outputs a reconfiguration sequence of minimum length.
why: It would settle the shortest-sequence complexity question for a graph class where reachability is already understood, extending the algorithmic theory of token-sliding reconfiguration beyond mere decidability to optimality.

title: Hereditary 2-WQO Graph Classes Have Bounded Clique-Width — conjecture conj:pouzet
open: Must every hereditary graph class that is well-quasi-ordered under both the induced and the (independent) minor-style orderings appearing in its definition have bounded clique-width? Formally, does every hereditary graph class that is 2-well-quasi-ordered (under the two standard orderings on graphs) have bounded clique-width?
solved_when: A proof that every hereditary 2-well-quasi-ordered graph class has bounded clique-width (or a counterexample class that is 2-wqo yet has unbounded clique-width) is given.
why: It would tie the combinatorial finiteness condition of 2-well-quasi-ordering directly to algorithmic tractability, since bounded clique-width yields polynomial-time algorithms for a wide range of NP-hard problems on the class.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10939v2 (Julien Duron, Nikolas Mählmann, Szymon Toruńczyk)

title: Hereditary 2-WQO Graph Classes Have Bounded Clique-Width
open: Does every hereditary graph class that is well-quasi-ordered under both the induced subgraph and induced minor orders have bounded clique-width? Formally, this asks whether every hereditary 2-WQO graph class has bounded clique-width.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Julien Duron, Nikolas Mählmann, Szymon Toruńczyk, http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10939v2.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given that every hereditary 2-WQO graph class has bounded clique-width.
why: It would link a purely order-theoretic property of a graph class (being well-quasi-ordered under two relations) to a tractability property (bounded clique-width), connecting structure theory with algorithmic consequences.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10939v2 (Julien Duron, Nikolas Mählmann, Szymon Toruńczyk)

title: Neighborhood Complexity and Radius-1 Merge-Width in Monadically Depend — conjecture conj:main
open: Let $ $ be a hereditary class of graphs. Then the first-order model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable on $ $ if and only if $ $ is monadically dependent.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10941v1 (Jan Dreier, Nikolas Mählmann, Rose McCarty)

title: Edge-chromatic $4$-critical graphs and Overfull Conjecture for graphs
open: Let $G$ be a graph whose maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ exceeds $|V(G)|/3$. Must it be the case that $G$ is Class 2 (i.e., its edge-chromatic number is $\Delta(G)+1$) if and only if $G$ contains an overfull subgraph $H$ with $\Delta(H)=\Delta(G)$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.10947v2 (Chunhui Ge, Gregory Gutin, Xuli Qi).
solved_when: A proof or counterexample is given, for all graphs $G$ with $\Delta(G) > |V(G)|/3$, of the equivalence: $G$ is Class 2 exactly when $G$ contains an overfull subgraph $H$ with $\Delta(H)=\Delta(G)$.
why: This is a restricted form of the Overfull Conjecture, a central question in edge-coloring; settling it would give a structural characterization of Class 2 graphs with large maximum degree relative to their order.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10947v2 (Chunhui Ge, Gregory Gutin, Xuli Qi)

title: Tight lower bound for the spectral radius of connected graphs with giv — problem P1
open: Among all connected graphs on \(n\) vertices with matching number \(k\), which ones have the smallest spectral radius, and what is that minimum value? A formal answer would identify the extremal graphs in the family \(G_{n,k}\) and determine their spectral radii.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11061v2 (Xinmin Hou, Li Tan). No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: The spectrally minimal graphs in \(G_{n,k}\) are characterized, and a tight lower bound on their spectral radius is established.
why: Determining the minimum spectral radius for graphs of given order and matching number completes the extremal picture for this invariant and yields a sharp quantitative link between a graph's matching structure and its spectrum.

title: Combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomi — conjecture conj:circular_poset_stat
open: Is there a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of a circular fence poset? That is, for a circular fence poset $P$ of size $n$, can the coefficients of its order polynomial be given a direct combinatorial meaning?
status: The conjecture (recorded as conj:circular_poset_stat) is stated as open in the source paper (2026), by Yakob Kahane, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11225v1.
solved_when: A combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of an arbitrary circular fence poset of size $n$ is provided.
why: It would give concrete combinatorial meaning to these polynomial invariants of circular fence posets, turning purely algebraic data into countable structures.

title: Fixed-point-free elements in two-orbit permutation groups
open: Which pairs of integers $(n_1, n_2)$ have the property that every two-orbit permutation group of orbit type $(n_1, n_2)$ contains a derangement?
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the pairs $(n_1, n_2)$ for which every two-orbit permutation group of orbit type $(n_1, n_2)$ contains a derangement.
why: It resolves the derangement existence question for the two-orbit case, a basic test case for fixed-point-free elements beyond the classical transitive-setting results.

title: Ray and end spaces: characterizations and classification up to homeomo — question QUE_AreOpenSubspaceofRayQuasi?
open: If $X$ is an open subspace of a ray space, must it be a quasi-ray space?
solved_when: A proof that every open subspace of a ray space is a quasi-ray space, or a counterexample exhibiting an open subspace of a ray space that is not a quasi-ray space.
why: Resolving it would clarify the relationship between ray spaces and quasi-ray spaces and whether the former class is stable under taking open subspaces.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11561v2 (Matheus Duzi, Gabriel Fernandes, Paulo Magalhães Júnior)

title: Ray and end spaces: characterizations and classification up to homeomo — question QUESTION_FirsCountRayProd
open: If $X$ and $Y$ are first-countable ray spaces, must their product $X \times Y$ also be a ray space? In other words, is the class of first-countable ray spaces closed under taking products?
solved_when: A proof that $X \times Y$ is a ray space for all first-countable ray spaces $X$ and $Y$, or an explicit counterexample of first-countable ray spaces whose product is not a ray space.
why: It tests whether the class of first-countable ray spaces is stable under a basic topological operation, which would sharpen the classification and characterization program for ray and end spaces.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11561v2 (Matheus Duzi, Gabriel Fernandes, Paulo Magalhães Júnior)

title: Ray and end spaces: characterizations and classification up to homeomo
open: If $T$ is a special Aronszajn tree, must $(T)^2$ arise as the end space (or the ray space) of some graph? Formally, is $(T)^2$ homeomorphic to an end space or a ray space?
solved_when: A proof that for every special Aronszajn tree $T$, $(T)^2$ is an end space or a ray space, or a counterexample exhibiting a special Aronszajn tree $T$ for which $(T)^2$ is neither.
why: It would extend the known characterizations of end and ray spaces to a class of spaces built from special Aronszajn trees, clarifying the classification of these spaces up to homeomorphism.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11561v2 (Matheus Duzi, Gabriel Fernandes, Paulo Magalhães Júnior)

title: Any Proof of Polynomial Hirsch Must be Completely Incoherent
open: Does there exist a version of the simplex method that runs in polynomial time? Formally, this asks whether the diameter of polytopes arising in linear optimization — governed by the polynomial Hirsch conjecture — can be bounded polynomially, since a false polynomial Hirsch conjecture would unconditionally answer the question in the negative.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.11628v1 (Alexander E. Black, Lei Xue).
solved_when: A polynomial-time variant of the simplex method is exhibited, or the polynomial Hirsch conjecture is refuted (which would unconditionally rule out any such polynomial-time simplex method).
why: A positive answer would give a pivoting rule for the simplex method with guaranteed polynomial running time, while a negative answer via polynomial Hirsch would definitively close off this route to polynomial-time linear optimization.

title: From roots to paths: graphs simultaneously irregular with respect to r — conjecture con1
open: For every connected graph $F$ of order at least $3$, there exists a nontrivial $F$-irregular graph.
solved_when: A proof (or explicit construction) establishes the existence of a nontrivial $F$-irregular graph for every connected graph $F$ on at least $3$ vertices, or a counterexample identifies a connected $F$ of order at least $3$ for which no such graph exists.
why: It would settle the basic existence question for simultaneous irregularity with respect to any connected root graph, determining whether irregularity assignments can always be realized nontrivially regardless of the choice of $F$.

title: From roots to paths: graphs simultaneously irregular with respect to r — conjecture con2
open: Does every connected graph $F$ with at least 3 vertices have infinitely many $F$-irregular graphs — graphs whose irregularity is witnessed through $F$ rather than a single vertex or edge? Formally: for each connected graph $F$ of order $|F| \ge 3$, do there exist infinitely many $F$-irregular graphs?
solved_when: For every connected graph $F$ of order at least 3, infinitely many $F$-irregular graphs are exhibited (or the conjecture is refuted by a counterexample $F$).
why: It extends classical irregularity questions from roots (vertices) to paths, settling whether connected graphs of order at least 3 all admit infinite irregular families.

title: From roots to paths: graphs simultaneously irregular with respect to r — conjecture con3
open: For every connected graph $F$ of order $|F| \ge 3$ and each root $r$ of $F$, do there exist infinitely many $(F)_r$-irregular graphs? Formally, the conjecture (con3) asserts this always holds, with the single exception that $F = K_{1,n-1}$ and $r$ is the center of the star.
solved_when: The conjecture is proved, or refuted by an explicit counterexample, for every connected rooted graph $(F, r)$ with $|F| \ge 3$ other than the star $K_{1,n-1}$ rooted at its center.
why: Settling it would determine exactly which rooted graphs can serve as irregularity targets in infinitely many host graphs, completing the classification promised by the "roots to paths" program.

title: Induced-Minor-Closed Classes have Linear, Square-Root, or Sub-Polynomi
open: Does Independent Set admit a polynomial-time algorithm on even-hole-free graphs? This is asked even though even-hole-free graphs form a class far less general than the induced-minor-closed families considered in the source paper.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2607.12090v1 (Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Ajaykrishnan E S), where it is remarked that the existence of a polynomial-time algorithm for Independent Set on even-hole-free graphs remains a prominent open problem.
solved_when: A polynomial-time algorithm for Independent Set on even-hole-free graphs is given (or the problem is shown to be hard on this class, settling the question in the negative direction).
why: Even-hole-free graphs are a much less general class than the induced-minor-closed classes studied, so a polynomial-time algorithm (or hardness) here would clarify the true algorithmic boundary for Independent Set on hereditary graph classes.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12090v1 (Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Ajaykrishnan E S)

title: On strongly regular signed graphs of higher girth
open: Are the strongly regular signed graphs of higher girth arising in this setting homogeneously signed? Formally, we conjecture that every such graph carries a homogeneous signing; this is proven for the small Clebsch graph, and the question remains open in general, including for bipartite cases with equal color classes.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), by Quaid Iqbal and Thomas Zaslavsky (http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12131v1), where the conjecture of homogeneous signing is made and proved only for the small Clebsch graph.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every strongly regular signed graph of higher girth in the considered family is homogeneously signed, extending beyond the small Clebsch graph where the result is already established.
why: Resolving the conjecture would complete the signing classification of these higher-girth strongly regular signed graphs, confirming that no genuinely non-homogeneous signings occur in this family.

title: A Survey on Code Equivalence: The State-of-the-Art and Open Questions
open: Given two $[n,k]_q$ linear codes $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{C}'$, can one efficiently decide whether they are equivalent — that is, find (if it exists) a map in $(\mathrm{GL}_k(\mathbb{F}_q) \times S_n)$ sending one code to the other?
solved_when: An algorithm is given that, on input two $[n,k]_q$ linear codes $\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C}'$, either outputs an element of $(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^n \rtimes S_n$ carrying $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{C}'$ or correctly reports that no such map exists.
why: The (permutation) code equivalence problem underlies the security of several post-quantum cryptographic schemes, so a resolution — either an efficient algorithm or a hardness proof — directly settles the safety of those constructions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12870v2 (Anna-Lena Horlemann, Abhinaba Mazumder, Michael Schaller)

title: A Survey on Code Equivalence: The State-of-the-Art and Open Questions
open: Given a multiplicative subgroup $U \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^*$ and two $[n,k]_q$ linear codes $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{C}'$, does there exist an isometry $\varphi = (d, \sigma) \in U^n \rtimes S_n$ with $\varphi(\mathcal{C}) = \mathcal{C}'$, and if so, can we find it? Formally, the problem asks to decide equivalence of codes under the semilinear action where scalings are restricted to $U$ and coordinates may be permuted.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source survey (2026), arXiv:2607.12870v2 (Anna-Lena Horlemann, Abhinaba Mazumder, Michael Schaller).
solved_when: An algorithm is given that, for any multiplicative subgroup $U \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^*$ and any two $[n,k]_q$ linear codes, either produces an isometry $\varphi = (d, \sigma) \in U^n \rtimes S_n$ mapping $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{C}'$ or proves none exists.
why: Code equivalence under restricted scaling groups interpolates between the classical permutation and monomial equivalence problems, so a solution clarifies the boundary between tractable and hard equivalence problems underlying code-based cryptography.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12870v2 (Anna-Lena Horlemann, Abhinaba Mazumder, Michael Schaller)

title: A Survey on Code Equivalence: The State-of-the-Art and Open Questions
open: Let $0 < k' \leq k \leq n$. Given an $[n,k]_q$ code $C$ and an $[n,k']_q$ code $C'$, does there exist a permutation $\sigma \in S_n$ such that $C' = \sigma(C)$? If so, can we find such a permutation efficiently?
solved_when: An algorithm is given that, for arbitrary $0 < k' \leq k \leq n$ and codes $C \in [n,k]_q$, $C' \in [n,k']_q$, decides whether some $\sigma \in S_n$ satisfies $C' = \sigma(C)$, and produces such a $\sigma$ when it exists.
why: This generalizes the classical code equivalence problem to codes of different dimensions, and a solution would clarify how much of the hardness underlying code-equivalence-based cryptography survives when the dimensions are allowed to differ.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12870v2 (Anna-Lena Horlemann, Abhinaba Mazumder, Michael Schaller)

title: A Survey on Code Equivalence: The State-of-the-Art and Open Questions
