open: Must the genus polynomial of every graph have only real roots? Equivalently, is it the case that for every finite graph, all roots of its genus distribution polynomial are real?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit graph whose genus polynomial has a non-real root) that every graph's genus polynomial has only real roots.
why: Real-rootedness would imply asymptotic normality and unimodality of genus distributions, settling the broader structural behavior of how graph embeddings distribute across genera.

title: On the Asymptotic Normality and Unimodality of Genus Distributions of — conjecture c1:1
open: Is the genus distribution of every graph log-concave, and hence unimodal? More formally, does the number of embeddings at genus g divided by the number at genus g−1 decrease monotonically as g increases, for all graphs?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.05584v2 (Yichao Chen, Yan Yang).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that the genus distribution sequence of every graph is log-concave, i.e., the conjecture as stated in the source paper.
why: Log-concavity would immediately yield unimodality and asymptotic normality of genus distributions, giving a clean structural picture of how embeddings spread across genera.

title: On the Asymptotic Normality and Unimodality of Genus Distributions of — conjecture c1:3
open: Is the genus distribution of every graph unimodal — that is, does the number of embeddings over the genera always rise to a single peak and then fall? In formal terms, is the sequence $\{d_i(G)\}$, where $d_i(G)$ counts the cellular embeddings of $G$ in the orientable surface of genus $i$, unimodal for every graph $G$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.05584v2 (Yichao Chen, Yan Yang); no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the genus distribution is unimodal for every finite graph; a counterexample consisting of a single graph whose genus distribution is not unimodal would resolve the conjecture negatively.
why: Unimodality would give a clean structural law for how embeddings spread across genera, guiding enumeration and asymptotic analysis of genus distributions.

title: On the Asymptotic Normality and Unimodality of Genus Distributions of — question q1:4
open: Are the genus distributions of bouquets, dipoles, and wheel graphs asymptotically normal? More precisely, does the sequence of coefficients of the genus polynomial, suitably normalized, converge in distribution to a Gaussian?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.05584v2 (Yichao Chen, Yan Yang); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the genus distributions of bouquets, dipoles, and wheel graphs are asymptotically normal, i.e., that the normalized coefficient counts of their genus polynomials converge to a normal distribution.
why: These families are among the most basic examples in topological graph theory, so confirming (or refuting) asymptotic normality would settle a fundamental structural question about how embeddings distribute across genera and would likely illuminate the technique needed for broader families.

title: Erdős--Ko--Rado and Hilton--Milner Theorems in the Partition Lattice
open: For intersecting families of partitions in the partition lattice, how large does the ground set need to be before the classical Erdős–Ko–Rado and Hilton–Milner type conclusions take hold? Formally, determine the least $n_0(k,t)$ for which the conclusion of the corresponding theorem holds, as stated as an open problem in the source paper.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Mengyu Cao, Jiaqi Liao, Haixiang Zhang, arXiv:2608.05951v1 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05951v1); no bounds on $n_0(k,t)$ are given in the record.
solved_when: An explicit determination of the least $n_0(k,t)$ (with matching upper and lower bounds) is given, so that the theorem's conclusion is proved to hold for all $n \geq n_0(k,t)$ and to fail for $n < n_0(k,t)$.
why: It supplies the sharp threshold at which the extremal structure of intersecting families of partitions is fully characterized, extending the classical set-system theory to the partition lattice.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05951v1 (Mengyu Cao, Jiaqi Liao, Haixiang Zhang)

title: Maximizing directed cycles in tournaments
open: Is it true that every graph with positive edge density must contain the "expected" number of copies of any fixed bipartite pattern? Formally, for every bipartite graph $H$ with $v$ vertices and $e$ edges, and every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with edge density $p>0$, must $G$ contain at least $(p^e + o(1))n^v$ copies of $H$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Maximizing directed cycles in tournaments — conjecture 1," available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06238v1 (Yijia Fang, Hao Huang).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given of the statement that every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with edge density $p>0$ contains at least $(p^e + o(1))n^v$ copies of every bipartite graph $H$ with $v$ vertices and $e$ edges, for all $H$, $G$, and $p>0$.
why: This is the natural counting counterpart to the Sidorenko-type embedding question for bipartite graphs: it would confirm that positive density alone forces asymptotically optimal copy counts, and a counterexample would reveal a fundamental obstruction to density-based counting.

title: Maximizing directed cycles in tournaments
open: For every fixed \(k \geq 3\), and every sufficiently large odd integer \(n\), does the carousel tournament \({Car}_n\) always contain more directed \(4k\)-cycles than any other \(n\)-vertex tournament? In other words, is \({Car}_n\) the extremal tournament for maximizing the number of directed \(4k\)-cycles in this regime?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06238v1 (Yijia Fang, Hao Huang); no partial results are recorded here.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that, for each fixed \(k \geq 3\) and all sufficiently large odd \(n\), the carousel tournament \({Car}_n\) maximizes the number of directed \(4k\)-cycles among all \(n\)-vertex tournaments.
why: It would extend the extremal theory of cycle counts in tournaments, showing the carousel structure is optimal for a broad infinite family of even-length cycles rather than isolated cases.

title: Shor's algorithm requires Fanout
open: Is fanout really necessary to perform the quantum Fourier transform in constant depth — that is, can no constant-depth circuit without a fanout gate compute the QFT, or does such a circuit exist? This is the question posed by Fang, Fenner, Green, Homer and Zhang in 2006, here asked in the setting relevant to Shor's algorithm.
solved_when: A proof that fanout is necessary for constant-depth quantum Fourier transform (or, conversely, an explicit constant-depth QFT construction avoiding fanout), affirmatively resolving the Fang–Fenner–Green–Homer–Zhang question.
why: It would pin down the exact depth resources required by the Fourier transform step of Shor's algorithm, clarifying which primitive gates are indispensable for constant-depth quantum arithmetic.

title: On the size of $(K_{t_1}, \ldots, K_{t_k})$-co-critical graphs — conj c:mindeg
open: Let $r = R(K_{t_1}, \ldots, K_{t_k})$ and let $G$ be a $(K_{t_1}, \ldots, K_{t_k})$-co-critical graph on $n \ge r$ vertices. Is the minimum degree of $G$ always at least $r-2$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07422v2 (Zi-Xia Song).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) that every $(K_{t_1}, \ldots, K_{t_k})$-co-critical graph on $n \ge r$ vertices, where $r = R(K_{t_1}, \ldots, K_{t_k})$, has minimum degree at least $r-2$.
why: A universal minimum-degree lower bound would give immediate control over the edge count of co-critical graphs, the central quantity in the study of their extremal size.

title: On the size of $(K_{t_1}, \ldots, K_{t_k})$-co-critical graphs
open: Are there infinitely many strongly minimal co-critical graphs? Here, a $(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$-co-critical graph is strongly minimal if it contains no proper subgraph which is itself $(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$-co-critical, and the question is whether such graphs exist in infinite number.
solved_when: A proof, or disproof, that infinitely many strongly minimal $(K_{t_1},\ldots,K_{t_k})$-co-critical graphs exist.
why: It would clarify the extremal structure of co-critical graphs, determining whether minimality is a rare finite phenomenon or a robust infinite family.

title: The $Δ$-Conjecture for CIS $d$-Graphs — conjecture conj:delta
open: Is every CIS \(d\)-graph a Gallai graph? Equivalently, does the conjecture (conj:delta) hold that the CIS property forces the Gallai structure for \(d\)-graphs?
solved_when: A proof that every CIS \(d\)-graph is Gallai, or a counterexample exhibiting a CIS \(d\)-graph that is not Gallai.
why: It would settle conjecture conj:delta and clarify the structural constraints the CIS property imposes on \(d\)-graphs.

title: A proof of the cyclotomic conjecture and the non-existence of almost M
open: Given natural numbers $d$ and $k$, what is the largest possible number of vertices in a directed graph whose maximum out-degree is at most $d$ and whose diameter is at most $k$? Formally, let $D(d,k)$ denote the collection of digraphs with maximum out-degree at most $d$ and diameter at most $k$, and determine the largest order $n_{d,k}$ of a digraph in $D(d,k)$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08997v1 (Jaskaran Kaur, Hitesh Kumar).
solved_when: An explicit determination of $n_{d,k}$ — the largest order of a digraph in $D(d,k)$ — for all natural numbers $d$ and $k$, or a proof characterizing it.
why: This is the degree–diameter problem for digraphs: bounding $n_{d,k}$ determines how large a communication network can be while keeping both the number of links per node and the maximum hop-distance bounded.

title: On a conjecture of Kolokolnikov on algebraic connectivity — conj conj::kolokolnikov
open: Among all graphs on $n$ vertices with exactly $2(n-2)$ edges, does the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,n-2}$ maximize the algebraic connectivity?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, with counterexample) that $K_{2,n-2}$ maximizes the second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalue among all graphs on $n$ vertices with exactly $2(n-2)$ edges.
why: It settles Kolokolnikov's conjectured extremal characterization of algebraic connectivity at this edge density, sharpening our understanding of how sparse graphs can maintain high connectivity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09822v1 (Cheng Chi, Junjie Wang, Jiaxin Zheng)

title: Disproving the Petersen Coloring Conjecture: Theoretical Analysis and
open: Does every bridgeless cubic graph admit a homomorphism to the Petersen graph ($P$-coloring), as the Petersen Coloring Conjecture asserts, and if not, what is the smallest bridgeless cubic graph with no such coloring? Equivalently: determine the minimum order of a counterexample, or prove none exists.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10028v4 (Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Edita Máčajová).
solved_when: Either a proof that every bridgeless cubic graph is $P$-colorable is given, or an explicit bridgeless cubic graph with no $P$-coloring is exhibited and its order is shown to be minimal among such graphs.
why: The Petersen Coloring Conjecture sits at the intersection of graph coloring and cycle-cover theory; a disproof via a smallest counterexample would overturn it, while a minimality result would sharply delimit where the conjecture can fail and guide the search for further counterexamples.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10028v4 (Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Edita Máčajová)

title: Disproving the Petersen Coloring Conjecture: Theoretical Analysis and — conjecture PCC
open: Does every bridgeless cubic graph admit a homomorphism to the Petersen graph — that is, a Petersen coloring? A second sentence could formalize: is there a mapping of vertices preserving adjacency into $P$ for every bridgeless cubic graph?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.10028v4, by Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, and Edita Máčajová.
solved_when: A proof that every bridgeless cubic graph admits a $P$-coloring, or an explicit bridgeless cubic graph with no such coloring, is given.
why: The Petersen Coloring Conjecture is a central unifying conjecture in cubic graph theory: it implies several other long-standing conjectures on cycle covers and edge colorings of cubic graphs, so a counterexample or proof would reshape that landscape.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10028v4 (Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Edita Máčajová)

title: Disproving the Petersen Coloring Conjecture: Theoretical Analysis and
open: Does every cyclically $5$-edge-connected cubic graph admit a Petersen coloring, or is there a counterexample? Formally: do there exist cyclically $5$-edge-connected cubic graphs that do not admit a $P$-coloring?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) (Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Edita Máčajová, arXiv:2608.10028v4, http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10028v4).
solved_when: Either a cyclically $5$-edge-connected cubic graph with no $P$-coloring is exhibited (disproof), or it is proved that every cyclically $5$-edge-connected cubic graph admits a $P$-coloring.
why: A counterexample would refute the Petersen Coloring Conjecture, while a proof would settle it for this natural class; either outcome sharply constrains the conjecture's scope.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10028v4 (Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Edita Máčajová)

title: Online Discrepancy Minimization for Sub-Gaussian Inputs via Regulariza — conjecture conj:OfflineDiscrepancy
open: For every fixed $k>1$, is there no randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, with high probability, finds a signing of $T = n^k$ independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with discrepancy $o(\sqrt{n})$?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given of the statement above: for every fixed $k>1$, either establish the impossibility of any randomized polynomial-time algorithm finding, with high probability, a signing of $T = n^k$ independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with discrepancy $o(\sqrt{n})$, or exhibit such an algorithm.
why: It would establish a computational complexity barrier for online discrepancy minimization: even with many samples ($T = n^k$) from a benign sub-Gaussian distribution, no efficient algorithm can push the discrepancy below the $\sqrt{n}$ scale.

title: A proof of the $m$-Symmetric Macdonald positivity at $t=1$ — conjecture mainconjec
open: Are the $m$-symmetric Macdonald polynomials, in their integral form, positive in an appropriate sense at $t=1$, as conjectured in conjecture mainconjec? More precisely, does the integrality form of these polynomials admit a positivity structure establishing the conjecture?
solved_when: A proof of the $m$-symmetric Macdonald positivity at $t=1$, as stated in conjecture mainconjec from paper 2608.10223, is given.

title: No extremal square-free words over alphabets of size at least 5 — conjecture conj:no-extremal-squarefree-4
open: There is no extremal square-free word over an alphabet of size at least~$4$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.10591v1 (Eng Keat Hng, Silas Rathke).
solved_when: A proof establishes that no extremal square-free word exists over any alphabet of size at least~$4$; equivalently, over every such alphabet, every square-free word can be extended to a longer square-free word.
why: It would settle whether arbitrarily long square-free words can always be grown from any starting word on these alphabets, a basic structural question about how square-freeness constrains word extension.

title: No extremal square-free words over alphabets of size at least 5 — conjecture conj:nonchalant-infinite
open: Is the sequence of nonchalant square-free words over any linearly ordered alphabet of size at least 5 infinite? Formally, for every alphabet of size k ≥ 5 with a linear ordering, the sequence of nonchalant words over that ordered alphabet is infinite.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that, for every alphabet of size at least 5 equipped with a linear ordering, infinitely many nonchalant words exist.
why: It would settle whether extremal square-free words — square-free words to which no letter can be appended while preserving square-freeness — fail to exist over large alphabets, resolving the conjecture conj:nonchalant-infinite.

title: No extremal square-free words over alphabets of size at least 5 — conjecture conj:no-extremal-squarefree-4-only
open: Does every alphabet of size at least 5 admit arbitrarily long square-free words, so that no word is extremal? In formal terms, the conjecture asserts that extremal square-free words exist only over the alphabet of size 4 and not over alphabets of size at least 5.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that no extremal square-free word exists over any alphabet of size at least 5.
why: It would complete the picture of where square-free words terminate, identifying size 4 as the unique alphabet where extremal square-free words occur.

title: Kohayakawa's conjecture and clique coverings of complements of paths a — conjecture conj:dcgp
open: Does the complement of every path admit a clique covering satisfying Kohayakawa's conjecture (as recorded for conjecture conj:dcgp in paper 2608.11132)?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjecture as stated in the record is given; no quantitative targets are specified in the record.

title: Reversible Analog Computation using Chemical Reaction Networks
open: Does adding one more chemical species strictly increase the class of reals computable by reversible chemical reaction networks? Formally, for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, is the set $R_{RevCRN}^{ns}$ of RevCRN-computable reals using $n$ species a strict subset of $R_{RevCRN}^{(n+1)s}$, the corresponding set with $n+1$ species?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Reversible Analog Computation using Chemical Reaction Networks — conjecture 4," available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11362v2 (Saptarshi Biswas, James I. Lathrop, Rana D. Parshad). No progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that $R_{RevCRN}^{ns} \subsetneq R_{RevCRN}^{(n+1)s}$ holds for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$; no quantitative budgets beyond the species-count parameter appear in the record.
why: Resolving it would establish whether reversible chemical reaction networks form a strict hierarchy of computational power by species count, characterizing the resources needed to compute specific reals reversibly.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11362v2 (Saptarshi Biswas, James I. Lathrop, Rana D. Parshad)

title: A dense-case theorem for Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture
open: Does every finite oriented graph have a Seymour vertex — a vertex whose second out-neighborhood is at least as large as its first? This is the first conjecture of Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the existence of a Seymour vertex in every finite oriented graph.
why: A resolution would settle the foundational case of Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture, a basic structural question about oriented graphs with connections to digraph coloring and extremal problems.

title: Sparse spanning $k$-strong oriented subdigraphs in split digraphs — conjecture conj1
open: Does every $2k$-strong digraph contain a spanning $k$-strong oriented subdigraph? Formally, the Jackson–Thomassen conjecture asserts that $2k$ vertex-strong-connectivity guarantees a spanning orientation-preserving subdigraph that remains $k$-strong.
status: The conjecture is due to Jackson and Thomassen and is stated as open in the source paper (2026), a curated open-problems paper by Jia Zhou, Jørgen Bang-Jensen, and Jin Yan (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11578v1).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the statement that every $2k$-strong digraph contains a spanning $k$-strong oriented subdigraph, for general $k$.
why: It would give a sharp relationship between strong connectivity and the existence of well-connected oriented spanning substructures, a basic structural question for digraphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11578v1 (Jia Zhou, Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Jin Yan)

title: Sparse spanning $k$-strong oriented subdigraphs in split digraphs — conjecture conj2
open: Does every highly connected directed graph contain a sparse spanning subgraph of the same connectivity? Formally, there is a constant $C > 0$ such that for integers $k, l, n$ with $n$ large enough, every $k$-strong digraph $D$ of order $n$ whose minimum degree exceeds $n - l$ contains a spanning $k$-strong subdigraph with at most $kn + kl + Ck^2$ arcs.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the existence of an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that the bound $kn + kl + Ck^2$ arcs holds for all integers $k, l, n$ satisfying the hypotheses on every $k$-strong digraph of order $n$ with minimum degree greater than $n - l$.
why: It would establish that near-complete connectivity in digraphs can be preserved by spanning subdigraphs with only a linear number of extra arcs, a sharp quantitative form of sparsification for highly connected directed networks.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11578v1 (Jia Zhou, Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Jin Yan)

title: Sparse spanning $k$-strong oriented subdigraphs in split digraphs
open: Does there exist a function $h(k)$ such that every graph $G$ which is weakly-$2k$-connected and with minimum degree $\delta(G) \geq h(k)$ has a $k$-strong orientation?
solved_when: An explicit function $h(k)$ is given (or its existence proved) such that every weakly-$2k$-connected graph with minimum degree at least $h(k)$ admits a $k$-strong orientation.
why: It would give a degree-based sufficient condition guaranteeing highly strong orientations, extending orientation theory beyond pure connectivity assumptions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11578v1 (Jia Zhou, Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Jin Yan)

title: Bijective proofs of several conjectures on Jacobi permutations — conjecture con1
open: Is it true that for all $n \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$ the number of Jacobi permutations $j_{n,k}$ equals $E_{n,k}$, and if so, can this identity be established by an explicit bijection? A formal statement of the goal is a bijective proof of the conjecture that $j_{n,k} = E_{n,k}$ for all $n \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Bijective proofs of several conjectures on Jacobi permutations" by Zhicong Lin, Yongzhou Wen, and Sherry H. F. Yan (arXiv:2608.11771v1).
solved_when: A construction (explicit bijection or rigorous proof) is given showing that $j_{n,k} = E_{n,k}$ holds for every $n \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$.
why: A bijective proof would reveal the structural correspondence between Jacobi permutations and the objects counted by $E_{n,k}$, turning an enumerative coincidence into a combinatorial explanation.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11771v1 (Zhicong Lin, Yongzhou Wen, Sherry H. F. Yan)

title: Two Relaxations of the Dominating Hadwiger's Conjecture — question q:Bruce
open: For which functions $f$ does $Rc(H) < f(c(H))$ hold for every graph $H$? In particular, is there a constant $c$ such that this holds with $f(x) = x + c$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12126v1 (António Girão, Sergey Norin, Youri Tamitegama).
solved_when: A characterization of the functions $f$ for which $Rc(H) < f(c(H))$ holds for every graph $H$ is given; in particular, a constant $c$ is identified such that $Rc(H) < c(H) + c$ for every graph $H$.
why: It would resolve a natural relaxation of the dominating Hadwiger's Conjecture, clarifying how the relevant two parameters of a graph can deviate.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12126v1 (António Girão, Sergey Norin, Youri Tamitegama)

title: Two Relaxations of the Dominating Hadwiger's Conjecture
open: For every positive integer $t$, must there exist a constant $c_t > 0$ such that the vertex set of any graph $G$ containing no dominating $K_t$-model can be partitioned into $t-1$ parts $X_1, \ldots, X_{t-1}$ where each induced subgraph $G[X_i]$ has no component with more than $c_t$ vertices?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Two Relaxations of the Dominating Hadwiger's Conjecture," available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12126v1 (António Girão, Sergey Norin, Youri Tamitegama); no cases are resolved.
solved_when: For each positive integer $t$, a constant $c_t > 0$ is exhibited (and the partition shown to exist for every graph with no dominating $K_t$-model) satisfying the stated bound, with all component sizes in each part bounded by $c_t$.
why: It would establish a bounded-component analogue of dominating Hadwiger's conjecture, showing that graphs without a dominating $K_t$-model admit an almost-proper coloring into $t-1$ parts whose components have uniformly bounded size.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12126v1 (António Girão, Sergey Norin, Youri Tamitegama)

title: On the Total Regularity of Almost Mixed Moore Graphs
open: Is every almost mixed Moore graph with defect 2 — that is, an $(r,z,k;-2)$-graph with $r, z \ge 1$ and $k \ge 2$ — totally regular? In other words, must such a graph be regular in both its arc and edge structure?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Ethan Shallcross, http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12425v1.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that all $(r,z,k;-2)$-graphs are totally regular for every $r, z \ge 1$ and $k \ge 2$.
why: Total regularity is a basic structural property expected of almost mixed Moore graphs; establishing it would complete our understanding of the defect-2 case of the degree/diameter problem for mixed Moore graphs.

title: On the Total Regularity of Almost Mixed Moore Graphs
open: For which values of $r$, $z$, and $k$ does there exist an $(r,z,k;-2)$-graph? In other words, determine the parameter triples for which such an almost mixed Moore graph exists.
solved_when: A complete characterization of the triples $(r,z,k)$ for which an $(r,z,k;-2)$-graph exists is given.
why: It would settle an existence question in the theory of almost mixed Moore graphs, refining the degree/diameter landscape beyond the Moore bound.

title: A relaxation of the Bermond-Thomassen conjecture
open: Is it true that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $2k-1$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles, for every positive integer $k$? Formally: for each positive integer $k$, must every digraph $D$ with $\delta^+(D) \geq 2k-1$ contain $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $2k-1$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles, for every positive integer $k$.
why: This is a relaxation of the Bermond–Thomassen conjecture; resolving it would advance our understanding of when high out-degree forces many disjoint directed cycles in digraphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12948v1 (Stéphane Bessy, Matthijs Muis, Jean-Sébastien Sereni)

title: On a conjecture of Corradi and Katai — question Question "Sarnak"
open: Is it true that $|{G}_{2}(N)| < N-1$ for all $N > 1$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.13266v1 (Krishnarjun Krishnamoorthy).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the bound $|{G}_{2}(N)| < N-1$ for every integer $N > 1$.
why: This is a question of Sarnak on a conjecture of Corradi and Kátai; resolving it settles the size of ${G}_{2}(N)$ unconditionally.

title: A Finite Automaton Approach to Combinatorial Games
open: Does every impartial or partizan octal game admit an outcome DFA — that is, can its outcome sequence be recognized by a finite automaton? More sharply, is finite automaton recognition of outcomes universal across the class of octal games?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "A Finite Automaton Approach to Combinatorial Games" by Kai Liang (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13273v2).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that all impartial or partizan octal games admit an outcome DFA, per the question as posed.
why: A positive answer would give a decidable, automaton-computable characterization of winning positions for the entire class of octal games; a negative answer identifies concrete games whose outcome sequences escape finite-state description.

title: Every fork-free graph is perfectly weight divisible — question ques:fork
open: Does every fork-free graph admit a polynomial χ-biding function? In other words, is there a polynomial p such that every induced subgraph G of a fork-free graph satisfies χ(G) ≤ p(ω(G))?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.13519v1 (Feng Liu, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang); no bound is currently recorded in the census.
solved_when: An explicit polynomial p is exhibited (or proved to exist) such that χ(G) ≤ p(ω(G)) for every fork-free graph G and all its induced subgraphs; equivalently, the class of fork-free graphs is shown to be χ-bounded by a polynomial binding function.
why: It would place fork-free graphs among the structurally tame hereditary classes, giving polynomial control of chromatic number by clique number; failure would exhibit a natural class where χ-boundedness cannot be polynomial.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13519v1 (Feng Liu, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang)

title: Every fork-free graph is perfectly weight divisible — conjecture forkconj
open: Is every fork-free graph perfectly weight divisible?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every fork-free graph is perfectly weight divisible.
why: Resolving it would advance the divisibility theory of hereditary graph classes defined by a single forbidden induced subgraph, a core theme of the source paper's program.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13519v1 (Feng Liu, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang)

title: Skew Hives, Skew Skeps, Skew Schur Log-Concavity — conjecture conj:log-concavity
open: Does the Schur Log-Concavity conjecture (conj:log-concavity) extend to skew shapes, as formulated in terms of skew hives and skew skeps?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the skew Schur log-concavity conjecture as stated in the source paper.
why: It would extend the Schur log-concavity framework to skew shapes, connecting hive and skep combinatorics with positivity and representation-theoretic structure beyond the non-skew setting.

title: Lower Bounds on Black-Box Constructions of Pseudorandom Functions
open: Can a pseudorandom function be constructed from a pseudorandom generator using only a single invocation of the PRG? More precisely, the question is whether black-box constructions of PRFs exist whose evaluation makes just one call to the underlying PRG oracle.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.14501v1 (Bar Alon, Itai Dinur, Muthuramakrishnan Venkitasubramaniam).
solved_when: A construction (or a proof of impossibility) of a PRF from a PRG with exactly one PRG invocation per evaluation, in the black-box setting, is established.
why: It would resolve the most basic efficiency question for black-box PRF constructions, settling whether the known invocation counts are inherent or merely an artifact of current techniques.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14501v1 (Bar Alon, Itai Dinur, Muthuramakrishnan Venkitasubramaniam)

title: Ordered Ruzsa-Szemeredi Numbers at Matching Size Two — problem prob:linear
open: Is the ordered Ruzsa–Szemerédi number of the two-edge matching, $2K_2$, exactly $32n + O(1)$? More weakly, does it grow linearly in $n$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.14695v2 (Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao). No bounds beyond the stated question are recorded.
solved_when: The value of $n2\text{-}(n, 2K_2)$ is determined to be $32n + O(1)$, or at minimum it is shown to be $O(n)$.
why: Determining this ordered Ruzsa–Szemerédi number pins down the exact extremal behavior for matchings in the ordered setting, where even matching-size-two cases can be open.

title: On the Log-submodularity for zonoids: from Mixed Volume inequalities t
open: Does the log-submodularity inequality for zonoids, formulated via mixed volume inequalities, hold for the hypercube? A second sentence would sharpen it formally, but the record gives only this informal framing, so we restate it plainly: is the hypercube inequality for log-submodularity of zonoids true, and it appears resistant to purely computational attack with current technology.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the hypercube inequality for log-submodularity of zonoids is established; no quantitative targets are stated in the record.
why: The source work reflects on the power and pitfalls of computer-assisted methods for exact inequalities, so settling this case would clarify the limits of such methods and advance mixed-volume inequality theory for zonoids.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14909v1 (Gennadiy Averkov, Katherina von Dichter, Ivan Soprunov)

title: On the Log-submodularity for zonoids: from Mixed Volume inequalities t
open: What is the largest possible volume of a simplex contained in a hypercube? This classical question, which remains open, is closely tied to the Hadamard maximum determinant problem.
status: Stated as an open question in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.14909v1 (Gennadiy Averkov, Katherina von Dichter, Ivan Soprunov); no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A complete determination of the maximum volume of a simplex inscribed in a hypercube (equivalently, a resolution of the corresponding instance of the Hadamard maximum determinant problem) is obtained.
why: Progress would advance the study of mixed volume inequalities and log-submodularity for zonoids, where maximum-determinant-type quantities arise naturally as extremal cases.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14909v1 (Gennadiy Averkov, Katherina von Dichter, Ivan Soprunov)

title: Linking invariants of spatial graphs — problem op:set_lk
open: For each $n$, which ordered tuples of integers can arise as the tuple of linking numbers of an embedding of $K_n^3$? Equivalently, characterize exactly the set of realizable linking-coefficient tuples for embeddings of the complete 3-partite graph $K_n^3$.
solved_when: For every $n$, a complete description is given of the ordered integer tuples realizable as the linking numbers of some embedding of $K_n^3$.
why: A full characterization would give an effective invariant-theoretic handle on spatial embeddings of spatial graphs, determining exactly what linking data embeddings of $K_n^3$ can carry.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15860v1 (E. Alkin, Yu. Khromin, A. Skopenkov)

title: Linking invariants of spatial graphs — problem e:wu-k5
open: What is the Wu–Simon number of the plane diagram shown in the figure (left)? Any choice of vertex numeration is allowed.
solved_when: A value of the Wu–Simon number is determined for the plane diagram of Figure (left), under some explicit numeration of the vertices.

title: Two conjectures on graphs and their edge-path matrices — conjecture C-2
open: Is a simple graph Eulerian exactly when every entry of its edge-path matrix is even? In other words, does all-evenness of the edge-path matrix characterize Eulerian graphs?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.15992v1 (Metrose Metsidik, Xian'an Jin); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof or disproof of the equivalence: a simple graph is Eulerian if and only if every entry of its edge-path matrix is even.
why: It would establish a clean parity characterization of Eulerian graphs via edge-path matrices, connecting graph traversability to a matrix invariant.

title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery
open: Theorem~ closes the route to the three-dimensional Nikodym conjecture through Conjecture~1.4 of , but says nothing about the Nikodym conjecture itself, which remains open.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16977v1 (Zeyu Zheng, Shengtong Zhang, Jeremy Avigad)

title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery
open: Does the MATH-uniform case of Conjecture 6.2 hold? This case, which constitutes the bulk of the conjecture, remains unresolved.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the MATH-uniform case of Conjecture 6.2 is given.
why: It settles the main portion of Conjecture 6.2 from the source paper, advancing the program of scalable mathematical discovery it proposes.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16977v1 (Zeyu Zheng, Shengtong Zhang, Jeremy Avigad)

title: Non-vanishing of Single, Double, and Triple Schubert Structure Constan
open: Do the Schubert structure constants exhibit a two-tier vanishing structure — that is, is the double support determined by the single support? Formally, with the single support ¹(u,v) = {w ∈ S : c_{u,v}^w ≠ 0} and the double support ²(u,v) = {w ∈ S : c_{u,v}^w(t) ≠ 0}, the conjecture is that ²(u,v) is determined by ¹(u,v).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given that the double support ²(u,v) is determined by the single support ¹(u,v) for all u, v.
why: Mulmuley identified Schubert coefficients as one of the fundamental structural constants whose vanishing needs to be understood; resolving this would give a systematic handle on the non-vanishing behavior of single, double, and triple Schubert structure constants.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17378v1 (Yiming Chen, Neil J. Y. Fan, Rui Xiong)

title: Non-vanishing of Single, Double, and Triple Schubert Structure Constan
open: Is there a positive combinatorial rule — an explicit combinatorial interpretation — for the single, double, and triple Schubert structure constants? A formal answer would give a manifestly positive counting description of these coefficients.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.17378v1 (Yiming Chen, Neil J. Y. Fan, Rui Xiong).
solved_when: A combinatorial interpretation of the Schubert structure constants is given that makes their positivity manifest.
why: These constants govern intersection numbers in flag varieties, and a positive rule would turn geometric computations into explicit counting arguments, resolving a central question of algebraic combinatorics and enumerative geometry.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17378v1 (Yiming Chen, Neil J. Y. Fan, Rui Xiong)

title: Positive definite, positive semidefinite and totally positive matrices
open: For fixed positive integers $m$ and $n$, what is the smallest prime power $q$ for which an $m \times n$ totally positive matrix exists over $\mathbb{F}_q$? Equivalently, determine the minimal prime power $q$ admitting an $mn$ totally positive matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.17702v1 (Arvind Ayyer, Shubhanshu Prasad); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A formula or algorithm is given that, for any fixed positive integers $m$ and $n$, determines the minimal prime power $q$ such that an $mn$ totally positive matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$ exists.
why: It establishes the exact finite-field thresholds at which total positivity can be realized, completing the picture of how positivity notions for matrices behave over finite fields rather than the reals.

title: Positive definite, positive semidefinite and totally positive matrices
open: For a prime $p$ and positive integers $m, n$, do there exist a positive integer $t$ and rational polynomials $g_0(x), \dots, g_{t-1}(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of degree $mn$ such that the number of totally positive matrices in $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{F}_{p^k})$ equals $g_i(p^k)$ whenever $k \equiv i \pmod{t}$? In other words, is this counting function eventually quasipolynomial in the field size $p^k$, with quasipolynomial pieces of degree $mn$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.17702v1 (Arvind Ayyer, Shubhanshu Prasad). No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: Such $t$ and polynomials are exhibited (or proven to exist) for every prime $p$ and all positive integers $m, n$, each $g_i$ of degree $mn$, giving the count of totally positive matrices in $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{F}_{p^k})$ as $g_i(p^k)$ when $k \equiv i \pmod{t}$.
why: It would establish that the number of totally positive matrices over finite fields is governed by a quasipolynomial of degree $mn$ in the field size, placing these counts in the same quasipolynomial framework as related matrix-counting results.

title: A Complete Classification of Complex Hadamard Matrices of Order Six
open: Does the family of complex Hadamard matrices constructed in this work intersect any of the remaining Karlsson classes of order-six complex Hadamard matrices? A precise determination of which, if any, of these classes contain members of the constructed family would complete the picture sketched here.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), from arXiv:2608.18053v2 (Mateo Cárdenes Wuttig, Joseph Tindall); no intersection with the remaining Karlsson classes is determined there.
solved_when: The intersection of the constructed family with each remaining Karlsson class is explicitly determined (empty, or exhibited by explicit members), up to the standard equivalence notion for complex Hadamard matrices.
why: It settles how the newly constructed matrices sit within the known order-six landscape, closing the gap left by the source construction.

title: Hyperfiniteness of bounded-to-one actions of commutative monoids
open: Are the equivalence relations generated by countable families of pairwise commuting Borel functions hyperfinite? In other words, can hyperfiniteness — known for actions of this bounded-to-one kind — be generalized from the commuting setting's simpler cases to equivalence relations generated by countably many pairwise commuting Borel functions?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18439v2 (Forte Shinko, Felix Weilacher, Jing Yu).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every equivalence relation generated by a countable family of pairwise commuting Borel functions is hyperfinite, in the bounded-to-one setting of the source problem.
why: Resolving it would extend the hyperfiniteness toolbox from single transformations and simpler generators to the full commuting family setting, a basic structural question for Borel equivalence relations; a negative answer would exhibit a natural non-hyperfinite obstruction in commutative dynamics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18439v2 (Forte Shinko, Felix Weilacher, Jing Yu)

title: Any $k$-graph with zero $\ell$-degree Turán density is layered — conjecture conj:1.6
open: Is it true that a $3$-graph $F$ has vanishing codegree Turán density exactly when it is layered with ordinary Turán density zero? Formally: for a $3$-graph $F$, $\pi^{\mathrm{co}}(F) = 0$ if and only if $F$ is layered and satisfies $\pi(F)=0$.
status: Stated as an open conjecture (Conjecture 1.6) in the source paper (2026): Jiabao Yang, Xiaona Fang, Yaojun Chen, arXiv:2608.18542v1.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the equivalence "$\pi^{\mathrm{co}}(F) = 0$ iff $F$ is layered and $\pi(F)=0$" for $3$-graphs.
why: It would characterize, by an explicit structural property (layeredness), the $3$-graphs whose Turán problems become trivial in the codegree density setting, sharpening the analogy between ordinary and codegree Turán extremal behavior.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18542v1 (Jiabao Yang, Xiaona Fang, Yaojun Chen)

title: Any $k$-graph with zero $\ell$-degree Turán density is layered — conjecture conj:1.7
open: Is every linear $3$-graph $F$ with $ _{ {co}}(F) = 0$ layered, and conversely? That is, for a linear $3$-graph $F$, does $ _{ {co}}(F) = 0$ hold if and only if $F$ is layered?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Jiabao Yang, Xiaona Fang, Yaojun Chen, http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18542v1.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that, for linear $3$-graphs $F$, $ _{ {co}}(F) = 0$ if and only if $F$ is layered.
why: It would give a complete structural characterization of the linear $3$-graphs whose codegree Turán density vanishes, settling conjecture conj:1.7.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18542v1 (Jiabao Yang, Xiaona Fang, Yaojun Chen)

title: Decisional Monogamy-of-Entanglement for Coset States and Applications
open: Does a decisional monogamy-of-entanglement property hold for coset states, and can it be used to build copy-protection schemes for broad classes of functionalities? In particular, this asks for copy-protection of point functions, copy-protection of compute-and-compare programs, and identical-challenge secure copy-protection of decryption keys and all puncturable functionalities.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), from arXiv:2608.18841v2 (Amit Behera, Alper Cakan, Vipul Goyal), which presents it among open problems on decisional monogamy-of-entanglement for coset states and its applications.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of decisional monogamy-of-entanglement for coset states is given, together with copy-protection constructions (with identical-challenge security where stated) for point functions, compute-and-compare programs, decryption keys, and all puncturable functionalities.
why: It would settle long-standing open questions on which cryptographic functionalities can be copy-protected, extending protection beyond the few primitives currently known to support it.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18841v2 (Amit Behera, Alper Cakan, Vipul Goyal)

title: On the odd independence number of the Queen graph — conjecture Con_kraljica
open: Does the Queen graph of every finite size admit an independent set of odd cardinality? More precisely, is the odd independence number defined (and nonzero) for the Queen graph of any finite board?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, with an explicit counterexample board) resolving the conjecture Con_kraljica as stated in the source paper.
why: It would settle a natural parity question about independence in Queen graphs, complementing the classical study of domination and independence on the chessboard.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19024v1 (Martin Knor, Jelena Sedlar, Riste Škrekovski)

title: String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Proble
open: Which finitely presented monoids can be presented by a finite complete string-rewriting system? In other words, characterize those finitely presented monoids whose presentation admits a finite confluent terminating rewriting system.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Problems" by Assaf Kfoury (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19397v2). No partial resolution is recorded there.
solved_when: A verifiable criterion is given — structural, algorithmic, or otherwise — that decides, for an arbitrary finite monoid presentation, whether the monoid admits some finite complete string-rewriting system.
why: A characterization would connect algebraic properties of monoids to algorithmic ones, since finite complete systems yield decidable word problems via normal forms; conversely, knowing which monoids lack such systems delimits the power of rewriting methods.

title: String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Proble
open: Does every one-relator monoid admit a finite complete string rewriting system? That is, given a monoid defined by a single relation, can its word problem always be resolved by some finite confluent and terminating rewriting presentation?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Problems" by Assaf Kfoury, arXiv:2608.19397v2.
solved_when: A proof that every one-relator monoid admits a finite complete string rewriting system, or an explicit one-relator monoid with no such system.
why: A positive answer would give a uniform algorithmic solution to the word problem for all one-relator monoids via rewriting; a negative answer would exhibit a fundamental limit of finite complete presentations for this basic class.

title: String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Proble
open: Does every one-relator monoid have a decidable word problem? That is, given a monoid defined by a single defining relation, is there an algorithm that decides equality of words in it?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Problems" by Assaf Kfoury (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19397v2). No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An algorithm is exhibited that decides the word problem for every monoid presented with exactly one defining relation, or a specific one-relator monoid is constructed whose word problem is undecidable.
why: The word problem is the most basic decision question about a presented algebraic structure; a resolution in either direction would sharply delineate the boundary between decidable and undecidable rewriting, complementing the classical one-relator group case.

title: String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction and Sample of Open Proble
open: Does having finite derivation type fully characterize those monoids that admit a finite complete presentation? In other words, how far does this homotopy-theoretic finiteness condition go toward capturing the existence of finite convergent rewriting systems for monoids?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), a curated open-problems paper available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19397v2 (Assaf Kfoury).
solved_when: A precise determination of the extent to which finite derivation type characterizes monoids admitting finite complete presentations — for instance, a proof that the characterization holds, or a counterexample delimiting it.
why: Finite derivation type is a decidable-looking finiteness invariant that could serve as a practical test for finite complete presentability; clarifying its exact reach would sharpen the toolkit for deciding when a monoid admits a finite convergent rewriting system.

title: Pattern avoidance in canon permutations
open: Is the number of canon permutations of length $3k$ avoiding both patterns $213$ and $312$ exactly four times the $k$-th Catalan number, that is, $c_3^k(213,312) = 4C_k$?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the identity $c_3^k(213,312) = 4C_k$ for all $k \geq 1$, where $C_k$ denotes the $k$-th Catalan number.
why: It would resolve one of the conjectures on pattern avoidance in the canon permutation family, clarifying how Catalan structure manifests in these generalized permutations.

title: Asymptotic entanglement in circle stabilizer states and states forbidd — conjecture conj:geelen2
open: Does every family of stabilizer states exhibit asymptotically bounded entanglement structure of circle-graph type? Formally, for every PVMC family $\{F\}$ of stabilizer states, do there exist $k, p \in \mathbb{N}$ such that each state in $\{F\}$ that is $k$-rank-connected is locally equivalent to a rank-$p$ perturbation of a circle graph state?
status: The conjecture (conj:geelen2) is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21526v1 (Kenneth Goodenough, Marcelo Sales).
solved_when: Positive constants $k$ and $p$ are exhibited for an arbitrary PVMC family of stabilizer states such that every $k$-rank-connected member of the family is locally equivalent to a rank-$p$ perturbation of a circle graph state.
why: A proof would show that large, structured stabilizer families always reduce to perturbed circle graph states, giving a normal form for their entanglement; a refutation would exhibit stabilizer families whose entanglement genuinely escapes circle-graph structure.

title: Asymptotic entanglement in circle stabilizer states and states forbidd — conjecture conj:geelen_main_text
open: Does every proper vertex-minor-closed class of stabilizer states exhibit asymptotic entanglement structure captured by circle graph states? Formally, for every proper vertex-minor-closed class $\mathcal{F}$ of stabilizer states, do there exist $k, p \in \mathbb{N}$ such that each state in $\mathcal{F}$ that is $k$-rank-connected is single-qubit Clifford equivalent to a rank-$p$ perturbation of a circle graph state?
solved_when: For every proper vertex-minor-closed class $\mathcal{F}$ of stabilizer states, explicit $k, p \in \mathbb{N}$ are established such that every $k$-rank-connected member of $\mathcal{F}$ is single-qubit Clifford equivalent to a rank-$p$ perturbation of a circle graph state.
why: It would characterize the asymptotic entanglement of broad families of stabilizer states through circle graph states, giving a structural normal form for vertex-minor-closed classes.

title: Asymptotic entanglement in circle stabilizer states and states forbidd — conjecture conj:geelen
open: Does every family of graphs defined by pivot-minor-closed properties eventually look like circle graphs, in the sense that some bounded rank-connectivity threshold and some bounded perturbation rank suffice? Formally: for every PVMC family ${F}$ of graphs, there exist $k, p \in \mathbb{N}$ such that each graph in ${F}$ that is $k$-rank-connected is a rank-$p$ perturbation of a circle graph.
solved_when: For every PVMC family ${F}$, explicit constants $k$ and $p$ (or a proof of their existence) are provided so that every $k$-rank-connected member of ${F}$ is a rank-$p$ perturbation of a circle graph.
why: It would give a structure theorem for pivot-minor-closed graph families, showing highly rank-connected members are essentially circle graphs up to bounded-rank perturbation — a key step toward an analogue of the Grid Theorem in the pivot-minor setting.

title: Chouinard's Conjecture for Graphical t-Designs
open: Is Chouinard's conjecture true for graphical t-designs? The conjecture's status remains unresolved even in the parameter ranges recently enumerated by Chee and Kaski.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21846v1 (Yeow Meng Chee); in that paper, Chee and Kaski enumerated graphical MATH-designs in a further range of parameters and noted that Chouinard's conjecture remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of Chouinard's conjecture for graphical t-designs is given; no quantitative targets are stated in the record, so the natural criterion for a conjecture-type problem applies.
why: The conjecture is a structural statement about graphical t-designs; resolving it would settle a basic open question in this corner of design theory that enumerative work has circled but not closed.

title: Chouinard's Conjecture for Graphical t-Designs
open: Does Chouinard's conjecture hold in its full generality for MATH-wise balanced designs? Despite progress in special cases, the general statement for graphical t-designs remains unproved.
status: The general case is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.21846v1 (Yeow Meng Chee); no partial resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: The conjecture is established for all MATH-wise balanced designs, with no restriction on the graph class or parameters beyond those inherent in the conjecture's statement.
why: A proof would complete the foundational theory of graphical t-designs and settle the last structural question raised in the source survey for this design family.

title: Trapezoidality of flat arrangement polynomials
open: Does the flat arrangement polynomial of every full-dimensional flat vector arrangement have trapezoidal coefficients? That is, is trapezoidality a universal property of these polynomials rather than a feature of special cases?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21855v1 (Yuan Gao, Tianyu Yuan); no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for whether the flat arrangement polynomial has trapezoidal coefficients for every full-dimensional flat vector arrangement.
why: Trapezoidality of such polynomials reflects deep structural symmetry in flat vector arrangements; establishing it universally would settle a question left open in the source paper and constrain the coefficient behavior of this polynomial class.

title: Spanning trees in the Assignment Problem: two theorems and two conject
open: In the Random Euclidean Assignment Problem, where points are i.i.d. on a planar domain, do the associated spanning trees exhibit a universal structure? We conjecture that the trees are asymptotically distributed as Uniform Spanning Trees, with free boundary conditions in one setting and wired boundary conditions in the other.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that, in the stated asymptotic regime for i.i.d. points on a planar domain, the spanning trees converge in distribution to Uniform Spanning Trees with free boundary conditions in the one setting and wired boundary conditions in the other.
why: It would connect the Random Euclidean Assignment Problem to the well-developed theory of Uniform Spanning Trees, transferring exact scaling-limit and conformal-invariance tools to assignment-problem geometry.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22308v1 (Sergio Caracciolo, Gabriele Sicuro, Andrea Sportiello)

title: Three-edge-coloring apex cubic graphs — conjecture conj:Tutte4Flow
open: Does every 2-connected graph with no Petersen graph minor admit a nowhere-zero 4-flow? Equivalently, is Tutte's 4-flow conjecture conj:Tutte4Flow true when restricted to this class of graphs?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, by an explicit counterexample) that every 2-connected graph without the Petersen graph as a minor admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow.
why: This is the famous Tutte 4-flow conjecture; a proof would settle a central case of the connection between forbidden minors and flow-coloring dualities in cubic graph theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22870v1 (Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Rintaro Matsuo)

title: Three-edge-coloring apex cubic graphs — conjecture conj:Tutte3edge
open: Is every $2$-connected cubic graph with no Petersen graph minor three-edge-colorable?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every $2$-connected cubic graph without the Petersen graph as a minor admits a proper three-edge-coloring.
why: It sharpens Tutte's classical three-edge-coloring conjecture to a structurally minimal excluded-minor setting, so a proof would settle the colorability of the entire Petersen-minor-free class of cubic graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22870v1 (Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Rintaro Matsuo)

title: An improved upper bound for Tuza's conjecture via 2-colorable triangle
open: Tuza's conjecture remains unresolved in general: while it has been proven for several classes of graphs, such as planar graphs, graphs with bounded treewidth, threshold graphs, and others, can it be established for all graphs?
status: The general case is stated as open in the source paper (2026); the conjecture is known to hold for planar graphs, graphs with bounded treewidth, and threshold graphs, among other classes. Key work: arXiv:2608.23010v1 (Lixing Yi).
solved_when: The conjecture is proven for arbitrary graphs, not just the known classes (planar graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, threshold graphs, etc.).
why: Extending the result beyond these special classes would settle one of the classic questions in this corner of graph theory, where the current proofs are confined to structurally restricted families.

title: Counterexamples to the Albertson-Berman conjecture: minimum order, con — conj conj:CP
open: Does every planar graph on $n$ vertices contain an induced subgraph on more than $\frac{2dn}{4d+1}$ vertices whose maximum degree is at most $d$, for every integer $d \geq 2$? In symbols, is $f_d(G) > \frac{2dn}{4d+1}$ for every planar graph $G$ and every $d \geq 2$?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the bound $f_d(G) > \frac{2dn}{4d+1}$ for all planar graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices and all integers $d \geq 2$; a counterexample resolving the question in the negative also counts.
why: This is the Albertson–Berman conjecture, a benchmark for how large a low-degree induced subgraph every planar graph must contain; settling it would fix a basic extremal parameter in structural graph theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23260v1 (Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken)

title: Counterexamples to the Albertson-Berman conjecture: minimum order, con — prob 4
open: Does a 5-connected counterexample to the Albertson–Berman conjecture exist? Equivalently, is there a graph of vertex-connectivity exactly 5 that refutes the conjecture?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.23260v1 (Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken).
solved_when: A 5-connected counterexample to the Albertson–Berman conjecture is exhibited, or the conjecture is proved for all 5-connected graphs.
why: Settling this would delimit the connectivity range in which the Albertson–Berman conjecture can fail, sharpening which structural hypotheses suffice for it.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23260v1 (Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken)

title: Counterexamples to the Albertson-Berman conjecture: minimum order, con — prob 5
open: Does the Albertson–Berman conjecture hold for the remaining cases $2 \le d \le 6$? Formally, is it true in these cases that $f_d(G) > \frac{2dn}{4d+1}$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.23260v1 (Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken).
solved_when: For each $d$ with $2 \le d \le 6$, it is proved (or disproved by counterexample) that $f_d(G) > \frac{2dn}{4d+1}$ for every relevant graph $G$.
why: Resolving the remaining cases would complete (or refute) the Albertson–Berman conjecture in the range $2 \le d \le 6$, settling the surviving small-dimension instances of the problem.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23260v1 (Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken)

title: Four hyperplanes do not always equipartition a mass in $\mathbb{R}^4$
open: Does Grünbaum's conjecture — on when arrangements of hyperplanes can equipartition a mass — hold, and in particular can four hyperplanes always equipartition a mass in $\mathbb{R}^4$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Pablo Soberón, http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23312v2; its fame is noted in {Simon2019, fakhrutdinov2025algorithms}.
solved_when: A proof or disproof of Grünbaum's conjecture as stated in the source; concretely, a determination of whether four hyperplanes always equipartition a single mass in $\mathbb{R}^4$.
why: Grünbaum's conjecture has been called one of the most famous open problems in topological combinatorics, so settling it resolves a central question on the power and limits of hyperplane equipartitions.

title: A nowhere-zero point for several linear mappings simultaneously — conjecture conj:prime-field
open: Let $p$ be prime, and let $M$ be loopless and representable over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Is there a nowhere-zero point common to several linear mappings simultaneously?
solved_when: The conjecture conj:prime-field is proven (or refuted) for loopless matroids representable over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$.
why: It would extend the nowhere-zero-point phenomenon from a single linear mapping to several simultaneously, for matroids representable over prime fields.

title: Synchronizing Automata: Open Problems
open: Does every synchronizing automaton on $n$ states admit a reset word of length at most $(n-1)^2$? In other words, is the Černý-type quadratic bound sharp in this exact form, with leading constant one?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Marek Szykuła, http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24245v1.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every $n$-state synchronizing automaton has a reset word of length at most $(n-1)^2$, for all $n$.
why: It pins down the tight worst-case length of shortest reset words, a parameter central to synchronizing-automata theory with algorithmic consequences for reset-word computation.

title: Synchronizing Automata: Open Problems
open: Does a uniformly random binary automaton on $n$ states have reset threshold at most on the order of $n^{1/2}$ with high probability? That is, is the quadratic (or near-quadratic) behavior suggested by worst cases absent in the random case, with the reset threshold lying in $(n^{1/2})$ asymptotically almost surely?
solved_when: It is proved that for a uniformly random binary automaton, the reset threshold is in $n^{1/2}$ with high probability.
why: It would pin down the typical synchronization speed of random automata, contrasting sharply with the worst-case Černý-type bounds and informing the expected behavior of reset-based algorithms on random inputs.

title: Parameterized Complexity of $L_p$-Lipschitz Constants for Input Convex
open: Are the parameterized problems of computing $L_p$-Lipschitz constants for input-convex functions also contained in W[1]? Establishing W[1]-membership would settle the parameterized complexity status of these problems completely.
solved_when: The problems are shown to lie in W[1], or equivalently their parameterized complexity classification is completed.
why: It completes the parameterized complexity picture for these problems, removing the gap between hardness and membership.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24865v1 (Aritra Das, Vincent Froese, Moritz Grillo)

title: Rainbow Turán numbers for paths of length four — conjecture conjecture
open: For every $k \ge 4$, determine the rainbow Turán number $\mathrm{ex}_k^{\mathrm{rain}}(P_5)$; in particular, is it true that the exact value is given by Construction I for $k \in \{4,7\}$, by Construction II for $k \in \{5,6,8,9,11,12\}$, and by Construction III for $k=10$ and $k \ge 13$?
solved_when: The value of $\mathrm{ex}_k^{\mathrm{rain}}(P_5)$ is proved for every $k \ge 4$, matching Construction I for $k \in \{4,7\}$, Construction II for $k \in \{5,6,8,9,11,12\}$, and Construction III for $k=10$ and $k \ge 13$.
why: It would settle the exact rainbow Turán number of the path of length four across all color multiplicities, completing the case analysis left open in the source paper.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25079v2 (Sylwia Antoniuk, Andrzej Grzesik, Magdalena Prorok)

title: Bounded diameter covering of 2-colored complete bipartite graphs — conjecture conjbip
open: In every $r$-edge-coloring of a complete bipartite graph, can the vertex set always be covered by the vertex sets of $2r-2$ monochromatic connected components? Formally, for every integer $r \ge 2$ and every $r$-edge-coloring of a complete bipartite graph $G$, is $V(G)$ a union of at most $2r-2$ monochromatic connected components?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every integer $r \geq 2$, every $r$-edge-coloring of a complete bipartite graph admits a cover of $V(G)$ by $2r-2$ monochromatic connected components.
why: It pins down the bipartite analogue of the classical monochromatic covering conjecture, fixing the exact constant $2r-2$ rather than order-of-magnitude bounds.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25081v1 (Louis DeBiasio, András Gyárfás, Gábor N. Sárközy)

title: Bounded diameter covering of 2-colored complete bipartite graphs — conjecture conjbipdiam
open: In any 2-coloring of the edges of a complete bipartite graph, can the vertex set always be covered by a bounded number of monochromatic connected components, each of bounded diameter? Formally, for every $r \geq 2$, is there a smallest integer $f(r)$ such that in every $r$-edge-coloring of a complete bipartite graph $G$, the set $V(G)$ can be covered by the vertex sets of $2r-2$ monochromatic connected components, each of diameter at most $f(r)$?
status: The conjecture (conjbipdiam) is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Louis DeBiasio, András Gyárfás, and Gábor N. Sárközy (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25081v1); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: For every $r \geq 2$, a finite bound $f(r)$ is established such that any $r$-edge-colored complete bipartite graph admits a cover of its vertex set by $2r-2$ monochromatic connected components of diameter at most $f(r)$.
why: A finite bound $f(r)$ would extend classical monochromatic partition results from complete graphs to the bipartite setting with an explicit diameter control, giving a sharp count ($2r-2$ components) analogue of known covering theorems.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25081v1 (Louis DeBiasio, András Gyárfás, Gábor N. Sárközy)

title: Bounded diameter covering of 2-colored complete bipartite graphs
open: Is it true that every $2$-colored complete bipartite graph can be covered by monochromatic subgraphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ where $H_1$ is a double star and $H_2$ has diameter at most three?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) resolves whether every $2$-colored complete bipartite graph admits such a cover: $H_1$ a monochromatic double star and $H_2$ a monochromatic subgraph of diameter at most three.
why: It would settle the third covering question from the source open-problems paper on $2$-colored complete bipartite graphs, clarifying how few and how structurally simple monochromatic pieces suffice to cover such graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25081v1 (Louis DeBiasio, András Gyárfás, Gábor N. Sárközy)

title: Matching complements in subcubic graphs and a proof of the 3-Decomposi — conjecture conj:3dc
open: Does every finite connected cubic loopless multigraph admit a partition of its edge set into the pieces demanded by the 3-Decomposition conjecture, via the study of matching complements in subcubic graphs?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the 3-Decomposition conjecture as stated in the source paper, for every finite connected cubic loopless multigraph.
why: It settles a long-standing structural conjecture about decomposing cubic graphs, with consequences for how matching complements in subcubic graphs can be understood.

title: Group Isomorphism and the Polylogarithmic-Time Hierarchy: Depth-2$\fra
open: Do depth-3 circuits for Group Isomorphism require super-polynomial size? Equivalently, is there no polynomial-size depth-3 circuit family deciding Group Isomorphism?
solved_when: A proof that every depth-3 circuit family deciding Group Isomorphism has super-polynomial size, or an explicit polynomial-size depth-3 construction refuting it.
why: A super-polynomial lower bound would give a genuine circuit-class separation for a natural algebraic problem, sharpening our picture of where Group Isomorphism sits in the polylogarithmic-time hierarchy; a construction would pull it further down the small-depth hierarchy than currently known.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26257v1 (Joshua A. Grochow, Gülce Kardeş, Michael Levet)

title: Group Isomorphism and the Polylogarithmic-Time Hierarchy: Depth-2$\fra
open: Does isomorphism testing of Abelian groups in the multiplication table model — with the promise that the tables are valid multiplication tables for groups — require DNFs of super-polynomial size? Equivalently, is there no polynomial-size DNF representation for this decision problem?
solved_when: A proof that any DNF computing Abelian group isomorphism testing in this model requires super-polynomial size, or an explicit polynomial-size DNF family for the problem.
why: It would delineate the limits of depth-2 Boolean circuit lower bounds for a natural, well-structured algebraic problem, separating shallow circuit models from the efficient algorithms known for group isomorphism.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26257v1 (Joshua A. Grochow, Gülce Kardeş, Michael Levet)

title: The Birthday Paradox for non-backtracking walks on regular graphs — conj 1
open: For any $\varepsilon > 0$, does there exist a constant $C = C(\varepsilon)$ such that if $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with all degrees at least $3$, and $k > C\sqrt{n}$, then for any edge $e$, the probability that a length $k$ random non-backtracking walk starting with $e$ is simple is less than $\varepsilon$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the stated birthday-paradox bound: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ a constant $C = C(\varepsilon)$ exists such that on any $n$-vertex graph of minimum degree at least $3$, every length-$k$ non-backtracking walk with $k > C\sqrt{n}$ starting from any edge fails to be simple with probability at least $1 - \varepsilon$.
why: It would give the birthday-paradox threshold for self-intersection of non-backtracking walks on arbitrary regular graphs, a basic sanity check for randomness of such walks beyond expanders.

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does every Borel Kakeya set contain a minimal Kakeya set — that is, a Kakeya subset whose no proper subset is still Kakeya? Formally, if $A$ is Borel and Kakeya, must there exist $K \subseteq A$ such that $K$ is Kakeya and no proper subset of $K$ is Kakeya?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), the curated open-problems paper "Open Problems in Mathematical Logic" by George Barmpalias, Su Gao, and Jialiang He (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2). No progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that every Borel Kakeya set contains a minimal Kakeya set, or a counterexample exhibiting a Borel Kakeya set with no minimal Kakeya subset.
why: It probes how much compactness or minimality structure is available in the descriptive-set-theoretic setting of Kakeya sets, a natural test question at the intersection of measure/geometric combinatorics and mathematical logic.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does there exist a Borel class of profinite groups whose isomorphism relation lies strictly between $S_\infty$-complete and smooth? In particular, what can be said in the Abelian case?
solved_when: An example is given of a Borel class of profinite groups (ideally of Abelian profinite groups) whose isomorphism relation is properly intermediate between $S_\infty$-complete and smooth.
why: It would exhibit a genuinely new complexity level for isomorphism of profinite groups within the Borel reducibility hierarchy, sharpening our picture of which classes are classifiable by countable invariants and which are maximally complex.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does there exist a Borel class $C$ of closed subgroups of $S_\infty$, invariant under isomorphism, whose isomorphism relation is not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism — and can such a class be analytic complete? In particular, does the class of pro-countable groups provide an example?
solved_when: An explicit Borel isomorphism-invariant class $C$ of closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ is exhibited whose isomorphism relation is not Borel below graph isomorphism (or shown analytic complete); alternatively, a proof that no such class exists. A definitive answer for the specific candidate $C$ of pro-countable groups also resolves the question.
why: It would calibrate the complexity of classification problems for closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ relative to graph isomorphism, the standard benchmark for non-Borel classification, and test whether graph isomorphism is truly universal for such group classifications.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: For every Borel ideal $I$, does there exist a closed set that is $I$-mediating ($I$-MED)? In other words, can the mediating structure required by $I$ always be realized by a closed set?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), a curated open-problems paper by George Barmpalias, Su Gao, and Jialiang He (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2).
solved_when: A proof that every Borel ideal $I$ admits a closed $I$-MED, or a counterexample exhibiting a Borel ideal with no closed $I$-MED.
why: Resolving it would clarify how the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of an ideal constrains the topological complexity of its mediating sets, a basic structural question in the study of Borel ideals.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does there exist a two-point set that is a Borel subset of the plane? Equivalently, can a set meeting every line in exactly two points be Borel?
solved_when: A Borel two-point set is constructed, or a proof is given that no two-point set can be Borel.
why: Two-point sets are classical test cases for the regularity properties of pathological sets of reals; settling their Borel status would resolve a long-standing question about how wild such transversal-like sets must be.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Is there a Davies example whose existence can be proved in ZFC alone? That is, can such an example be constructed without additional set-theoretic axioms beyond Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with Choice?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Open Problems in Mathematical Logic" (arXiv:2608.26628v2, George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He).
solved_when: A Davies example is exhibited together with a proof of its existence carried out in ZFC; dually, the problem is settled by a proof in ZFC that no such example exists.
why: It would remove the dependence of the Davies example on assumptions beyond ZFC, settling its status within the standard foundations of set theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Is the equivalence relation of topological isomorphism on oligomorphic groups smooth? Nies, Schlicht, and Tent proved in 2019 that it is classifiable by countable structures (Borel equivalent to E-infinity), and the question is whether this classification can be sharpened to smoothness.
solved_when: The isomorphism relation on oligomorphic groups is shown to be smooth, or a proof is given that it is not smooth.
why: It would settle the exact descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of classifying oligomorphic groups, a natural test case linking computable/descriptive set theory with the structure theory of automorphism groups of omega-categorical structures.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: If $G$ is an oligomorphic group, must its outer automorphism group $Out(G)$ be profinite? In other words, does oligomorphy of $G$ force a profinite structure on $Out(G)$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Open Problems in Mathematical Logic" by George Barmpalias, Su Gao, and Jialiang He (arXiv:2608.26628v2).
