solved_when: A proof that $Out(G)$ is profinite for every oligomorphic group $G$, or a counterexample exhibiting an oligomorphic $G$ with non-profinite outer automorphism group.
why: Resolving it would clarify the structural constraints oligomorphy imposes on automorphisms, a basic question about how these groups sit within profinite group theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does every (effectively) compact left-c.e. Polish space have a computable (right c.e.) Polish copy? Related to this problem, Melnikov and Ng proved that there is a left c.e. Polish space with no computable Polish presentation. Similarly, Koh, Melnikov, and Ng proved that there is a left c.e. Polish space with no right c.e. Polish presentation.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does there exist an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical? That is, can such a space be given a computable presentation that is unique up to a computable homeomorphism?
solved_when: An explicit example of an infinite computable Polish space that is topologically computably categorical is constructed, or a proof is given that none exists.
why: It would settle the basic existence question for computable categoricity in the topological setting, clarifying which infinite Polish spaces admit computably unique presentations.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does the Baire space have a degree of categoricity? More precisely, is there a single Turing degree that is precisely the degree of categoricity for some structure isomorphic to Baire space?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Open Problems in Mathematical Logic," available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 by George Barmpalias, Su Gao, and Jialiang He.
solved_when: A specific degree is identified as a degree of categoricity for (a presentation of) the Baire space, or it is proved that no such degree exists.
why: It would settle a basic question about whether the Baire space, a canonical example in descriptive set theory and computable structure theory, fits into the degree-of-categoricity framework.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Does every family $(A_s)$ in this setting admit a choice function that is definable in $M$ — that is, an $f$ with $f(s) \in A_s$ for all $s$? More precisely, is there a function $f$ definable in $M$ such that $f(s) \, A_s \, X$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), the curated open-problems list "Open Problems in Mathematical Logic," problem 49, by George Barmpalias, Su Gao, and Jialiang He (http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2).
solved_when: A definable-in-$M$ function $f$ is exhibited (or proven to exist) with $f(s) \in A_s$ for every $s$, or the existence of such a function is refuted in the setting of the source paper.
why: A definable choice function would give an internal, uniform way to select witnesses inside $M$, whereas failure shows such selections must remain external to the model.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: If a countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ can be written as the union of a sequence of hyperfinite equivalence relations $F_n$ with $F_n \subseteq F_{n+1}$ for each $n$, must $E$ itself be hyperfinite? Equivalently, is the increasing union of such a chain of hyperfinite relations again hyperfinite?
solved_when: A proof that every such $E$ (a countable Borel equivalence relation that is the union of a nested sequence of hyperfinite equivalence relations) is hyperfinite, or a counterexample exhibiting one that is not.
why: It would settle a basic structural question about when hyperfiniteness is preserved under countable increasing unions, refining our understanding of the boundary between hyperfinite and non-hyperfinite countable Borel equivalence relations.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: If a countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ is hyperfinite on both a set and its complement (hf/hf), must $E$ be hyperfinite? A formal restatement: does hyperfiniteness of both $E$ and its restriction to the complementary part force hyperfiniteness of the whole relation?
solved_when: A proof that every hf/hf countable Borel equivalence relation is hyperfinite, or a construction of an hf/hf equivalence relation that is not hyperfinite.
why: Resolving it would clarify how hyperfiniteness behaves under gluing equivalence relations from complementary pieces, a basic structural question in the theory of countable Borel equivalence relations.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: Is the orbit equivalence relation of any Borel action of a countable amenable group hyperfinite? Equivalently, does amenability of the acting group guarantee that its Borel orbit equivalence relations are always hyperfinite?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Open Problems in Mathematical Logic" (problem 55), by George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every Borel action of every countable amenable group has hyperfinite orbit equivalence relation, as posed in problem 55 of the source paper.
why: Resolving it would settle a central case of the measured/Borel theory of orbit equivalence for amenable groups, determining when such equivalence relations admit the simplest possible Borel-structure description.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: in Mathematical Logic
open: If $G$ is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose in-degrees are uniformly bounded and whose out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, must the connected equivalence relation of $G$ be hyperfinite?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation via counterexample) that every Borel locally finite directed graph with uniformly bounded in-degrees and polynomially growing out-neighborhoods has hyperfinite connected equivalence relation.
why: It would extend the hyperfiniteness toolkit beyond the standard undirected/schlicht settings, clarifying which directed growth conditions still force Borel hyperfiniteness.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26628v2 (George Barmpalias, Su Gao, Jialiang He)

title: An Exposition of the $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ Bound for the Komló
open: Is the Komlós conjecture true — that any matrix whose columns each have Euclidean norm at most one admits a signed coloring of its columns keeping the discrepancy bounded by a universal constant, independent of the number of columns?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that every matrix $A$ with all columns of Euclidean norm at most $1$ satisfies $\operatorname{disc}(A) = \min_{x \in \{-1,1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty \le C$.
why: It is a central open problem in discrepancy theory; resolving it would settle the worst-case behavior of discrepancy for column-normalized matrices, the setting underlying many applications of the partial-coloring and entropy methods.

title: An Alexander Polynomial Refinement for Alternating Links, with Trapezo — conj conj:m_convex
open: For any alternating link $K$, does the polynomial $P_K$ have $M$-convex support in $\mathbb{Z}^4$? More precisely, is the support of $P_K$ an $M$-convex set, so that its exponent vectors behave like the bases of a matroid?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.28484v1 (Joe Boninger), which is a curated open-problems paper; no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every alternating link $K$, the support of $P_K$ is an $M$-convex subset of $\mathbb{Z}^4$; no quantitative budget beyond the four-dimensional exponent lattice appears in the record.
why: $M$-convexity would impose a strong discrete-geometric structure on these link invariants, connecting them to matroid theory and opening the way to techniques from discrete convex analysis for alternating links.

title: Nonnegative conorms, regular matroids, and the tropical Schottky probl — question ques:CKS
open: If $Q$ is a positive-definite matrix whose matroid $M(Q)$ is cographic with positive weights, must $Q$ lie in the tropical Schottky locus? Equivalently, does every such nonnegative conorm configuration satisfy the tropical analogue of the classical Schottky condition?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper arXiv:2608.28783v1 (Yelena Mandelshtam, 2026); no progress toward it is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that positive-definiteness of $Q$ together with $M(Q)$ being cographic with positive weights implies (or does not imply) membership of $Q$ in the tropical Schottky locus.
why: It would clarify the boundary between combinatorial conditions on quadratic forms and tropical theta-null conditions, connecting regular matroid theory to the tropical Schottky problem.

title: On $(1,2^4)$ and $(1,2^5)$-packing edge-coloring of sparse subcubic gr — conj 1
open: Is every subcubic planar graph of girth at least $5$ colorable in the $(1,2^5)$-packing edge-coloring sense? Formally: can the edges of every such graph be colored with one color class forming a matching and five color classes each inducing components of size at most $2$?
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.29163v1 (Seog-Jin Kim, Xujun Liu, Boyan Xu).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) of the statement that every subcubic planar graph with girth at least $5$ admits a $(1,2^5)$-packing edge-coloring.
why: It would extend the known landscape of packing edge-colorings of sparse subcubic graphs, pinning down how many 2-packing colors are needed once girth $5$ is assumed for planarity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29163v1 (Seog-Jin Kim, Xujun Liu, Boyan Xu)

title: Proper Conflict-Free Choosability for Graphs with Bounded Average Degr — conjecture con1
open: Is every connected graph other than $C_5$ proper conflict-free $f_G$-choosable? In other words, does the single exception $C_5$ characterize exactly which connected graphs admit such a coloring even in the list-coloring setting?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2608.29375v1 (Zhijun Lu, Qirui Ying, Huimin Song); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every connected graph other than $C_5$ is proper conflict-free $f_G$-choosable.
why: A positive answer would give a complete characterization of connected graphs admitting proper conflict-free list colorings, closing the natural choosability analogue of the structural question.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29375v1 (Zhijun Lu, Qirui Ying, Huimin Song)

title: Fair Division of Graphs: Beyond Traceability — conjecture conj:spectrum
open: For every connected graph, is the spectrum of fair-division outcomes always of the form yes…yes, then no…no, then yes forever — that is, an initial finite string of "yes" answers, followed by a (possibly empty) string of "no" answers, followed by an infinite string of "yes" answers? Formally, the spectrum of any connected graph must be composed of an initial yes string, followed by a (possibly empty) no string, followed by an infinite string of yes.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, via a connected graph whose spectrum violates this shape) of the conjectured trichotomy structure for the spectrum of every connected graph.
why: Establishing this structure would characterize exactly which fair-division outcomes are possible on connected graphs, ruling out spectra with alternating or anomalous yes/no behavior.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29902v1 (Nicolas Bousquet, Frank Connor, Agnès Totschnig)

title: Avoiding patterns with three distinct letters in Canon permutations — conjecture conj:Q-nonalgebraic
open: Is the D-finite series \(Q(z)\) transcendental over \((z)\)? In other words, does \(Q(z)\) fail to satisfy any algebraic equation over the ring of polynomials in \(z\)?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that \(Q(z)\) is transcendental over \((z)\) is given.
why: Establishing transcendence of \(Q(z)\) would resolve the conjecture conj:Q-nonalgebraic on pattern avoidance with three distinct letters in Canon permutations, distinguishing genuinely nonalgebraic behavior among such generating series.

title: Avoiding patterns with three distinct letters in Canon permutations — conjecture conj:moment-property
open: Are the sequences $(B_k)_{k\ge 0}$ and $(Q_k)_{k\ge 0}$ both Stieltjes moment sequences?
solved_when: Both sequences are shown to be Stieltjes moment sequences (i.e., each admits a representing measure on $[0,\infty)$, equivalently the Hankel matrices of the sequence and its shifts are positive semidefinite).
why: A proof would give a measure-theoretic characterization of these permutation-pattern enumeration sequences, revealing hidden structure in Canon permutations; the sequences are stated as open in the source paper.

title: An Improved Bound for Smith's Longest Cycles Conjecture via a Forbidde — conjecture conj: smith
open: In every $k$-connected graph with $k \geq 2$, must any two longest cycles share at least $k$ common vertices?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that any two longest cycles in every $k$-connected graph, $k \geq 2$, intersect in at least $k$ vertices.
why: This is Smith's Longest Cycles Conjecture; a proof would settle a classic question on how connectivity forces longest cycles to overlap.

title: The Ramsey threshold for trees versus odd cycles — problem pb:be
open: For every odd integer $m \geq 3$, what is the least integer $f(m)$ such that the Ramsey number $R(T_n, C_m)$ equals $2n-1$ whenever $n \geq f(m)$? In other words, we seek the exact threshold beyond which the classical tree-versus-cycle Ramsey formula kicks in for each odd cycle length.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00944v2 (Qizhong Lin, Chunlin You).
solved_when: An explicit determination of $f(m)$ for every odd $m \geq 3$, with proof that $R(T_n, C_m) = 2n-1$ for all $n \geq f(m)$ and that $f(m)$ is minimal with this property.
why: It pins down the exact onset of the asymptotic Ramsey behavior for trees versus odd cycles, converting a limiting statement into a sharp, finite bound.

title: The real-rootedness of the toric $g$-contribution polynomials — conjecture EHR2
open: Are the toric $g$-contribution polynomials always real-rooted, as conjectured by EHR2?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.01086v1 (Qiqi Xiao); no further results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the real-rootedness of the toric $g$-contribution polynomials, settling conjecture EHR2.
why: A solution would resolve a stated open conjecture in the theory of toric $h^*$/$g$-polynomials and advance the real-rootedness program for combinatorial polynomials attached to polytopes.

title: Common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs fail at every base size
open: Does there exist a base-two counterexample of almost simple or diagonal type to the common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs? We conjecture that no such counterexample exists.
status: The conjecture that no base-two counterexample of almost simple or diagonal type exists is stated as open in the source paper (Aluna Rizzoli, Adam R. Thomas, arXiv:2609.01367v1, 2026); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every base-two group of almost simple or diagonal type satisfies the relevant common neighbour conjecture for its Saxl graph, as stated in arXiv:2609.01367v1.
why: It settles the base-two case of the common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs, clarifying which families of finite transitive permutation groups can serve as counterexamples.

title: Common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs fail at every base size — conj bgconj
open: If $G$ is a primitive permutation group of base size $b(G)=2$, must any two vertices of its Saxl graph $\Gamma(G)$ share a common neighbour? Formally, is the conjecture true that for every such $G$, any two vertices of $\Gamma(G)$ have a common neighbour?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given: either every primitive group $G$ with $b(G)=2$ has the property that any two vertices of $\Gamma(G)$ have a common neighbour, or a primitive group of base size 2 is exhibited for which some pair of vertices fails to have a common neighbour.
why: It would settle a basic structural property of Saxl graphs for primitive groups of base size 2, clarifying how base size constrains local graph structure.

title: Common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs fail at every base size — conj ourconj
open: Let $G$ be a primitive permutation group of almost simple or diagonal type with base size $b(G)=2$ — must any two vertices of its Saxl graph $\Gamma(G)$ share a common neighbour?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that for every primitive permutation group of almost simple or diagonal type with base size $b(G)=2$, any two vertices of the Saxl graph have a common neighbour.
why: Resolves the common-neighbour conjecture for Saxl graphs of base-size-two primitive groups, a structural question about how bases encode adjacency in primitive permutation groups.

title: Common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs fail at every base size
open: Do common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs admit counterexamples (or proofs) in the remaining primitive group types? Since the source paper's sections provide counterexamples of affine, product and twisted wreath type, only the almost simple and diagonal types remain open.
solved_when: The status of the common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs is resolved for almost simple and diagonal type primitive groups — either by counterexamples in those types or by proofs that the conjectures hold there.
why: Resolving the remaining cases would complete the classification of which primitive group types satisfy the common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs.

title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Re
open: Can the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial completely determine a graph action up to isomorphism, or are there distinct actions it fails to separate? More formally, is the multiorbital polynomial a complete invariant for graph actions?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Melanie Gerling, arXiv:2609.01866v3, where an example shows the multiorbital polynomial can distinguish graph actions with the same orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial.
solved_when: Either a proof is given that the multiorbital polynomial completely determines graph actions, or an explicit pair of non-isomorphic graph actions with the same multiorbital polynomial is exhibited.
why: The invariant already distinguishes graph actions that share the same orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial; establishing completeness would settle whether this stronger polynomial fully classifies graph actions, while a counterexample would show an even finer invariant is needed.

title: Regularised double shuffle relations for planar Arborified Zeta Values — conj conj:azvs
open: Are all rational relations among planar arborified zeta values generated by the known structural relations? That is, does every rational relation follow from the quasi-shuffle relations, the shuffle relations, the arborified Hoffman relation, the planarity relations, and the iterated integral representation of these values?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026): arXiv:2609.02346v1 (Pierre Catoire, Pierre J. Clavier, Ku-Yu Fan).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation with counterexample) that the space of rational relations among planar arborified zeta values is exactly the span of the quasi-shuffle relations, the shuffle relations (theorem), the arborified Hoffman relation (theorem), the planarity relations (proposition), together with the iterated integral representation (corollary).
why: It would give a complete, finite structural description of all linear identities satisfied by planar arborified zeta values, reducing any rational relation among them to a computable set of generators.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02346v1 (Pierre Catoire, Pierre J. Clavier, Ku-Yu Fan)

title: Extremal Asymmetric Depth of Planar Graphs and Hidden Near-Mirror Symm — conjecture conj:mirror
open: Can the asymmetric depth of every asymmetric IPR fullerene with depth 2 or 3 be realized by a near-mirror partial automorphism? Formally: for every asymmetric IPR fullerene $F$ with $d(F) \in \{2,3\}$, there exists a near-mirror partial automorphism of $F$ realizing $d(F)$.
status: The conjecture (conj:mirror) is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.02585v1 (Ján Pastorek); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every asymmetric IPR fullerene $F$ with $d(F) \in \{2,3\}$ admits a near-mirror partial automorphism realizing its asymmetric depth.
why: It would uncover a hidden near-mirror symmetry governing the depth extremes, explaining why small asymmetric depth in IPR fullerenes always arises from mirror-like structure rather than arbitrary asymmetry.

title: Extremal Asymmetric Depth of Planar Graphs and Hidden Near-Mirror Symm — question q:genus-tight
open: Is the genus-bound theorem of the source paper tight — do infinitely many genera $g$ admit a graph $F$ of genus $g$ whose asymmetric depth $d(F)$ reaches $2H(g) - 2$? A weaker but still interesting target is whether infinitely many $g$ admit graphs attaining even the order $d(F) = \Theta(g)$ suggested by the bound.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.02585v1 (Ján Pastorek); no constructions or partial results are recorded.
solved_when: Infinitely many values of $g$ are exhibited for which some graph of genus $g$ attains $d(F) = 2H(g) - 2$ (or, for the weaker form, $d(F) = \Theta(g)$); disproof requires showing the bound is not attained for all but finitely many $g$.
why: Tightness would confirm that the genus-bound theorem captures the true extremal behavior of asymmetric depth, giving exact extremal examples; failure would force a revised upper bound and reveal hidden structural constraints on near-mirror symmetry.

title: Extremal Asymmetric Depth of Planar Graphs and Hidden Near-Mirror Symm — question q:sharpness
open: Does every 3-connected planar cubic graph of girth 5 contain a localised partial automorphism of the kind described in the source paper — extending the conclusion of the unified localisation theorem beyond the IPR fullerenes to all fullerenes, and more generally to the entire class?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the existence of such a localised partial automorphism in every 3-connected planar cubic graph of girth 5, which in particular settles whether the conclusion of the unified localisation theorem holds for all fullerenes and not only the IPR ones.
why: It would extend a structural symmetry/localisation guarantee from a restricted chemical class (IPR fullerenes) to the full family of 3-connected planar cubic graphs of girth 5, the natural extremal setting for such automorphisms.

title: Structural rigidity in the Erdős-Graham two-set permutation problem
open: Does there exist a partition of the positive integers into two sets such that every permutation of the positive integers can be obtained by interleaving, in order, its restrictions to the two parts — that is, is the Erdős–Graham problem #197 realizable by some two-set partition? The canonical candidate partition is ruled out by the paper's Theorem, but the general existence question is untouched.
solved_when: A two-set partition with the required interleaving property is exhibited and proved correct, or the impossibility of any such partition is proved, thereby settling Erdős–Graham problem #197.
why: Theorem eliminates the natural candidate, so the problem now requires either a genuinely new construction or an impossibility argument; settling it resolves a long-standing numbered question of Erdős and Graham.

title: Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids — question q:2mostperk
open: For a fixed budget of $k$ black squares in an $n \times n$ grid, which arrangement of those squares admits the most non-attacking rook placements, and how many placements does it achieve? A formal answer would identify the extremal arrangement (up to symmetry) and give a formula or tight characterization of the maximum count.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Joel Brewster Lewis and Robert Won, arXiv:2609.03081v1.
solved_when: An explicit characterization of the maximizing arrangement of $k$ black squares, together with the number of non-attacking rook placements it admits, is proved for general $n$ and $k$.
why: It resolves the extremal question for rook placements on partially blocked boards, showing precisely how obstruction placement controls enumeration and completing the counting picture for crossword-style grids.

title: Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids — question q:8maxperm
open: Which $n \times n$ crossword grids maximize the number of non-attacking rook placements, and how many placements do they admit? A second question is how this maximum grows asymptotically as $n \to \infty$.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03081v1" (Joel Brewster Lewis, Robert Won); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: For each $n$, the permutation grids attaining the maximum number of non-attacking rook placements are identified, the exact maximum is determined, and its asymptotic behavior as $n \to \infty$ is established.
why: It pins down the extremal structure of crossword grids for rook placements, completing the natural optimization question in this corner of combinatorial enumeration.

title: Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids — question q:7whichk
open: For which positive integers $r$ does there exist a crossword grid admitting exactly $r$ non-attacking rook placements? More precisely, can the crossword grids that realize exactly $r$ such placements be characterized?
solved_when: A characterization is given of the set of positive integers $r$ for which some crossword grid admits exactly $r$ non-attacking rook placements, together with a description of the grids realizing each such $r$.
why: It would settle which counting behavior is possible for rook placements on crossword grids, giving a complete realizability picture for this class of boards.

title: Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids
open: Fix a positive integer $n$: what fraction of $n \times n$ crossword grids admit a non-attacking rook placement, and how does this fraction behave asymptotically as $n$ grows? In particular, what is the expected number of such placements on a random $n \times n$ grid?
solved_when: An answer is obtained for the fraction of $n \times n$ grids admitting a rook placement, its asymptotic behavior as $n \to \infty$, and the expected number of rook placements on a random $n \times n$ grid.
why: It would determine the typical counting behavior of non-attacking rook placements on crossword-style grids, a natural quantitative invariant of these combinatorial structures left open by the source paper.

title: On uniquely colorable Cayley graphs
open: Unitary Cayley graphs capture only a specific subset of integral circulant graphs — can we classify, in full, which integral circulant graphs are perfect?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03184v1 (Milan Bašić).
solved_when: A complete classification of perfect integral circulant graphs is given, covering the cases beyond the unitary Cayley subfamily.
why: It would extend structural understanding of perfect graphs from the unitary Cayley subfamily to the entire integral circulant family, closing a natural gap in their coloring theory.

title: Toughness Bounds for Fractional Hamiltonicity and Resistance Positivit — conjecture conj:Chvatal
open: Does there exist a constant $t_0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph on sufficiently many vertices is Hamiltonian? This is Chvátal's celebrated toughness conjecture: is high enough toughness enough to force a Hamiltonian cycle?
solved_when: An explicit constant $t_0$ is identified, together with a proof that every $t_0$-tough graph on at least the required number of vertices contains a Hamiltonian cycle.
why: A positive answer would establish toughness as a sharp structural parameter guaranteeing Hamiltonicity, resolving a long-standing link between connectivity-based measures and cycle structure in graphs.

title: Odd denominators in the Lonely Runner spectrum for six speeds — question q:ratio
open: Does the bound $\max_i t v_i < 3q$ hold for every near-tight sextuple, where $q$ is the relevant denominator? The known theorem gives the bound on part of the range, and the ratio is below $1$ elsewhere; among all near-tight sextuples with speeds at most $110$ the largest ratio is $105/43$, and the largest ratio among the sporadic ones is $46/25$, attained by $(1,3,4,5,18,46)$ — a case where $q=25$ even though the maximum is attained only at times with denominator $50$. More generally, as Kravitz has pointed out, a bound $\max_i t v_i < C(n)\,q$ for all but finitely many near-tight $n$-tuples follows whenever the Lonely Runner Conjecture holds for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, with the constant a maximum over the finitely many critical subtori (computable via the homogeneity argument in the proof of the theorem); its value for other $n$, and whether the sporadic tuples respect it, are open.
solved_when: The bound $\max_i t v_i < 3q$ is proved for every near-tight sextuple; more generally, an explicit value of $C(n)$ is determined for other $n$ and it is settled whether the sporadic tuples respect it.
why: It sharpens the Lonely Runner picture for six speeds by controlling which denominators can carry near-tight behavior, extending the theorem beyond the range where it is currently proved.

title: Graded Betti numbers of graded Möbius algebras of uniform matroids — conjecture conj:Sylv_iff_lin_pres
open: For which simple matroids with at least 3 elements and quadratic graded Möbius algebra is the graded Möbius algebra linearly presented exactly when the matroid is Sylvester?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that, for every simple matroid with at least 3 elements whose graded Möbius algebra is quadratic, the algebra is linearly presented if and only if the matroid is Sylvester.
why: It characterizes the linear presentation of graded Möbius algebra Betti numbers in terms of the Sylvester property, connecting algebraic presentation to matroid combinatorics for uniform matroids.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03827v1 (Louiza Fouli, Sean Grate, Selvi Kara)

title: Real-rootedness and interlacing for parking functions and Chow polynom — problem prob:consecutiveChowInterlacing
open: Do the Chow polynomials $H_{n+1}(t)$ and $H_{n+2}(t)$ interlace for every $n$? More precisely, is it true that consecutive members of the Chow polynomial sequence always form an interlacing pair of real-rooted polynomials?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2609.05131v2, Per Alexandersson, 2026).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that $H_{n+1}(t)$ and $H_{n+2}(t)$ interlace for every $n$.
why: Establishing interlacing of consecutive Chow polynomials would place them among the structured real-rooted polynomial families tied to parking functions, unlocking standard consequences such as log-concavity and unimodality of the underlying coefficients.

title: Ramsey properties of maximal (outer)planar graphs
open: Which outerplanar graphs $H$ are unavoidable in every sufficiently large maximal outerplanar graph? Formally, characterise all outerplanar graphs $H$ for which there exists an integer $N(H)$ such that for all $n \geq N(H)$, every maximal outerplanar graph on $n$ vertices contains a copy of $H$.
solved_when: A complete characterisation of the outerplanar graphs $H$ admitting such a linear Ramsey-type threshold $N(H)$ is given (and proved tight, i.e., for graphs outside the family some arbitrarily large maximal outerplanar graphs avoid $H$).
why: Such a characterisation would yield a Ramsey-type theory for the class of maximal outerplanar graphs, identifying exactly which patterns are forced by maximality alone.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05268v1 (Adriana Baldacchino, Yair Caro, Xandru Mifsud)

title: Algebraic characterizations of generating and affinely generating $Γ$- — conjecture conj:generating-distance-magic
open: Does every distance magic graph of order $n$ admit a generating $\Gamma$-magic map for every abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $n$? Formally: if $G$ is a distance magic graph of order $n$, then for every abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $n$, the graph $G$ admits a generating $\Gamma$-magic map.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05934v1 (Ahmet Batal); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every distance magic graph of order $n$ admits, for every abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $n$, a generating $\Gamma$-magic map — or, in the negative direction, an explicit distance magic graph and abelian group of the same order for which no such map exists.
why: It would give a purely algebraic characterization of when distance magic labeling strength can be guaranteed across all abelian target groups, tightening the link between distance magic graphs and group-based labelings.

title: Comparisons between ordinary and symbolic powers of edge ideals with r
open: Does the containment-comparison question between ordinary and symbolic powers admit a counterexample within the class of edge ideals? Although the question has a negative answer in general, no counterexample is known among edge ideals.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Yuji Muta, arXiv:2609.05945v1 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05945v1); the question is known to have a negative answer in general, but no counterexample among edge ideals is known.
solved_when: Either an edge ideal is exhibited for which the containment-comparison in question fails, or a proof is given that it holds for all edge ideals.
why: Edge ideals are a tractable, combinatorially described class, so resolving the question there would clarify whether the general failure reflects intrinsic combinatorial structure or pathology outside the class.

title: Resolution of a problem of Mohar on non-positive inertia — problem prob:Mohar
open: Is the order of a graph bounded by a constant times the square of the number of non-positive eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix? In other words, does every graph with exactly $k$ non-positive eigenvalues have $O(k^2)$ vertices?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) settles whether $|V(G)| = O(k^2)$ for every graph $G$ whose adjacency matrix has $k$ non-positive eigenvalues.
why: It would resolve Mohar's problem on non-positive inertia by tying a graph's size directly to its spectral inertia, giving a sharp structural constraint on graphs with few non-positive eigenvalues.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06319v1 (Clive Elphick, Hitesh Kumar, Shivaramakrishna Pragada)

title: Multicolor Ramsey and list Ramsey numbers for star-like trees
open: Does the list Ramsey number of a star \(K_{1,n}\) always coincide with its ordinary Ramsey number? Formally, is it true that for all \(k \geq 1\) and \(n \geq 1\), \(r_\ell(K_{1,n};k) = r(K_{1,n};k)\)?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Qinghong Zhao, Yaping Mao, Xiangqian Zhou, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06378v1.
solved_when: An equality \(r_\ell(K_{1,n};k) = r(K_{1,n};k)\) is proved for every \(k \geq 1\) and \(n \geq 1\), or a counterexample pair \((k,n)\) exhibiting strict inequality is found.
why: It would show that star-like trees are Ramsey-forcing even in the stronger list-coloring setting, giving a clean multicolor analogue of the fact that list coloring cannot beat ordinary coloring for these graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06378v1 (Qinghong Zhao, Yaping Mao, Xiangqian Zhou)

title: Feedback edge set in bipartite digraph — conj 1.2
open: What is the correct extremal bound for the size of a minimum feedback edge set in a bipartite digraph, as proposed in Conjecture 1.2 of the source paper? In other words, does the conjectured function of the bipartition sizes and arc count hold for every bipartite digraph?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.06462v1 (Bin Chen, Jianfeng Hou, Siyue Liu). No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: Conjecture 1.2 of the source paper is proved in full or refuted by an explicit counterexample.
why: Resolving it settles a natural extremal question about how bipartiteness constrains feedback edge sets in digraphs, completing a program explicitly posed as open in the source paper.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06462v1 (Bin Chen, Jianfeng Hou, Siyue Liu)

title: Permutation Representations on Cohomology of Toric Varieties — question ques-permu
open: If a rational complete simplicial fan admits a proper action of a finite group $G$, is the induced (ungraded) representation of $G$ on the cohomology $H^*(X_{ })$ of the associated toric variety always isomorphic to a permutation representation?
solved_when: A proof that for every rational complete simplicial fan with a proper finite group action, the ungraded $G$-representation on $H^*(X_{ })$ is a permutation representation (or a counterexample).
why: It would characterize a concrete class of representations arising from toric geometry and constrain how finite symmetries of fans act on cohomology.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06597v1 (Tao Gui, Chushi Qin, Kaizhe Shen)

title: Residual structure and growing inversion-monotonicity regions for 1324 — conjecture conj:del
open: Does every residual of length at least $10$ for the permutation class $1324$ admit an admissible deletion?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with an explicit counterexample) that every residual of length at least $10$ admits an admissible deletion.
why: Establishing growing inversion-monotonicity regions would advance the residual-structure analysis of $1324$ begun in the source paper.

title: Shellability of semidistributive lattices
open: Is every finite semidistributive lattice shellable? This is a question of M\"uhle and Segovia that the source paper leaves open.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.07382v1 (Shuo Chen, Adrien Segovia).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of shellability for all finite semidistributive lattices; absent quantitative targets in the record, the natural criterion is a complete answer to the M\"uhle–Segovia question for finite semidistributive lattices.
why: Shellability would give a unified topological handle on the order complexes of semidistributive lattices, a class central to modern lattice theory; without it, their combinatorial topology remains inaccessible in general.

title: Markov Chain CLTs: Resolving Open Problems
open: If a Markov chain is ergodic but satisfies none of the usual strengthenings — reversibility, geometric ergodicity, or uniform ergodicity — must it still be true that $A = B$ (allowing both to be infinite)? In particular, does this hold when the transition kernel factors as $P = P_1 P_2$ with each $P_i$ reversible?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether $A = B$ — possibly both infinite — for general ergodic chains, and at least for kernels of the form $P = P_1 P_2$ with each $P_i$ reversible.
why: It would determine whether central limit behavior extends to the full class of ergodic Markov chains, or identify the precise structural assumptions (reversibility-type decompositions) that such CLT results genuinely require.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07819v1 (Austin Brown, Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, Quan Zhou)

title: Nowhere-zero $3$-flows in graphs with forbidden edge-cuts — conjecture CONJ1.1
open: Does every $4$-edge-connected graph admit a nowhere-zero $3$-flow?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, to the statement that every $4$-edge-connected graph admits a nowhere-zero $3$-flow.
why: It is a fundamental test case for Tutte's $3$-flow conjecture, resolving the extent to which edge-connectivity alone forces a nowhere-zero $3$-flow.

title: Coloring Small $K_t$-Minor-Free Graphs — conjecture conj:hadwiger
open: For every integer $t$, must every $K_t$-minor-free graph satisfy the stated coloring bound? (The record's statement of the conjecture is truncated, so the full formal claim — including the bound on the number of colors as a function of $t$ — cannot be reproduced from the record alone.)
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, by counterexample) of the conjecture as stated in the source paper; no quantitative targets are recoverable from the record.
why: It is a variant of Hadwiger's conjecture for graphs of small size, extracted from a curated open-problems collection.

title: Degenerating orbits of the Longest Edge Bisection process — conj 1
open: Does almost every simplex of dimension $d \geq d_0$ admit a branch of the longest edge bisection process whose shapes degenerate without bound? In measure-theoretic terms, the claim is that for almost every simplex in dimension $d_0$ and above, the bisection orbit contains a degenerating branch.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.08846v1 (Karim A. Adiprasito, Daniel Kalmanovich, Yaar Solomon); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that almost every $d$-dimensional simplex with $d \geq d_0$ has a degenerating branch under longest edge bisection, for some explicitly identified threshold dimension $d_0$.
why: It would determine whether the most widely used simplex-refinement scheme inevitably produces arbitrarily ill-shaped elements in higher dimensions, which directly affects the reliability of mesh-generation and finite-element error bounds built on it.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08846v1 (Karim A. Adiprasito, Daniel Kalmanovich, Yaar Solomon)

title: Are trees really just butterflies in disguise? — conjecture conj:main
open: Is it true that every digraph on $n$ vertices with more than $(k-1)n$ arcs contains a copy of every antidirected tree with $k$ arcs? Equivalently, is $(k-1)n$ the correct extremal threshold for embedding antidirected trees in dense digraphs?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.09142v2 (Giovanne Santos, Maya Stein, Ella Williams).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the statement that every digraph on $n$ vertices with more than $(k-1)n$ arcs contains a copy of every antidirected tree with $k$ arcs.
why: It would determine the exact extremal number for antidirected trees in digraphs, settling the directed analogue of the classic Erdős–Sós-type embedding question for trees.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09142v2 (Giovanne Santos, Maya Stein, Ella Williams)

title: Are trees really just butterflies in disguise? — conjecture conj:Burr
open: Is it true that every digraph with chromatic number at least $2k$ contains a copy of every oriented tree $T$ on $k$ arcs? In other words, does a $2k$-chromatic digraph embed every oriented tree with $k$ arcs?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.09142v2 (Giovanne Santos, Maya Stein, Ella Williams).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, by explicit construction) of the statement that every digraph of chromatic number at least $2k$ contains every oriented tree with $k$ arcs.
why: It would give a sharp, uniform embedding guarantee for oriented trees in digraphs of bounded chromatic number, a directed analogue of classical tree-embedding results for undirected graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09142v2 (Giovanne Santos, Maya Stein, Ella Williams)

title: Oriented paths with two blocks in bipartite oriented graphs
open: What is the smallest value $f(t)$ such that every bipartite oriented graph of minimum semidegree greater than $k/4 + f(t)$ contains any oriented path of length $k$ with $t$ blocks? Formally, determine $f(t)$ for integers $k, t$ with $t k$.
solved_when: An exact determination (or tight bounds) for $f(t)$ such that minimum semidegree greater than $k/4 + f(t)$ guarantees containment of every oriented path of length $k$ with $t$ blocks in bipartite oriented graphs.
why: It pins down the precise semidegree threshold beyond which all two-block-type oriented paths of given length must appear, closing the gap left by the general $k/4$ bound.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09935v1 (Bin Chen, Meishuang Chen, Xinmin Hou)

title: On Two Conjectures Related to the Boros-Moll Sequences — conj reverse_ULC_conj
open: Is the tail of the Boros–Moll sequence $\{u_i(m)\}_{2 \le i \le m-2}$ reverse ultra log-concave for all $m \ge 2$? That is, does the subsequence $u_i(m)$ indexed by $2 \le i \le m-2$ satisfy the reverse ultra log-concavity inequalities?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10234v2 (Heshan Aravinda); no resolution is known.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, with counterexample) that $\{u_i(m)\}_{2 \le i \le m-2}$ is reverse ultra log-concave for every $m \ge 2$.
why: Resolving this would complete the log-concavity picture of the Boros–Moll polynomials' coefficient sequences, a basic structural question about these much-studied sequences.

title: On Two Conjectures Related to the Boros-Moll Sequences — conj LC_BM_conj
open: For $m \ge 2$, the sequence $\{u_i(m)\}_{2 \le i \le m-2}$ is log-concave.
solved_when: The log-concavity of $\{u_i(m)\}$ for $m \ge 2$ (as indexed in the record) is proved or disproved.
why: It settles a conjecture from a curated open-problems paper on the Boros–Moll sequences, a basic positivity/shape question for these polynomials' coefficients.

title: Induced Forest Minor Theorem for Graphs Without an Induced Star — conj ConjInducedMinorObsDomination
open: Is there a function $f$ such that, for every $h$, every graph $G$ with no induced minor isomorphic to the star $T_h$ has path domination number at most $f(h)$?
solved_when: Such a function $f$ and a proof that, for all $h$, every graph with no $T_h$ induced minor has path domination number bounded by $f(h)$ are given.
why: It would extend the induced forest minor framework to star-free graphs, giving a structural obstruction-to-boundedness theorem for path domination in the induced-minor setting.

title: Induced Forest Minor Theorem for Graphs Without an Induced Star — conj ConjInducedMinorObs
open: Is there a function bounding the path independence number of graphs that exclude both $K_{t,t}$ and $T_h$ as induced minors? Formally: does there exist a function $f$ such that, for all $t, h$, every graph $G$ with no $K_{t,t}$ or $T_h$ induced minor has path independence number at most $f(t,h)$?
solved_when: Such a function $f(t,h)$ is exhibited (via proof) bounding the path independence number of every graph with no $K_{t,t}$ or $T_h$ induced minor, for all $t$ and $h$.
why: It would extend induced-minor structure theory to a forest-like obstruction setting, yielding a bounded path independence number — a hereditary measure of path-like independent structure — for graphs excluding a complete bipartite minor and a star forest minor.

title: Some Early Results by Tutte Regarding the Cycle Double Cover Conjectur
open: Does every bridgeless graph admit a cycle double cover — a collection of cycles such that each edge appears in exactly two of them? In formal terms, is it true that for every graph with no cut-edge there exists a family of cycles covering each edge precisely twice?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every bridgeless graph has a cycle double cover is given; equivalently, an explicit construction of such a family of cycles for arbitrary bridgeless graphs, or a counterexample graph.
why: The Cycle Double Cover Conjecture is one of the central and most challenging open problems in graph theory; a resolution would settle a question that has stood open for at least 80 years, tracing back to early results by Tutte.

title: Some Early Results by Tutte Regarding the Cycle Double Cover Conjectur
open: Does every bridgeless graph admit a cycle double cover? This is the question the source paper lists as its open problem, drawing on early results by Tutte.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the cycle double cover statement as posed in the source paper; the record states no further quantitative targets.
why: The record does not elaborate; it notes only that the problem was extracted from a curated open-problems paper, and media reports have characterized it as a 50-year-old open problem.

title: Some Early Results by Tutte Regarding the Cycle Double Cover Conjectur
open: Does every bridgeless graph admit a cycle double cover? This is the question raised in the source paper's discussion of Tutte's early work, left as one of the open problems awaiting resolution.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every bridgeless graph has a cycle double cover, resolving open problem 4 as stated in the source paper.
why: Resolving it would settle one of the central open questions connected to Tutte's original techniques on the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture.

title: Some Early Results by Tutte Regarding the Cycle Double Cover Conjectur
open: Is it accurate to describe the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture as a roughly 50-year-old open problem, as most media reports have characterized it? The question asks for a precise account of the conjecture's age and Tutte's early results on it.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026); see the curated open-problems paper arXiv:2609.10618v1 (Cun-Quan Zhang).
solved_when: A verified statement of when the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture was first posed, confirming or correcting the "50-year-old" characterization that most media reports rely on.
why: It grounds the historical framing of a well-known conjecture in verifiable fact rather than media shorthand, which matters for how the problem's difficulty and lineage are understood.

title: Erdős-Sós for digraphs — conjecture conj:directed-es
open: Does every Eulerian digraph with more than $t-1$ arcs contain every orientation of every tree with $t$ edges? Formally, for $t \geq 1$, if $G$ is an Eulerian digraph with $a(G) > t - 1$, must $G$ contain every orientation of every tree with $t$ edges?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.10987v1 (Dhruv Mubayi, Jacques Verstraete).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given that every Eulerian digraph $G$ with $a(G) > t - 1$ contains every orientation of every tree on $t$ edges.
why: This is the natural directed analogue of the Erdős–Sós conjecture; a resolution would extend one of the central tree-embedding problems to the directed setting and settle when arc density alone forces every oriented tree.

title: Erdős-Sós for digraphs — conjecture conj:path
open: Does every Eulerian oriented graph contain a directed path of length at least its average degree $d(G)$? In other words, is the Erdős–Sós path bound, known for undirected graphs, also valid for Eulerian orientations?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10987v1 (Dhruv Mubayi, Jacques Verstraete).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every Eulerian oriented graph $G$ contains a directed path of length at least $d(G)$.
why: It would extend the classical Erdős–Sós phenomenon from undirected graphs to directed graphs, giving a sharp structural guarantee for long paths in Eulerian digraphs.

title: A Proof of the Tratnik-Ye Medianity Conjecture of Resonance Graphs on — conjecture conj:ty
open: Is every connected component of the resonance graph $R(G;\Omega)$ a median graph, when $G$ is a finite simple graph embedded in a connected closed surface and $\Omega(G)$ is a set of even faces? Formally, the Tratnik–Ye medianity conjecture asserts that every such component of $R(G;\Omega)$ is a median graph.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.12009v1 (Guangfu Wang, Ke Kang).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) is given for the conjecture conj:ty as stated in the source paper: for every finite simple graph $G$ embedded in a connected closed surface and every set $\Omega(G)$ of even faces, every connected component of $R(G;\Omega)$ is a median graph.
why: A proof would establish medianity for resonance graphs in the general surface-embedded setting, extending the structural theory of median graphs to a class arising in chemical graph theory and matching theory.

title: Long Cycles in 2-Connected Tough Graphs — question ques:three
open: Let $t>1$. Is there a positive constant $B=B(t)$ such that — the record's statement cuts off here, and the full quantified question (over 2-connected $t$-tough graphs) is as posed in the source paper; read as: does such a constant $B$ exist?
solved_when: An explicit positive constant $B$ depending only on $t$ is exhibited and proved to satisfy the condition stated in the source paper, for every $t>1$.
why: It would give a quantitative lower bound on cycle length in 2-connected tough graphs, directly extending the classical link between toughness and Hamiltonicity-type properties.

title: Learning Sparse Quantum States
open: Does there exist an algorithm for learning quantum states that are sparse in a fixed (possibly unknown) Fock basis, which is both sample optimal and time efficient? In other words, can we obtain (near) optimal time complexity bounds, along with the scaling in MATH, for this problem?
solved_when: An algorithm is given that learns states sparse in a fixed (possibly unknown) Fock basis and is simultaneously sample optimal and time efficient, with (near) optimal time complexity bounds and explicit scaling in MATH.
why: Optimal sample complexity bounds for learning general MATH-mode bosonic and fermionic Gaussian states have recently been obtained, but the analogous time-efficient, sample-optimal guarantee for Fock-sparse states is missing; such an algorithm would close that gap.

title: The $q$-analogues of $γ$-positivity of Eulerian polynomials via group — conjecture con
open: Is it true that for every positive integer $n$, all coefficients of the polynomial $G^*_{2n}(q)$ are positive? This is the $q$-analogue of $γ$-positivity of Eulerian polynomials considered in the source paper, where the conjecture remains open.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper arXiv:2609.12405v1 (Taifeng Ding, Lintong Wang, Sherry H. F. Yan), published 2026; no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) of the statement that for all $n > 0$, every coefficient of $G^*_{2n}(q)$ is positive.
why: Positivity of these coefficients would establish the conjectured $q$-analogue of $γ$-positivity for Eulerian polynomials, giving a refined combinatorial structure that plain $γ$-positivity cannot see.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12405v1 (Taifeng Ding, Lintong Wang, Sherry H. F. Yan)

title: Torus actions on compactified braid varieties and polytopality of subw — question question
open: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a cluster variety with a partial compactification $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$. Does the natural torus action on $\mathcal{A}$ extend to an algebraic action on $\overline{\mathcal{A}}$?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that the torus action on the cluster variety does or does not extend to an algebraic action on the partial compactification.
why: An extension would connect the combinatorics of cluster varieties to the geometry of their compactifications, giving a torus-equivariant framework for studying their boundary structure.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12414v1 (Lara Bossinger, Mikhail Gorsky, José Simental)

title: Invariance of rowmotion for variants of the Tamari lattice — conjecture conj:homomesy
open: Is rowmotion on the variants of the Tamari lattice homomesic in the same way it is on the classical Tamari lattice? More precisely, does the conjecture conj:homomesy — asserting invariance of the relevant statistic's average across orbits — hold for these variants?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.12983v1 (Ben Adenbaum, Emily Barnard, Cesar Ceballos).
solved_when: Conjecture conj:homomesy is resolved: a proof (or refutation) that rowmotion on the Tamari-lattice variants exhibits the asserted homomesy, i.e., that the statistic in question has the same average on every orbit.
why: A proof would extend the homomesy phenomenon, a central structural theme of dynamical algebraic combinatorics, from the Tamari lattice to its variants, revealing which features of rowmotion are intrinsic rather than lattice-specific.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12983v1 (Ben Adenbaum, Emily Barnard, Cesar Ceballos)

title: Invariance of rowmotion for variants of the Tamari lattice — conjecture conj:cross_tamari
open: Do cross Tamari lattices coming from moon polyominoes related by row and column permutations have identical rowmotion dynamics? Formally, if $L_1$ and $L_2$ are cross Tamari lattices associated to such moon polyominoes, is there a bijection $L_1 \to L_2$ under which rowmotion behaves the same?
solved_when: For any two cross Tamari lattices $L_1, L_2$ associated to moon polyominoes related by a sequence of row and column permutations, a bijection conjugating rowmotion on $L_1$ with rowmotion on $L_2$ is constructed and proved.

title: Matroids with cycle systems are regular
open: Is it true that no matroid $M\{C\}$ arising from a cycle system can contain $R_{10}$ as a minor? More precisely, does the class of matroids with cycle systems exclude $R_{10}$ from its minor structure?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit example of a matroid $M\{C\}$ having $R_{10}$ as a minor) is given for whether $R_{10}$ can appear as a minor of any matroid with a cycle system.
why: Resolving this would clarify the structural relationship between matroids with cycle systems and regular matroids, since excluding $R_{10}$ (alongside other excluded minors) bears directly on regularity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13361v1 (Anton Dochtermann, Evan Huang, Kai Mawhinney)

title: Matroids with cycle systems are regular
open: If a matroid $M$ has a cycle system $\mathcal{C}$, does the simplification of $M$ always admit a cycle system as well? If so, can such a system be constructed explicitly from $\mathcal{C}$?
solved_when: A proof that the simplification of any matroid with a cycle system itself admits a cycle system, together with a construction of that system from the original $\mathcal{C}$ (or a counterexample).
why: It would establish that the existence of a cycle system is preserved under simplification, clarifying which matroids can carry such structures.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13361v1 (Anton Dochtermann, Evan Huang, Kai Mawhinney)

title: Matroids with cycle systems are regular
open: Suppose $M$ is a connected binary matroid and ${B} = \{B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_g\}$ is a unique union basis for its circuit space. Must ${B}$ be a cycle system for $M$?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, showing that every unique union basis of the circuit space of a connected binary matroid is (or is not) a cycle system.
why: It would clarify the structural relationship between circuit-space bases and cycle systems in connected binary matroids, a basic regularity question in this corner of matroid theory.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13361v1 (Anton Dochtermann, Evan Huang, Kai Mawhinney)

title: Coincidences and Growth of Boxed Mesh Patterns — conjecture conj:2143-factorial
open: Does the avoidance sequence of the boxed mesh pattern $(2143)$ have factorial growth? Formally, the conjecture asserts that the number of permutations avoiding this pattern grows factorially in the length.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the avoidance sequence of $(2143)$ has factorial growth.
why: It would determine the asymptotic growth class of a natural boxed mesh pattern's avoidance set, settling the stated conjecture and clarifying how boxed mesh patterns behave relative to classical permutation patterns.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13764v1 (Sergey Kitaev, Dun Qiu, Chao Xu)

title: Sharp stability for cross $t$-intersecting families of permutations in — conjecture conjEllis
open: For $n$ sufficiently large depending on $t$, must every $t$-intersecting family of permutations in $S_n$ have almost all of its members inside a single $t$-coset — with at most $t((n-t-1)!-(n-t-2)!)$ exceptions?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) that for all $n$ sufficiently large depending on $t$, every $t$-intersecting ${F} \subseteq S_n$ has a $t$-coset containing all but at most $t((n-t-1)!-(n-t-2)!)$ members of ${F}$.
why: This is the sharp stability statement for cross $t$-intersecting permutation families, pinning down the exact exceptional size; it completes the quantitative picture beyond the extremal classification.

title: Fast and Theoretically-Efficient Batch-Parallel Link-Cut Trees, Euler
open: Is there a batch-parallel algorithm for link-cut trees? Existing batch-parallel algorithms for Euler-tour trees are tightly coupled to skip lists, and no batch-parallel algorithm for LCTs is known.
status: The source paper (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14746v1, Quinten De Man, Laxman Dhulipala, 2026) states this as an open problem.
solved_when: A batch-parallel algorithm for link-cut trees is given, with a provable work/span (round) guarantee comparable in spirit to the known batch-parallel ETT results.
why: It would extend theoretically-efficient batch-parallel dynamic-tree processing beyond the skip-list-based Euler-tour-tree setting, removing the current structural dependence on skip lists.

title: The Komlós conjecture for complex discrepancy
open: Does the Komlós conjecture admit an extension to complex-valued settings, in the sense suggested by the source paper's discussion of open problems following the Kadison–Singer proof? More precisely, the paper asks whether the techniques it develops — rooted in the analysis of roots of hyperbolic polynomials, which generalize the determinant and originate in PDE theory — can be pushed to resolve the complex-discrepancy analogue of the Komlós conjecture.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the complex-valued Komlós discrepancy statement as posed in open problem 1 of the source paper, in a form publishable against that precise formulation; the record states no additional quantitative targets.
why: The Kadison–Singer proof succeeded through hyperbolic-polynomial root analysis, and settling the complex analogue would show whether that machinery extends beyond the real case — or pinpoint where it breaks.

title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
open: In the one-dimensional reduction of the coin-collecting environment of Langosco et al., two policies fit the training data perfectly—"move right" (the proxy) and "go to the coin" (the intended goal)—and they agree whenever the coin sits at the right end. If a two-layer network is trained by gradient descent on the logistic loss to imitate optimal play, with the coin's position randomized in an $ $-fraction of training episodes, what is the probability—over the random initialization—that the trained network follows the proxy on a probe state where the two policies disagree, as a function of $ $, the width, and the input encoding? For linear policies the answer is a theorem (the encoding, not the initialization, decides), and the standard infinite-width limits follow it under their convergence hypotheses; for finite-width networks it is open at every $ $, including $ =0$, already at width two.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the probability, over random initialization, that the gradient-descent-trained two-layer network follows the proxy policy on a disagreement probe state, as a function of the coin-randomization fraction $ $, the network width, and the input encoding—at minimum for width two, including the case $ =0$.
why: It is a minimal, fully rigorous setting in which one can analyze when gradient-descent training on a perfect-fit proxy leads a network to reward hacking rather than the intended goal, which is the core failure mode this theory aims to predict.

title: The Existence of Maximin Share Allocations is $Δ_2^P$-complete
open: Is the problem of deciding whether a maximin share (MMS) allocation exists for a given fair-division instance computationally hard — specifically, is it $Δ_2^P$-complete — even when valuations are additive? More broadly, is there any valuation class for which both membership and hardness (i.e., completeness) can be established?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that deciding the existence of an MMS allocation is $Δ_2^P$-complete for additive valuations, or the identification of some valuation class for which the problem is shown complete.
why: It pins down the exact complexity of a central existence question in fair division, telling us whether the existence of MMS allocations can be characterized by any tractable criterion or inherently requires the full power of the second level of the polynomial hierarchy.

title: The Existence of Maximin Share Allocations is $Δ_2^P$-complete
open: Is there an efficient characterization of when a maximin share (MMS) allocation exists for agents with additive valuations, and more generally for MATH-additive valuations? In other words, what is the computational complexity of deciding MMS allocation existence in these settings?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.15841v2 (Sushmita Gupta, Sanjay Seetharaman), where the complexity of MMS existence for additive and MATH-additive valuations is posed as an open question.
solved_when: The complexity of deciding whether an MMS allocation exists is resolved for additive valuations and for MATH-additive valuations, e.g., by a completeness result for a natural complexity class or a polynomial-time algorithm.
why: It settles the natural boundary of MMS existence beyond the settings already understood, informing both fair-division theory and the design of algorithms that either find MMS allocations or certify their nonexistence.

title: Local measures of interval edge-uncolorability
open: Does there exist a complete multipartite graph whose (weak) local deficiency equals 2? More precisely, the question asks for any complete multipartite graph attaining (weak) local deficiency $2$.
solved_when: An explicit complete multipartite graph is exhibited whose (weak) local deficiency is $2$, or a proof is given that no such graph exists.
why: It would settle a concrete extremal case for local measures of interval edge-uncolorability in complete multipartite graphs, sharpening the boundary between locally interval-colorable and deficient graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15873v1 (Carl Johan Casselgren, Petros A. Petrosyan)

title: A short proof of the Erd\H os--Sós Conjecture — conjecture AHLRTconj
open: Does every graph of average degree greater than $k-1$ contain every tree with $k$ edges — the Erdős–Sós conjecture, posed here as conjecture AHLRTconj of Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares Sales, Reed and Thomassé? More precisely, is it true that any graph with average degree exceeding $k-1$ contains as a subgraph every tree on $k$ edges?
solved_when: The conjecture holds: every graph with average degree greater than $k-1$ contains every tree with $k$ edges as a subgraph.
why: This would give a sharp, unified extremal condition embedding every bounded tree, settling a long-standing question at the interface of extremal graph theory and the study of tree containment.

title: A short proof of the Erd\H os--Sós Conjecture — conjecture ESconj
open: Is the Erdős–Sós Conjecture true — that is, does every graph of sufficiently large average degree contain every given tree as a subgraph? A formal proof establishing the conjecture in full generality would settle this long-standing question.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the Erdős–Sós Conjecture is given in full generality; a short proof would be a natural goal.
why: The conjecture is a foundational statement linking average degree to containment of arbitrary trees, and a proof would resolve a basic structural question about sparse graphs.

title: Logarithmic Circumference In Tough Graphs — conjecture conj-main
open: For each $t > 0$, does there exist a constant $c_t > 0$ such that every 2-connected $t$-tough $n$-vertex graph contains a cycle of length at least $c_t n$? In other words, must toughness force a cycle spanning a constant fraction of the graph's vertices?
status: Stated as an open conjecture (conjecture conj-main) in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.16083v2, by Levi Segal and Jacques Verstraete; no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: For every $t > 0$ a constant $c_t > 0$ is exhibited (or proven to exist) with the property that every 2-connected $t$-tough $n$-vertex graph contains a cycle of length at least $c_t n$; a disproof would exhibit some $t > 0$ and 2-connected $t$-tough graphs whose longest cycles have length $o(n)$.
why: It would establish that toughness alone guarantees long cycles spanning a linear fraction of the vertices, a basic structural link between toughness and Hamiltonicity-type properties.

title: Twisted Rational Zeros and Local-Global Principles for Linear Recurren
open: Given a linear recurrence sequence $u$, decide whether there exists an index $n$ with $u_n = 0$. Equivalently, give an algorithm (or a proof of decidability) for the existence of a zero in an arbitrary linear recurrence sequence.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16392v1 (Piotr Bacik); no partial resolution is recorded.
solved_when: An algorithm is provided that, for any linear recurrence sequence $u$, decides whether some $n$ satisfies $u_n = 0$, together with a proof of its correctness and termination.
why: This is the classical zero-emptiness question for linear recurrence sequences; a decision procedure would resolve a fundamental decidability frontier at the interface of number theory, algebra, and theoretical computer science.

title: Twisted Rational Zeros and Local-Global Principles for Linear Recurren — conjecture conj:failed-conj
open: If a simple linear recurrence sequence $u$ has a $p$-adic zero for every regular prime $p$, must it actually have a rational zero — that is, must there exist an index $n$ with $u_n = 0$? In other words, does this restricted local-global principle hold for simple linear recurrence sequences?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16392v1 (Piotr Bacik).
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, of the statement that every simple linear recurrence sequence possessing a $p$-adic zero for every regular prime $p$ must have some term $u_n = 0$.
why: It tests how far local-global principles extend to linear recurrence sequences when the local conditions are imposed only at regular primes, sharpening our understanding of which local information forces a rational zero.

title: Twisted Rational Zeros and Local-Global Principles for Linear Recurren
open: Is there an effective version of the result on zeros of linear recurrences — an algorithm that computes the set of zeros, or decides whether it is empty, for the relevant twisted rational setting? The proof of the existing result is ineffective, so the question is whether effectivity can be restored.
solved_when: An algorithm is given that computes the set of zeros or decides its emptiness, with a proof of correctness and termination.
why: Without an algorithm, the local-global statement gives existence information only; an effective procedure would turn it into a usable decision method for the zeros of these linear recurrences.

title: Twisted Rational Zeros and Local-Global Principles for Linear Recurren
open: Can the failure of the strengthened Skolem Conjecture be fully explained by the presence of twisted rational zeros? The conjecture asserts that the existence of twisted rational zeros is the only mechanism by which the strengthened Skolem Conjecture may fail, a claim supported by a heuristic argument.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the strengthened Skolem Conjecture holds for every linear recurrence sequence of rational numbers that has no twisted rational zeros; equivalently, twisted rational zeros are the sole source of counterexamples.
why: A proof would upgrade the heuristic evidence for the strengthened Skolem Conjecture into a structural local-global principle for zeros of linear recurrence sequences, sharply delimiting how the Skolem Problem can fail.

title: A deterministic $(2 + \varepsilon)$-approximation for directed feedbac
open: Does every directed graph admit a deterministic polynomial-time 2-approximation for the Directed Feedback Vertex Set problem? This nearly answers the open question posed by Lokshtanov, Misra, Mukherjee, Panolan, Philip and Saurabh (SODA 2020), who asked for a deterministic 2-approximation in polynomial time.
status: The question was stated as open in the source paper (2026), arising from the open question of Lokshtanov, Misra, Mukherjee, Panolan, Philip and Saurabh (SODA 2020) who asked for a deterministic 2-approximation in polynomial time; see Ebrahim Ghorbani, Matthias Mnich, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16723v1.
solved_when: A deterministic algorithm running in polynomial time that, for every directed graph, returns a feedback vertex set of size at most 2 times the optimum.
why: A deterministic 2-approximation would remove the reliance on randomness in approximating directed feedback vertex sets, settling the derandomization question left open since SODA 2020.

title: Linear matroid products: a synthetic approach — conj 1
open: Can the generic tensor product of the uniform matroids $U_{m-a,m}$ be described explicitly — that is, can one characterize this linear matroid product in a synthetic, concrete form?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.16747v2 (Mykhaylo Tyomkyn); no progress beyond the statement is recorded.
solved_when: An explicit description or characterization of the generic tensor product of the uniform matroids $U_{m-a,m}$ is given and proved.
why: It would advance the synthetic understanding of linear matroid products, a basic structural question in matroid theory.

title: Linear matroid products: a synthetic approach
open: Does the natural case of MATH and MATH being uniform matroids admit a linear matroid product of the synthetic kind? Its restriction to tensor products is known in the modern literature as Mason's conjecture: the generic tensor product of the uniform matroids MATH and MATH is their freest matroid tensor product.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), extracted from a curated open-problems paper; see http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16747v2 (Mykhaylo Tyomkyn).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the generic tensor product of the uniform matroids MATH and MATH is their freest matroid tensor product, settling the uniform case of the synthetic linear matroid product problem.
why: It settles the canonical uniform case of the synthetic approach to matroid products and resolves Mason's conjecture, a question that has become standard in the matroid theory literature.

title: Counterexamples and symmetry for uneven orthogonal mass partitions in — problem q:barany
open: If $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ assigning measure zero to every affine line, and $0 \le t \le 1/4$, must there be two orthogonal lines whose four regions, in cyclic order, have masses $t, 1/2 - t, t, 1/2 - t$?
solved_when: A proof or counterexample is given for the existence of such a pair of orthogonal lines for every Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with no mass on affine lines and every $t$ in $[0, 1/4]$.
why: It resolves whether uneven orthogonal mass partitions with this alternating structure always exist, settling a natural quantitative generalization of the classical equipartition question in the plane.

title: Counterexamples and symmetry for uneven orthogonal mass partitions in — problem prob:quadri
open: Does every convex quadrilateral satisfy Grünbaum's conjecture for every target of an uneven orthogonal mass partition? A second sentence may ask whether any convex quadrilateral and target pair yields a counterexample.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) resolving, for every target, whether every convex quadrilateral satisfies Grünbaum's conjecture.
why: It settles Grünbaum's conjecture in the quadrilateral case, either confirming symmetry of the partitions universally or identifying explicit counterexamples among convex quadrilaterals.

title: High-Multiplicity Bin Packing is FPT
open: Is High-Multiplicity Bin Packing fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) in MATH? More precisely, does an algorithm exist that decides or optimally solves the problem in time f(MATH) · n^O(1) for some computable function f?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.16923v1 (Tomohiro Koana, Soh Kumabe); no FPT algorithm or hardness result is recorded there.
solved_when: An FPT algorithm for High-Multiplicity Bin Packing parameterized by MATH is given, or a hardness result rules out such an algorithm (e.g., W[1]-hardness) under standard assumptions.
why: A resolution would settle a central complexity question for encoding-succinct input models, determining whether multiplicity-encoded instances can be handled as tractably as their explicitly listed counterparts.

title: Concise tensors with maximal symmetries
open: What is the sharp upper bound on the stabilizer dimension of an arbitrary concise tensor, and which tensors attain it? The known tight bound applies only to balanced tensors, where the maximizers have been classified; the question is to extend both the bound and the classification to all concise tensors.
solved_when: A tight upper bound on stabilizer dimension is proved for all concise tensors, together with a classification of the tensors achieving it.
why: Completing the picture of which tensors carry the largest symmetry groups, extending the balanced case that currently forms the frontier of this classification program.

title: Concise tensors with maximal symmetries
