open: What is the largest possible dimension of the symmetry group of a concise tensor, once the binding assumption used in prior work is dropped? Formally, determine the maximum stabilizer dimension attained by concise tensors.
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.17280v1 (Annika Holtrup, Jeroen Zuiddam), following Conner, Gesmundo, Landsberg and Ventura, who posed determining the largest possible dimension of the symmetry group of a concise tensor without the binding assumption.
solved_when: A determination (with proof) of the maximum possible dimension of the symmetry group of a concise tensor, without the binding assumption imposed in earlier work.
why: It removes an artificial hypothesis from the study of tensor symmetries, telling us the true extremal behavior of stabilizer dimensions for concise tensors.

title: Relaxed coparking functions and Stanley's conjecture for matroid $h$-v
open: Is the $h$-vector of every matroid a pure $O$-sequence — that is, the degree sequence of a finite order ideal? A positive answer would confirm the matroid case of Stanley's conjecture on $h$-vectors.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every matroid, its $h$-vector equals the degree sequence of a finite order ideal of monomials.
why: It would settle Stanley's conjecture in the matroid setting, connecting the combinatorics of matroids to Hilbert functions of Artinian monomial algebras.

title: Relaxed coparking functions and Stanley's conjecture for matroid $h$-v
open: Is the pair $(M,B_0)$'s invariant $h(M,B_0)$ realizable as the $h$-vector of some matroid? More precisely, does this relaxation of Stanley's conjecture for matroid $h$-vectors continue to hold in the relative setting anchored at a distinguished basis $B_0$?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.17446v2 (SuHo Oh); no progress beyond its posing is recorded in the census.
solved_when: An explicit answer is given: either a matroid whose $h$-vector equals $h(M,B_0)$ is constructed (or its existence proven) for the relevant class of pairs, or a counterexample pair $(M,B_0)$ is produced for which no such matroid exists.
why: It tests whether Stanley's conjecture on matroid $h$-vectors survives passage to this relative/relaxed coparking-function setting, so a positive answer extends the conjecture's reach while a counterexample would sharply delimit it.

title: A $\sqrt{2}$-Approximation to the Bilu-Linial Conjecture — conjecture conj:BL
open: Does every $d$-regular graph admit a signing whose spectral behavior is controlled, in the spirit of the Bilu–Linial conjecture — specifically, when $d2$ is an integer? A second sentence may sharpen it formally.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that, whenever $d2$ is an integer, every $d$-regular graph $G$ has such a signing.

title: Every graph with no $K_7^=$ minor is 6-colorable — conjecture conj:k7minus
open: Does every 5-connected graph with at least $4n-2$ edges contain a $K_7^-$ minor? Formally: every $5$-connected graph with $n \ge 6$ vertices and at least $4n-2$ edges contains $K_7^-$ as a minor.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the statement that every $5$-connected graph with $n \ge 6$ vertices and at least $4n-2$ edges contains $K_7^-$ as a minor.
why: Resolving it would settle conjecture conj:k7minus, that every graph with no $K_7^=$ minor is 6-colorable.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17760v1 (Zdeněk Dvořák, Sergey Norin, Neil Rahman)

title: A near-linear upper bound for Burr's conjecture
open: Does every tournament on $2k-2$ vertices contain a copy of every oriented tree on $k$ vertices? This is the first conjecture of Burr, asking whether the Burr–Erdős–Lovász embedding bound holds at this vertex count.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every tournament on $2k-2$ vertices contains every oriented tree on $k$ vertices, for all $k$.
why: It would pin down a sharp, near-linear vertex bound for embedding oriented trees in tournaments, a basic extremal question in directed graph containment.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18175v1 (Liangdong Fan, Junying Lu, Yaojun Chen)

title: Finite and infinite barrycades — conjecture Guyc
open: For every even $n$, does there exist a break-free $n$-barrycade? Formally, the conjecture asserts existence of a break-free structure for each even positive integer $n$.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, with counterexample) of the statement that a break-free $n$-barrycade exists for every even $n$.
why: The problem is extracted from a curated open-problems paper; resolving it advances the combinatorial theory of barrycades.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18476v2 (Michał Dębski, Jarosław Grytczuk, Paweł Naroski)

title: Finite and infinite barrycades
open: Is the sequence {A399898} infinite? That is, does this integer sequence, arising in the study of finite and infinite barrycades, contain infinitely many terms?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.18476v2 (Michał Dębski, Jarosław Grytczuk, Paweł Naroski); no progress beyond this statement is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the sequence {A399898} is infinite; no quantitative target is stated in the record, so establishing or refuting the sequence's infinitude is the criterion.
why: The problem originates from a curated open-problems collection, so settling it advances the combinatorial understanding of barrycade structures that the source paper develops.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18476v2 (Michał Dębski, Jarosław Grytczuk, Paweł Naroski)

title: Bounded VC-dimension implies the Erdős--Rado sunflower conjecture
open: Does the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture hold — that is, can the factorial term in the bound for \(f_r(k)\) be replaced by a constant \(K(r)\) depending only on \(r\), so that \(f_r(k) \le K(r)^k\)? This long-standing conjecture of Erdős and Rado remains one of the most important open problems in extremal combinatorics.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.18995v1 (Gennian Ge, Jian Wang, Zixiang Xu); it remains open in general.
solved_when: (see above)
why: Removing the factorial term would give the tight exponential-in-\(k\) sunflower bound, resolving a favorite open problem of Erdős and a central question in extremal combinatorics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18995v1 (Gennian Ge, Jian Wang, Zixiang Xu)

title: On the Strong Matroid Secretary Conjecture and Beyond — conjecture conj:strong
open: Does every matroid admit a secretary algorithm that is $1/e$-competitive? That is, can the elements of an arbitrary matroid, revealed in random order, be selected online so that the expected weight of the chosen independent set is at least a $1/e$ fraction of the optimum?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "On the Strong Matroid Secretary Conjecture and Beyond" (arXiv:2609.19118v1, Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi).
solved_when: A $1/e$-competitive secretary algorithm is exhibited for every matroid, or the conjecture is refuted by a matroid family for which no such algorithm exists.
why: The strong matroid secretary conjecture is a central test case for online selection under matroid constraints; a positive resolution would settle the natural competitive-ratio benchmark for the entire class of matroids at once.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19118v1 (Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi)

title: On the Strong Matroid Secretary Conjecture and Beyond
open: Is the truncated matroid's secretary performance never worse than the original's? Formally, the conjecture asserts that for every matroid M and every truncation level k, the competitive ratio achievable on the truncation is at least that achievable on M — a monotonicity the computed values on small matroids and their truncations were consistent with.
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), where computed values on small matroids and their truncations were consistent with the monotonicity conjecture; the record notes the conjecture is false in general. Key work: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19118v1 (Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the truncation monotonicity conjecture for all matroids M and every k; note the record indicates it is false in general, so a resolution may be a counterexample or a characterization of when it holds.
why: Truncation is a basic structural operation on matroids; establishing (or bounding the failure of) this monotonicity would clarify how secretary competitive ratios behave under truncation, informing the Strong Matroid Secretary Conjecture and beyond.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19118v1 (Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi)

title: Unimodality for IDP Lattice Simplices of Prime Normalized Volume — problem OpenIDPUniom
open: If a lattice polytope has the integer decomposition property (IDP), must its $h^*$-polynomial be unimodal?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19637v1 (Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether every IDP lattice simplex of prime normalized volume has a unimodal $h^*$-polynomial.
why: Unimodality of $h^*$-polynomials is a central structural question in Ehrhart theory; resolving it for IDP polytopes would clarify how the integer decomposition property constrains Ehrhart data.

title: Is the Signed Zarankiewicz Number the Same as the Recursive-line Zaran
open: Do the signed Zarankiewicz number and the recursive-line Zarankiewicz number coincide in every dimension — that is, is \(z_{SL}(m,n)=z_{RL}(m,n)\) for all \(m,n\)? More precisely, does the recursive-line construction always achieve the optimal value of the signed crossing-number variant?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.20071v1 (Zhiwei Chen, Yannan Chen, Liqun Qi).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with an explicit counterexample) that \(z_{SL}(m,n)=z_{RL}(m,n)\) holds for all pairs \(m,n\).
why: Equality would reduce the signed Zarankiewicz number to a recursively computable quantity, making it tractable; any gap would reveal dimensions where the signed variant is genuinely harder than its recursive counterpart.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20071v1 (Zhiwei Chen, Yannan Chen, Liqun Qi)

title: New upper bounds for the chromatic numbers of Euclidean spaces
open: Are the recently proposed lattice colorings optimal among all lattice colorings of the Euclidean spaces in question? Formally, the ABPR conjecture (Open question 1 of the paper) asserts that these coloring values are optimal among all lattice colorings of the respective spaces.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.20436v1 (Leonid Ivanov, Nadezhda Glushkova); no partial results are recorded here.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with a better lattice coloring) of the optimality of the proposed colorings among all lattice colorings of the spaces in question.
why: Establishing optimality would settle the exact lattice-chromatic behavior of these Euclidean spaces and pin down whether the proposed constructions leave any room for improvement.

title: Longest cycles intersect linearly in highly connected graphs — conjecture conj:smith
open: Do any two longest cycles in a highly connected graph have to meet in many vertices? Conjecturally, for every integer $k \geq 2$, any two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph share at least $k$ vertices.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Jie Ma, Bo Ning, Ziyuan Zhao, arXiv:2609.20724v1 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20724v1); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the statement that, for every integer $k \geq 2$, any two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph intersect in at least $k$ common vertices.
why: It would give a tight, linear connection between connectivity and the unavoidable overlap of longest cycles, a basic structural fact about how longest cycles can sit inside a graph.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20724v1 (Jie Ma, Bo Ning, Ziyuan Zhao)

title: The Strong Secretary Conjecture is True for Linear Matroids
open: Does the strong Matroid Secretary Conjecture hold, i.e., do arbitrary matroids admit a constant-factor competitive secretary algorithm? More precisely, the question is whether the strong form of the conjecture — constant-factor competitiveness for every matroid — is true for linear matroids, while the general conjecture remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the strong Matroid Secretary Conjecture is established; success means demonstrating a constant-factor competitive guarantee for arbitrary matroids, or resolving the conjecture's status for linear matroids. No quantitative constant or other budget is specified in the record.
why: A proof would settle the long-standing question of whether arbitrary matroids admit a constant-factor competitive secretary guarantee, completing a central goal of the matroid secretary literature.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20797v1 (Kristóf Bérczi, Shaddin Dughmi, Vasilis Livanos)

title: On the Word-Representability of Tensor Product Graphs
open: Can the tensor product of two graphs, each of which is not word-representable, itself be word-representable? In other words, does word-representability behave monotonically under tensor products, or can non-representability be "cancelled" by taking such a product?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Nawaf Alshammari, "On the Word-Representability of Tensor Product Graphs" (arXiv:2609.20881v1, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20881v1).
solved_when: A solution is achieved when either an explicit pair of non-word-representable graphs whose tensor product is word-representable is exhibited, or a proof is given that the tensor product of any two non-word-representable graphs is never word-representable.
why: It would clarify how the class of word-representable graphs interacts with graph products, refining the boundary of the class and informing which constructions can preserve or destroy word-representability.

title: On the Word-Representability of Tensor Product Graphs
open: Can anything definite be said about taking the tensor product of two word-representable graphs? Or the tensor product of a word-representable and a non-word-representable graph? Or the tensor product of two non-word-representable graphs?

title: An elementary proof of the Komlós conjecture
open: Does an elementary proof exist for conjecture 1 of the source paper, namely that there is a universal constant $C>0$ such that the stated property holds?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.20979v2 (Sankeerth Rao Karingula, Shachar Lovett).
solved_when: A complete proof of conjecture 1, establishing the universal constant $C>0$, is given by elementary means.
why: An elementary proof would make the result accessible and self-contained where the conjecture currently stands unproven.

title: Erdős-Sós via random cyclic orderings — conjecture conj:main
open: Does every graph of average degree greater than $k-1$ contain every tree with $k$ edges as a subgraph, for every integer $k \geq 1$? This is the classical Erdős–Sós conjecture, here approached via random cyclic orderings.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.21159v1 (Bryce Frederickson).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the statement that for every integer $k \geq 1$, every graph of average degree more than $k-1$ contains every tree with $k$ edges as a subgraph.
why: The conjecture is a cornerstone of extremal graph theory; a proof would settle a decades-old question generalizing many results on tree embeddings and would tightly characterize the extremal average degree for containing all $k$-edge trees.

title: Surface subgroups of Baumslag doubles along short words — question gromov_q
open: Does every one-ended word-hyperbolic group contain a hyperbolic surface subgroup? Equivalently, must such a group contain a subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic surface?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.21191v2 (Hoang Le Xuan, Nam Hung Tran Nguyen). No further progress is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every one-ended word-hyperbolic group contains a hyperbolic surface subgroup, or exhibiting a one-ended word-hyperbolic group with none.
why: This is a central test case for Gromov's surface subgroup conjecture; a positive answer would give a uniform structural feature shared by all one-ended word-hyperbolic groups, while a counterexample would reveal a fundamentally new kind of hyperbolic group.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21191v2 (Hoang Le Xuan, Nam Hung Tran Nguyen)

title: Hardness of Online Directed Steiner Network
open: Does the need to commit to decisions before seeing future demands — the essence of the online setting — by itself rule out polylogarithmic-competitive algorithms for Online Directed Steiner Network?
status: Stated as an open question in the source paper (2026); see http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22605v1 (Gary Hoppenworth, Yaowei Long, Sepideh Mahabadi).
solved_when: Either a polylogarithmic-competitive online algorithm for Online Directed Steiner Network is given, or a proof that no such algorithm exists.
why: It separates what is hard about the problem: the directed Steiner structure or the online uncertainty. A resolution in either direction sharpens the landscape of competitive ratios achievable for online network design.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22605v1 (Gary Hoppenworth, Yaowei Long, Sepideh Mahabadi)

title: Interval number for tournaments in P3-convexity
open: Is the problem {pro:tinps} NP-complete, as conjectured?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that {pro:tinps} is NP-complete is established; in case of refutation, a polynomial-time algorithm deciding it.
why: Settling the complexity of computing the interval number of tournaments in P3-convexity resolves whether this invariant can be efficiently computed or is intrinsically hard.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22640v1 (Idian C. Capozzoli, Yan S. Couto, Enrique Junchaya)

title: Exact Area-Range Minima in the Quantitative Monsky Problem for Five an — question q:two-level
open: For every odd \(n \ge 3\), does there exist a minimizing dissection whose triangle areas take only two distinct value?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper arXiv:2609.22693 (Muxi Li, 2026).
solved_when: A construction (or proof of impossibility) is given for every odd \(n \ge 3\), exhibiting a minimizing dissection of the square into \(n\) equal-area triangles whose triangle areas assume only two distinct values.
why: A solution would sharpen the quantitative Monsky problem by showing optimality can always be achieved with maximally simple area structure, constraining how minimizers can look and informing lower-bound techniques.

title: An Odd Pfaffian Number
open: Is there a graph whose Pfaffian orientation count is an odd number other than the known ones — specifically, can 7, 9, or 11 occur — and are there infinitely many odd Pfaffian numbers?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.22928v1 (Priyanshu Pant, Ranveer Singh).
solved_when: Either an example is produced realizing 7, 9, or 11 as a Pfaffian number, or these values are ruled out; and, separately, it is settled whether the set of odd Pfaffian numbers is infinite or finite.
why: It determines the structure of the set of possible Pfaffian orientation counts, clarifying which small odd values are attainable and whether the family is infinite.

title: An Odd Pfaffian Number
open: For general graphs, what is the computational complexity of deciding whether a Pfaffian orientation exists? That is, is there an efficient algorithm that determines, for an arbitrary input graph, whether it admits an orientation under which every even cycle is oddly directed?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026); see http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22928v1 (Priyanshu Pant, Ranveer Singh).
solved_when: The complexity of deciding whether a Pfaffian orientation exists for general graphs is resolved, e.g. by a polynomial-time algorithm or a proof of hardness for an appropriate class.
why: Resolving this would complete the complexity picture for Pfaffian orientation, a central tool underlying counting perfect matchings via the FKT method; without it, the boundary between the known tractable and intractable cases remains uncharted.

title: An Odd Pfaffian Number
open: What is the exact Pfaffian number of three copies of \(K_{3,3}\), and, more generally, of any number of copies of \(K_{3,3}\)?
solved_when: The exact Pfaffian number of three copies of \(K_{3,3}\) is determined, together with the exact value for any number of copies.
why: It resolves the basic counting question for the smallest non-Pfaffian building block, completing our picture of how repeated \(K_{3,3}\) copies govern Pfaffian orientation behavior.

title: The Last Seven Open Radii for Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme
open: Do nontrivial e-perfect codes exist in the Johnson scheme J(n,w) for the remaining open radii e ∈ {1,2,4,9,10,12,16}, or can their existence be excluded?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (Xiande Zhang, Wenjie Zhong, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23368v1, 2026); no cases among the seven radii are resolved in the record.
solved_when: Nonexistence of nontrivial e-perfect codes in J(n,w) is proved for each of the seven radii e ∈ {1,2,4,9,10,12,16}, or an explicit nontrivial example is constructed for one of them.
why: These seven radii are the last unsettled cases for perfect codes in the Johnson scheme, so resolving them would complete the classification problem for this family of codes.

title: A Fixed-Parameter Algorithm for 4-Block Integer Programming
open: Does 4-block integer programming admit a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm, as conjectured by Eisenbrand and Rothvoss and regarded in the theoretical integer programming community as a popular open problem?
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper arXiv:2609.23711v1 (Klaus Jansen, Felix Ohnesorge, Corinna Wambsganz), which reports Eisenbrand and Rothvoss formulating the explicit conjecture in 2026 and describes the existence of an FPT-type algorithm as a popular open problem.
solved_when: An FPT-type algorithm for 4-block integer programming is given and proved correct; the record states no further quantitative targets (parameter bounds or exponents).
why: The source paper presents this conjecture as a central open question in the theoretical IP community, and resolving it would settle whether 4-block IP is tractable in the parameterized sense.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23711v1 (Klaus Jansen, Felix Ohnesorge, Corinna Wambsganz)

title: The Exponential Price of Determinism in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimizati
open: Is there a deterministic algorithm for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization that substantially beats exhaustive grid search? Known lower bounds are only linear in dimension, while the best deterministic method remains a grid search, leaving a possibly exponential gap between the upper and lower bounds.
status: The source paper (arXiv:2609.23837v1, Guy Kornowski, 2026) proves a linear-in-dimension lower bound for deterministic algorithms, but no deterministic algorithm better than exhaustive grid search is known, so an exponential gap remains open.
solved_when: A deterministic algorithm for the task is found whose complexity is significantly better than exhaustive grid search (closing, or nontrivially shrinking, the exponential gap relative to the known linear lower bound), or a matching stronger lower bound is proved showing the grid-search cost is unavoidable.
why: Closing the gap settles whether determinism truly carries an exponential price in nonsmooth nonconvex settings, directly shaping what guarantees randomized-free methods can hope for in practice.

title: Regular Solutions of the Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations in Arbitra
open: Are suitable weak solutions of the stationary Navier–Stokes equations necessarily regular in dimensions five and six? A formal version asks whether the partial regularity theory extends to give full regularity of suitable weak solutions in these high dimensions.
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.24206v1 (Wendong Wang, Guoxu Yang); no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every suitable weak solution of the stationary Navier–Stokes equations in dimension five and dimension six is smooth, or the identification of a singular suitable weak solution.
why: It would complete the regularity picture for stationary Navier–Stokes in the critical higher dimensions, closing a basic gap between the known partial regularity theory and full regularity.

title: Optimal Ferrers Diagram Rank-Metric Codes: New Constructions, Diagram — open problem 2 3
open: Do optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric (FDRM) codes exist for every square $n\times n$ Ferrers diagram? More precisely, the question left open by Etzion et al. asks for which parameters the upper bound of Lemma 3 can be attained on this important class of diagrams.
solved_when: An optimal FDRM code supported on any $n\times n$ square Ferrers diagram is constructed, attaining the upper bound of Lemma 3 for the general case, beyond the known cases $d=2$, $d=3$, the family with $d=n$, the cases $d=n$ and $d=n-1$ of Zhang et al., and the $n\times n$ upper-triangular diagrams with $d=n-1$ of Antrobus et al.
why: Square Ferrers diagrams are a fundamental class for the general theory of FDRM codes, and resolving the existence of optimal codes on them would close a basic gap between known upper bounds and constructions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24239v1 (Fang-Wei Fu, Xuan Gao, Sihem Mesnager)

title: Optimal Ferrers Diagram Rank-Metric Codes: New Constructions, Diagram — open problem 1 2
open: Is the optimality of a Ferrers diagram rank-metric (FDRM) code preserved when the underlying Ferrers diagram is suitably enlarged or reduced? Zhang et al. observed that an optimal FDRM code supported on a relatively small Ferrers diagram may remain optimal when viewed as a code over a larger Ferrers diagram, so one may ask whether optimal FDRM codes continue to exist for Ferrers diagrams obtained by deleting "vain" points from known feasible diagrams, i.e., diagrams for which optimal FDRM codes have already been constructed — for example, for $F=[1,2,3,4,8,8,8,8,9]$, for which an optimal $[F, 6, 7]_q$ code exists.
solved_when: A construction (or impossibility proof) of optimal FDRM codes on Ferrers diagrams obtained by deleting vain points from known feasible diagrams is given, including the specific case of an optimal code for $F=[1,2,3,4,8,8,8,8,9]$ and analogous instances.
why: Explicit constructions of optimal FDRM codes are often highly nontrivial, so a principle transferring optimality across diagram enlargements or deletions would yield many new optimal codes without case-by-case constructions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24239v1 (Fang-Wei Fu, Xuan Gao, Sihem Mesnager)

title: The Generalized Lax Conjecture for Strictly Hyperbolic Polynomials
open: Does the generalized Lax conjecture hold for every strictly hyperbolic polynomial, beyond the generic case?
status: The generalized Lax conjecture has been established for the generic case; the full conjecture remains open, as stated in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.24542v1 (Mario Kummer, Tim Netzer).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the generalized Lax conjecture for all strictly hyperbolic polynomials is given, extending beyond the generic case.
why: Settling it would extend the hyperbolicity-cone/determinantal-representation correspondence central to real algebraic geometry and optimization from generic polynomials to the full class.

title: On infinite families of $[P_n]$-irregular graphs — conjecture con1
open: For every connected graph $F$ of order $|F| 3$, does there exist a non-trivial $F$-irregular graph? Formally, the question is whether every connected graph of order $|F| 3$ arises as the obstruction to irregularity, i.e., admits some non-trivial $F$-irregular graph.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.24707v1 by Tatiana Dovzhenok, Ilya Lukashenko, and Andrei Mikhalev.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) is given that for every connected graph $F$ of order $|F| 3$ there exists a non-trivial $F$-irregular graph.
why: A positive answer would establish that irregularity strength-type constructions exist for every connected graph of this order, completing the conjecture (con1) posed in the source paper.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24707v1 (Tatiana Dovzhenok, Ilya Lukashenko, Andrei Mikhalev)

title: Improved polynomial-time algorithms for detecting and recovering plant — conjecture conj:clique
open: For every fixed $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, is there truly no polynomial-time algorithm that achieves strong detection — and therefore no polynomial-time algorithm that achieves strong recovery — for the planted clique problem in the regime $k \le n^{1/2-\epsilon}$? In other words, prove the conjectured computational hardness of both detection and recovery below the $n^{1/2}$ clique-size threshold.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that for every fixed $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, no polynomial-time algorithm achieves strong detection, and hence strong recovery, in the planted clique problem when $k \le n^{1/2-\epsilon}$; alternatively, a polynomial-time algorithm achieving strong detection or recovery in that regime.
why: Establishing this would give a rigorous foundation for the widely believed hardness of planted clique below the square-root threshold, anchoring hardness assumptions used throughout average-case complexity and cryptographic applications.

title: A Proof of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture
open: Is the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture true, and can a proof be established? The conjecture was posed on the Google side of this research line, where the team was actively attempting to resolve it, and it was explicitly flagged as an open problem in an AI acceleration paper.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.24931v2 (Zijie Chen, Amin Gohari, Adel Javanmard), where it is highlighted as an open problem the team was attempting to solve using AI.
solved_when: A rigorous proof (or refutation) of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture is given, resolving the question as stated in the source paper.
why: The problem was surfaced in a curated open-problems paper and targeted by an AI-assisted research effort, so a solution would directly answer a question that both the Google team and the AI acceleration program identified as a key obstruction.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24931v2 (Zijie Chen, Amin Gohari, Adel Javanmard)

solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of conjecture c1 of Berkovich and Dhar on hook lengths, as stated in paper 2609.26324, is given.

title: Ample vector bundles without Griffiths-semipositive metrics — question qu:cotangent
open: Fix integers $n \geq 2$ and $c \geq n$. If $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+c}$ is a general smooth complete intersection of multidegree $(d_1, \dots, d_c)$, does the cotangent bundle $\Omega_Y^1$ admit a smooth Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric for all sufficiently large degrees $d_1, \dots, d_c$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that, for fixed $n \geq 2$ and $c \geq n$ and all sufficiently large degrees $d_1, \dots, d_c$, the cotangent bundle $\Omega_Y^1$ of a general smooth complete intersection $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+c}$ of multidegree $(d_1, \dots, d_c)$ does (respectively does not) admit a smooth Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric.
why: It would exhibit natural ample vector bundles carrying Griffiths-positive metrics, or show that ampleness of such cotangent bundles fails to guarantee one — directly probing the Griffiths-semipositivity conjecture for ample bundles.

title: Analytic toroidal 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows with invari
open: Do there exist non-axisymmetric toroidal equilibria that satisfy quasisymmetry exactly, or is exact quasisymmetry only achievable in axisymmetric configurations? In formal terms, the question asks for existence (or non-existence) of non-axisymmetric analytic 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows obeying exact quasisymmetry.
solved_when: A rigorous construction of a non-axisymmetric toroidal MHD equilibrium (or steady Euler flow) satisfying exact quasisymmetry, or a proof that no such equilibrium exists.
why: Exact quasisymmetry is the confining-property target for optimized stellarator designs, so an existence or non-existence theorem would determine whether the exact ideal can be achieved or must be replaced by approximate symmetry.

title: Analytic toroidal 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows with invari
open: Do there exist exact analytic solutions describing non-axisymmetric toroidal magnetic fields with nested toroidal flux surfaces when the field is required to be curl-free (vacuum) or force-free? In other words, can such equilibria be written down in closed form, beyond the axisymmetric setting?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), a curated open-problems paper available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26742v2 (Matt Landreman).
solved_when: An explicit analytic (closed-form) non-axisymmetric toroidal field with nested toroidal flux surfaces is exhibited and proved curl-free (vacuum) or force-free; a proof that no such analytic solution exists would equally resolve the question.
why: Such solutions would provide exact benchmarks for 3D stellarator equilibrium codes and deepen the theory of steady Euler and MHD equilibria; their absence indicates that non-axisymmetric equilibria may be intrinsically non-analytic.

title: Explicit channels with unbounded gains in classical communication usin
open: While Hastings' result proved the existence of this phenomenon, it has remained a major open problem to find an explicit channel with this property. Can one write down an explicit channel exhibiting the superadditivity phenomenon Hastings showed to exist nonconstructively?
solved_when: An explicit channel is constructed whose classical communication capacity exhibits the unbounded gain in question, matching the phenomenon whose existence Hastings established.
why: An explicit construction would turn a nonconstructive existence result into a usable object, enabling analysis of how and why such capacity gains arise.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26743v2 (Hao-Chung Cheng, Benjamin Lovitz, Peixue Wu)

title: An Exponential Succinctness Gap between Three-Variable Logic and the C
open: Does an exponential succinctness gap survive when the signature is fixed? The known formulas live over relation symbols that vary with the construction, and since size charges each symbol occurrence one node, it is unclear whether a fixed-signature family of structures can still witness an exponential separation.
status: The gap is established by uniform lower bounds, but the source paper states as open whether an exponential gap holds for a family over a fixed signature (Remark in the paper). The open question is stated in the source paper (2026) by Yuya Uezato, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26778v1.
solved_when: An explicit family over a fixed signature is exhibited for which the exponential succinctness gap holds, or a proof shows no such fixed-signature family can realize an exponential gap.
why: It determines whether the observed exponential separation is a genuine expressivity phenomenon of three-variable logic versus the richer logic, rather than an artifact of growing signatures; a uniform lower bound over a fixed signature would considerably strengthen the separation.

title: Tight Regret Bound for Online Inverse Linear Optimization via Multisca
open: Can the known regret order for online inverse linear optimization be achieved by an algorithm whose running time is polynomial in the dimension, the horizon, and the input length? In other words, is there a computationally efficient algorithm matching the best known regret guarantee in this multiscale setting?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper, arXiv:2609.26978v1 (Shinsaku Sakaue, 2026).
solved_when: An algorithm is given that attains the same regret order as the existing bound while running in time polynomial in the dimension, horizon, and input length.
why: It would close the gap between the information-theoretic regret guarantee and computational feasibility, making the optimal regret order actually attainable in practice; without it, the best regret order may be achievable only by methods too slow to run.

title: The switching conjecture for main eigenvalues is asymptotically true — conjecture conj:switching_n_main_eigenvalues
open: Given any unsigned connected graph $G$ not isomorphic to $K_2$ or $K_4 - e$, does there exist a switching of $G$ such that all distinct eigenvalues of the switched graph $G^{\sigma}$ are main?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27046v1 (Saieed Akbari, Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) is given, for every unsigned connected graph $G \notin \{K_2, K_4 - e\}$, of the existence of a switching under which all distinct eigenvalues of $G^{\sigma}$ are main.
why: Settling the switching conjecture for main eigenvalues would clarify how Seidel switching interacts with spectral properties, resolving a natural question about which spectra can be made "main" by switching.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27046v1 (Saieed Akbari, Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar)

title: The switching conjecture for main eigenvalues is asymptotically true — conjecture conj:signature
open: Does every connected unsigned graph $G$ of order $n \geq 3$ admit a signature $\sigma$ such that all eigenvalues of the signed graph $(G, \sigma)$ are main?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, via an explicit counterexample) of the existence, for every unsigned connected graph $G$ of order $n \geq 3$, of a signature $\sigma$ making every eigenvalue of $(G, \sigma)$ main.
why: It would establish asymptotically the switching conjecture for main eigenvalues (conjecture conj:signature), showing switching can control which eigenvalues of a signed graph are main.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27046v1 (Saieed Akbari, Hitesh Kumar, Bojan Mohar)

why: It answers an open question posed by Hong, Kwak, and Yang (2021) concerning the rigorous validity of the KdV approximation for the FPU system.

solved_when: The conjecture is proved (or disproved with a counterexample): a good parity representation of the classical groups under consideration is unitary exactly when it is of Arthur type, including for pure inner forms of the split group in the case treated in the paper.

title: Credible AUctions via MPC Gadgets: Bounding Information Leakage Under
open: Can a constant-round MPC protocol yield a credible auction that is simultaneously incentive-compatible and revenue-optimal for all product distributions with vanishing revenue tails?

why: It would establish that strong credibility and revenue guarantees for auctions do not require many rounds of interaction, making such auctions practical where communication rounds are costly.

title: Credible AUctions via MPC Gadgets: Bounding Information Leakage Under
open: Can the information leaked when participants abort a multiparty-computation-based auction be bounded tightly enough that a suitable penalty makes aborting never profitable — and can this yield a constant-round, incentive-compatible, revenue-optimal auction that is credible for all product distributions over bidder valuations with vanishing revenue tails?
solved_when: A construction is given that is constant-round, incentive-compatible, revenue-optimal, and credible for all product distributions over bidder valuations with vanishing revenue tails, with a penalty ensuring aborting is never profitable, where the relevant benchmark is the optimal single-bidder revenue for a bidder with valuation drawn from the value distribution profile of real bidders.
why: It resolves the open problem left by the source paper on credible auctions via MPC gadgets, extending credibility guarantees to a broad class of valuation distributions.

title: Milnor's inequality and circular elastic knots
open: Does the spherical elastic knot conjecture — the analogue of Milnor's inequality for elastic knots constrained to the sphere — hold true? A second, sharper formulation asks whether the conjecture as stated in the source paper can be proved in full.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.27643v1 by Tatsuya Miura, and no progress beyond that statement is recorded.
solved_when: The spherical elastic knot conjecture is proved (or disproved) as posed in arXiv:2609.27643.
why: The record gives no specific consequence; the problem is extracted from a curated open-problems paper, so resolving it advances the elastic-knot programme laid out there.

title: Milnor's inequality and circular elastic knots
open: Does Milnor's inequality for circular elastic knots extend to limit curves with arbitrary self-intersections, beyond the finitely many isolated self-intersections assumed by Wacker? A proof covering any configuration of self-intersections would sharpen the theorem formally.
status: Wacker proved the inequality under the assumption that the limit curve has only finitely many isolated self-intersections, and posed the extension to arbitrary self-intersections as an open problem; the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.27643v1 (Tatsuya Miura), states the problem as open and {thm:milnor} resolves it.
solved_when: Milnor's inequality is established for limit curves with arbitrary self-intersections, removing the finite isolated self-intersection hypothesis.
why: It removes the last regularity restriction on the limit curve in the elastic-knot compactness argument, making the inequality fully general.

title: Refuting the QAOA fixed-angle conjecture — conjecture conjecture:FixedAngle
open: Does the QAOA fixed-angle conjecture hold — that is, can fixed angles chosen independently of the input graph achieve good performance on all $d$-regular graphs at depth $p$? A precise formulation would exhibit, or refute the existence of, a single set of angles working uniformly across a $d$-regular graph $G$ at given $p, d$.
solved_when: The conjecture is settled: either fixed angles are proven to achieve the conjectured uniform performance on $d$-regular graphs for the given depth $p$, or an explicit counterexample (a $d$-regular graph and angle set) refuting it is produced.
why: A resolution determines whether QAOA parameters can be fixed once and for all rather than optimized per instance, which directly affects whether the algorithm can be implemented without costly classical parameter optimization.

status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "An Introduction to the Lagrange and Markov Spectra through the Lens of —" by Yasuaki Gyoda (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28097v1); no resolution is recorded.

why: A solution would clarify how uniqueness phenomena in the classical Markov and Lagrange spectra persist or break under generalization, informing the structural theory of these Diophantine approximation spectra.

open: For any Markov number $c$, is the positive integer solution of the Markov equation whose largest component is $c$ uniquely determined up to permutation of its components?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper, "An Introduction to the Lagrange and Markov Spectra through the Lens of" (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28097v1, Yasuaki Gyoda), from 2026.

title: A tris of perfect matchings in bridgeless claw-free cubic graphs
open: Does every bridgeless claw-free cubic graph admit a cycle double cover whose even subgraphs arise from a small family of perfect matchings — in particular, does the assertion with five even subgraphs, the cycle double cover (CDC) conjecture, hold in this setting? This question remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every bridgeless claw-free cubic graph has a cycle double cover consisting of five even subgraphs, as in the CDC conjecture.
why: Resolving it would extend the CDC conjecture to an important structured class of cubic graphs, connecting matching theory and cycle covering.

title: Inverse knapsack at two capacities: which pairs of value-cardinality h — question q:ec-three
open: Is every rational target with value-cardinality $b_w = 3$ achievable in the uncapped inverse-knapsack model? Formally, does $EC = FWC$ hold for all rational targets with $b_w = 3$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.28128v1 (Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal); no case at $b_w = 3$ has been resolved either way.
solved_when: A proof that $EC = FWC$ for all rational targets with $b_w = 3$ in the uncapped model, or an explicit rational target with $b_w = 3$ witnessing $EC \neq FWC$.
why: It settles the boundary of which rational targets are achievable in the uncapped model, the next case beyond smaller cardinalities in the inverse-knapsack framework.

solved_when: Explicit counterexamples are exhibited answering van der Kallen's long-standing open question on relative Schubert filtrations negatively, already for tensor products of two dual Joseph modules.

title: Counterexamples to the Reiner-Shimozono conjecture and the failure of
open: Do tensor products of modules with excellent filtrations admit relative Schubert filtrations, as van der Kallen's long-standing question asks? Formally, such filtrations would have successive quotients with atom-positive characters and would therefore imply the Reiner–Shimozono conjecture.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), which comes from a curated open-problems paper; see http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28169v2 (Reuven Hodges).
solved_when: A construction of a relative Schubert filtration on tensor products of modules with excellent filtrations whose successive quotients have atom-positive characters is given (thereby implying the Reiner–Shimozono conjecture), or a counterexample is produced.
why: It supplies the geometric mechanism behind the expectation underlying the Reiner–Shimozono conjecture: atom-positive quotients in such filtrations would give a structural explanation for the conjecture's character positivity.

title: Static Solitons in an Expanding Universe
open: Does a static 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole solution exist in an expanding universe? More precisely, one asks whether the field equations in this cosmological setting admit a monopole configuration that remains static rather than being swept along by the expansion.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.28540v1 (Nagabhushana Prabhu); no solution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A rigorous construction (or proof of nonexistence) of a static 't Hooft–Polyakov monopole solution to the field equations of the expanding-universe setting considered in the source paper is established.
why: A static soliton surviving cosmological expansion would clarify how localized topological objects persist on an expanding background, a question of direct interest to cosmology and to the stability theory of solitons.

title: Towards a more structured search for Erdős-Gyárfás counter-examples — myconjecture conj:deg-2
open: Does every graph with at most one vertex of degree at most two and at least one vertex of degree at least three contain a cycle whose length is a power of two? This is a sharpened form of the Erdős–Gyárfás power-of-two-cycles question, restricting to graphs that are essentially 2-degenerate-free.
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) is given for the statement that every graph with at most one vertex of degree at most two and at least one vertex of degree at least three has a cycle of power-of-two length; a counterexample would likewise resolve it as a potential Erdős–Gyárfás counter-example.
why: It narrows the search space for Erdős–Gyárfás counter-examples to a structured, near-minimum-degree class, so any counterexample found here would immediately disprove the broader conjecture while any proof reduces it to graphs with two or more low-degree vertices.

title: There are no nontrivial chordal square-complementary graphs
open: Do there exist any nontrivial square-complementary graphs that are chordal or contain a simplicial vertex? Establishing the implication at stake would show that nontrivial square-complementary graphs have no simplicial vertices and are not chordal, thereby solving two open problems posed in Discrete Mathematics 327 (2014) 62--75.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper arXiv:2609.28702v1 (Pierre Aboulker, Martin Milanič, Peter Muršič, no year given); it is posed as open problem 1 there.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every nontrivial square-complementary graph has no simplicial vertices and is not chordal, resolving the two open problems posed in Discrete Mathematics 327 (2014) 62--75.
why: It settles two long-standing structural questions about square-complementary graphs, sharply constraining what such graphs can look like.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28702v1 (Pierre Aboulker, Martin Milanič, Peter Muršič)

title: There are no nontrivial chordal square-complementary graphs
open: Does there exist a nontrivial square-complementary graph that is chordal? Equivalently, among nontrivial squco graphs, is none chordal — settling Problem 5 of Milanič et al.'s open-problem list, which also asks (Problem 6) whether any nontrivial squco graph can contain a simplicial vertex?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28702v1 (Pierre Aboulker, Martin Milanič, Peter Muršič), in 2026.
solved_when: A proof that no nontrivial squco graph is chordal, or an explicit construction of a nontrivial squco graph that is chordal, is given; the related question of whether a nontrivial squco graph can contain a simplicial vertex may likewise be resolved.
why: It would settle two of the open problems posed on square-complementary graphs, delineating which graph classes are compatible with square-complementarity and sharpening the structural theory of squco graphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28702v1 (Pierre Aboulker, Martin Milanič, Peter Muršič)

title: Packing Tails of Reciprocal Rectangles into Squares of Equal Area
open: Is it possible to pack the sequence of rectangles with sides \(1/n\) and \(1/(n+1)\), starting from \(n=1\), into a square of area equal to the total area of the sequence?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.28791v1 (Yu Jiang); only the tail versions are settled, and the original \(n=1\) case remains open.
solved_when: A packing (or a proof of impossibility) of the full reciprocal-rectangle sequence starting at \(n=1\) into a square of equal area is given.
why: It would resolve the original form of this packing question, which is only known for tails of the sequence, not the full sequence from the start.

title: Packing Tails of Reciprocal Rectangles into Squares of Equal Area
open: Does the Meir–Moser rectangle-packing problem admit a solution for the full sequence of reciprocal rectangles starting at \(n=1\), packed into squares of equal area? The existing result covers only sufficiently late tails of the sequence, leaving the initial segment unresolved.
status: The problem remains open; the source paper (2026) proves a result only for sufficiently late tails of the sequence and does not resolve the full problem from \(n=1\). Key work: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28791v1 (Yu Jiang).
solved_when: A packing of the reciprocal rectangles for the full sequence beginning at \(n=1\) into squares of equal area is established, not merely for sufficiently late tails.
why: Resolving the initial segment would complete the original Meir–Moser packing problem rather than only its asymptotic tail, closing the gap left by the current probabilistic and row-geometry arguments.

title: Computations of Cohomology of Arithmetic Groups, Part 1
open: Is the cohomology of GL_m over the relevant arithmetic setting entirely accounted for by Eisenstein classes in the two degrees predicted by duality — that is, does \(H^p(GL_m(\cdot),V) = H^p_{Eis}(GL_m(\cdot),V) + H^{N-p}_{Eis}(GL_m(\cdot), V\det^{m-1})\) hold?
solved_when: The displayed equality \(H^p(GL_m(\cdot),V) = H^p_{Eis}(GL_m(\cdot),V) + H^{N-p}_{Eis}(GL_m(\cdot), V\det^{m-1})\) is proven, or disproved by an explicit counterexample.
why: A proof would give a complete, computable decomposition of arithmetic-group cohomology into Eisenstein pieces, making such cohomology directly calculable and constraining the non-Eisenstein (e.g., cuspidal) part.

title: Computations of Cohomology of Arithmetic Groups, Part 1
open: Does the cohomology of arithmetic groups exhibit the duality suggested by the paper, namely \(E^{p,q}_r(V,r)=E^{p-r+1,N-q+r-1}_r(V\otimes \det^{m-1},r)\)? In other words, do the spectral-sequence pages for \(V\) and for \(V\) twisted by \(\det^{m-1}\) mirror each other in the stated bidegrees?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.28869v1 (Ivan Horozov); no proof or partial result is recorded in the census.
solved_when: The displayed equality of spectral sequence terms holds, i.e. a proof (or disproof with counterexample) of \(E^{p,q}_r(V,r)=E^{p-r+1,N-q+r-1}_r(V\otimes\det^{m-1},r)\) is given.
why: Such a duality would give a structural handle on the cohomology of arithmetic groups, relating computations for one coefficient system to computations for a twisted one, effectively halving the work needed to determine these groups.

title: Computations of Cohomology of Arithmetic Groups, Part 1
open: Is the Eisenstein cohomology of $GL_4$ built up entirely from data coming from the inner cohomology of its proper Levi subgroups $GL_1$ and $GL_2$? Formally, the Euler characteristic of the Eisenstein cohomology, $\sum_q (-1)^q \dim H^q_{Eis}(GL_4(\,\cdot\,), V_\cdot)$, is conjectured to contain only terms induced by the inner cohomology of $GL_1$ and $GL_2$, with no contributions from $GL_3$ or $GL_4$.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjecture that the Euler characteristic of the Eisenstein cohomology of $GL_4$ receives contributions only from the inner cohomology of $GL_1$ and $GL_2$, and none from $GL_3$ or $GL_4$.
why: It would clarify precisely which smaller-rank cohomological data determines the Eisenstein part of the cohomology of $GL_4$, constraining the structure of arithmetic-group cohomology.

title: Computations of Cohomology of Arithmetic Groups, Part 1
open: When a piece of the inner cohomology of a Levi quotient $S_P$ of a parabolic subgroup $P$ of $GL_m(\,)$ with coefficients in a highest weight representation shows up in the boundary cohomology, must it either survive into the Eisenstein cohomology or vanish entirely? Formally: is $H^k_!(S_P,V)$, whenever it occurs in the boundary cohomology of $GL_m(\,)$, either entirely captured by Eisenstein cohomology or completely absent?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every occurrence of $H^k_!(S_P,V)$ in the boundary cohomology of $GL_m(\,)$ with highest weight coefficients either contributes entirely to the Eisenstein cohomology or completely disappears.
why: It would clarify precisely which boundary classes of arithmetic group cohomology contribute to the actual cohomology of $GL_m(\,)$, sharpening the structure of Eisenstein cohomology for such groups.

status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29054v1 (Julien Baste, Simon Dreyer, Clara Marcille).
solved_when: An algorithm is exhibited that solves Temporal Zero Forcing Set in time f(treewidth, lifespan) times a polynomial in the input size.
why: It would extend zero-forcing tractability from static to temporal graphs, delineating which temporal parameters suffice for efficient solution.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29054v1 (Julien Baste, Simon Dreyer, Clara Marcille)

title: Refinements of Peck's theorem on simultaneous approximation to algebra
open: Does Theorem 1.1 remain true when the regularity condition (1.2) on the approximation functions is dropped? In other words, can the conclusion of Peck's theorem on simultaneous approximation to algebraic numbers be extended without the hypothesis that currently guarantees it?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.29360v1 (Yann Bugeaud, Bernard de Mathan).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation, via counterexample) of Theorem 1.1 without assuming condition (1.2), keeping the remaining hypotheses — the bounds MATHQ^{1/n} Q _i {C^{n/(n-1)} f_i(Q)} for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1 and Q^{1/n} Q _n C — intact.
why: It would clarify whether the regularity imposed by (1.2) is essential to simultaneous approximation to algebraic numbers or merely an artifact of the current proof technique.

title: The coarse Erdős-Pósa theorem — conjecture conj:qi
open: For every finite graph $H$, is there a function $f^H$ such that any graph excluding $H$ as a $q$-fat minor is $f^H(q)$-quasi-isometric to a graph with no $H$ minor?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the stated conjecture: for every finite graph $H$, there exists a function $f^H$ such that, for every $q$ and every graph $G$ with no $H$ as a $q$-fat minor, $G$ is $f^H(q)$-quasi-isometric to a graph $G'$ with no $H$ minor.
why: It would give a coarse-geometry analogue of the Erdős–Pósa theorem, explaining how fat-minor exclusions can be quasi-isometrically flattened into ordinary minor exclusions.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29414v1 (Sandra Albrechtsen, Marthe Bonamy, Romain Bourneuf)

title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
open: How many distinct Boolean threshold functions are there on n variables? Despite how basic this counting question is, the exact number remains unknown.
solved_when: A formula or exact characterization of the number of distinct Boolean threshold functions on n variables is given, for general n.
why: It is a fundamental counting quantity in the theory of threshold functions, underlying results on neuron capacity and memory retrieval models, so knowing it would sharpen the foundations of those areas.

title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
open: Since then, this problem has been extensively investigated and the upper bounds have continued to improve~, and the current best result is due to Tikhomirov~, who proved \[ P\{M_n is singular\}=(1/2+o(1))^n, \] which captures the probability at the correct exponential scale, whereas the conjectured finer asymptotic P\{M_n is singular\} =(1+o(1))\, {n^2}{2^{n-1}} still remains open.

title: On the Exact Turán Number of $F^-_{4,3}$ — conjecture conj:FHR
open: What is the exact Turán number of the hypergraph $F^-_{4,3}$? In particular, does the conjecture conj:FHR hold, asserting that there is an integer $m_0$ such that for every integer $m>m_0$ the exact value is given by the conjectured formula?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Chun-Qiu Fang, available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29903v1. No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: The conjecture conj:FHR is resolved: a threshold $m_0$ is established such that for all $m>m_0$ the exact Turán number of $F^-_{4,3}$ is determined, matching the conjectured value.
why: An exact determination would settle a specific case of the exact Turán problem for hypergraphs, where exact results are rare and typically require heavy stability machinery.

title: Chromatic word-quasisymmetric functions of matroids — conj:kernel 2
open: Is the kernel of the map from matroids to chromatic word-quasisymmetric functions generated exactly by the valuative relations and the loop-coloop relations? In other words, do these two families of relations span the entire kernel of this map?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the kernel of the map from matroids to chromatic word-quasisymmetric functions is spanned by the valuative relations and the loop-coloop relations, as stated in the source paper.
why: It gives a complete presentation of the algebra of chromatic word-quasisymmetric functions of matroids by generators and relations, showing the valuative and loop-coloop relations are the only obstructions.

title: Chromatic word-quasisymmetric functions of matroids — quest 7
open: What is the actual witness function certifying that the chromatic quasisymmetric and word-quasisymmetric functions of matroids are strongly valuative? A concrete description of this witness would make the strong valuativity property explicit rather than merely asserted.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.29927v1 by Raul Penaguiao and Sophie Rehberg.
solved_when: An explicit formula or construction of the witness function to the strong valuativity of the chromatic quasisymmetric and word-quasisymmetric functions is given and verified.
why: It converts the known strong valuativity statement into an explicit object, which can be used in computations and in extending invariant-theoretic results for matroid subdivisions.

title: Chromatic word-quasisymmetric functions of matroids — quest 9
open: Are loopless lattice-path matroids distinguished by their chromatic quasisymmetric function? That is, does this invariant separate loopless lattice-path matroids from all other matroids?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing whether the chromatic quasisymmetric function is a complete invariant for loopless lattice-path matroids.
why: It would establish how fine an invariant the chromatic quasisymmetric function is on a well-studied class of matroids, a key step toward understanding which matroids can be reconstructed from chromatic-type data.

title: Primality of dilated closed path polyominoes — conjecture Conj:ZZW
open: Is a closed path polyomino's edge ideal always prime precisely when the polyomino avoids zig-zag walks? More formally: for a polyomino $P$, must $I_P$ be prime if and only if $P$ contains no zig-zag walks?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Niall Larney, arXiv:2609.30086v1 (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30086v1). No other progress is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation by counterexample) of the equivalence: $I_P$ is prime exactly when the polyomino $P$ contains no zig-zag walks.
why: It would give a complete combinatorial characterization of primality for the edge ideals arising from these polyominoes, reducing an algebraic question to a simple visual inspection of the shape.

title: Thinning and sprinkling: from robust sampling to almost Hamiltonicity
open: Another central open problem concerning Hamiltonicity is the Lovász conjecture for connected vertex-transitive graphs. Does every connected vertex-transitive graph admit a Hamiltonian cycle?
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper, "Thinning and sprinkling: from robust sampling to almost Hamiltonicity" (arXiv:2609.30165v1, Micha Christoph, Zach Hunter, Benny Sudakov), 2026.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every connected vertex-transitive graph contains a Hamiltonian cycle.
why: Vertex-transitive graphs are among the most symmetric graph classes, and the conjecture sits at the heart of Hamiltonicity theory; resolving it would settle the basic structural question of how symmetry forces a Hamiltonian cycle.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30165v1 (Micha Christoph, Zach Hunter, Benny Sudakov)

title: Optimal spectrum estimation
open: Can optimal spectrum estimation of an unknown quantum state be achieved with unentangled measurements that are all fixed in advance, with no adaptivity? More formally, we conjecture that the sample complexity established in {thm:unentangled} is optimal among all adaptive single-copy protocols.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that the copy bound of {thm:unentangled} is achievable using single-copy measurements fixed in advance, and optimal among all adaptive single-copy protocols.
why: It determines whether adaptivity is genuinely necessary for optimal unentangled spectrum estimation, separating (or collapsing) the power of adaptive versus non-adaptive measurement strategies.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30171v1 (Ainesh Bakshi, Apoorv Vikram Singh, Xinyu Tan)

title: Optimal spectrum estimation
open: Is the copy complexity achieved for spectrum estimation the best possible? We conjecture that this copy complexity is optimal among all algorithms using possibly adaptive unentangled measurements.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) — arXiv:2609.30171v1 (Ainesh Bakshi, Apoorv Vikram Singh, Xinyu Tan).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that no algorithm using possibly adaptive unentangled measurements can achieve spectrum estimation with lower copy complexity than the conjectured value.
why: It would settle the exact measurement and copy requirements for learning the spectrum of an unknown quantum state, separating what adaptivity and entanglement can or cannot save.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30171v1 (Ainesh Bakshi, Apoorv Vikram Singh, Xinyu Tan)

title: On the Binary Rank of Matrices with Constant Real Rank
open: What is the maximal binary rank a matrix can have when its real rank is a fixed constant? The source paper solves one of its open problems of this form and asks for purely mathematical proofs of results previously established only with computer assistance.
solved_when: The maximal binary rank of a matrix with constant real rank is determined, together with complete mathematical (computer-free) proofs of the results that were previously proved with the assistance of a computer program.
why: It replaces computational verification with rigorous argument, giving certainty and insight into the structure relating real rank and binary rank.

title: On the Binary Rank of Matrices with Constant Real Rank
open: Does there exist a matrix whose binary rank is exponentially larger than its real rank? Such an exponential separation would be directly connected to the log-rank conjecture.
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.30203v1 (Michal Parnas).
solved_when: An explicit matrix (or a proof of existence) is given whose binary rank exceeds its real rank by an exponential factor, or the possibility of such an exponential gap is ruled out.
why: The question is directly connected to the log-rank conjecture, so resolving it either supplies the separation needed to challenge the conjecture or removes a route toward refuting it.

title: On the completeness of gravitational pp-wave spacetimes: A counterexam — conjecture ek-conjecture
open: Is every geodesically complete gravitational pp-wave spacetime necessarily isometric to a plane wave spacetime?
solved_when: A proof that geodesic completeness forces any gravitational pp-wave to be a plane wave, or an explicit counterexample of a complete gravitational pp-wave not isometric to a plane wave.
why: It would settle whether completeness rigidly constrains the geometry of pp-waves, a basic structural question in Lorentzian geometry and general relativity.

title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conj
open: Is the general cross-product inequality at the heart of the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture within reach, or does the infinite barrier persist beyond the special case already in hand? Formally, the problem is to prove the general case of the inequality, of which only the special case—sufficient to derive the associated quadratic inequality—has been established.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30888v1 (Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak). The quadratic inequality follows from the special case of the cross-product inequality proved there, while the general case of the inequality remains a challenging open problem.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the general cross-product inequality is given, going beyond the special case from which the quadratic inequality currently follows.
why: The special case already yields the quadratic inequality, so resolving the general case would complete a key pillar of the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture framework that currently stands only partially proven.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30888v1 (Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak)

title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conj
open: Does the 1/3–2/3 conjecture hold — that is, does every finite partially ordered set that is not a chain contain two elements such that the proportion of linear extensions placing one above the other lies between 1/3 and 2/3? A sharpened version would establish the conjecture in full for all finite posets, a central question in order theory independently proposed by Kislitsyn and Fredman, in connection with sorting under partial information.
status: The problem is a central open problem in order theory, independently proposed by Kislitsyn and Fredman; it is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the 1/3–2/3 Conjecture" (Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak, arXiv:2609.30888).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the 1/3–2/3 conjecture for all finite posets; equivalently, showing that every non-chain finite poset contains a pair (x, y) with 1/3 ≤ Pr[x precedes y in a random linear extension] ≤ 2/3, or exhibiting a counterexample poset.
why: The conjecture underpins sorting with partial information: such a balanced pair guarantees a constant-factor reduction in the linear-extension search space, so resolving it settles the theoretical foundation of that sorting paradigm.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30888v1 (Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak)

title: Two-coloring cubic graphs with small monochromatic components, but wit
open: For every cubic graph that admits a perfect matching, what is the smallest bound $k$ such that the vertices can always be two-colored red and blue so that every monochromatic component has order at most $k$ and no monochromatic component is a single vertex? In other words, determine the minimum $k$ for which such a singleton-free coloring with small monochromatic components is guaranteed on this class of graphs.
solved_when: An exact value of $k$ is determined (with proof that every perfect-matchable cubic graph admits such a coloring with maximum monochromatic component order $k$ and no monochromatic singletons, and that $k$ is best possible).
why: It pins down how far the classical small-monochromatic-component coloring guarantee survives once singletons are forbidden, refining the structural theory of two-colorings on cubic graphs.

title: Attacking Diophantus: Special Cases of Bag Containment
open: Is query containment decidable under bag semantics? This is the version of the classical containment question in which query answers are multisets rather than sets, and it has remained open in database theory for over thirty years.
solved_when: A decision procedure for bag-semantics query containment is given (with a proof of decidability and finite complexity bound), or the problem is shown undecidable.
why: Bag semantics is the semantics real database systems actually use, so containment — the basis of query optimization and rewriting — is currently without a firm foundation in that setting.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30956v1 (George Konstantinidis, Xinzhuo Li, Fabio Mogavero)

title: Attacking Diophantus: Special Cases of Bag Containment
open: Is bag containment of conjunctive queries decidable? After decades of work, no algorithm or undecidability proof is known for this basic question in query evaluation semantics.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Attacking Diophantus" by George Konstantinidis, Xinzhuo Li, and Fabio Mogavero (http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30956v1).
solved_when: A decision procedure for bag containment of conjunctive queries is given, or the problem is proved undecidable.
why: Bag semantics is the natural model of how databases actually store and count tuples, so settling decidability determines whether containment checking — fundamental to query optimization — can ever be automated under bag semantics.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30956v1 (George Konstantinidis, Xinzhuo Li, Fabio Mogavero)

title: The number of touching pairs of congruent sphere packings in Euclidean
open: For sufficiently large $n$ of the form $n=16k^3-33k^2+24k-6$ with $k \in \mathbb{N}$, is the maximum number of touching pairs among $n$ congruent spheres in Euclidean space exactly $c(n)=6n-6(8k^2-11k+4)$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that, for all sufficiently large $n$ with $n=16k^3-33k^2+24k-6$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the contact number equals $c(n)=6n-6(8k^2-11k+4)$.
why: It settles the exact contact number for an infinite explicit family of sphere counts, advancing the determination of maximum contact numbers of congruent sphere packings.

title: Acyclic orientations of mixed graphs
open: What is the computational complexity of deciding whether a given digraph admits a non-separating out-branching? Equivalently, is this decision problem polynomial-time solvable, or is it NP-complete?
solved_when: A proof that deciding whether a digraph has a non-separating out-branching is in P, or a proof that the problem is NP-complete.
why: It settles a natural structural decision problem for digraphs left open in the source literature, refining the complexity landscape around out-branching existence questions.

title: Acyclic orientations of mixed graphs
open: What is the computational complexity of deciding whether a mixed graph $P$ admits an acyclic completion that contains a non-separating out-branching? Formally, determine whether this decision problem is polynomial-time solvable or NP-complete.
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32403v1 (Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Anders Yeo).
solved_when: A proof that the decision problem is solvable in polynomial time, or a proof of its NP-completeness, is established.
why: It settles a natural decision problem on mixed graphs left open in the source paper, completing the complexity picture around acyclic completions and out-branching structure.

title: Single-Exponential Algorithms for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on Plan
open: Does Directed Feedback Vertex Set admit a polynomial kernel when parameterized by the size of the solution, on general digraphs? That is, can every instance be reduced in polynomial time to an equivalent instance of size polynomial in the solution-size parameter?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2609.32728v1 (Daniel Lokshtanov, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue); no resolution is recorded here.
solved_when: An explicit polynomial-size kernelization algorithm for DFVS parameterized by solution size on general digraphs is given, together with a proof of correctness; equivalently, a lower bound ruling out such a kernel (subject to standard assumptions) would resolve the question negatively.
why: DFVS is a central digraph optimization problem, and a polynomial kernel would enable effective data reduction and compression of instances before any exact or parameterized algorithm is run.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32728v1 (Daniel Lokshtanov, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue)

title: Network Topology That Excludes Braess's Paradox and Maintains Monotoni — conjecture conj:BP
open: For a fixed positive constant inflow rate, does a single-source single-sink graph admit Braess's paradox precisely when it contains at least one of the graphs $M_1, M_2, M_3$ as a topological minor?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that, for a fixed positive constant inflow rate, a single-source single-sink graph $G$ admits Braess's paradox if and only if $G$ contains at least one of $M_1, M_2, M_3$ as a topological minor.
why: A characterization of this kind would give a purely structural, checkable criterion for when network upgrades can degrade equilibrium performance, allowing planners to rule out Braess's paradox by inspecting topology alone.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32738v1 (Xujin Chen, Xiyuan Deng, Changjun Wang)

title: Čech complexes for finite sets — conj i2-contractible
open: Is the inclusion $i_2:K_1 K_2 K_2$ null-homotopic — equivalently, is $K_1 K_2$ contractible inside $K_2$?
solved_when: The map $i_2:K_1 K_2 K_2$ is shown to be null-homotopic, i.e., a contraction of $K_1 K_2$ inside $K_2$ is constructed (or the assertion is refuted).
why: It settles a basic contractibility question about these Čech complexes for finite sets, left explicitly open in the source paper.

title: Simultaneous recovery of various time-dependent coefficients in a hype
open: Can multiple time-dependent coefficients of a hyperbolic equation be recovered simultaneously from its source-to-solution map? In other words, is there a uniqueness result establishing that such coefficients are determined by this data in the linear setting?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026) by Yavar Kian and Gungun Uhlmann, http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33393v1.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether various time-dependent coefficients of a linear hyperbolic equation are simultaneously recoverable from the source-to-solution map.
why: It would extend inverse-problem uniqueness theory for hyperbolic equations beyond the settings currently handled, where simultaneous recovery of several time-dependent coefficients remains unresolved.

title: A generalized Terao Conjecture for line arrangements — conjecture C1
open: Suppose two line arrangements in the complex projective plane have isomorphic intersection lattices; conjecture C1 asks whether this lattice-level data alone forces the property at issue to agree for the two arrangements, in the spirit of Terao's freeness conjecture but for a broader class of arrangements.
status: Conjecture C1 is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33584v2 (Alexandru Dimca, Piotr Pokora); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of conjecture C1 as stated in the source paper is given, with the claim verified for all line arrangements in the plane.
why: It would extend the philosophy that the combinatorics of an arrangement controls its algebraic geometry beyond the classical freeness setting, and a counterexample would expose a genuinely non-combinatorial invariant.

title: The Fibonacci numbers are not 3-accessible
open: What is the smallest number of terms of a monochromatic diffsequence that a 3-coloring of the integers can avoid? Formally, determine the minimum length L such that no 3-coloring of the integers avoids all monochromatic diffsequences of length L.
