title: Autonomous Quantum Memories from Classical Stochastic Processes
open: Can an autonomous quantum memory be realized by a time-independent Lindbladian driven only by a classical stochastic process — for instance, by the specific Lindbladian proposed in the source paper — rather than by time-dependent control?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.05589v1 (Nadav Drechsler, Yuval Oreg, Dorit Aharonov); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A time-independent Lindbladian of the proposed form is shown to preserve quantum information for the memory lifetime targeted in the source framework (or a proof is given that no such time-independent Lindbladian achieves it).
why: A time-independent, classically driven construction would remove the need for active time-dependent correction, pointing to genuinely autonomous quantum memories feasible with simple classical noise sources.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05589v1 (Nadav Drechsler, Yuval Oreg, Dorit Aharonov)

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var — conjecture conj:occ
open: Does every positive integer occur infinitely many times in the sequence $(a(N))_{N \geq 1}$ arising from the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$? This is one of three Kimberling conjectures on that array, and the occurrence-of-every-integer part remains unsettled.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05776v1 (Alex Ashburn).
solved_when: A proof that each positive integer appears infinitely often in $(a(N))_{N \geq 1}$ — equivalently, that no value occurs only finitely many times.
why: It completes the resolution of Kimberling's conjectures on the $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$ array, settling the occurrence structure of a Beatty-type sequence connected to the golden ratio.

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var — conjecture conj:strong
open: Is it true that for every $n \geq 1$, if the entries of rows $2n-1$ and $2n$ of Kimberling's array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$ are merged and arranged together in increasing order, then replacing each number by its rank in this ordering reproduces rows $1$ and $2$?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Alex Ashburn, arXiv:2610.05776v1.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the rank-replacement property stated above, for every $n \geq 1$, covering all three of Kimberling's conjectures if the record's remaining ones are subsumed.
why: It settles one of Kimberling's conjectures on this array, confirming an unexpected self-similarity property of the Beatty sequence $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$.

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var
open: Is the least index $N$ at which the value $v$ first appears in Kimberling's array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$ always the Lucas number $L_{4v-5}$, for every $v \ge 2$? Formally: for every $v \ge 2$, the least $N$ with $a(N) = v$ equals $L_{4v-5}$.
status: Stated as an open conjecture (the fourth of three conjectures of Kimberling addressed in the source) in the paper arXiv:2610.05776v1 (Alex Ashburn), 2026.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every integer $v \ge 2$, the first occurrence of $v$ in the array is exactly at position $N = L_{4v-5}$.
why: A proof would give a complete, exact description of when each value enters Kimberling's array, tying the array's structure to Lucas numbers; a disproof would expose unexpected irregularity in first occurrences.

title: The Complexity of Computing Nash Equilibria in Colonel Blotto Games
open: Is computing Nash equilibria hard in Colonel Blotto games even when the number of players is a fixed constant? This would settle the open question posed by Bichler and Ghosh, who established hardness in the player-specific equal-splitting setting when the number of players grows with the instance and asked whether hardness persists for a constant number of players.
solved_when: The complexity of computing Nash equilibria in the player-specific equal-splitting Colonel Blotto setting is determined for any constant number of players, resolving the question of Bichler and Ghosh.
why: It pins down whether the hardness of equilibrium computation in Colonel Blotto games is an artifact of many players or a robust structural feature, clarifying the boundary of tractability for a classic allocation game.

title: The Complexity of Computing Nash Equilibria in Colonel Blotto Games
open: Can Nash equilibria be computed efficiently in discrete Colonel Blotto games with monotonic, piecewise constant battlefield payoffs? Formally, is there a polynomial-time algorithm for this setting, or can computational hardness be established?
status: The question was posed as an open problem by Kontogiannis et al. (stated as open in the source paper, 2026); the paper by Vasilis Pollatos and Andreas Kontogiannis (http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05956v1) claims to answer it in the negative via hardness results.
solved_when: The question is settled by either a polynomial-time algorithm for computing Nash equilibria in discrete Colonel Blotto games with monotonic, piecewise constant battlefield payoffs, or a proof that no such efficient computation is possible (hardness).
why: Deciding between an efficient algorithm and hardness determines whether equilibrium analysis of Colonel Blotto games is computationally tractable in practice or fundamentally intractable, shaping both algorithm design and the interpretation of Blotto-based strategic models.

title: When the BSD Real Period Remembers Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ — unnumberedquestion 1
open: Can an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ be reconstructed, up to isomorphism, from the invariants that enter the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture alone? In other words, does the BSD data — including the real period — determine the curve itself?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06015v1 (Asuka Shiga); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) showing that the BSD invariants, among them the real period, do or do not determine an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ up to isomorphism over $\mathbb{Q}$.
why: It would show whether the analytic side of the BSD conjecture already encodes the geometry of the curve, telling us how much information the conjecture's ingredients actually carry about the object they describe.

title: A proof of GW/DT4 conjecture on local projective plane — conj main conj
open: Is the GW/DT4 conjecture true for the local projective plane — that is, can Gromov–Witten invariants of the local projective plane be matched by the corresponding DT4 invariants, proving the conjectured correspondence in this setting?
solved_when: A proof of the main conjecture of paper 2610.06024 establishing the GW/DT4 correspondence for the local projective plane is given.

title: On rigidity properties of unit-distance graphs
open: Does there exist a penny graph that is generically globally rigid yet penny-rigid but not globally penny-rigid — and likewise a marble graph that is marble-rigid but not globally marble-rigid? In other words, is the relationship between local and global rigidity nontrivial at the level of individual penny and marble graphs, rather than only at the generic level?
solved_when: An explicit example is given of a generically globally rigid penny graph that is penny-rigid but not globally penny-rigid, or an analogous example in the marble-graph setting — or a proof that no such graph exists.
why: Such an example would show that local and global rigidity genuinely diverge for penny and marble graphs, sharpening our understanding of how rigidity theory for disk-contact graphs differs from classical bar-and-joint rigidity.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06246v1 (Sean Dewar, Georg Grasegger, Alison La Porta)

title: The Lebrun--Salamon conjecture is true in dimension up to 56
open: Is every connected complete positive quaternionic Kähler manifold, up to rescaling, a Wolf space?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.06336v1 (Jordi Daura Serrano, Aron Gohr, Marie-Amélie Lawn), where it is noted to hold in dimension up to 56.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every connected complete positive quaternionic Kähler manifold is, up to rescaling, a Wolf space.
why: A positive answer would give a complete classification of positive quaternionic Kähler manifolds, reducing their study to the known symmetric Wolf spaces.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06336v1 (Jordi Daura Serrano, Aron Gohr, Marie-Amélie Lawn)

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: Can every simple non-bipartite quadrangulation map of the projective plane be realized as the diameter graph of an extremal set with full symmetry preserved? Formally, given such a quadrangulation $Q$, does there exist an extremal set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ whose diameter graph realizes $Q$ and on which $Aut(Q)$ acts as a group of isometries?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), "Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II" (Gábor Damásdi), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06340v1.
solved_when: A construction is given that, for any simple non-bipartite quadrangulation map $Q$ of the projective plane, produces an extremal set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ whose diameter quadrangulation is $Q$ and on which $Aut(Q)$ acts as a group of isometries.
why: It would complete a geometric realization program for diameter graphs, showing that combinatorial quadrangulations and their automorphism groups can be faithfully realized geometrically as extremal sets.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap — problem prob:densesym
open: Let $H$ be a symmetry group of a Reuleaux polyhedron. Is the family of Reuleaux polyhedra having symmetry group containing $H$ dense in the family of bodies of constant width having symmetry group $H$?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with an explicit counterexample) that, for every symmetry group $H$ of a Reuleaux polyhedron, the Reuleaux polyhedra with symmetry group containing $H$ are (or are not) dense in the bodies of constant width with symmetry group exactly $H$.
why: A positive answer would let the rich combinatorial structure of Reuleaux polyhedra approximate arbitrary constant-width bodies with prescribed symmetry, transferring finite, discrete data to a continuous geometric class.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: If $G$ is a stress-free diameter framework in $\mathbb{R}^d$, must $G$ be $(d+1)$-colorable?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every stress-free diameter framework in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is $(d+1)$-colorable, for general $d$.
why: It would connect the geometric rigidity condition of stress-freeness to graph coloring, extending chromatic constraints on geometric graph classes.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: Suppose $C$ is a smooth strictly convex body in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Which graphs can arise as the tangency graph of a family of pairwise intersecting translates of $C$?
solved_when: A characterization — structural or otherwise checkable — is given of exactly the graphs realizable as tangency graphs of families of pairwise intersecting translates of such a body $C$.
why: A characterization would extend the classical theory of contact graphs of translated convex bodies to the setting where all translates pairwise intersect, clarifying which combinatorial structures survive this strong intersection constraint.

title: Decreasing Diagrams are Complete for Confluence
open: Can confluence of a rewrite relation always be localized — that is, witnessed by a decreasing labeling of the one-step rewrite relation? This is Problem 56 of the RTA List of Open Problems, posed by van Oostrom in 1993.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06368v1 (Jörg Endrullis, Ievgen Ivanov, Femke van Raamsdonk).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given of the existence, for every confluent rewrite relation, of a decreasing labeling of its one-step steps that establishes confluence via the decreasing-diagrams technique.
why: A positive answer would make decreasing diagrams a complete confluence-proving method, so any confluent system would admit a local, checkable confluence witness — greatly extending the reach of automated confluence tools.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06368v1 (Jörg Endrullis, Ievgen Ivanov, Femke van Raamsdonk)

title: Decreasing Diagrams are Complete for Confluence
open: Is every abstract rewriting system that is confluent also decreasing Church–Rosser? In other words, does the decreasing-diagrams technique capture confluence in full, resolving Problem 56 of the RTA List of Open Problems?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.06368v1 (Jörg Endrullis, Ievgen Ivanov, Femke van Raamsdonk), where it appears as a main theorem that every confluent ARS is decreasing Church–Rosser.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every confluent abstract rewriting system is decreasing Church–Rosser over itself.
why: It would establish decreasing diagrams as a complete — not merely sound — method for proving confluence, settling a long-standing question from the RTA List of Open Problems.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06368v1 (Jörg Endrullis, Ievgen Ivanov, Femke van Raamsdonk)

title: Regularity of soda-can domains for the $p$-parabolic equation
open: Does a single barrier suffice to characterize boundary regularity for the $p$-parabolic equation in the degenerate range, or can it fail? Formally, the question is whether one barrier is enough for boundary-regularity characterization in the Perron solution framework for $\partial_t u - \Delta_p u = 0$ on soda-can domains.
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.06497v1 (Benny Avelin, Mikko Parviainen), where boundary regularity is studied for the $p$-parabolic equation $\partial_t u - \operatorname{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)=0$ via the Perron method.
solved_when: The question is answered either by a proof that one barrier always suffices to characterize boundary regularity in the degenerate range, or by an explicit counterexample (a soda-can domain construction) showing that one barrier does not suffice.
why: A negative answer of this kind shows that the standard single-barrier characterization breaks down in the degenerate regime, forcing a barrier-family approach to boundary regularity for the $p$-parabolic equation.

title: Regularity of soda-can domains for the $p$-parabolic equation
open: For the $p$-parabolic equation, is there a Wiener criterion — a necessary and sufficient condition on the geometry of the boundary — characterizing regularity of boundary points in a general space-time domain? The original statement is framed for "soda-can" domains, and the question is whether a complete Wiener-type characterization extends beyond such special geometries.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper arXiv:2610.06497v1 (Benny Avelin, Mikko Parviainen), dated 2026.
solved_when: A Wiener criterion for boundary-point regularity of the $p$-parabolic equation is proved to be both necessary and sufficient in general space-time domains, not just soda-can domains.
why: A complete Wiener criterion would give a geometric characterization of when solutions attain their boundary data, closing the regularity theory for the $p$-parabolic equation in the same way the classical Wiener criterion does for the Laplacian.

title: Uniform oscillation properties of almost periodic functions
open: Do solutions in the special case considered possess an oscillation time that is uniform in a stronger sense — independent of a certain parameter? Formally, while any solution has a uniform oscillation time by the cited Theorem, it is unknown whether this time can be made independent of that parameter, a problem raised in 1985 and already mentioned in the literature.
solved_when: An oscillation time independent of the parameter is established (or disproven) for all solutions in the special case.
why: It would settle a uniform oscillation question dating back to 1985, sharpening known oscillation estimates that currently depend on the parameter.

title: ON THE DISTANCE TO DISCRIMINANTS AND OSCULATING VARIETIES
open: What are the expectations of these invariants under the Bombieri–Weyl product? More precisely, compute $E(\,)$ and $E(\,^k)$ with respect to the Bombieri–Weyl product.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06538v1 (Khazhgali Kozhasov, Bernard Mourrain, Adam Parusi{ń}ski).
solved_when: The expectations $E(\,)$ and $E(\,^k)$ with respect to the Bombieri–Weyl product are computed in closed form.
why: A solution would extend the distance-to-discriminants and osculating-variety framework of the source paper with the missing expectation computations, giving the average-case behavior of these invariants.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06538v1 (Khazhgali Kozhasov, Bernard Mourrain, Adam Parusi{ń}ski)

title: Information causality does not single out the set of quantum correlati
open: Does the principle of information causality hold for the entire set of almost quantum correlations? A sharpened form: is it the case that every correlation in the almost quantum set satisfies the information-causality constraint?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.06604v1 (Marco Pompili, Mirjam Weilenmann); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof that all almost quantum correlations satisfy information causality, or an explicit counterexample of an almost quantum correlation violating it.
why: It determines whether information causality, a physical principle intended to characterize quantum theory, is in fact weaker than quantumness itself or exactly matches the (larger) almost quantum set.

title: Separating ClonableQMA and QCMA Relative to a Classical Oracle
open: Does there exist a classical oracle relative to which ClonableQMA and QCMA are separated? In other words, can one exhibit a classical oracle $O$ such that ClonableQMA^O ≠ QCMA^O?
solved_when: A classical oracle $O$ is explicitly constructed (or its existence proved) relative to which ClonableQMA and QCMA differ.
why: Such a separation would clarify whether the clonability of quantum proofs genuinely adds proving power beyond classical witnesses, delineating the structural boundary between these proof-system classes.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06740v1 (Alper Cakan, Kai-Min Chung, Wei-Hsiang Hung)

title: The compress-with-another threshold of Szykuła's Figure 3 family
open: What is the exact compress-with-another threshold of the corrected Figure 3 family in Szykuła's survey of open problems, and can it be established by a self-contained pair-automaton argument?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2026), which gives a self-contained pair-automaton proof of the exact compress-with-another threshold of the corrected Figure 3 family in Szykuła's survey of open problems (http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07044v1, Qichao Wang).
solved_when: The exact compress-with-another threshold of the corrected Figure 3 family is proven, ideally via a self-contained pair-automaton proof.
why: It resolves one of the open problems posed in Szykuła's survey of open problems on synchronizing automata, extending exact pair-distance knowledge to a named family of automata.

title: Cyclic Hamilton Cycle Decompositions of Carousel Tournaments of Order — problem prob:carousel
open: For which odd integers $n$ does the carousel tournament $T_n$ admit a decomposition of its arc set into Hamilton cycles that is invariant under a cyclic rotation of the vertices?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.07102v1 (Hongci Liao, Yongju Peng, Guang Li); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: A complete characterization of the odd integers $n$ for which $T_n$ admits a cyclic Hamilton cycle decomposition is given, together with constructions for the $n$ where it exists and proofs of nonexistence where it does not.
why: It would settle a natural structural question about carousel tournaments, connecting cyclic symmetry with Hamilton cycle decompositions of highly regular digraphs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07102v1 (Hongci Liao, Yongju Peng, Guang Li)

title: The One-Power Erdős Conjecture for Primes $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$ — conjecture conj:onepower
open: Can every prime $p$ with $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$ be written as $p = 2^a + m$, where $a \geq 0$ is an integer and $m$ is a squarefree positive integer?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.07214v1 (Shen Harman, Dana Paquin).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit prime $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$ admitting no such representation) of the claim that every such prime has this form is given.
why: It is a concrete case of the one-power Erdős conjecture, and resolving it would advance the general program of representing primes as a power of two plus a squarefree integer.

title: The One-Power Erdős Conjecture for Primes $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$ — conjecture conj:cofinite
open: Are all but finitely many primes $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$ expressible as $p = 2^a + m$ with $a \geq 0$ and $m$ squarefree? In other words, does this restricted arithmetic progression of primes admit such a representation with at most finitely many exceptions?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every prime $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$, with at most finitely many exceptions, can be written as $p = 2^a + m$ with $a \geq 0$ and $m$ squarefree.
why: It is a specific instance of the one-power Erdős conjecture on a restricted congruence class of primes, so a resolution would test how far the conjecture holds beyond its original setting and could reveal new methods for handling squarefree shifts of powers of two in arithmetic progressions.

title: Pattern avoidance in alternating sign rectangles I: Extended avoidance
open: Is there a closed-form formula for the number of extendably MATH-avoiding alternating sign rectangles? Computer experiments suggest such a formula exists, and the conjecture is that it can be written down explicitly.
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07442v1 (Hans Höngesberg, Matjaž Konvalinka, Svante Linusson), where it is motivated by computer experiments.
solved_when: A closed-form expression for the enumeration of extendably MATH-avoiding ASRs is proved, matching the formula suggested by the computer experiments.
why: A proof would turn experimental enumeration data into an exact enumerative result, settling the conjecture raised in the source paper.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07442v1 (Hans Höngesberg, Matjaž Konvalinka, Svante Linusson)

title: The Geometry of Empowerment
open: Is the potential-empowerment lower bound on adaptation in discrete MDPs tight, and does it extend to continuous state geometries? In formal terms, the question is whether the bound — which trades Gaussian widths against KL divergence — can be achieved exactly, and whether an analogue holds beyond discrete MDPs.
status: The bound — potential empowerment lower bounds adaptation in discrete MDPs — is established, with full experimental details in the paper's proof-adaptation appendix; the source paper (2026) explicitly states the tightness and continuous-geometry questions as open. Key work: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07796v1 (Catherine Ji, Vivek Myers, Sergey Levine).
solved_when: Either a matching upper bound (or counterexample) resolves the tightness question in discrete MDPs, or the lower bound is proved or refuted for continuous state geometries.
why: Tightness would tell us whether potential empowerment fully characterizes adaptation, and the continuous extension would make the bound usable in realistic settings beyond discrete MDPs.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07796v1 (Catherine Ji, Vivek Myers, Sergey Levine)

title: Semisimplicity, purity and Mumford-Tate conjecture for hyper-Kähler va
open: Does the Mumford–Tate conjecture hold for hyper-Kähler varieties? The conjecture was originally formulated for abelian varieties and remains open in general, even in that case.
solved_when: The Mumford–Tate conjecture is proven for hyper-Kähler varieties (and, in the abelian case, for all abelian varieties), together with the semisimplicity and purity statements posed alongside it.
why: A proof would extend the Mumford–Tate framework beyond the classical abelian setting, tying Hodge-theoretic and l-adic monodromy data for hyper-Kähler varieties into the standard comparison formalism.

title: When Plans Change Answers: Formalizing Cost-Accuracy Optimization for
open: When some relations carry no semantic operator, their atoms become deterministic — under what conditions does this move the tractability boundary? The exact dichotomy between easy and hard cases in that setting remains to be characterized.
solved_when: A complete dichotomy is proven for the case where some relations carry no semantic operator, so that every query in this setting is classified as tractable or hard, covering the deterministic-atom regime left open in the source paper.
why: It would complete the complexity classification for cost–accuracy query optimization under bag semantics, telling optimizer designers exactly which sum-of-products queries can be handled efficiently and which are provably hard.

title: On Sárközy's Local Extrema Conjectures — conj conj:53
open: Suppose $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is a multiplicative function such that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$ there are at least two primes $p_1,p_2$ with $f(p_j) > p_j^k$ for $j=1,2$. Must the sets $L_f$ and $S_f$ of local extrema both be infinite?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given that, under the stated hypothesis on $f$, both $L_f$ and $S_f$ are infinite sets.
why: This is one of Sárközy's local extrema conjectures concerning the behavior of multiplicative functions; resolving it advances our understanding of how multiplicativity constrains local oscillation of arithmetic functions.

title: Relative isoperimetry in the three-dimensional cube: classification an
open: Which sets in the three-dimensional cube minimize the relative (interior-boundary) isoperimetric functional for a prescribed enclosed volume, and can the minimizers be completely classified? A full classification would in particular resolve the isoperimetric conjecture in Milman's formulation (Conjecture 1.1) for all cuboids and the three-dimensional case of Brezis's Open Problem 10.1.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), Bin Deng, Jiahuan Li, Yilu Liu, http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08644v1; that work resolves the isoperimetric conjecture in Milman's formulation (Conjecture 1.1) for all cuboids and the three-dimensional case of Brezis's Open Problem 10.1.
solved_when: A complete classification of relative-isoperimetric minimizers in the three-dimensional cube is given, resolving Milman's Conjecture 1.1 for all cuboids and Brezis's Open Problem 10.1 in dimension three.
why: It settles the sharp relative isoperimetric inequality in the cube — the model case for cuboids — and closes a three-dimensional instance of Brezis's problem, with consequences for sharp constants in Sobolev-type trace and isoperimetric inequalities on bounded domains.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08644v1 (Bin Deng, Jiahuan Li, Yilu Liu)

title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach sp — problem prob:duall_1
open: Does every infinite-dimensional real Banach space satisfy the stated duality condition on numerical index left open in the source paper?
status: The problem was stated as open in the source paper (2006); no further progress is recorded in the census. Key work: http://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605781v1 (Vladimir Kadets, Miguel Martin, Rafael Paya).
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) of the duality question for the numerical index of infinite-dimensional real Banach spaces, as formulated in the source paper.
why: It would advance understanding of how the numerical index behaves under duality, a central tool in the geometry of Banach spaces.
key_works: http://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605781v1 (Vladimir Kadets, Miguel Martin, Rafael Paya)
